## Geometry-serialization

# NetWorks JSON geometry format
The NetWorks geometry format uses object-model approach. It uses the set of geometry primitives used by NetWorks Core.
## Serialization in JSON[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Data-Service/Geometry-serialization/NetWorks-JSON-geometry-format.html#serialization-in-json)
Geometries are serialized to WKT strings wrapped in a JSON object with a single `networksjson` property, which contains a JSON object. The first property of the geometry JSON object is always type.

```
{
  "networksjson": {
    "type": "OrientedPoint",
    "origin": [1, 2, 3],
    "orientation": [1, 1, 0]
  }
}

```

## Coordinate[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Data-Service/Geometry-serialization/NetWorks-JSON-geometry-format.html#coordinate)
Array of ordinates. The array is expected to have 2 or 3 members ([X, Y] or [X, Y, Z]). Other members beyond Z are ignored. If Z is missing, it is assumed to be 0.
## OrientedPoint[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Data-Service/Geometry-serialization/NetWorks-JSON-geometry-format.html#orientedpoint)
Point with orientation vector (unit vector).  
| Name  | Type  | Mandatory  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| type  | string  | Y  | Constant `OrientedPoint`  |  
| origin  | [Coordinate](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Data-Service/Geometry-serialization/NetWorks-JSON-geometry-format.html#coordinate)  | Y  | Position  |  
| orientation  | [Coordinate](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Data-Service/Geometry-serialization/NetWorks-JSON-geometry-format.html#coordinate)  |   | Orientation unit vector.  |  
**Example**

```
{
    "type": "OrientedPoint",
    "origin": [1, 2, 3],
    "orientation": [1, 1, 0]
}

```

## TextPoint[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Data-Service/Geometry-serialization/NetWorks-JSON-geometry-format.html#textpoint)
Point with orientation vector (unit vector), text and alignment. This type is not used to represent label geometries.  
| Name  | Type  | Mandatory  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| type  | String  | Y  | Constant `TextPoint`  |  
| origin  | [Coordinate](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Data-Service/Geometry-serialization/NetWorks-JSON-geometry-format.html#coordinate)  | Y  | Position  |  
| rotation  | double  |   | Orientation angle.  |  
| text  | String  |   | Label  |  
| alignment  | integer  |   | Alignment (see Networks Core constants for alignment).  |  
**Example**

```
{
    "type": "TextPoint",
    "origin": [1, 2, 3],
    "rotation": 1.57,
    "text": "text",
    "alignment": 5
}

```

## Polyline[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Data-Service/Geometry-serialization/NetWorks-JSON-geometry-format.html#polyline)
Linear sequence of points.  
| Name  | Type  | Mandatory  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| type  | string  | Y  | Constant `Polyline`  |  
| points  | Array of [Coordinate](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Data-Service/Geometry-serialization/NetWorks-JSON-geometry-format.html#coordinate)  | Y  | Points  |  
**Example**

```
{
    "type": "Polyline",
    "points": [
        [ 1, 2, 3 ],
        [ 4, 5, 6 ],
        [ 7, 8, 9 ]
    ]
}

```

## Polygon[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Data-Service/Geometry-serialization/NetWorks-JSON-geometry-format.html#polygon)
Closed polygon formed by linear sequence of points. The first and last points are the same.  
| Name  | Type  | Mandatory  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| type  | string  | Y  | Constant `Polygon`  |  
| points  | Array of [Coordinate](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Data-Service/Geometry-serialization/NetWorks-JSON-geometry-format.html#coordinate)  | Y  | Points  |  
**Example**

```
{
    "type": "Polygon",
    "points": [
        [ 1, 2, 1 ],
        [ 3, 4, 2 ],
        [ 5, 6, 3 ],
        [ 7, 8, 4 ],
        [ 1, 2, 1 ]
    ]
}

```

## Arc[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Data-Service/Geometry-serialization/NetWorks-JSON-geometry-format.html#arc)
Circular arc defined by start point, point on the arc and end point.
**Note**
Arc is not used as a standalone top-level geometry. It is a part of CompositePolyline, CompositePolygon or Boundary geometries.  
| Name  | Type  | Mandatory  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| type  | string  | Y  | Constant `Arc`  |  
| points  | Array of [Coordinate](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Data-Service/Geometry-serialization/NetWorks-JSON-geometry-format.html#coordinate)  | Y  | Points. Exactly 3 points must be specified.  |  
**Example**

```
{
    "type": "Arc",
    "points": [
        [ 0, 1, 0 ],
        [ 0.5, 0.5, 0 ],
        [ 0, 0, 0 ]
    ]
}

```

## PolylineSegment[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Data-Service/Geometry-serialization/NetWorks-JSON-geometry-format.html#polylinesegment)
[Polyline](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Data-Service/Geometry-serialization/NetWorks-JSON-geometry-format.html#polyline) | [Arc](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Data-Service/Geometry-serialization/NetWorks-JSON-geometry-format.html#arc)
## CompositePolyline[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Data-Service/Geometry-serialization/NetWorks-JSON-geometry-format.html#compositepolyline)
Collection of linear segments formed by polyline and arc segments. Starting and ending points of internal segments are the same (end point of segment 1 is the same as start point of segment 2, etc).  
| Name  | Type  | Mandatory  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| type  | string  | Y  | Constant `CompositePolyline`  |  
| geometries  | Array of [PolylineSegment](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Data-Service/Geometry-serialization/NetWorks-JSON-geometry-format.html#polylinesegment)  | Y  | Polyline segments. Only Polyline and Arc geometries are allowed.  |  
**Example**

```
{
    "type": "CompositePolyline",
    "geometries": [{
            "type": "Polyline",
            "points": [[0, 0, 0], [1, 1, 0]]
        }, {
            "type": "Polyline",
            "points": [[1, 1, 0], [2, 2, 0], [0, 0, 0]]
        }
    ]
}

```

## CompositePolygon[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Data-Service/Geometry-serialization/NetWorks-JSON-geometry-format.html#compositepolygon)
Polygon formed by a collection of linear and circular arc segments. Starting and ending points of internal segments are the same (end point of segment 1 is the same as start point of segment 2, etc).  
| Name  | Type  | Mandatory  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| type  | string  | Y  | Constant `CompositePolygon`  |  
| geometries  | Array of [PolylineSegment](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Data-Service/Geometry-serialization/NetWorks-JSON-geometry-format.html#polylinesegment)  | Y  | Polygon segments. Only Polyline and Arc geometries are allowed.  |  
**Example**

```
{
    "type": "CompositePolygon",
    "geometries": [
        {
            "type": "Polyline",
            "points": [
                [ 0, 0, 0 ],
                [ 1, 0, 0 ],
                [ 1, 1, 0 ]
            ]
        },
        {
            "type": "Polyline",
            "points": [
                [ 1, 1, 0 ],
                [ 1, 2, 0 ],
                [ 0, 1, 0 ]
            ]
        },
        {
            "type": "Arc",
            "points": [
                [ 0, 1, 0 ],
                [ 0.5, 0.5, 0 ],
                [ 0, 0, 0 ]
            ]
        }
    ]
}

```

## Boundary[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Data-Service/Geometry-serialization/NetWorks-JSON-geometry-format.html#boundary)
Polygon with zero or more holes.  
| Name  | Type  | Mandatory  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| type  | string  | Y  | Constant `Boundary`  |  
| exterior  | Geometry  | Y  | Exterior Polygon or CompositePolygon geometry.  |  
| holes  | Array of Geometry  |   | Geometry collection of holes. Each hole must be a Polygon or CompositePolygon.  |  
**Example**

```
{
    "type": "Boundary",
    "exterior": {
        "type": "Polygon",
        "points": [
            [ 0, 0, 0 ],
            [ 5, 5, 0 ],
            [ 3, 3, 0 ],
            [ 4, 4, 0 ],
            [ 0, 0, 0 ]
        ]
    },
    "holes": {
        "type": "GeometryCollection",
        "geometries": [
            {
                "type": "Polygon",
                "points": [
                    [ 0, 0, 0 ],
                    [ 1, 1, 0 ]
                ]
            },
            {
                "type": "CompositePolygon",
                "geometries": [
                    {
                        "type": "Polygon",
                        "points": [
                            [ 0, 0, 0 ],
                            [ 1, 1, 0 ]
                        ]
                    },
                    {
                        "type": "Arc",
                        "points": [
                            [ 0, 0, 0 ],
                            [ 1, 2, 0 ],
                            [ 1, 1, 0 ]
                        ]
                    }
                ]
            }
        ]
    }
}

```

## GeometryCollection[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Data-Service/Geometry-serialization/NetWorks-JSON-geometry-format.html#geometrycollection)
Heterogenous collection of multiple geometries. This type is not used for top-level geometries in NetWorks.  
| Name  | Type  | Mandatory  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| type  | string  | Y  | Constant `GeometryCollection`  |  
| geometries  | Array of Geometry  |   | Child geometries.  |  
**Example**

```
{
    "type": "GeometryCollection",
    "geometries": [{
            "type": "OrientedPoint",
            "origin": [1, 2, 3],
            "orientation": [1, 1, 0]
        }, {
            "type": "Polyline",
            "points": [
                [1, 2, 3],
                [4, 5, 6],
                [7, 8, 9]
            ]
        }, {
            "type": "Polygon",
            "points": [
                [1, 2, 1],
                [3, 4, 2],
                [5, 6, 3],
                [7, 8, 4],
                [1, 2, 1]
            ]
        }
    ]
}

```

## Raster[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Data-Service/Geometry-serialization/NetWorks-JSON-geometry-format.html#raster)
NetWorks Core Raster geometry.  
| Name  | Type  | Mandatory  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| type  | string  | Y  | Constant `Raster`  |  
| points  | Array of [Coordinate](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Data-Service/Geometry-serialization/NetWorks-JSON-geometry-format.html#coordinate)  | Y  | Raster polygon. 5 points are expected.  |  
| filename  | string  |   | Name of the file with raster geometry.  |  
| matrix  | Array of Number  |   | Raster transformation 4x4 matrix stored in as rows (each inner array is a row in the matrix). The rightmost column of the array is omitted.  |  
**Example**

```
{
    "type": "Raster",
    "polygon": {
        "type": "Polygon",
        "points": [
            [1, 2, 1],
            [3, 4, 2],
            [5, 6, 3],
            [7, 8, 4],
            [1, 2, 1]
        ]
    },
    "filename": "test.jpg",
    "matrix": [[0, 0, 0], [1, 1, 1], [2, 2, 2], [3, 3, 3]]
}

```

# WKT
## Serialization in JSON[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Data-Service/Geometry-serialization/WKT.html#serialization-in-json)
Geometries are serialized to WKT strings wrapped in a JSON object with a single wkt property:

```
{
  "wkt": "POINT (241791.888738 485831.672920)"
}

```

## Supported geometry types[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Data-Service/Geometry-serialization/WKT.html#supported-geometry-types)  
| Geometry type  | WKT  | Notes  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| [Point](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Data-Service/Geometry-serialization/WKT.html#point)  | POINT  |   |  
| [OrientedPoint](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Data-Service/Geometry-serialization/WKT.html#orientedpoint)  | POINT M  
POINT ZM  | Orientation vector is stored in the M dimension  |  
| [TextPoint](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Data-Service/Geometry-serialization/WKT.html#textpoint)  | POINT M  
POINT ZM  | Orientation vector is stored in the M dimension  |  
| [Polyline](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Data-Service/Geometry-serialization/WKT.html#polyline)  | LINESTRING  |   |  
| [Polygon](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Data-Service/Geometry-serialization/WKT.html#polygon)  | POLYGON  |   |  
| [CompositePolyline](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Data-Service/Geometry-serialization/WKT.html#compositepolyline)  | LINESTRING  
COMPOUNDCURVE  |   |  
| [CompositePolygon](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Data-Service/Geometry-serialization/WKT.html#compositepolygon)  | POLYGON  
CURVEPOLYGON  |   |  
| [Boundary](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Data-Service/Geometry-serialization/WKT.html#boundary)  | POLYGON  
CURVEPOLYGON  |   |  
3D versions of the geometries use the Z layout specifier (e.g. `LINESTRING Z(1 2 3, 4 5 6))`.
## Point[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Data-Service/Geometry-serialization/WKT.html#point)
Native WKT Point without orientation.
Example

```
{
  "wkt": "POINT (241791.888738 485831.672920)"
}

```

## OrientedPoint[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Data-Service/Geometry-serialization/WKT.html#orientedpoint)
Used of point symbol and text geometries. Orientation vector is stored in the M dimension using the following formula:

```
M = (Azimuth * 1000000) + (Elevation / 10)

```

Azimuth is angle in radians in the XY plane. Vector (1,0) has azimuth of 0, positive values are counterclockwise. Elevation is the angle in radians between the XY plane and the vector, with positive values towards positive Z values. Elevation of 0 is a vector on the XY plane, e.g. (1,0,0). The allowed values are between 0 and π/2 (positive elevation) and 2π and 2π-π/2 (negative elevation + 2π, to avoid negative values).
The result M is a number whose integer part is the azimuth in the XY plane multiplied by 1000000. The decimal part is the elevation in the Z axis divided by 10, to account for all numbers in the 0-2π range.  
| Vector  | Azimuth  | Elevation  | M  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| (1,0,0)  | 0  | 0  | 0  |  
| (0,1,0)  | 1.570796  | 0  | 1570796  |  
| (0,-1,0)  | -1.570796  | 0  | -1570797  |  
| (0.7071068, 0.7071068,0)  | 0.785398  | 0  | 785398  |  
| (0.5, 0.5, 0.7071068)  | 0.785398  | 0.785398  | 785398.0785398  |  
| (0,0,1)  | 0  | 1.570796  | 0.1570796  |  
| (0,0,-1)  | 0  | 1.570796  | -0.1570796  |  
For reference see [Spherical coordinate system on Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spherical_coordinate_system).
The semantics of the orientation follow G/Technology logic. The vector is rotated 90 degrees clockwise from the upright position of the symbol. For symbol geometry to be rendered horizontally (i.e. text or symbol "sits" on the unit vector line), vector (1,0,0) should be used.
Example 2D

```
{
  "wkt": "POINT M(241791.888738 485831.672920 1570796.0)"
}

```

Example 3D

```
{
  "wkt": "POINT ZM(241791.888738 485831.672920 123.345 1550000.066)"
}

```

## TextPoint[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Data-Service/Geometry-serialization/WKT.html#textpoint)
As [OrientedPoint](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Data-Service/Geometry-serialization/WKT.html#orientedpoint). The difference to OrientedPoint is semantic. TextPoint is used to display labels. Alignment is stored as a part of the component data outside of the geometry. Rotation vector is only 2D.
## Polyline[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Data-Service/Geometry-serialization/WKT.html#polyline)
String of vertices encoded as WKT LINESTRING.
_Example_

```
{
  "wkt": "LINESTRING (241790.888738 485830.672920, 241785.672213 485832.860495, 241747.978613 485851.202470)"
}

```

## Polygon[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Data-Service/Geometry-serialization/WKT.html#polygon)
One or more rings of vertices. The first ring is the outer ring, the other are holes. WKT POLYGON geometry can map to G/Technology Polygon, CompositePolygon if it contains only one ring. If there are multiple rings, it always maps to Boundary geometry.
_Example_

```
{
  "wkt": "POLYGON ((4502009.984 5925469.015, 4502009.03 5925467.513, 4502011.735, 5925467.513, 4502009.984, 5925469.015))"
}

```

## CompositePolyline[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Data-Service/Geometry-serialization/WKT.html#compositepolyline)
Polyline composed of linestring and circular arc segments. Encoded as WKT COMPOUNDCURVE.
**Note** This type of geometry is supported by the server workflows, but not for placement and editing in the interactive clients.
_Example_

```
{
  "wkt": "COMPOUNDCURVE Z(CIRCULARSTRING (0 0 0,1 1 0,2 0 0),(2 0 0,6 6 0),(6 6 0,5 5 0))"
}

```

## CompositePolygon[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Data-Service/Geometry-serialization/WKT.html#compositepolygon)
Polygon composed of linestring and circular arc segments. Encoded as WKT CURVEPOLYGON.
**Note**
This type of geometry is supported by the server workflows, but not for placement and editing in the interactive clients.
_Example_

```
{
  "wkt": "CURVEPOLYGON Z(COMPOUNDCURVE (CIRCULARSTRING (0 0 0,1 1 0,2 0 0),(2 0 0,6 6 0),(6 6 0,5 5 0)))"
}

```

## Boundary[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Data-Service/Geometry-serialization/WKT.html#boundary)
As [Polygon](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Data-Service/Geometry-serialization/WKT.html#polygon) and [CompositePolygon](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Data-Service/Geometry-serialization/WKT.html#compositepolygon), with multiple inner rings.
_Example_

```
{
  "wkt": "POLYGON ((4502009.984 5925469.015, 4502009.03 5925467.513, 4502011.735 5925467.513, 4502009.984 5925469.015), (4502019.984 5925469.015, 4502029.03 5925467.513, 4502031.735 5925467.513))"
}

```

_Example 2_

```
{
  "wkt": "CURVEPOLYGON Z(COMPOUNDCURVE (CIRCULARSTRING (0 0 0,1 1 0,2 0 0),(2 0 0,6 6 0),(6 6 0,5 5 0)),COMPOUNDCURVE (CIRCULARSTRING (0 0 0,1 1 0,2 0 0),(2 0 0,6 6 0),(6 6 0,5 5 0)))"
}

```

# Geometry serialization
Multiple geometry formats are supported in the interfaces:
  * [NetWorks geometry format](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Data-Service/Geometry-serialization/NetWorks-JSON-geometry-format.html) JSON based serialization of the IGTGeometry-like format, which supports all types of geometry.
  * [WKT](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Data-Service/Geometry-serialization/WKT.html) String-based format.
  * GeoJSON JSON-based serialization format, limited to basic types Point, LineString and Polygon. This format does not support features like Arc and CompositePolyline/Polygon geometries.

In JSON, geometries are always serialized as JSON objects. The type of the enclosed geometry is determined from the property name of the object:  
| Property  | Format  |  
| --- | --- |  
| networksjson  | NetWorks geometry format  |  
| wkt  | WKT  |  
| geojson  | GeoJSON  |  
**Examples**
NetWorks JSON geometry format

```
{
  "networksjson": {
    "type": "OrientedPoint",
    "origin": [1, 2, 3],
    "orientation": [1, 1, 0]
  }
}

```

WKT

```
{
    "wkt": "LINESTRING(4502788 5925546, 4502798 5925546)"
}

```

GeoJSON

```
{
  "geojson": {
    "type": "Point",
    "coordinates": [1, 2, 3]
  }
}

```

## Metadata

# GetDetailMetadata
Returns detail metadata for a G3E_FNO, based on G3E_DETAILS_OPTABLE and G3E_DETAILLEGEND_OPTABLE.
## Request[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Data-Service/Metadata/GetDetailMetadata.html#request)
**Method**
GET
**URL Template**
`/metadata/relationships/detail/{fno}`
**Path variables**  
| Name  | Type  | Mandatory  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| {fno}  | Integer  | Y  | G3E_FNO  |  
## Response[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Data-Service/Metadata/GetDetailMetadata.html#response)
Serialized rows from G3E_DETAILS_OPTABLE for given G3E_FNO grouped by G3E_DRNO, as well as:
  * list of fno, cno to be placed in
  * list of legends for this FNO
  * reverse list - where this FNO can be placed (owner FNOs)

## Example[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Data-Service/Metadata/GetDetailMetadata.html#example)

# GetDetailOwners
Returns list of G3E_FNO which can own a detail or schematic window. The list is sorted by the localized user name of the feature class.
## Request[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Data-Service/Metadata/GetDetailOwners.html#request)
**Method**
GET
**URL Template**
`/metadata/relationships/detail/owners[?type={type}]`
**Query parameters**  
| Name  | Type  | Mandatory  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| type  | Integer  |   | When missing returns all owners. When `0`, returns detail window owners, when `1` returns schematic window owners.  |  
## Response[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Data-Service/Metadata/GetDetailOwners.html#response)
List of G3E_FNO and their user names, sorted by user name.

# GetDialogMetadata
Returns content of metadata tables G3E_DIALOGS_OPTABLE for given G3E_FNO and G3E_TYPE.
## Request[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Data-Service/Metadata/GetDialogMetadata.html#request)
**Method**
GET
**URL Template**
`/metadata/dialog/tabs/{fno}?type={type}[&attributes={attributes}]`
**Path variables**  
| Name  | Type  | Mandatory  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| {fno}  | Integer  | Y  | G3E_FNO. 0 can be passed in to retrieve dialog tabs for FK queries.  |  
**Query params**  
| Name  | Type  | Mandatory  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| {type}  | String  | Y  | G3E_TYPE  |  
| {attributes}  | Integer  |   | Flag: 1=include dialog tab attribute metadata in response. Other values: attributes are not included. Default is 1.  |

# GetFeatureRoleInfo
Returns list of feature classes which can be reviewed, edited and deleted by the caller. The list is based on roles configured in G3E_FEATURE: G3E_SELECTROLE, G3E_EDITROLE and G3E_DELETEROLE.
## Request[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Data-Service/Metadata/GetFeatureRoleInfo.html#request)
**Method**
GET
**URL Template**
`/metadata/feature/roleinfo`
## Response[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Data-Service/Metadata/GetFeatureRoleInfo.html#response)
Structure IFeatureRoleInfo  
| Property  | Type  | Mandatory  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| select  | number[]  |   | Array of G3E_FNOs which can be reviewed.  |  
| edit  | number[]  |   | Array of G3E_FNOs which can be edited.  |  
| delete  | number[]  |   | Array of G3E_FNOs which can be deleted.  |  
## Example[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Data-Service/Metadata/GetFeatureRoleInfo.html#example)
**Example Request**
http://machinename/fds/metadata/feature/roleinfo
**Example Response**

```
{
    "select": [
        100,
        101,
        102,
        103,
        104
    ],
    "edit": [
        100,
        101,
        102,
        103,
        104,
        105,
        106,
        107
    ],
    "delete": [
        100
    ]
}

```

# GetGeneralParameters
Return general parameter values from NWG_GENERALPARAMETER_OPTABLE. Returns only rows where NWG_PUBLISH=1.
## Request[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Data-Service/Metadata/GetGeneralParameters.html#request)
**Method**
GET
**URL Template**
`/metadata/parameter[?application={application}]`
**Query params**  
| Name  | Type  | Mandatory  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| {application}  | Integer  |   | Bitmask for NWG_APPLICATION field. Rows which yield non-zero AND with bitmask are returned. Allowed values: `8` - NetWorks Portal, `16` - NetWorks Core Mobile.  |  
## Response[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Data-Service/Metadata/GetGeneralParameters.html#response)
Serialized rows from NWG_GENERALPARAMETER_OPTABLE.
## Example[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Data-Service/Metadata/GetGeneralParameters.html#example)
**Example Request**
http://machinename/fds/metadata/parameter
**Example Response**

```
{
  "generalparameters": [
    {
      "name": "Test param",
      "value": "lorem ipsum"
    },
    {
      "name": "Second test param",
      "value": "test"
    }
  ]
}

```

# Feature Data Service
Feature Data Service is a web service designed to support data and metadata retrieval workflows for Feature Editor module and 3rd party applications. It provides API to retrieve the following kinds of data and metadata:
**[Metadata](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Data-Service/Metadata.html)**
  * General parameters
  * Feature placement
  * Dialog and dialog tabs
  * Style and label rules
  * Role information

**[Data](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Data-Service/Data.html)**
  * Picklist data
  * Feature data and geometries
  * Feature relationships
  * Dialog tab data
  * Detail data

## Common API parameters[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Data-Service.html#common-api-parameters)
All APIs accept these optional query parameters in the URL.
`?jobs={jobs}&lcid={lcid}`  
| Name  | Type  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| jobs  | String  | Comma-separated list of job identifiers. Only applicable to APIs which retrieve data from the database. The parameter is ignored in metadata-only APIs.  |  
| lcid  | String  | LCID to use when retrieving metadata. When not present, the default LCID is used – explicitly configured LCID in service settings or the current culture of the process if no LCID is configured.  |  
## Specification[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Data-Service.html#specification)
OpenAPI 3.0.0 specification is available under `\NetWorks\Program\WebHelp\Console\doc\openapi\FeatureDataService`.

# Feature-Model-Service

## Edit-Feature-Data

# Delete a Repeating Component
Deletes the specified repeating component instance from the specified feature instance.
## DELETE[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Model-Service/Edit-Feature-Data/Delete-a-Repeating-Component.html#delete)
**Request URL Template**
http://{hostname}/{service instance}/data/{featureName}/{fid}/{componentName}/{cid}?[ActiveJob={jobName}]
**Request Parameters**  
| Parameter Name  | Optional or Required  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| featureName  | Required  | Specifies the model feature type that is being deleted.  |  
| fid  | Required  | Specifies the G3E_FID value for the model feature instance that is being deleted.  |  
| componentName  | Required  | Specifies a repeating component of the model feature type.  |  
| cid  | Required  | Specifies the G3E_CID value for the repeating component that is being deleted.  |  
| jobName  | Optional  | Specifies the active HxGN NetWorks Core job that will hold the edits.  |  
**Sample Request**
http://localhost/NetWorksFeatureModelService/data/Substation/7693116/HYPERLINK_RECORD/1?ActiveJob=16205
**Sample Response** There is no response from this method.

# Delete Feature
Deletes the specified feature instance.
## DELETE[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Model-Service/Edit-Feature-Data/Delete-Feature.html#delete)
**Request URL Template**
http://{hostname}/{service instance}/data/{featureName}/{fid}?[ActiveJob={jobName}]
**Request Parameters**  
| Parameter Name  | Optional or Required  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| featureName  | Required  | Specifies the model feature type that is being deleted.  |  
| fid  | Required  | Specifies the G3E_FID value for the model feature instance that is being deleted.  |  
| jobName  | Optional  | Specifies the active HxGN NetWorks Core job that will hold the edits.  |  
**Sample Request**
http://localhost/NetWorksFeatureModelService/data/SubStation/7688101?ActiveJob=16205
**Sample Response** There is no response from this method.

# Insert a New Feature
Returns a new instance of the specified feature type.
## POST[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Model-Service/Edit-Feature-Data/Insert-a-New-Feature.html#post)
**Request URL Template**
http://{hostname}/{service instance}/data/{featureName}?[{oDataExpandSelectOptions}][&ActiveJob={jobName}]
**Request Parameters**  
| Parameter Name  | Optional or Required  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| featureName  | Required  | Specifies the model feature type to create a new instance for.  |  
| oDataExpandSelectOptions  | Optional  | The $expand={componentList} and $select={attributeList} OData query parameters can be used to control how much information about the newly created feature to return in the response. Usually, the $ select clause is nested in the componentList (e.g. "$ expand=Substation_Record($select=Sub_Name,Sub_Type)" where Sub_Name and Sub_Type are attributes of the Substation_Record component).  |  
| jobName  | Optional  | Specifies the active HxGN NetWorks Core job that will hold the edits.  |  
**Request Post Body** The Post body of the request specifies a Json object that defines the new feature. The minimum input contains a Json object that defines just the G3E_FNO type for the new feature. The maximum input would supply values for all attributes of the feature's components (including repeating components). See examples below.
**Sample Request**
http://localhost/NetWorksFeatureModelService/data/SubStation?$expand=Substation_Record,Hyperlink_record,Substation_AR,Common_Record&ActiveJob=16205
**Sample Post Body**

```
{
  "G3E_FNO": 326
}

```

**Sample Response** Notice that some of the newly created components have values for their attributes when nothing was included in the Post body. The values are either the default attribute value from the HxGN NetWorks Core metadata, or the values were set by functional interfaces associated with attribute creation events.

```

# Update Existing Feature
Updates the feature instance that matches the specified G3E_FID value and returns the requested feature information.
This method is invoked via an Http Put request because it implements a full replace operation on the input components - not a partial update of attributes. The smallest object that can be updated is a single feature component - not a single attribute. Hence, the normal workflow is for the client to first fetch the feature components that have attributes that need to be updated, then update those attributes, then call this method to replace the component in the feature.
This method can also be used to insert a new instance of a repeating component in the feature by providing the component object without a G3E_CID value or setting the G3E_CID value to zero.
## PUT[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Model-Service/Edit-Feature-Data/Update-Existing-Feature.html#put)
**Request URL Template**
http://{hostname}/{service instance}/data/{featureName}/{fid}?[{oDataExpandSelectOptions}][&ActiveJob={jobName}]
**Request Parameters**  
| Parameter Name  | Optional or Required  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| featureName  | Required  | Specifies the model feature type that is being edited.  |  
| fid  | Required  | Specifies the G3E_FID value for the model feature instance that is being edited.  |  
| oDataExpandSelectOptions  | Optional  | The $expand={componentList} and $select={attributeList} OData query parameters can be used to control how much information about the newly updated feature to return in the response. Usually, the $ select clause is nested in the componentList (e.g. "$ expand=Substation_Record($ select=Sub_Name,Sub_Type)" where Sub_Name and Sub_Type are attributes of the Substation_Record component).  |  
| jobName  | Optional  | Specifies the active HxGN NetWorks Core job that will hold the edits.  |  
**Request Put Body** The Http Put body of the request specifies a Json object that defines the new values for the feature. See examples below.
**Sample Request**
http://localhost/NetWorksFeatureModelService/data/SubStation/7688101?$expand=Substation_Record,Hyperlink_record,Substation_AR,Common_Record&ActiveJob=16205
**Sample Post Body** In this example, the Http Put body updates values for several attributes of the SUBSTATION_RECORD and COMMON_RECORD components, defines one new instance of the HYPERLINK_RECORD repeating component, and updates the geometry for the SUBSTATION_AR primary geographic component. Note that G3E_GEOMETRY attributes are populated using standard GeoJson syntax. Note also that the new instance of the HYPERLINK_RECORD repeating component omitted the G3E_CID value (which indicates an insert instead of an update of an existing component).

```

# Edit Feature Data
## Edit Feature Data[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Model-Service/Edit-Feature-Data.html#edit-feature-data-1)  
| Method  | Uri  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| POST  | [/data/{featureName}?[{oDataOptions}][& ActiveJob={job name} ]](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/NetWorks/API/Feature-Model-Service/Edit-Feature-Data/Insert-a-New-Feature)  | Returns a new instance of the specified feature type.  |  
| PUT  | [/data/{featureName}/{fid}?[{oDataOptions}][& ActiveJob={job name} ]](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/NetWorks/API/Feature-Model-Service/Edit-Feature-Data/Update-Existing-Feature)  | Updates the specified feature instance that matches the specified G3E_FID value and returns the requested feature information.  |  
| DELETE  | [/data/{featureName}/{fid}?[ ActiveJob={job name}]](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/NetWorks/API/Feature-Model-Service/Edit-Feature-Data/Delete-Feature)  | Deletes the specified feature instance.  |  
| DELETE  | [/data/{featureName}/{fid}/{componentName}/{cid}?[ ActiveJob={job name} ]](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/NetWorks/API/Feature-Model-Service/Edit-Feature-Data/Delete-a-Repeating-Component)  | Deletes the specified component instance from the specified feature.  |

# Feature Model API Overview
The HxGN NetWorks Feature Model Service is a standard OData v4.0 web service that exposes HxGN NetWorks Core data and metadata as a simple, hierarchical data model of features, components, attributes and relationships. Support for the OData protocol makes the Feature Model Service immediately accessible by clients (such as Microsoft Excel and Power BI) that understand OData data sources. This greatly simplifies the extract, transform and load steps when performing business analytics on the HxGN NetWorks Core data.
The HxGN NetWorks Core Web Services | Admin Console's Service Deployment module allows the administrator to easily define a feature model by selecting the features and components to include from a grid of all possible features and their components. After defining the model, the administrator deploys an instance of the Feature Model Service that can work with the model.
The model features have simple properties for the FNO and FID and have complex properties for the components of the feature. The components have properties for each of their attributes. Repeating components are collections of complex properties. The relationship types that the feature participates in are also modeled as collection properties of the feature (e.g. Owns, OwnedBy, ConnectsTo, ConnectsFrom, Contains, ContainedBy, Node1Connects, Node2Connects).
All of the workflows supported by the HxGN NetWorks Feature Model Service require a NetWorks_WFS license feature, except for the edit workflows, which require a NetWorks_WFST license feature.
# Supported Feature Model Service Workflows
## Querying feature data:[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Model-Service/Feature-Model-API-Overview.html#querying-feature-data)
The Feature Model Service supports a workflow that is essentially a spatially restricted, ad-hoc query within a single feature class.
Clients use the $filter query parameter in the service call to fetch just the instances of the feature class that match the filter expression. The OData filter syntax supports logical, relational, arithmetic operators and a set of built-in functions that operator on numeric, string, date / time and collection data types.
The queries for feature data can be spatially restricted via an optional bounding box parameter. OData’s support for spatial operations was limited to point features, which was insufficient for HxGN NetWorks Core data. Hence, the Feature Model Service replaced those built-in functions with a new bounding box (BBox) query parameter that spatially restricts the search for all feature geometry types.
The queries for feature data can be further restricted to just the set features that are contained in a specified “FilterSet” parameter. The filter set can specify the result of a previous analytical operation (such as a trace or search from the Analytical Service) or from the pending feature edits in a job as follows:
FilterSet = Trace.
FilterSet = Search.
FilterSet = Job.
FilterSet = ..
FilterSet can be used in addition to OData $filter expression and the BBOX spatial restriction query parameter.
When the MeasureFeatures=true parameter is specified, then the linear and area type geometry components will be measured and returned in the response. If the BBOX parameter is specified then the percent of the feature that falls within the bounding box is also computed. For linear geometry feature components, there will be Length and Percent attributes added to the component. For area geometry components, there will be Area and Percent attributes added to the component.
By default, all measurements are done using the curved Earth model (i.e. using geographic reference space). If MeasureOnCurvedEarth=false is specified, then the measurement will use the projection reference space.
Client applications have full control over which feature properties are returned in the service response. There is also support for pagination of the response data via OData’s "$count=true", “$top=N”, “$skip=N” and "$orderBy={attribute}" query parameters.
For details, see the following topic:
[Get Feature Data](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Model-Service/Query-Feature-Data.html)
## Editing feature data:[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Model-Service/Feature-Model-API-Overview.html#editing-feature-data)
The Feature Model Service provides a simple set of REST APIs for creating, updating and deleting HxGN NetWorks Core features.
Clients create a new feature by sending an HTTP POST body with a Json description of the feature. This can be as simple as a Json object with just a G3E_FNO property specified. If the client requests that some or all components be returned in the response, it will see the components with their default attribute values filled in plus any attribute values populated by functional interfaces associated with feature creation.
To update a feature, the client simply queries for the feature and requests that the components to be modified be returned in the response. Then the client updates the attributes and sends the feature and modified components back to the service with a HTTP PUT operation. To add a new repeating component to a feature, the client creates the Json for the component and omits the G3E_CID value or sets it to zero and includes the new component in a feature update operation.
Features are easily deleted by sending a HTTP DELETE message with the feature type and G3E_FID in the URL.
For details, see the following topic:
[Edit Feature Data](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Model-Service/Edit-Feature-Data.html)
## Querying feature metadata:[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Model-Service/Feature-Model-API-Overview.html#querying-feature-metadata)
The Feature Model Service also provides easy access to feature metadata. There are two sets of API for metadata; one set returns metadata about the features, components, attributes and relationships for just the features in the published model, and the other set of APIs returns metadata on all HxGN NetWorks Core features, components, attributes and relationships. For details, see the following topics:
[Get Model Metadata for Features](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Model-Service/Model-Feature-Metadata.html)
[Get General Metadata for Features](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Model-Service/General-Feature-Metadata.html)

## General-Feature-Metadata

# Get Metadata for Attribute by Ano
Returns metadata about the specific HxGN NetWorks Core attribute type.
## GET[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Model-Service/General-Feature-Metadata/Get-Metadata-for-Attribute-by-Ano.html#get)
**Request URL Template**
http://{hostname}/{service instance}/metadata/attribute/{ano}
**Request Parameters**  
| Parameter Name  | Optional or Required  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| ano  | Required  | Specifies the G3E_ANO value of a specific feature attribute.  |  
**Sample Request**
http://hostname/NetworksFeatureModelService/metadata/attribute/326010003
**Sample Response**

```
{
"Ano": 326010003,
"Username": "Type",
"Table": "SUBSTATION_N",
"Field": "SUB_TYPE",
"DataType": "Text",
"IsPicklist": true
}

```

# Get Metadata for Component by Cno

**Request URL Template**
http://{hostname}/{service instance}/metadata/component/{cno}
**Request Parameters**  
| Parameter Name  | Optional or Required  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| cno  | Required  | Specifies the G3E_CNO value of a specific HxGN NetWorks Core feature component.  |

# Get Metadata for Features
Returns metadata about the HxGN NetWorks Core feature types.
## GET[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Model-Service/General-Feature-Metadata/Get-Metadata-for-Features.html#get)
**Request URL Template**
http://{hostname}/{service instance}/metadata/features/{filter?}
**Request Parameters**  
| Parameter Name  | Optional or Required  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| filter  | Optional  | Controls what type of metadata is returned in the response. Possible values are as follows: (1)  - default response includes basic metadata about the feature. (2) all - include metadata for all components, attributes and relationships of the feature. (3) components - include metadata about the components of the feature. (4) relationships - include metadata about the relationships of the feature. (5) components,relationships - include metadata about the components and relationships of the feature.  |  
**Sample Request**
http://hostname/NetworksFeatureModelService/metadata/features/components
**Sample Response**

```

# Get Metadata for Model Features
Returns metadata about all feature types in the published feature model.
## GET[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Model-Service/Model-Feature-Metadata/Get-Metadata-for-Model-Features.html#get)
**Request URL Template**
http://{hostname}/{service instance}/metadata/modelfeatures/{filter?}
**Request Parameters**  
| Parameter Name  | Optional or Required  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| filter  | Optional  | Controls what type of metadata is returned in the response. Possible values are as follows: (1)  - default response includes basic metadata about the feature. (2) all - include metadata for all components, attributes and relationships of the feature. (3) components - include metadata about the components of the feature. (4) relationships - include metadata about the relationships of the feature. (5) components, relationships - include metadata about the components and relationships of the feature.  |  
**Sample Request**
http://hostname/NetworksFeatureModelService/metadata/modelfeatures/relationships
**Sample Response**

## Query-Feature-Data

# Get Feature By Fid
Returns the requested feature data for the feature instance that matches the specified G3E_FID value.
## GET[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Model-Service/Query-Feature-Data/Get-Feature-By-Fid.html#get)
**Request URL Template**
http://{hostname}/{service instance}/data/{featureName}/{fid}?[{oDataOptions}][&Jobs={listOfJobNames} | ActiveJob={jobName}]
**Request Parameters**  
| Parameter Name  | Optional or Required  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| featureName  | Required  | Specifies the model feature type to retrieve data for.  |  
| fid  | Required  | Specifies the G3E_FID value for the model feature to retrieve data for.  |  
| oDataOptions  | Optional  | See the OData Options section below.  |  
| listOfJobNames  | Optional  | Specifies a comma separated list of HxGN NetWorks Core jobs whose pending edits will participate in the query and response.  |  
| jobName  | Optional  | Specifies the active HxGN NetWorks Core job whose pending edits will participate in the query and response.  |  
**OData Options**
Since a specific instance of the feature type has been selected, the only OData parameters that apply are the $expand and $select parameters.
  * **$expand={featureComponentsRelationships}** - a comma separated list of components and relationships of the feature instance to include in the response.
  * **$select={attributes}** - a comma separated list of the feature attributes to return in the response. Usually, the $select clause is nested in the componentList of the $expand option (e.g. "$expand=Substation_Record($select=Sub_Name,Sub_Type)" where Sub_Name and Sub_Type are attributes of the Substation_Record component).

**Sample Request**
http://localhost/NetWorksFeatureModelService/data/SubStation/7693135?$expand=substation_record,substation_ar,hyperlink_record($select=G3E_CID,FILEPATH),common_record&ActiveJob=16205
**Sample Response**
A JSON response is returned. If the G3E_GEOMETRY attribute is included, it will be formatted as GeoJson.

```

# Get Feature Component Attribute
Returns the requested component attribute for the specified feature instance that matches the G3E_FID value, and G3E_CID if component is repeating.
If the request route ends with /$value, then only the raw value of the component attribute is returned in the response (i.e. without the OData Json wrapper).
## GET[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Model-Service/Query-Feature-Data/Get-Feature-Component-Attribute.html#get)
**Request URL Template**
http://{hostname}/{service instance}/data/{featureName}/{fid}/{componentName}[/{cid}]/{attributeName}[/$value]?[Jobs={listOfJobNames} | ActiveJob={jobName}]
**Request Parameters**  
| Parameter Name  | Optional or Required  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| featureName  | Required  | Specifies the model feature type to retrieve data for.  |  
| fid  | Required  | Specifies the G3E_FID value for the model feature to retrieve component attribute data for.  |  
| componentName  | Required  | Specifies the feature component type.  |  
| cid  | Optional  | Specifies the G3E_CID value for the repeating component instance to retrieve.  |  
| attributeName  | Required  | Specifies the feature component attribute to return.  |  
| listOfJobNames  | Optional  | Specifies a comma separated list of HxGN NetWorks Core jobs whose pending edits will participate in the query and response.  |  
| jobName  | Optional  | Specifies the active HxGN NetWorks Core job whose pending edits will participate in the query and response.  |  
**Sample Request**
http://localhost/NetWorksFeatureModelService/data/SubStation/3747375/Substation_Record/Sub_Name?ActiveJob=16205
**Sample Response** A JSON response is returned.

```
{
"@odata.context": "http://localhost/NetWorksFeatureModelService/data/$metadata#Substation(3747375)/SUBSTATION_RECORD/SUB_NAME",
"value": "MADISON KIPP"
}

```

**Sample Request 2**
http://localhost/NetWorksFeatureModelService/data/SubStation/3747375/Substation_Record/Sub_Name/$value?ActiveJob=16205
**Sample Response 2** Just the value of the Sub_Name attribute is returned.

```
"MADISON KIPP"

```

# Get Feature Component
Returns the requested component for the specified feature instance that matches the G3E_FID value, and G3E_CID if component is repeating.
## GET[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Model-Service/Query-Feature-Data/Get-Feature-Component.html#get)
**Request URL Template**
http://{hostname}/{service instance}/data/{featureName}/{fid}/{componentName}[/{cid}]?[{oDataOptions}][&Jobs={listOfJobNames} | ActiveJob={jobName}]
**Request Parameters**  
| Parameter Name  | Optional or Required  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| featureName  | Required  | Specifies the model feature type to retrieve data for.  |  
| fid  | Required  | Specifies the G3E_FID value for the model feature to retrieve component data for.  |  
| componentName  | Required  | Specifies the feature component type to retrieve.  |  
| cid  | Optional  | Specifies the G3E_CID value for the repeating component instance to retrieve.  |  
| oDataOptions  | Optional  | See the OData Options section below.  |  
| listOfJobNames  | Optional  | Specifies a comma separated list of HxGN NetWorks Core jobs whose pending edits will participate in the query and response.  |  
| jobName  | Optional  | Specifies the active HxGN NetWorks Core job whose pending edits will participate in the query and response.  |  
**OData Options**
Since a specific component instance of the feature has been selected, the only OData parameter that applies is $select parameter.
  * **$select={attributes}** - a comma separated list of the feature attributes to return in the response. Usually, the $select clause is nested in the componentList of the $expand option (e.g. "$expand=Substation_Record($select=Sub_Name,Sub_Type)" where Sub_Name and Sub_Type are attributes of the Substation_Record component).

**Sample Request**
http://localhost/NetWorksFeatureModelService/data/SubStation/7693135/Hyperlink_Record/2?$select=G3E_CID,FILEPATH&ActiveJob=16205
**Sample Response** A JSON response is returned. If the G3E_GEOMETRY attribute is included, it will be formatted as GeoJson.

```
{
    "@odata.context": "http://localhost/NetWorksFeatureModelService/data/$metadata#Substation(3747378)/HYPERLINK_RECORD(G3E_CID,FILEPATH)",
    "value": 
    {
       "G3E_CID": 2,
       "FILEPATH": "InstallInstructions.txt"
    }
}

```

# Get Features By Filter
Returns the requested feature data for the specified feature type that matches the optional OData filter options and bounding box.
If the feature type in the route is followed by "/$count", then just the count of requested feature data that matches the OData filter option and bounding box is returned.
## GET[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Model-Service/Query-Feature-Data/Get-Features-By-Filter.html#get)
**Request URL Template**
http://{hostname}/{service instance}/data/{featureName}[/$count]?[{oDataOptions}] [&BBOX={left,bottom,right,top}][&FilterSet={filterSetId}] [&MeasureFeatures={true|false}][&MeasureOnCurvedEarth={true|false}] [&Jobs={listOfJobNames} | ActiveJob={jobName}]
**Request Parameters**  
| Parameter Name  | Optional or Required  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| featureName  | Required  | Specifies the model feature type to retrieve data for.  |  
| oDataOptions  | Optional  | See the OData Options section below.  |  
| BBOX=left,bottom,right,top  | Optional  | Specifies a comma separated list of values (in the projection of the HxGN NetWorks Core configuration) that define a bounding box to use to spatially restrict the feature instances that will be included in the response.  |  
| MeasureFeatures= true or false  | Optional  | Specifies that the feature components that have linear or area geometry be measured. If the BBOX parameter is specified then the percent of the feature that falls within the bounding box is also computed. For linear geometry feature components, there will be Length and Percent attributes added to the component. For area geometry components, there will be Area and Percent attributes added to the component.  |  
| MeasureOnCurvedEarth= true or false  | Optional  | Specifies that the feature components that have linear or area geometry should be measured using the geographic reference space. If the parameter is false, then the measurement will use the projection reference space. If not specified, the measurement will be done using the geographic reference space.  |  
| FilterSet=filterSetId  | Optional  | Specifies a previous trace or search result set to join against to restrict the feature instances that will be included in the response. The pending edits in a job can also serve as a filter set. The filterSetId must match one of the following: (1) Trace.{traceId} (2) Search.{searchId} (3) Job.{jobId} (4) {table}.{column}.{value}  |  
| Jobs=listOfJobNames  | Optional  | Specifies a comma separated list of HxGN NetWorks Core jobs whose pending edits will participate in the query and response.  |  
| ActiveJob=jobName  | Optional  | Specifies the active HxGN NetWorks Core job whose pending edits will participate in the query and response.  |  
**OData Options**
The OData parameters are used to query for specific instances of the feature type; and to select which information about the feature type to return; and to control how much feature information is returned in each response via the pagination parameters.
  * **$filter={oDataExpression}** - the filter parameter selects which feature instances to return. The oDataExpression can consist of the following items:
    * attribute - the value of the referenced attribute. For the simple attributes of the feature, just the attribute name is used (e.g. $filter=G3E_FID gt 15903 and G3E_FID lt 16000). For the attribute of a component or relationship, the qualified form {component/attribute} of the reference is used (e.g. $filter=SUBSTATION_RECORD/SUB_NUMBER eq 1145).
    * Logical operators -
      * **and** - returns true if both the left and right operands evaluate to true, otherwise it returns false. The null value is treated as unknown, so if one operand evaluates to null and the other operand to false, the and operator returns false. All other combinations with null return null.
      * **or** - returns false if both the left and right operands both evaluate to false, otherwise it returns true. The null value is treated as unknown, so if one operand evaluates to null and the other operand to true, the or operator returns true. All other combinations with null return null.
      * **not** - returns true if the operand returns false, otherwise it returns false. The null value is treated as unknown, so not null returns null.
      * **eq** - returns true if the left operand is equal to the right operand, otherwise it returns false. When applied to operands of entity types, the eq operator returns true if both operands represent the same entity, or both operands represent null. Each of the special values null, -INF, and INF is equal to itself, and only to itself. The special value NaN is not equal to anything, even to itself.
      * **ne** - returns true if the left operand is not equal to the right operand, otherwise it returns false. When applied to operands of entity types, the ne operator returns true if the two operands do not represent the same entity. Each of the special values null, -INF, and INF is equal to itself, and only to itself. The special value NaN is not equal to anything, even to itself.
      * **gt** - returns true if the left operand is greater than the right operand, otherwise it returns false. The special value INF is greater than any number, and any number is greater than -INF. The Boolean value true is greater than false. If any operand is null, the operator returns false.
      * **lt** - returns true if the left operand is less than the right operand, otherwise it returns false. The special value -INF is less than any number, and any number is less than INF. The Boolean value false is less than true. If any operand is null, the operator returns false.
      * **ge** - returns true if the left operand is greater than or equal to the right operand, otherwise it returns false. See rules for gt and eq for details.
      * **le** - returns true if the left operand is less than or equal to the right operand, otherwise it returns false. See rules for lt and eq for details.
    * Arithmetic operators - require operands that evaluate to numeric types. If an operand of an arithmetic operator is null, the result is null.
      * **"-"** - negation operator, represented by a minus (-) sign, changes the sign of its numeric operand.
      * **add** - adds the left and right numeric operands.
      * **sub** - subtracts the right numeric operand from the left numeric operand.
      * **mul** - multiplies the left and right numeric operands.
      * **div** - divide the left numeric operand by the right numeric operand.
      * **mod** - returns the remainder when the left numeric operand is divided by the right numeric operand. The sign of the result is the same as the sign of the left operand. If the right operand is zero, the request fails.
      * **( )** - The Grouping operator (open and close parenthesis) controls the evaluation order of an expression.
    * String built-in functions -
      * **string concat( string, string )** - returns a string that appends the second parameter string value to the first.
      * **boolean contains( string, string )** - returns true if the second string is a substring of the first string, otherwise it returns false. String comparison is case-sensitive, case-insensitive comparison can be achieved in combination with tolower or toupper.
      * **boolean endswith( string, string )** - returns true if the first string ends with the second string, otherwise it returns false. String comparison is case-sensitive.
      * **int32 indexof( string, string )** - returns the zero-based character position of the first occurrence of the second string in the first string, or -1 if the first string does not contain the second string. String comparison is case-sensitive.
      * **int32 length( string )** - returns the number of characters in the string.
      * **boolean startswith( string, string )** - returns true if the first string begins with the second string, otherwise it returns false. String comparison is case-sensitive.
      * **string substring( string, int32 )** - returns the substring that begins with the Nth character (the integer second argument) and goes to the end of the string.
      * **string substring( string, int32, int32 )** - returns a substring of the first parameter string value identified by selecting up to M characters starting at the Nth character (where N is the second parameter integer value and M is the third parameter integer value).
      * **string tolower( string )** - returns the input parameter string value with all uppercase characters converted to lowercase according to Unicode rules.
      * **string toupper( string )** - returns the input parameter string value with all lowercase characters converted to uppercase according to Unicode rules.
      * **string trim( string )** - returns the input parameter string value with all leading and trailing whitespace characters, according to Unicode rules, removed.
    * Arithmetic built-in functions -
      * **double ceiling( double )** - rounds the input numeric parameter up to the nearest numeric value with no decimal component.
      * **double floor( double)** - rounds the input numeric parameter down to the nearest numeric value with no decimal component.
      * **double round( double )** -rounds the input numeric parameter to the nearest numeric value with no decimal component. The mid-point between two integers is rounded away from zero, i.e. 0.5 is rounded to 1 and ‑0.5 is rounded to -1.
    * Date / Time built-in functions - these function operate on three types: dateTimeOffset, date, and timeOfDay. A dateTimeOffset represents a date and time and time zone offset value. Literal operands are specified as YYYY "-" MM "-" DD "T" HH ":" mm [ ":" ss [ "." fractionalSeconds ] ] ( "Z" / SIGN HH ":" mm ) where HH is 24 hour value. The date type is specified as YYYY "-" MM "-" DD. The timeOfDay is specified as HH ":" mm [ ":" ss [ "." fractionalSeconds ] ].
      * **date date( dateTimeOffset )** - returns the date part of the DateTimeOffset parameter value, evaluated in the time zone of the DateTimeOffset parameter value.
      * **int32 day( date | dateTimeOffset )** - returns the day component Date or DateTimeOffset parameter value, evaluated in the time zone of the DateTimeOffset parameter value.
      * **int32 hour( timeOfDay | dateTimeOffset )** - returns the hour component (0 to 23) of the DateTimeOffset or TimeOfDay parameter value, evaluated in the time zone of the DateTimeOffset parameter value.
      * **int32 minute( timeOfDay | dateTimeOffset )** - returns the minute component (0 to 59) of the DateTimeOffset or TimeOfDay parameter value, evaluated in the time zone of the DateTimeOffset parameter value.
      * **int32 month( date | dateTimeOffset )** - returns the month component of the Date or DateTimeOffset parameter value, evaluated in the time zone of the DateTimeOffset parameter value.
      * **dateTimeOffset now( )** - returns the current point in time (date and time with time zone) as a DateTimeOffset value.
      * **int32 second( timeOfDay | dateTimeOffset )** - returns the second component (0 to 59 for regular seconds, and 60 for leap seconds, without the fractional part) of the DateTimeOffset or TimeOfDay parameter value.
      * **timeOfDay time( dateTimeOffset )** - rreturns the time part of the DateTimeOffset parameter value, evaluated in the time zone of the DateTimeOffset parameter value.
      * **int32 year( date | dateTimeOffset )** - returns the year component of the Date or DateTimeOffset parameter value, evaluated in the time zone of the DateTimeOffset parameter value.
    * Collection built-in functions - the "any" and "all" lamda expressions are used to filter features based on instances of repeating components and relationships.
      * **boolean {componentName}/any( var : var/{attribute} gt 0 )** - The any operator applies a Boolean expression to each instance of a repeating component or relationship and returns true if and only if the expression is true for any instance, otherwise it returns false. This implies that the any operator always returns false for an empty collection. The any operator can be used without an argument expression. This short form returns false if and only if the collection is empty. Example: $filter=Hyperlink_Record/any( q: contains(q/filePath, "schematic") will return true for any feature that has at least one Hyperlink_Record with a FilePath attribute that contains "schematic" as a substring.
      * **boolean {componentName}/all( var : var/{attribute} gt 0 )** - The all operator applies a Boolean expression to each instance of a repeating component or relationship and returns true if and only if the expression is true for every instance, otherwise it returns false. This implies that the all operator always returns true for an empty collection.
  * **$expand={featureComponentsRelationships}** - a comma separated list of components and relationships of the feature instances to include in the response.
  * **$select={attributes}** - a comma separated list of the feature attributes to return in the response. Usually, the $select clause is nested in the componentList of the $expand option (e.g. "$expand=Substation_Record($select=Sub_Name,Sub_Type)" where Sub_Name and Sub_Type are attributes of the Substation_Record component).
  * **$count=true** - include a count of the feature instances in the response. The $count, $skip, $top and $orderBy parameters are used together to paginate the results when a large number of feature instances are expected in the response. For example, suppose the client wants to process the features in chunks of 1000 until all feature instances that match the filter criteria are processed. The first call the client makes includes $count=true&$top=1000&$orderBy={attribute}. If the odata.Count property in the response is less than 1000, the client knows that it has processed all of the results; otherwise, the client continues calling with $count=true&$skip={1000 * number of previous calls}&$top=1000&$orderBy={attribute} until the odata.Count value is less than 1000. Note that it is important to use an $orderBy attribute that will produce a deterministic order to the feature results.
  * **$skip={numberToSkip}** - specifies the number of feature instances from the query to skip over before forming the response.
  * **$top={numberToReturn}** - specifies the number of feature instances from the query to return in the response.
  * **$orderBy={attributes}** - specifies a comma separated list of component or relationship attributes used to order feature instances from the query before forming the response.

**Sample Request**
http://localhost/NetWorksFeatureModelService/data/SubStation?$expand=substation_record,substation_ar,hyperlink_record($select=G3E_CID,FILEPATH),common_record&$filter=Substation_Record/Sub_Number eq 1119&ActiveJob=16205
**Sample Response**
A JSON response is returned. The content is constrained by applying the $expand and $select parameters to the feature query results obtained after applying the $filter, BBOX, and / or FilterSet query parameters.
If a geographic component is included in the response, its G3E_GEOMETRY attribute will be formatted as GeoJson. Every geographic component will also include Longitude and Latitude properties. Only the first point in the component geometry is selected and converted to a geographic coordinate in decimal degrees. The primary use of this geographic longitude / latitude point is to allow OData clients (such as Excel and Power BI) that have simple map visualizers to display the feature’s location on a map. The Longitude and Latitude properties are directly bound to input fields of the map visualizers.
