## NWP.map.source.WFS[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/API/Type-definitions/map/source.html#nwpmapsourcewfs)

```
import Style from "ol/style/Style";
import { StyleFunction } from "ol/style/Style";

interface WFS extends Base {
    /** Type identifier. Must always be 'WFS'. */
    type: "WFS";

    /** Whether geometry placement operations should snap to data in this map source. Default is false. */
    allowSnapping?: boolean;

    /** Whether the map tooltips mode will query this source. Default is false. */
    enableTooltips: boolean;

    /** The namespace URI used for features. */
    featureNS: string;

    /** The prefix associated with the namespace URI. */
    featurePrefix: string;

    /** The feature type name to be requested. */
    featureType: string;
    
    /** Filter to apply to requested features. */
    filter?: Filter,   

    /** The HTTP method to use to request data. Default is GET. */
    method?: "GET" | "POST";

    /** When request an extent use y1,x1,y2,x2 instead of x1,y1,x2,y2. Default is false. */
    reverseAxesOrdering?: boolean;

    /** Style for the vectors as an open layers style, open layers style function or style definition. */
    style?: Style | StyleFunction | StyleDef;

    /** Timeout in milliseconds before aborting map request. */
    timeout? : number;

    /** URL to the WFS service. */
    url: string;

    /** Whether geometry in the map source is spatially indexed. Default is true. */
    useSpatialIndex?: boolean;

    /** If true then use a ol/layer/VectorImage instead of an ol/layer/Vector. Default is false. */
    useVectorImage?: boolean;

    /** WFS service version. Default is 1.1.0 */
    version?: "1.0.0" | "1.1.0" | "2.0.0";
}

```

**Notes**
  * Setting a `filter` will force the source to request data using POST regardless of `method`.
  * If `useSpatialIndex` is set to false then fit operations for source are disabled.
  * Setting `useVectorImage` to true can significantly improve zoom and pan performance. The only disadvantage is that point symbols and texts are always rotated with the view and pixels are scaled during zoom animations.

## NWP.map.source.WMS[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/API/Type-definitions/map/source.html#nwpmapsourcewms)

```
interface WMS extends Base {
    /** Type identifier. Must always be 'WMS'. */
    type: "WMS";

    /** Sets the BGCOLOR parameter in WMS GetMap requests. */
    bgColor?: string;

    /** If singleTile is false the initial tile cache size. */
    cacheSize?: number;

    /** The value for the crossOrigin attribute for loaded images. Defaults to anonymous. */
    crossOrigin?: "anonymous" | "use-credentials";

    /** Denotes whether this source is defined by the workspace or was created dynamically. */
    dynamic?: boolean;
    
    /** The format for exceptions as advertised by the services capabilities document e.g. XML */
    exceptions?: string,
    
    /** The map image format as a MIME type as advertised by the services capabilities document e.g. image/png */
    format: string;

    /** If singleTile is false the amount of overlap between tiles in CSS pixels. */
    gutter?: number;
 
    /** The list of WMS layer names to request. */
    layers?: string[];

    /** If singleTile is true the ratio of the requested image to the map viewport. 
     * 1 means image requests are the size of the map viewport, 2 means twice the width and height of the map viewport, and so on. Must be 1 or higher.
     * Defaults to 1.5. */
    ratio?: number;

    /** If singleTile is true the list of map resolutions at which images are requested. */
    resolutions?: number[],

    /** Denotes whether to request a map extent as a single tile or multiple tiles of a fixed size. Default is false. */
    singleTile?: boolean;

    /** If layers is defined the optional list of style names to associated with each WMS layer name. */
    styles?: string[];    
    
    /** The height OR width and height of tiles in CSS pixels if singleTile is false. Default is 256. */
    tileSize?: number | [number, number];

    /** URL to the WMS service. */
    url1: string;
    
    /** Secondary URL to the WMS service if available. */
    url2?: string;

    /** Tertiary URL to the WMS service if available. */
    url3?: string;

    /** The version of the WMS service e.g. '1.3.0' */
    version?: string;
}

```

**Notes**
  * The property `dynamic` should always be set to true when adding a WMS source via the API. It is required to be true if either allLayers or queryable is true in the owning source entry.
  * The property `gutter` can be used to reduce issues with, for example, label clipping when requesting tiles from a WMS service. However it is always recommended that such issues are fixed in the service where possible.
  * If `singleTile` is false then requests will be spread over url1, url2 and url3 if available. If true then url2 and url3 are ignored.
  * The `layers` and optional `styles` properties are intended for when one wishes to have a fixed set of layers requested from the WMS service each time and the user cannot select which layers to view. Typically it is better to define layer entries for the owning source entry instead. If `styles` is supplied it should be an array of the same length as `layers` and padded with empty strings as necessary.
  * See <https://www.ogc.org/standard/wms/> for more information about `layers`, `styles` and other WMS request parameters.

## NWP.map.source.WMTS[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/API/Type-definitions/map/source.html#nwpmapsourcewmts)

```
interface WMTS extends Base {
    /** Type identifier. Must always be 'WMTS'. */
    type: "WMTS";

    /** The value for the crossOrigin attribute for loaded images. Defaults to anonymous. */
    crossOrigin?: "anonymous" | "use-credentials";

    /** The tile MIME type. Defaults to image/jpeg. */
    format?: string;

    /** The identifier of the layer to be requested as advertised by the WMTS capabilities document. */
    layer: string;

    /** The identifiers of each tile matrix of the tile matrix set to be requested as advertised by the WMTS capabilities document. */
    matrixIds: string[];

    /** The identifier of the tile matrix set within the layer to be requested as advertised by the WMTS capabilities document. */
    matrixSet: string;

    /** The origin of the tile matrix set. */
    origin?: Position;

    /** The origin of each tile matrix. */
    origins?: Position[];

    /** The request encoding to use. Default is KVP. */
    requestEncoding?: "KVP" | "REST";

    /** The resolution of each tile matrix. */
    resolutions: number[];

    /** Optional style identifier to be sent with tile requests as advertised by the WMTS capabilities document. */
    style?: string;

    /** The height or width and height of each tile in CSS pixels. Default is 256. */    
    tileSize?: number | [number, number];

    /** URL to the WMTS service. */
    url1: string;
    
    /** Secondary URL to the WMTS service if available. */
    url2?: string;

    /** Tertiary URL to the WMTS service if available. */
    url3?: string;

    /** The version of the WMTS service e.g. '1.0.0' */
    version?: string;
}

```

**Notes**
  * WMTS sources are not locatable/queryable in the map.
  * Requests for tiles are spread across url1, url2 and url3 if they are defined.
  * Variable tile sizes for each tile matrix are not supported.
  * Typically you need supply either an `extent`, `origin` or `origins`; not all three. See <https://openlayers.org/en/latest/apidoc/module-ol_tilegrid_WMTS-WMTSTileGrid.html> for more information about these parameters.
  * The length of `matrixIds`, `resolutions` and if used, `origins` must match. Origin and resolution are mapped to tile matrix id by array index position.
  * See <https://www.ogc.org/standard/wmts/> for more information about WMTS and its request parameters.

# Using postMessage with the API
Via the postMessage API you can make the following posts:
maplegendupdate maplegendstate mapviewupdate mapviewstate featuredisableedit featurehighlight featurehighlightclear gtechfeaturehighlight sidebarpanelupdate sidebarpanelstate
To make a post to the application encode the notification in an object of the structure Hxgn.postMessageArgs. To send it for example from an iframe use:

```
var msg = {
   type: 'post',
   name: 'postname',
   data: {…}
};
window.parent.postMessage(JSON.stringify(msg), '*');

```

To receive post notifications or results from requests then you first must register the frame with the portal client. To do this use:

```
var msg = {
   type: 'request',
   name: 'registerframe'
};
window.parent.postMessage(JSON.stringify(msg), '*');

window.addEventListener("message", receiveMessage, false);

function receiveMessage(event) {
  if (event.source !== window.parent)
    return;
  var msg = JSON.parse(event.data);
  // msg will be structured as Hxgn.postMessageArgs
  ...
  
}

```

Via the postMessage API you can make the following requests:
maplegendupdate maplegendstate mapviewupdate mapviewstate featuredisableedit featurehighlight featurehighlightclear gtechfeaturehighlight sidebarpanelupdate sidebarpanelstate
For requests with arguments set the arguments to the data property of the message you post. The results will be returned to the calling frame via a message of type 'response' where name is set to the request name and data to the array of the results.

# API
**Introduction**
There are two extensions to the application to allow for integration of third party code.
  1. A [postMessage](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/postMessage) API to allow for content in iframes from a separate origin to communicate with the portal. For security reasons this has some limitations.
  2. A direct API available from the global `$NWP` object.

If you have an ExtJS license then you can also use the full client object model.
**Communication within the client**
Components in the client do not communicate directly but instead are linked to a component called the databus. For example.
[![UP6Architecture1.png](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/.attachments/UP6Architecture1-dde48f90-d9e7-4985-b940-b7f9ea1c114d.png)](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/.attachments/UP6Architecture1-dde48f90-d9e7-4985-b940-b7f9ea1c114d.png)
The databus has three main methods associated with it.
  1. `post`. Sends a notification to all registered handlers. Optionally with data.
  2. `registerPostHandler`. Associates a function/handler to a particular notification.
  3. `request`. Sends a notification to all registered handlers. Optionally with arguments. The results from each handlers are returned as an array.

**Communication with the server** The direct API has two methods for sending requests to the server
`serviceRequest` - Used to send requests to a registered portal service. `serverRequest` - Generic method for sending requests to the server.

#### Configuration

# coordsys.json
## Introduction[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/coordsys.json.html#introduction)
The Portal client uses a JavaScript port of PROJ to do client side coordinate transforms. See <https://github.com/proj4js/proj4js> for more information about this library. The coordinate system definitions available to the client are current defined in the `coordsys.json` file. The `coordsys.json` file is located in the root directory of a deployed Portal.
## File structure[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/coordsys.json.html#file-structure)
The coordsys.json file is in strict [JSON](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/JSON). No comments allowed. Property names and strings must be in double quotes. It is structured as follows.

```
{
  "defs": [
    {
       "code": "3857",
       "bbox": [ 85.06, -180.0, -85.06, 180.0 ],
       "proj4": "+proj=merc +a=6378137 +b=6378137 +lat_ts=0.0 +lon_0=0.0 +x_0=0.0 +y_0=0 +k=1.0 +units=m +nadgrids=@null +wktext  +no_defs",
       "name": "WGS 84 / Pseudo-Mercator"
    },
    {
       "code": "4326",
       "bbox": [ 90.0, -180.0, -90.0, 180.0 ],
       "proj4": "+proj=longlat +datum=WGS84 +no_defs",
       "name": "WGS 84"
    },
    {
       "code": "25832",
       "aliases": [ "urn:ogc:def:crs:EPSG::25832", "http://www.opengis.net/gml/srs/epsg.xml#25832" ],
       "bbox": [ 83.92, 12, 38.76, 6 ],
       "proj4": "+proj=utm +zone=32 +ellps=GRS80 +towgs84=0,0,0,0,0,0,0 +units=m +no_defs",
       "name": "ETRS89 / UTM zone 32N"
    }
   ]
}

```

Each entry in the `defs` array is a JSON object with the following properties  
| Name  | Required  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| code  | Yes  | The EPSG code of the projection.  |  
| proj4  | Yes  | The Proj.4 projection definition.  |  
| name  | Yes  | User identifier for the projection.  |  
| bbox  | No  | The geographic extent of the extent in degrees N, W, S, E.  |  
| aliases  | No  | An array of aliases for the projection. See below.  |  
The portal uses Proj4 for client side 2D transformations. The easiest place to find Proj.4 definitions is on <http://epsg.io/>.
Internally in the portal, projections are looked up by simple EPSG codes i.e. `EPSG:3857`. However some OGC services return projection codes in GML responses using other other 'standards', these are typically either of the following
  1. `urn:ogc:def:crs:EPSG::{code}`
  2. `http://www.opengis.net/gml/srs/epsg.xml#{code}`

This can cause issues when parsing geometry. To counter this you can define aliases with each projection so the portal can correctly match these codes with an actual projection.

# Load balancing
Portal instances can be deployed behind a load balancer. The configurations of the Portal instances must be identical. Some parts of the configuration require special attention.
## Machine key[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Load-balancing.html#machine-key)
When running Portal with OpenId Connect, Portal [web.config file](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/web.config-file/system.html) must contain a configured `machineKey`. The same machineKey must be present on all Portal load-balanced instances.
The machine key is used to encrypt session cookies. If not configured, each Portal instance generates its own keys. In such case, cookies created by other instances are not recognized.
## OpenID Connect Redirect URL[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Load-balancing.html#openid-connect-redirect-url)
The `RedirectUri` parameter in _OpenIdConfig.json_ file should be configured with external (load balancer) URL of the Portal.
## Sticky sessions[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Load-balancing.html#sticky-sessions)
Some Portal workflows (Print, Attach CAD, Export to Excel, Trace) are long running processes, which require that the original (submit) and subsequent (status, result) requests are targeting the same Portal instance. To ensure this, sticky sessions (connections) must be enabled on the load balancer.

##### Print

# Controlling print processes
## Overview[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Print/Controlling-print-processes.html#overview)
There are three settings which can be defined in the **web.config** file to control print processes.
  1. maxConcurrentPrints. Number of prints that can be generated concurrently. If the portal is configured to print large format prints (such as A1 or A0) and is deployed on a server with limited available memory it can be necessary to limit how many prints are generated concurrently to prevent performance problems.
  2. printTimeout. Time in milliseconds that print map rendering is allowed to run until it is cancelled. If the map contains data from very slow or unreliable map services it can be necessary to modify this value.
  3. maxQueuedPrints. How many print requests that can be queued by the server.

These are all attributes on the  element. The following shows their default values:

```
<webGIS maxConcurrentPrints="5" printTimeout="600000" maxQueuedPrints="1000">

```

# Controlling print resolution
## Overview[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Print/Controlling-print-resolution.html#overview)
This page documents how the map image resolution in a PDF document can be adjusted. By increasing the resolution the quality of the map image can in some circumstances be improved. This comes at the cost of increasing the time it takes to produce a print and the amount of system memory required.
Print in the Portal is designed to quickly generate ad-hoc PDF documents containing the contents of the users current map. While it _can_ be configured to generate page sizes up to A0 in size, it is not suitable for generating high quality prints on large paper sizes. For this purpose NetPlot is recommended.
Note that what is documented here does not constitute any significant change to existing print functionality. What was configured and functioned in previous versions will continue to function in this version. It is merely intended as a clarification of existing functionality.
## Pixels per inch[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Print/Controlling-print-resolution.html#pixels-per-inch)
When discussing resolution the term 'Pixels per inch' or PPI will be used. The Portal uses the CSS definition of a pixel (see <https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Glossary/CSS_pixel>) which is defined as 1/96th of a CSS inch. Or put another way, 'screen' resolution is 96 PPI.
PPI should not be confused with the more commonly used DPI or 'Dots per inch'. DPI is most often used as a measurement of printer output resolution but 1 pixel does not equal 1 dot. Generally multiple dots are required to draw a single pixel but how many depends on the pixel color and shade and the printer hardware being used.
## Default settings[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Print/Controlling-print-resolution.html#default-settings)
By default the Portal is delivered with A4 and A3 print templates and is configured to print at 150 PPI. The default PPI is defined in [settings](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Settings/Settings.html) by `print.ppi`. These defaults were chosen so that print would function well on even heavily loaded server without a lot of spare memory or processor resources.
However at 150 PPI and with sufficient server resources it is potentially possible to reliably print up to and including A0 sized templates. It depends very much on what you are printing. To give an idea on one of our own test servers printing an A0 template with 5 different map sources including a Vector Service, WMS, WMTS, WFS and OSM, a single print process took 8 minutes and used up to 900MB of memory during the process lifetime. Tile based map services such as WMTS and OSM put a particularly large load on the print process. A0 is approximately 33x47 inches which at 150 PPI is a viewport 4950x7050 pixels. To fill that with 256x256 pixel tiles requires at least 560 tiles which all need to be requested and positioned. If you have multiple tile services in a single print then this becomes a very heavy process indeed. Unfortunately there is no simple calculation for how much memory and processing time a print will require. If larger templates are required it is recommended that testing is done to ensure that the server is not overwhelmed by print requests. To prevent excessive usage of resources it is possible to 'throttle' the number of parallel print processes. See  
[Controlling print processes](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Print/Controlling-print-processes.html).
It is not recommended that the default PPI is raised. Doing so can lead to server instability or crashes. It is possible to raise PPI for smaller templates though as described in the following section.
## Overriding PPI[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Print/Controlling-print-resolution.html#overriding-ppi)
It is possible override the default PPI on a per template basis. These overrides are defined in [settings](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Settings/Settings.html) by `print.templatePpi`. This setting defines a list of entries of the form:
`{ name: <template name>, ppi: <print resolution> },`
Where _template name_ matches a name of a print template in the portal workspace and _ppi_ is the resolution as a whole number. For example:

```
print.templatePpi = [
   { name: "A4", ppi: 300 },
   { name: "A4_", ppi: 300 },
]

```

In terms of system resources used, printing A4 at 300 PPI is effectively the same as printing A3 at 150 PPI. It is not recommended that PPI is raised above 300. It is also not recommended that templates above the size of A2 are printed above 150 PPI. On our test server with our configuration we could print A1 at 300 PPI reliably so it is potentially possible, however, an individual print process did take 10+ minutes to execute and used well over 1GB of memory. This is the upper limit of what can be printed reliably. From our testing printing A0 at 300 PPI cannot be run reliably and attempting to do so can lead to server instability or server crashes.

# Customization of print settings
## Overview[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Print/Customization-of-print-settings.html#overview)
The portal allows customization of some service parameters when using print functionality.
Customization of parameters is done by adding entries to the `settings/printsettings_custom.js` file.
## Customizable parameters[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Print/Customization-of-print-settings.html#customizable-parameters)  
| Parameter  | Service Type  | Description  | Default  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| singleTile  | WMS  | When true, a single image is requested for the whole map. When false, multiple tiled images are requested.  |   |  
| tileSize  | WMS  | Size of tiles in pixels. Applies when singleTile = false  |   |  
| gutter  | WMS  | The size in pixels of the gutter around image tiles to retrieve from server and ignore. Applies only when WMS.singleTile = false  | 0  |  
| ratio  | WMS  | The factor by which requested image width and height is expanded. Applies only when WMS.singleTile = true  | 1.5  |  
| params  | WMS  | Object with properties to be appended to the WMS request URL  |   |  
| url  | WMS  | URL of alternative WMS to be used when printing. The WMS must accept the same parameters as the original one.  |   |  
| url  | WMTS  | URL of alternative WMTS to be used when printing. The WMTS must accept the same parameters as the original one.  |   |  
| hidpi  | BingMaps  | When true, high DPI maps are requested from Bing Maps.  | true  |  
| maxZoom  | BingMaps  | Maximum zoom level to request when printing Bing Maps. When not set, Bing Maps are requested to a zoom level according to print frame size and map scale, which may exceed Bing Maps resolution. In such case, the map missing from the printed PDF.  | 19  |  
| renderBuffer  | NetworksVector  | The buffer in pixels around the viewport extent used by the renderer when getting features from the vector source for the rendering or hit-detection. Recommended value: the size of the largest symbol, line width or label.  | 100  |  
| imageRatio  | NetworksVector  | Ratio by which the rendered extent should be larger than the viewport extent. A larger ratio avoids cut images during panning, but will cause a decrease in performance.  | 1  |  
## Apply changes[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Print/Customization-of-print-settings.html#apply-changes)
Add customized parameters grouped JavaScript objects to `Hxgn.printSettings` keyed on the services URL. For example:

```
Hxgn.printSettings["http://myserver/wms"] = {
   singleTile: false,
   tileSize: 512
   gutter: 60
}

```

See `printsettings_custom.js` file for further instructions.

# NetWorks print scale adjustment
The portal allows different coordinate systems for maps and prints. The conversion between these different projections does not preserve true lengths and angles in some areas. The usage of various coordinate systems for maps and prints may lead to prints where the map scale is broken. The measured lengths on the printed map are not accurate.
For example when printing, portal tries to fit the map section (in EPSG:3857 coordinates) to the paper area. However, due to the the non-conformity of EPSG:3857, the ratio of the sizes of the plot frame and paper is not the same in EPSG:5514 and EPSG:3857. E.g the side ratio of an A3 (420 x 297mm) is 1.4142 which is sqrt(2). This is also true for EPSG:5514 plot frame, but not for EPSG:3857 frame, which has the ratio 1.306 (at roughly 48deg N), with the horizontal side slightly shorter. The portal needs to fit this frame into the paper and picks the maximum resolution (i.e. best of Fit width or Fit height), in order to fit the whole requested area. This results in a print which is not 1:100, as it would be if only EPSG:5514 was used.
The portal allows to configure the way how dimensions of the map frame are calculated. The resulting frame should preserve the correct aspect ratio of the map and page. One side of the frame (height or width) is fixed and the other side is recalculated.
The frame fitting calculation can be set in print settings (`assets/js/printsettings.js`) through the parameter **fixRatioMode.**
Possible configuration are values:
  * **none** - The aspect ratio of the map frame is untouched. No modification of the frame is done.
  * **width** - Recalculates the map frame width according to the page ratio. The height of the map frame is untouched (fixed).
  * **height** - Recalculates the map frame height according to the page ratio. The width of the map frame is untouched (fixed).

# Print frame size computation
The Print function uses by default the main view projection to compute the physical size of the print frame for the given scale. For non-cartesian projections like EPSG:3857, this does not return correct results and the requested scale does not fit.
Portal allows configuration of a coordinate system, in which the computation of the frame size is performed.
## Static configuration[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Print/Print-frame-size-computation.html#static-configuration)
All computations will use a single defined CS. Override setting `print.cartesianCoordinateSystem` and set it to a name of a coordinate system registered in `coordsys.json`.
## Dynamic configuration[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Print/Print-frame-size-computation.html#dynamic-configuration)
All computations will use a single defined CS. Override setting `print.cartesianCoordinateSystemSelector` and set it to a function, which receives coordinates of the frame center and returns name of a coordinate system. The name must be registered in `coordsys.json`.

# Print Vector Service data with mapped colors
## Overview[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Print/Print-Vector-Service-data-with-mapped-colors.html#overview)
Some legends use other colors than white for the map background (typically black). However when printing, the default background color is white so some styles might become unreadable.
Print functionality can be configured to use different colors for Vector Service data when printing. It works by mapping a color code to another and this mapping is applied to all styles published by the Vector Service.
The color map can be configured in `settings\printsettings_custom.js` for all Vector Services at once or for individual Vector Service instances (identified by service URL).
The `colorMap` element is an array of objects with `from` and `to` properties. Both properties contain color codes as an array of integers between 0 and 255 `[R, G, B]`.
**Example 1: color mapping for all Vector Service sources**

```
Hxgn.printSettings.NetworksVector: {
        colorMap: [{
            from: [255, 255, 255],
            to: [0, 0, 0]
        }, {
            from: [255, 255, 0],
            to: [128, 128, 0]
        }]
    },
    ...
}

```

**Example 2: color mapping for single Vector Service instance**

```
Hxgn.printSettings['http://networks-server/VectorService1/'] = {
    colorMap: [{
            from: [255, 255, 255],
            to: [0, 0, 0]
        }, {
            from: [255, 255, 0],
            to: [128, 128, 0]
        }
    ]
}

```

# Use Puppeteer for Print
The Print function in the Portal uses Node.js and Puppeteer to re-render the map on the background and print the result into a PNG, which is then wrapped in a PDF.
##### Note
Administration Console automatically deploys Portal with Puppeteer.
For instructions how to install Puppeteer manually, see [Print](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/troubleshooting/Known-Issues/HxGN-NetWorks-Portal/Print.html).

##### Settings

# Localized Help
The Portal help function is a simple function which opens a URL in a new browser tab or window.
[![image.png](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/.attachments/image-996e6a98-9f3c-4aa4-b935-ed293a188225.png)](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/.attachments/image-996e6a98-9f3c-4aa4-b935-ed293a188225.png)
When deployed a Portal instance is configured with a URL which links to the documentation delivered with the product which is in English. If a localized version of the help is available via a web server then this URL can be overridden so that it points to that help. To do this use either of the following workflows.
## Workflow 1 - Use custom configuration XML[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Settings/Localized-Help.html#workflow-1---use-custom-configuration-xml)
  1. On the NetWorks server create an empty XML file with a `.xml` extension e.g. `c:\customizations\settings.xml`.
  2. In the file add the following text:

```
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8" ?>
<configuration>
	<settings>
		<setting name="settings.help.url" value="&quot;https://myserver/help/&quot;" />		
	</settings>
</configuration>

```

Replace the URL `https://myserver/help/` with the correct URL. The URL can be absolute or relative. Note that the start and end `&quot;` are required.
  1. In the Administration Console - Services Deployment Module, edit the Portal instance and switch to the Workspace tab. Check the 'Enable Custom Configurations' check box and enter the file path to your xml file e.g. `c:\customizations\settings.xml`. Then save, this will re-deploy the portal.

Note that if you make further changes to your xml file you will need to re-deploy the Portal for these changes to be made available. Note also that due to browser caching, a user may need to clear their browser cache for these changes to be immediately available.
## Workflow - Use windows script[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Settings/Localized-Help.html#workflow---use-windows-script)
  1. On the NetWorks server create a file in an empty folder called 'settings_custom.js' e.g. `c:\customizations\settings_custom.js`
  2. In this file add the following line:

`Hxgn.resourceTables.settings.help.url = 'https://myserver/help/';`
Replace the URL `https://myserver/help/` with the correct URL. The URL can be absolute or relative.
  1. Create an empty `.bat` file in the same folder e.g. `c:\customizations\copysettings.bat`
  2. In this file add the following text: `copy /y c:\customizations\settings_custom.js .\settings\`
  3. In the Administration Console - Services Deployment Module, edit the Portal instance and switch to the Workspace tab. Check the 'Enable Custom Configurations' check box and enter the folder path to your files e.g. `c:\customizations\`. Then save, this will re-deploy the portal.

Note that if you make further changes to your js file you will need to re-deploy the Portal for these changes to be made available. Note also that due to browser caching, a user may need to clear their browser cache for these changes to be immediately available.

# Redline
## Overview[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Settings/Redline.html#overview)
The redline settings table defines which colors, text fonts and symbol fonts that are available for selection in the Portal UI. It also defines the default Redline XML document tag used when saving redlines to XML. The following names can be customized.  
| Name  | Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
| colors  | The names and associated color codes available for redlines.  |  
| fontfamilies  | The list of font names available for redline texts.  |  
| symbolfamilies  | The list of symbol font names available for redline symbols together with the list of available symbols.  |  
| xmlTags  | Default redline XML document tag used when exporting redlines.  |  
## colors[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Settings/Redline.html#colors)
List of color names with corresponding color codes available for styling redline geometries. Each item in the list has two properties:
  * `display` - The label shown in the color picklists.
  * `value` - The RGB code for the color.

RGB codes should be specified using a six digit hexadecimal number preceded with a `#`. Letters should be uppercase.
The default colors are defined as follows:

```
Hxgn.resourceTables.redline.colors = [
    { display: Hxgn.resourceTables.strings['common.colors.red'], value: "#FF0000" },
    { display: Hxgn.resourceTables.strings['common.colors.aqua'], value: "#00FFFF" },
    { display: Hxgn.resourceTables.strings['common.colors.black'], value: "#000000" },
    { display: Hxgn.resourceTables.strings['common.colors.blue'], value: "#0000FF" },
    { display: Hxgn.resourceTables.strings['common.colors.green'], value: "#008000" },
    { display: Hxgn.resourceTables.strings['common.colors.grey'], value: "#808080" },
    { display: Hxgn.resourceTables.strings['common.colors.lime'], value: "#00FF00" },
    { display: Hxgn.resourceTables.strings['common.colors.maroon'], value: "#800000" },
    { display: Hxgn.resourceTables.strings['common.colors.navy'], value: "#000080" },
    { display: Hxgn.resourceTables.strings['common.colors.olive'], value: "#808000" },
    { display: Hxgn.resourceTables.strings['common.colors.purple'], value: "#800080" },
    { display: Hxgn.resourceTables.strings['common.colors.silver'], value: "#C0C0C0" },
    { display: Hxgn.resourceTables.strings['common.colors.teal'], value: "#008080" },
    { display: Hxgn.resourceTables.strings['common.colors.white'], value: "#FFFFFF" },
    { display: Hxgn.resourceTables.strings['common.colors.yellow'], value: "#FFFF00" }
]

```

## fontfamilies[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Settings/Redline.html#fontfamilies)
The list of fonts available for redline texts. Each item in the list has two properties:
  * `display` - The label display in the font picklist.
  * `value` - A CSS font family as a string.

Note that if the font is not available to the browser, then it will use its default font to render the text.
For compatibility with Designer, if a font name contains whitespace or other non letter characters then the font name must be wrapped in _double_ quotes. If it does not then it should not be wrapped in double quotes. For example, the font `Courier New` must be specified as `"Courier New"` whereas `Arial` requires no modification. Then when adding them to settings place the modified font name in _single_ quotes e.g.

```
{ display: "Arial", value: 'Arial' },
{ display: "Courier New", value: '"Courier New"' },

```

Note that the value is written `'"Courier New"'` and _not_ `"'Courier New'"`. Note the order of the quotes. When wrapping a font name it must be in _double_ quotes and not _single_ quotes. These rules for wrapping font names is only applicable to the settings js file in the portal and not any associated `categories.xml` file. The `categories.xml` files is a Redline XML file and uses the rules defined in the Hxgn NetWorks Admin Help for those types of file.
Also for compatibility with Designer, `value` should only contain a single font name.
The default fontfamilies are defined as follows:

```
Hxgn.resourceTables.redline.fontfamilies = [
   { display: "Calibri", value: 'Calibri' },
   { display: "Arial", value: 'Arial' },
   { display: "Blackletter", value: 'Blackletter' },
   { display: "Cambria", value: 'Cambria' },
   { display: "Courier New", value: '"Courier New"' },
   { display: "Rockwell", value: 'Rockwell' },
   { display: "Stencil", value: 'Stencil' },
   { display: "Tahoma", value: 'Tahoma' },
   { display: "Times New Roman", value: '"Times New Roman"' },
   { display: "Verdana", value: 'Verdana' }
]

```

## symbolfamilies[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Settings/Redline.html#symbolfamilies)
List of fonts available for redline symbols. Each item in the list has three properties:
  * `display` - The label display in the font picklist.
  * `value` - A CSS font family as a string.
  * `symbols` - A string containing the characters that symbols are mapped to. Each character in the string will be available to the user as a separate symbol.

See the previous section for notes about how to specify font names which contain whitespace or other none word characters.
The `symbols` string can contain 'character escapes' to represent characters that cannot be conveniently represented in their literal form. It uses normal JavaScript rules for escaping characters which uses the backslash `\` plus a sequence of one or more characters to represent another character. The backslash character itself is represented by two backslash characters `\\`, double quotes as `\"`. You can also represent a character by its Unicode code point using `\uHHHH` where HHHH is a _four digit_ hexadecimal number.
Note that if the font is not available to the browser, then it will use its default font to render the symbol. This can lead to symbols being displayed as a square or an empty character. Note also that if exporting to Redline XML then this format can currently only encode symbols which are mapped to printable ANSI characters.
The default symbolfamilies are defined as follows:

```
Hxgn.resourceTables.redline.symbolfamilies = [
   {

      value: 'INGR_WATERRegular',
      symbols: "½§1!23#4¤5%6&7/8(9)0=+?`´¨^åÅpPoOiIuUyYtTrReEwWqQaAsSdDfFgGhHjJkKlLæÆøØ'*-_.:,;mMnNbBvVcCxXzZ<>"
   },
   {

      value: 'ELDKSYMBOLRegular',
      symbols: "½123456789=?pPoOiIuUyYtTrReEwWqQaAsSdDfFgGhHjJkKlL:;mMnNbBvVcCxXzZ<>"

## xmlTags[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Settings/Redline.html#xmltags)
Defines the default redline document tag used when generating a redline XML export. The values in braces `{}` are replaced when exporting.
The default document tag is defined as follows:

```
Hxgn.resourceTables.redline.xmlTags = {
        document: '<RedlineDocument xmlns="urn:Redlines.xsd" ProgID="GNetClient.GRedlineDisplayCtrl" Version="1" Configuration="{configuration}" SessionID="{session}">',
    }

```

## Overriding style properties[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Settings/Redline.html#overriding-style-properties)
The default style properties can be changed by overriding them in settings\settings_custom.js. To do this copy the relevant styles into the file using the following template:

```
Hxgn.resourceTables.redline.{redlineName} = {value};

```

# Settings
The following is a table of setting names that can be adjusted in a deployed Portal web site.  
| Name  | Value  | Remarks  |   |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| analysis.resultExtentBuffer  | `50`  | Number in map units to buffer the extent of a result set added to the legend. Affects legend fit operations.  |   |  
| analysis.warnOnEmptyResult  | `true`  | If a result set is added to the legend which is empty, warn the user via a message.  |   |  
| api.enableInternalBroadcastChannel  | `true`  | If true enable the BroadcastChannel used to communicate between the Portal, Portal3D and Utilities Shell Web.  |   |  
| coordinates.componentSeparator  | `'; '`  | Used by the coordinates toolbar copy & paste functionality.  |   |  
| coordinates.decimalSeparator  |   | Used by coordinates toolbar copy & paste functionality. Defaults to the localized string common.format.decimalSeparator.  |   |  
| coordinates.geographicFormat  | `'dms'`  | The format geographic coordinates are shown in. Can be `'dms'` or `'dec'`.  |   |  
| coordinates.geographicPrecision  | `6`  | Number of decimal places shown for geographic coordinates shown in decimal format.  |   |  
| coordinates.geographicSecondsPrecision  | `3`  | Number of decimal places shown for second when geographic coordinates are shown in d : m : s format.  |   |  
| coordinates.geographicSwapAxes  | `true`  | If true geographic coordinates are shown latitude, longitude.  |   |  
| coordinates.projectedPrecision  |   | Number of decimal places shown for projected coordinates. Defaults to strings common.format.decimalPrecision.  |   |  
| coordinates.projectedSwapAxes  | `false`  | If true projected coordinates are shown X,Y.  |   |  
| coordinates.updateOnExtentChange  | `true`  | If true then when the map extent is changed then coordinates toolbar is updated with the map views new center  |   |  
| editor.default.height  | `400`  | Initial height of the default editor in pixels  |   |  
| editor.default.width  | `400`  | Initial width of the default editor in pixels  |   |  
| editor.editColor  | `'#A5D867'`  | Background color as RGB code of editable fields  |   |  
| editor.gtdws.height  | `500`  | Initial height of the feature editor in pixels  |   |  
| editor.gtdws.lhsWidth  | `170`  | Initial width of the left hand panel in the feature editor in pixels  |   |  
| editor.gtdws.tabsHeight  | `250`  | Initial height of the tabs panel in the feature editor in pixels  |   |  
| editor.gtdws.width  | `600`  | Initial width of the feature editor in pixels  |   |  
| editor.maxDateLength  | `20`  | Maximum number of characters that can be entered into a date field  |   |  
| editor.maxNumberLength  | `26`  | Maximum number of characters that can be entered into a numeric field  |   |  
| editor.maxTextAreaLength  | `500`  | Maximum number characters for 'memo' fields (G3E_DATATYPE = 12)  |   |  
| editor.maxTextLength  | `50`  | Maximum number of characters that can be entered into text fields  |   |  
| editor.nameColumnWidth  | `150`  | Width of field names column in pixels  |   |  
| filter.defineWindowHeight  | `400`  | Default height of the Filter definition window (in CSS pixels).  |   |  
| filter.defineWindowWidth  | `700`  | Default width of the Filter definition window (in CSS pixels).  |   |  
| filter.selectWindowHeight  | `200`  | Default height of the Filter selection window (in CSS pixels).  |   |  
| filter.selectWindowWidth  | `300`  | Default width of the Filter selection window (in CSS pixels).  |   |  
| help.url  | `'/NetWorksPortalDoc/'`  | The url to the help file.  |   |  
| jobs.autoDeleteInterval  | `1`  | How to long before netplot and netexport jobs are deleted in hours  |   |  
| jobs.autoDownload  | `true`  | Automatically download a netplot or netexport job when its completed  |   |  
| jobs.pollInterval  | `3`  | Poll interval for netplot and netexport jobs in seconds.  |   |  
| jobs.highlightFeaturesTreshhold  | `10000`  | Treshold limit for highlighting Edited Geometries in `Fit Job` functionality. Jobs with more edited feature will just fit the map  |   |  
| map.detailBackgroundColor  | `null`  | Background color for detail legends. See geographicBackgroundColor.  |   |  
| map.detailFitMinResolution  | `0.005`  | Map resolution used when fitting the map to a point in a detail legend.  |   |  
| map.fitMinResolution  | `0.03`  | Map resolution used when fitting the map to a point.  |   |  
| map.fitPadding  | `5`  | Padding (in percentage) added to the map when fitting map to edited features in job.  |   |  
| map.geographicBackgroundColor  | `null`  | Background color for geographic legends. Can be null or RGB value defined as an array of three numbers between 0 and 255 e.g. `[0,0,0]` is black and `[255,255,255]` is white. If null then background color is white.  |   |  
| map.gpsTrackingMode  | `0`  | Sets how GPS functions. Can be 0 center map on initial GPS position, 1 center map when GPS position changes or 2 center map when position changes to outside current map extent.  |   |  
| map.highlightGeometryFilter  | `'excludeLabels'`  | Determines, when highlighting GTech features, what geometry are filtered out. This can be `'none'`, `'excludeLabels'`, `'primaryOnly'`.  |   |  
| map.highlightTimeout  | `3000`  | Timeout in milliseconds for temporary highlights e.g. Areas highlight  |   |  
| map.hitTolerance  | `10`  | Hit tolerance in pixels when selecting vector features.  |   |  
| map.locateTolerance  | `3`  | Hit tolerance in pixels when editing geometry e.g. redlines.  |   |  
| map.panDelta  | `128`  | Value used to determine pan distance when panning the map with arrow keys.  |   |  
| map.readQueryString  | `true`  | If set to false the portal will ignore any query string parameters on startup.  |   |  
| map.schematicBackgroundColor  | `null`  | Background color for schematic legends. See geographicBackgroundColor.  |   |  
| map.schematicFitMinResolution  | `0.015`  | Map resolution used when fitting the map to a point in a schematic legend.  |   |  
| map.showQueryString  | `true`  | As the user pans and zooms the map the query string is updated with the current location which can be book marked.  |   |  
| map.timeout  | `120000`  | Timeout in milliseconds for requests for map data.  |   |  
| map.useHistory  | `true`  | Enable the browser back and forward buttons to cycle through previous map positions.  |   |  
| map.useHistoryForDetails  | `true`  | Enable browser back and forward buttons to cycle through previous map positions in detail and schematic legends. When set to false and useHistory is `true` pressing the back button returns immediately to the geographic view.  |   |  
| map.zoomDelta  | `1`  | Value used to determine zoom when zooming with buttons or mouse wheel.  |   |  
| measure.anglePrecision  | 0  | Number of decimal places used when displaying angles.  |   |  
| measure.enableArea  | `true`  | Whether total area labels are displayed or not.  |   |  
| measure.enableCoordinate  | `true`  | Whether coordinate marker labels are displayed or not.  |   |  
| measure.enableSegmentLength  | `true`  | Whether segment length labels are displayed or not.  |   |  
| measure.enableTotalLength  | `true`  | Whether total length labels are displayed or not.  |   |  
| measure.persistGeometry  | `true`  | Whether measure geometry is stored on the client between sessions or not.  |   |  
| measure.precision  |   | Number of decimal places shown for measures e.g. distance and area. Defaults to strings common.format.decimalPrecision.  |   |  
| measure.useGeodesicCalculations  | `true`  | Whether the client calculates the geodesic distance or projected distance.  |   |  
| netplot.defaultPrinters  |   | "Array of printers to be available for all configurations. Each item in the array has _printerID_ and _printerUsername_ property. This setting is used to add the built-in ""G/Technology PDF Printer"" with a fixed printerID of -1 to the list. "  |   |  
| netplot.frameoverlap  | `0.1`  | Value between 0 and 1 representing overlap when placing multi frames.  |   |  
| paging.pageSize  | `25`  | Number of records shown on page. Only applicable to results set that support paging.  |   |  
| placementMsg.align  | `"Top Center"`  | Position of placement info message. Can be "Top Left", "Top Center", "Top Right", "Bottom Left", "Bottom Center" or "Bottom Right".  |   |  
| placementMsg.autoClose  | `false`  | If true then close placement info message after autoCloseDelay milliseconds. If false close when placement operation is concluded.  |   |  
| placementMsg.autoCloseDelay  | `7000`  | If `autoClose` is set to true then the delay in milliseconds after which the message is automatically closed.  |   |  
| placementMsg.width  |   | The width the message is constrained to in CSS pixels.  |   |  
| print.cartesianCoordinateSystem  |   | See [Print frame size computation](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Print/Print-frame-size-computation.html).  |   |  
| print.cartesianCoordinateSystemSelector  |   | See [Print frame size computation](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Print/Print-frame-size-computation.html).  |   |  
| print.ppi  | `150`  | The default print image resolution. See [Controlling print resolution](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Print/Controlling-print-resolution.html).  |   |  
| print.scales  | `[]`  | List of scales available for printing. Defaults to `[50, 100, 250, 500, 1000, 2000, 5000, 10000]`.  |   |  
| print.templatePpi  | `[]`  | Allows for overriding the default print image resolution for a particular template. See [Controlling print resolution](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Print/Controlling-print-resolution.html).  |   |  
| query.addResultsToLegendEnabled  | `true`  | When `true`, the _Add results to legend_ button is displayed in Query dialog.  |   |  
| query.defaultCategoryACNO  | `4`  | ACNO of default pre-selected query category  |   |  
| query.resultsGeometryFilter  | `'excludeLabels'`  | Determines, when adding results to legend, what geometry are filtered out. This can be `'none'`, `'excludeLabels'`, `'primaryOnly'`.  |   |  
| query.windowHeight  |   | `600`  | Default height of query window (in CSS pixels).  |  
| query.windowWidth  | `300`  | Default width of query window (in CSS pixels).  |   |  
| redlines.importGeometryCollectionAsGeometry  | `true`  | If `true` then when a set of geometries is imported as a [GeometryCollection](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7946#section-3.1.8) then it split into individual geometry.  |   |  
| redlines.showUploadButton  | `true`  |  `true` to show Export and Upload button in Export redlines section.  |   |  
| scaleline.displayScale  | `true`  | Whether the scale is displayed.  |   |  
| scaleline.dpi  | `90.7`  | The 'dots per inch' used to calculate scale. The default is the OGC default value.  |   |  
| scaleline.scaleBar  | `true`  | Whether the scale bar is a bar or a line.  |   |  
| scaleline.steps  | `1`  | If scale bar is true then the number of sections the bar is split into. It is recommended that this is 1 or an even number.  |   |  
| scaleline.units  | `'metric'`  | The units used by the scale bar. Can be `'metric'`,`'degrees'`,`'imperial'`,`'us'` or `'nautical'`.  |   |  
| search.desktopColumnWidth  | `100`  | Default width of a column in search results in desktop client.  |   |  
| search.mobileColumnWidth  | `200`  | Default width of a column in search results in mobile client.  |   |  
| search.hideableColumns  | `['G3E_FID', 'G3E_FNO']`  | List of column names which can be hidden in the search results.  |   |  
| search.defaultHiddenColumns  | `['G3E_FID', 'G3E_FNO']`  | List of column names which are hidden by default in the search results.  |   |  
| search.windowHeight  | `600`  | Default height of search window (in CSS pixels).  |   |  
| search.windowWidth  | `300`  | Default width of search window (in CSS pixels).  |   |  
| settingsDlg.height  | `330`  | Default height of the settings dialog in CSS pixels.  |   |  
| settingsDlg.width  | `500`  | Default width of the settings dialog in CSS pixels.  |   |  
| sidebar.width  | `380`  | Initial width of the side bar in pixels  |   |  
| snapping.pixelTolerance  | `10`  | Pixel tolerance for considering if the pointer close enough to a segment or vertex for snapping.  |   |  
| snapping.snapToEdge  | `true`  | Enable snapping to to the closest edge in tolerance distance. See [Snapping](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Placement/Snapping.html).  |   |  
| snapping.snapToVertex  | `true`  | Enable snapping to to the closest vertex in tolerance distance. See [Snapping](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Placement/Snapping.html).  |   |  
| tooltip.hoverTimeout  | `1000`  | How long (ms) should the mouse hover until map tooltip is shown.  |   |  
| tooltip.maxItems  | `10`  | Maximum number of items displayed in one map tooltip box.  |   |  
| trace.autoAddToLegend  | `true`  | When switching legends, for example, between geographic and detail legends, automatically add all active traces to the new legend if not already added.  |   |  
| trace.autoExpandFolder  | `true`  | When adding a trace result to the legend automatically expand the 'Traces' folder in the legend tree.  |   |  
| workspace.timeout  | `60000`  | Timeout in milliseconds for service requests.  |   |  
##### Note
If using the custom configuration XML to override settings you must append `settings.` to the name e.g.

```
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8" ?>
<configuration>
	<settings>
		<setting name="settings.paging.pageSize" value="10" />
	</settings>
</configuration>

```

# Style Properties
## Overview[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Settings/Style-Properties.html#overview)
Style properties are used to the default styles for redline and measuring geometries. There are the following names in the style properties table.  
| Name  | Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
| coordinateMarker  | Defines the style for the coordinate marker point.  |  
| coordinateMarkerText  | Defines the style for the coordinate marker label (see notes below).  |  
| measureArea  | Defines the style for the measuring area.  |  
| measureLine  | Defines the style for the measuring line.  |  
| redlineLine  | Defines the default style for redline two point lines.  |  
| redlineLinestring  | Defines the default style for redline polylines.  |  
| redlineFreehandlinestring  | Defines the default style for redline freehand polylines.  |  
| redlinePolygon  | Defines the default style for redline polygons.  |  
| redlineRectangle  | Defines the default style for redline rectangles.  |  
| redlineCircle  | Defines the default style for redline circles.  |  
| redlineText  | Defines the default style for redline texts.  |  
| redlineSymbol  | Defines the default style for redline symbols.  |  
The reference to style properties are defined [here](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Redlines/Style-property-reference.html).
## coordinateMarker[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Settings/Style-Properties.html#coordinatemarker)

```
Hxgn.resourceTables.styleProperties.coordinateMarker = {
        enableCoordinate: true,
        fontSize: 14,
        fontColor: "#ff00ff",
        fontFamily: "INGR_WATERRegular",
        text: "u",
        rotateWithView: true,
        scaleDependent: true
    }

```

## coordinateMarkerText[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Settings/Style-Properties.html#coordinatemarkertext)
The coordinateMarkerText is a special case which is used to adjust the style of coordinate labels. The following properties are overridden by the style of the geometry the label is associated with:
  * `scaleDependent`
  * `rotateWithView`
  * `fontColor`
  * `fontOpacity`
  * `fontSize`

In addition text offsets are calculated as:
  * offsetX = `textOffsetX` * `fontSize`
  * offsetY = `textOffsetY` * `fontSize`

Where fontSize is that defined by the style of the geometry the label is associated with.

```
Hxgn.resourceTables.styleProperties.coordinateMarkerText = {
        fontFamily: "Calibri",
        textAlign: 'left',
        textOffsetX: 1,
        textOffsetY: -1,
        fontOutlineColor: '#000000',
        fontOutlineWidth: 1.0,
        textBox: true,
        textBoxFillColor: '#FFFFFF',
        textBoxFillOpacity: 1.0,
        textBoxPadding: [2, 2, 2, 2]
    }

```

## measureArea[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Settings/Style-Properties.html#measurearea)

```
Hxgn.resourceTables.styleProperties.measureArea = {
        enableArea: true,
        enableSegmentLength: true,
        strokeColor: '#FF00FF',
        strokeDashstyle: 'dot',
        strokeOpacity: 1.0,
        strokeWidth: 2,
        fontFamily: 'Calibri',
        fontSize: 14,
        textAlign: 'left',
        textBox: true,
        textBoxFillColor: '#FFFFFF',
        textBoxFillOpacity: 1.0,
        textBoxPadding: [2, 2, 2, 2],
        fontOutlineColor: '#FF00FF',
        fontOutlineWidth: 1.0,
        scaleDependent: false,
        rotateWithView: true,
        fillColor: '#ff00ff',
        fillOpacity: 0.3
    }

```

## measureLine[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Settings/Style-Properties.html#measureline)

```
Hxgn.resourceTables.styleProperties.measureLine = {
        enableSegmentLength: true,
        enableTotalLength: true,
        strokeColor: '#ff00ff',
        strokeDashstyle: 'dot',
        strokeOpacity: 1.0,
        strokeWidth: 2,
        fontFamily: 'Calibri',
        fontSize: 14,
        textAlign: 'left',
        textBox: true,
        textBoxPadding: [2, 2, 2, 2],
        textBoxFillColor: '#ffffff',
        textBoxFillOpacity: 1.0,
        fontOutlineColor: '#ff00ff',
        fontOutlineWidth: 1.0,
        textOffsetX: 9,
        textOffsetY: -9,
        scaleDependent: false,
        rotateWithView: true
    }

```

## redlineLine[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Settings/Style-Properties.html#redlineline)

```
Hxgn.resourceTables.styleProperties.redlineLine = {
        strokeDashstyle: "solid",
        strokeWidth: 2,
        strokeColor: "#FF0000",
        strokeOpacity: 0.9,
        fontFamily: "Calibri",
        fontSize: 14, 
        fontOutlineColor: '#FFFFFF',
        fontOutlineWidth: 3.0,
        rotateWithView: true,
        scaleDependent: false,
        enableSegmentLength: false,
        enableTotalLength: false,
        enableArrows: false,
        enableAngle: false
    }

```

```

        strokeDashstyle: "solid",
        strokeWidth: 2,
        strokeColor: "#FF0000",
        strokeOpacity: 0.9,
        fillColor: "#FF0000",
        fillOpacity: 0.4,
        fontFamily: "Calibri",
        fontSize: 14,
        fontOutlineColor: '#FFFFFF',
        fontOutlineWidth: 3.0,

    }

```

## redlineLabel[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Settings/Style-Properties.html#redlinelabel)
For redline labels setting enableCoordinate to true has no effect.

```
Hxgn.resourceTables.styleProperties.redlineLabel = {
        fontFamily: "Calibri",
        fontSize: 14,
        fontStyle: "normal",
        fontColor: "#FF0000",
        fontOpacity: 1.0,
        text: "Text",
        rotateWithView: true,
        scaleDependent: false,
        textAlign: 'left',
        textBaseline: 'bottom'
    }

```

```
Hxgn.resourceTables.styleProperties.redlineSymbol = {
        fontFamily: 'INGR_WATERRegular',
        fontSize: 14,
        fontColor: "#FF0000",
        fontOpacity: 1.0,
        text: "A",
        textAlign: 'center',
        rotateWithView: true,
        scaleDependent: false,
        enableCoordinate: false
    }

```

## Overriding style properties[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Settings/Style-Properties.html#overriding-style-properties)
The default style properties can be changed by overriding them in settings\settings_custom.js. To do this copy the relevant styles into the file using the following template:

```
Hxgn.resourceTables.styleProperties.{styleName} = {value};

```

For example to make the measure line green without text boxes use:

```
Hxgn.resourceTables.styleProperties.measureLine = {
        enableSegmentLength: true,
        enableTotalLength: true,
        strokeColor: '#00FF00',
        strokeDashstyle: 'dot',
        strokeOpacity: 1.0,
        strokeWidth: 2,
        fontFamily: 'Calibri',
        fontSize: 14,
        textAlign: 'left',
        textBox: false,
        fontOutlineColor: '#FFFFFF',
        fontOutlineWidth: 2.0,
        textOffsetX: 9,
        textOffsetY: -9,
        scaleDependent: false,
        rotateWithView: true
    }

```

The following are the system styles that can be adjusted.

Hxgn.resourceTables.styles = {

    highlight: {
        circle: {

            },

                color: [0, 255, 255, 1],

        },

            color: [0, 255, 255, 0.7],
            width: 6
        }
    },
    // Style for highlighting trace parameter features; start, hint and goal.
    trace: {
        circle: {
            fill: {
                color: [0, 255, 0, 0.3]
            },
            stroke: {
                color: [0, 255, 0, 1],
                width: 3
            },
            radius: 10
        },
        fill: {
            color: [0, 255, 0, 0.3]
        },

            color: [0, 255, 0, 0.7],

        }
    },
    // Style for GPS location

        circle: {
            radius: 6,
            fill: {
                color: '#3399CC'
            },
            stroke: {
                color: '#fff',

            }
        }
    },

        },

        },

};

The default styles can be changed by overriding them in settings\settings_custom.js. To do this copy the relevant styles into the file using the following template:

```
Hxgn.resourceTables.styles.{styleName} = {value};

```

For example to make highlight color green

```
Hxgn.resourceTables.styles.highlight = {
        circle: {
