        }
    }

```

# Settings
## Overview[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Settings.html#overview)
The portal has many different client settings which can be used to customize the user experience. These are divided into a number of tables each with a specific purpose. These are named as follows:
  * [settings](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Settings/Settings.html) - Client function settings and defaults e.g. request time out and map pan distance.
  * [styles](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Settings/Styles.html) - Defines basic client map styling e.g. feature highlight.
  * [styleProperties](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Settings/Style-Properties.html) - Defines redline and measure geometry styling.
  * [redline](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Settings/Redline.html) - Defines available fonts for redlining.

The default portal settings are defined in the assets/js/settings.js file in a deployed portal instance.
It is not recommended to edit the `settings.js` file directly as this will make upgrading to newer versions of Networks more complicated. The recommended approach is to override settings by providing a `settings/settings_custom.js` file in a deployed portal. This can be done by using the custom configuration XML used by the Admin Console. Alternatively it is possible to create the file manually and define overrides by adding lines using the following template.
`Hxgn.resourceTables.{table name}.{setting name} = {value};`
Replace {table name} with a value from the above list {setting name} with a name defined in the table section. For example the following line will redirect the portal help function to open a different URL.
`Hxgn.resourceTables.settings.help.url = 'http://help.com';`
See [Localized Help](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Settings/Localized-Help.html) for more information about help.
See [Customization file syntax](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Administration-Console/Deployment-customization/Customization-file-syntax.html) for more information about using custom configuration XML.
See [Customization from folder](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Administration-Console/Deployment-customization/Customization-from-folder.html) for how to automatically copy in a manually created settings_custom.js file when deploy a portal website.
Note that you cannot both use the custom configuration XML file to override settings _and_ the manual approach, you must choose one or the other.

##### web.config-file

# appSettings and connectionStrings
## appSettings[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/web.config-file/appSettings-and-connectionStrings.html#appsettings)
The appSettings section in the web.config file can be used to override various low level functionality in the portal.  
| Name  | Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
| Analysis.MaxResults  | Maximum number of features to retrieve from an analysis (query, trace) from Analytical Service when adding results to legend. Default is 10000.  |  
| Analysis.PageSize  | The number of features requested internally from NetWorks services at one time when building an analysis result set. Default is 10000.  |  
| directPlotExportClientId  | GDR_CLIENTID used for integration to NetPlot and NetExport.  |  
| Google.StaticMapsApiUrl  | URL to google static maps API. If google maps is being used this can be used to override the URL. Default value is <https://maps.googleapis.com/maps/api/staticmap>.  |  
| HttpClient.Timeout  | Default timeout for requests made from a portal service to another service in seconds.  |  
| OIDC.RestrictByRole  | See [Restrict access to Portal by role](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Security/Restrict-access-to-Portal-by-role.html).  |  
| OIDC.ValidRoles  | See [Restrict access to Portal by role](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Security/Restrict-access-to-Portal-by-role.html).  |  
| OIDC.RoleClaim  | See [Restrict access to Portal by role](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Security/Restrict-access-to-Portal-by-role.html).  |  
| Portal.CookieSameSite  | Used to set the SameSite of attribute of cookies generated directly by the Portal. This does not include cookies used by OIDC. This can be set to `Strict`, `Lax` or `None`. By default the value is `Strict`.  |  
| Portal.CookieSecure  | Used to set the Secure attribute of cookies generated directly by the Portal. This does not include cookies used by OIDC. This can be `true` or `false`. By default the value is `true`.  |  
| tempDirectory  | Temporary directory. Used by various functions including print as a location to generate temporary files in. Must be writable by the portal services.  |  
## connectionStrings[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/web.config-file/appSettings-and-connectionStrings.html#connectionstrings)
By default the portal does not use any connectionStrings as it does not connect to any external databases. However if NetPlot or NetExport are used then they require a connectionString named `GTech` to be configured e.g.

```
  <connectionStrings>
    <add name="GTech" connectionString="Data source=GTECHDB;User ID=gtusr;Password=*******;" />
  </connectionStrings>

```

# Authentication
The recommended approach for authentication and authorization of users in the Portal is to use OpenID Connect. This can be enabled or disabled by changing the `<infrastructureAppAuthentication>` section of the [web.config](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/web.config-file.html) file. Here you can enable or disable OpenID Connect support by changing the `mode` attribute between `Anonymous` or `Oidc`.
## Anonymous[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/web.config-file/Authentication.html#anonymous)

```
<infrastructureAppAuthentication mode="Anonymous" />

```

## OpenID Connect[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/web.config-file/Authentication.html#openid-connect)

```
<infrastructureAppAuthentication mode="Oidc">
    <parameters>
        <add key="OpenIdConfigFile" value="~/OpenIdConfig.json" />
        <add key="RequiredClaims" value="gtechnologyDBConnect,role" />
    </parameters>
</infrastructureAppAuthentication>

```

### Parameters[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/web.config-file/Authentication.html#parameters)  
| Name  | Required  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| OpenIdConfigFile  | Y  | Path to OpenID Connect configuration file. Can be relative to Portal root (using `~/{path}`) or absolute.  |  
| RequiredClaims  |   | Comma-separated list of required claim names. Required claims not included in the access token are retrieved from the OpenID Connect userinfo endpoint.  |  
See also [Restrict access to Portal by role](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Security/Restrict-access-to-Portal-by-role.html).
## Published claims[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/web.config-file/Authentication.html#published-claims)
List of OpenID Connect claims available on the client via the `$NWP.user` API is configurable via `<publishedClaims>` section of `/configuration/webGIS` element.
##### Important
Claims which are not present in the OIDC access token must be present in the `RequiredClaims` parameter of the `<infrastructureAppAuthentication>` section.
Example:

```
<webGIS>

   <publishedClaims>
      <add name="name" />
      <add name="email" />
      <add name="preferred_username" />
      <add name="sub" />
   </publishedClaims>

</webGIS>

```

# Localized files
## Introduction[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/web.config-file/Localized-files.html#introduction)
The portal includes a mechanism to load files containing, for example, localized strings dynamically based on the ['Accept-Language'](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Accept-Language) header the browser sends with HTTP requests.
## Configuration[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/web.config-file/Localized-files.html#configuration)
The path to the files containing localizations on the server is configured by this entry in the [web.config](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/web.config-file.html) file

```
<localizedFiles rootFolder="assets\locale" defaultLanguage="en" />

```

The root folder is relative to the portal instance. Under the root folder files are arranged in sub folders. Each sub folder should be named after a language code, for example, `en` or `en-gb`. The default language property should be set to the name of one of the sub folders.
From a browser the files are accessed via the path defined in this element from the web.config file.

```
<add name="LocaleHandler" path="assets.localized" verb="GET" type="HexagonsiDK.Core.Services.Handlers.LocalizedFilesHandler, HexagonsiDK.Core.Services" allowPathInfo="true" />

```

## How it works[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/web.config-file/Localized-files.html#how-it-works)
Consider a portal deployed on IIS in a web application named `nwportal` with the settings defined in the above section. A file containing localizations can be accessed via a browser using, for example, the following URL
`http://localhost/nwportal/assets.localized/strings.js`
What happens on the server is that it checks the 'Accept-Language' header sent in with the request. If this is set to, for example,
`Accept-Language: da-dk;de`
Then it will look for, in this order:
  * `assets\locale\da-dk\strings.js`
  * `assets\locale\da\strings.js`
  * `assets\locale\de\strings.js`

As soon as it finds 'strings.js' in one of those folders it will return it. If it does not find the file then it will look for the `defaultLanguage` folder, in this case `wn` e.g
`assets\locale\en\strings.js`
If `strings.js` is still not found the server will return a 404 code.
## Limitations[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/web.config-file/Localized-files.html#limitations)
Due to caching on the browser if the user changes the language then they will need to empty their browser cache to load a new localized file.
## Localizing the portal to another language[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/web.config-file/Localized-files.html#localizing-the-portal-to-another-language)
To localize the portal to another language, for example, Portuguese then three things are required.
  1. A folder with the correct name is is created under the localized files root folder e.g. assets\locale\pt
  2. A copy of strings.js is taken from one of the existing locale folders and placed in the new folder.
  3. Replace the display strings inside the copy of strings.js with translations.

Keep in mind the following:
  * The file is a JavasScript file and structured such that you have `"_string name_":"_displayed string_"` on each line.
  * Only modify the display strings.
  * Some strings can contain HTML markup e.g. `'<b>'`. However not all strings support HTML markup.
  * All translations must start and end with the `"` character.
  * The last character on the line must be a single `,` character.

See [Deployment customization](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Administration-Console/Deployment-customization.html) for information about how to automate the deployment of new language files.

# Logging
Server logging for the Portal uses <https://nlog-project.org/> the same as NetWorks Web Services. Nlog can support logging to many different types of sources depending on customer requirements.
Server log settings are defined by default in a separate file. This is file is called **NLog.config** and is placed in the same folder as the [web.config](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/web.config-file.html) file. The name and location of the log settings file is defined under the `common/logging` section e.g.

```
<configuration>
    ...
    <common>
        <logging>
            <factoryAdapter type="Common.Logging.NLog.NLogLoggerFactoryAdapter, Common.Logging.NLog4412">
                <arg key="configType" value="FILE" />
                <arg key="configFile" value="~/NLog.config" />
            </factoryAdapter>
        </logging>
    </common>
    ...
</configuration>

```

The default logging configuration when deployed logs to a file and just logs errors. See the example below. The logging level can be modified by changing the minlevel attribute in the settings file to `Warning`, `Debug` or `Trace`. The logging level can also be changed via the Admin Console.

```
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<nlog xmlns="http://www.nlog-project.org/schemas/NLog.xsd" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" internalLogLevel="Warn" internalLogFile="NLogInternal.log" autoReload="true">
  <variable name="instanceName" value="NwPortal" />
  <variable name="logFolder" value="C:/ProgramData/Intergraph/NetWorks/Logs" />
  <variable name="standardColumns" value="${counter}|${longdate}|${machinename}|${processname}|${processid}|${threadid}|${level}|${logger}|${message}" />
  <targets>
    <target name="file" xsi:type="File" layout="${standardColumns}" fileName="${logFolder}/${instanceName}-${shortdate}.log" maxArchiveFiles="5" archiveAboveSize="500000" archiveNumbering="Rolling" />
  </targets>
  <rules>
    <logger name="*" minlevel="Error" writeTo="file" />
  </rules>
</nlog>

```

# Proxy
The portal includes a simple non caching proxy. Its main purpose is to ease integration of external vector based map services (eg. WFS) which do not support CORS. The configuration has been enhanced in this release to be more flexible with regards to headers.
## Important note[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/web.config-file/Proxy.html#important-note)
When using NetWorks together with OpenID Connect the Admin Console will add a number of entries to the `<proxyUrls>` section. These should _not_ be modified.
## Basic setup[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/web.config-file/Proxy.html#basic-setup)
To setup a proxy requires you to add an entry to the `<proxyUrls>` section of the [web.config](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/web.config-file.html) file eg.

```
<configuration>
…
   <webGIS>
      …
      <proxyUrls>
         <add name="myproxy" path="https://remote.domain.com/mapservice" />
      </proxyUrls>
      … 
   </webGIS>

```

It is then possible to make a call to the portal instance e.g.

```
http(s)://my.domain.com/nwportal/proxy/myproxy

```

And this will be forwarded to the remote service. It is also possible to append path and query string information to the call i.e.

```
http(s)://my.domain.com/nwportal/proxy/myproxy/wfs?request=GetMap&BBOX=1,2,3,4

```

will be forwarded to:

```
https://remote.domain.com/mapservice/wfs?request=GetMap&BBOX=1,2,3,4

```

It also supports all HTTP methods such as POST and DELETE with the exception of PATCH.
## Http headers[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/web.config-file/Proxy.html#http-headers)
By default the proxy does not forward headers from the browser to the specified URL, nor does it return headers from the specified URL. The proxy can however be configured to forward and/or return specific headers by specifying them as a comma separated lists. For example:

```
<proxyUrls>
   <add name="myproxy" path="https://remote.domain.com/" forwardHeaders="if-modified-since, if-none-match" returnHeaders="last-modified, etag"/>
</proxyUrls>

```

The above example allows the browser to make conditional requests and for the remote server to return information allowing the browser to cache responses for it. Specification of header name is not case sensitive.
## Authentication[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/web.config-file/Proxy.html#authentication)
If the portal is configured to use Open ID Connect then it will by default attach an authorization header to the request to the remote server. If this server is an external server, for example, an external WMS server then this may not be desirable and can cause the server to respond with 4xx responses. In these cases you can change the authentication mode for the proxy by adding an authMode attribute to it i.e.

```
<proxyUrls>
   <add name="myproxy" path="https://remote.domain.com/" authMode="Anonymous" />
</proxyUrls>

```

If the proxy is being used to link to a map service then you must also do a similar change to its [map source](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/Map-sources.html) in the workspace.

# system
## system.web/customErrors[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/web.config-file/system.html#systemwebcustomerrors)
By default custom errors is set to `On` and on server errors the user is redirected to a default html page. This is a security measure to prevent potentially sensitive information in error messages and stack traces being published. If you need to view errors for debugging purposes then set custom errors to `RemoteOnly` or `Off`.

```
<customErrors mode="RemoteOnly" defaultRedirect="ServerError.html" />

```

## system.web/httpRuntime[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/web.config-file/system.html#systemwebhttpruntime)
To allow upload of files larger than the default limit (~4MB), set the `maxRequestLength` of the `<httpRuntime>` element.
Example

```
<httpRuntime targetFramework="4.8" maxQueryStringLength="32768" maxUrlLength="65536" requestValidationMode="2.0" maxRequestLength="30000000" />

```

### system.web/machineKey[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/web.config-file/system.html#systemwebmachinekey)
When multiple Portal instances are deployed behind a load balancer and OpenID Connect authentication is used, all instances must have configured the same decryption and validation keys. Use standard IIS management tools to generate the keys on one machine and then copy the keys to other instances.
Example

```
<system.web>
  <!-- other content -->
  <machineKey 
    decryption="AES" 
    decryptionKey="6F2174308B8356EF57AE57350AFB3160C1C30CA346101814" 
    validation="HMACSHA256"
    validationKey="D0BB06DE510F1CBA1F54FB7133485E62DB856C908014EDA7619784A781BAABFE1EABF019E0D76B6A23A8EB52B02ABFE104307691BA3FBA82340F81B559422141" 
  />
</system.web>

```

# Transforms
## Overview[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/web.config-file/Transforms.html#overview)
To parse data from external services the portal uses various transform documents to transform content into something the portal can read. For example this is the case for WMS GetFeatureInfo results.
## Adding transform documents[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/web.config-file/Transforms.html#adding-transform-documents)
It is recommended that if you add transform documents to the portal that you do so in a sub directory under the portals `App_GlobalResources\Transforms` directory. To register the transform document with the portal you must then add an entry in the [web.config](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/web.config-file.html) file under the `/configuration/webGIS/transforms` section. It is recommended you prefix your name to prevent clashes with updates in future Networks releases. For example.

```
<configuration>
...
   <webGIS>
   ...
      <transforms>
      ...
         <add name="custom-wmsFeatureInfo1" path="App_GlobalResources\Transforms\Custom\wmsFeatureInfo.xslt" />

```

You can then refer to your new transform in the workspace. For example.

```
<WMSSource name="wms1" username="WMS 1">
   <FeatureInfoTransform>custom-wmsFeatureInfo1</FeatureInfoTransform>
</WMSSource>

```

# webGIS
## Overview[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/web.config-file/webGIS.html#overview)
This section is used to define various settings required by the Portal services. By default this section is pre-configured by the deployment tools. Under this section is configured
  * Various attributes. See below
  * `<applicationBaseUrl>` - The application base URL. See below.
  * `<clients>` - The location of the portal HTML template. This should note be changed.
  * `<printFiles>` - Print process file locations and configuration. This should not be changed.
  * [`<proxyUrls>`](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/web.config-file/Proxy.html)
  * [`<publishedClaims>`](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/web.config-file/Authentication.html)
  * `<services>` - Portal service endpoints. This should not be changed.
  * [`<transforms>`](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/web.config-file/Transforms.html)
  * [`<workspaceFolders>`](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/web.config-file/Workspaces.html)

## Attributes[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/web.config-file/webGIS.html#attributes)
Various attributes can be defined on the `<webGIS>` element, they are all optional. The print process [control](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Print/Controlling-print-processes.html) parameters are defined here.
In addition there is the `cacheExpiration` attribute, this defines how long some metadata is cached on the Portal server in minutes. If OIDC is being used then it must be set to 0 otherwise it is possible that some users can receive incorrect _metadata_. Even if OIDC is not being used then it is recommended that it is set to 0. The mechanism that this parameter controls is being replaced by caching directly by NetWorks services and by more advanced client caching so its usage is deprecated.
## Application base URL[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/web.config-file/webGIS.html#application-base-url)
This is used to resolve relative URLs to absolute URLs. It should be a valid _absolute_ URL to the portal. For example:

```
   <webGIS>
      <applicationBaseUrl path="https://my.server.com/networksportal" />

```

## NetWorks services URLs[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/web.config-file/webGIS.html#networks-services-urls)
The following is still valid but its usage is **deprecated**. The preferred and recommended approach is to now define service URLs and configuration in the [workspace](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace.html)..
The Coordinate service, NetPlot and NetExport require the attribute GTechConfiguration to be set to a valid GTech configuration name e.g.

```
<webGIS GTechConfiguration="GINIUS">

```

It is also recommended that the path to the solution service and coordinate service is defined.

```
<solutionServiceUrl path="http://server/NetworksSolutionService" />
<coordinateSystemServiceUrl path="http://server/NetworksCoordinateSystemService/" />

```

The solution service is used by the portal to find URLs to the other NetWorks services instead of needing to specify them in the web.config file and/or workspace.
It is however still possible to manually specify URLs to the NetWorks services by omitting the solutionServiceUrl and using the following elements.
  * `<analyticalWebServiceUrl>`
  * `<dialogWebServiceUrl>`
  * `<jobWebServiceUrl>`
  * `<dataTransferServiceUrl>`
  * `<workServiceUrl>`
  * `<dynamicServiceUrl>`

If you are using NetPlot and NetExport then URLs to the web services need be specified here e.g.

```
<directPlotServiceUrl path="http://server/NetPlot" />
<directExportServiceUrl path="http://server/NetExportWS" />

```

# Workspaces
## Overview[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/web.config-file/Workspaces.html#overview)
It is required to link a portal to at least one workspace. This can be done by defining one or more folders for the portal to load workspace xml files from _or_ one of more workspace files. The default and recommended way is to define folders.
##### Note
If you define both folders and files then the files will be ignored.
## Defining folders[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/web.config-file/Workspaces.html#defining-folders)
Workspace locations are defined by the following sub section:

```
<configuration>
…
   <webGIS>
      …
      <workspaceFolders>
         <add name="default" path="%ProgramData%\Intergraph\NetWorks\Portal\Nwportal" />
      </workspaceFolders>

```

The name attribute is used by [deployment customization files](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Administration-Console/Deployment-customization/Customization-file-syntax.html) and should only contain printable characters. The path attribute must be a valid _folder_ path. The path can be relative to the file location of the web.config file. Path segments which start and end with the '%' character will be interpreted as environment variables and will be replaced by the value of the variable. You can specify multiple folders by adding more  elements in which case the name attribute must be unique for each element.
## Defining files[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/web.config-file/Workspaces.html#defining-files)
Workspace files are defined by the following sub section::

```
<configuration>
…
   <webGIS>   
      …
      <workspaces>
        <add name="default" path="App_GlobalResources\Workspaces\default.xml" />
        <add name="primary" path="App_GlobalResources\Workspaces\primary.xml" />
      </workspaces>
   </webGIS>

```

The name attribute is used by [deployment customization files](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Administration-Console/Deployment-customization/Customization-file-syntax.html) and should only contain printable characters. The path attribute must be a valid _file_ path. The path can be relative to the file location of the [web.config](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/web.config-file.html) file. Path segments which start and end with the `%` character will be interpreted as environment variables and will be replaced by the value of the variable. You can specify multiple folders by adding more `<add>` elements in which case the name attribute must be unique for each element.

# web.config file
## Overview[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/web.config-file.html#overview)
The web.config file is a standard ASP.NET configuration file. It is used to configure various server and application settings. See:
  * [appSettings and connectionStrings](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/web.config-file/appSettings-and-connectionStrings.html)
  * [Authentication](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/web.config-file/Authentication.html)
  * [Localized files](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/web.config-file/Localized-files.html)
  * [Logging](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/web.config-file/Logging.html)
  * [Proxy](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/web.config-file/Proxy.html)
  * [system](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/web.config-file/system.html)
  * [Transforms](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/web.config-file/Transforms.html)
  * [webGIS](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/web.config-file/webGIS.html)
  * [Workspaces](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/web.config-file/Workspaces.html)

See also:
  * [Controlling print processes](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Print/Controlling-print-processes.html)

# Bing maps source
## Specifying a Bing Maps source[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/Bing-maps-source.html#specifying-a-bing-maps-source)
To add a Bing maps source use the following.

```
<Section type="mapsource">
   … 
    <BingSource name="bing_roads" username="Roads">
      <Key>abcdefg...</Key>
      <ImagerySet>RoadOnDemand</ImagerySet>
      <Hidpi>true</Hidpi>
      <MaxZoom>19</MaxZoom>
      <Print_MaxZoom>21</Print_MaxZoom>
    </BingSource>

```

It can then be added to a legend as normal eg.

```
<Section type="maplegend">
   <Legend name="mylegend" username="My Legend">
      <SourceEntry>
        <SourceName>bing_roads</SourceName>
        <Group>Basemap</Group>
      </SourceEntry>

```

## BingSource properties[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/Bing-maps-source.html#bingsource-properties)  
| Name  | Required  | Remarks  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| Key  | Y  | Should be set to your BingMaps API key.  |  
| ImagerySet  | Y  | Imagery set. Allowed values: `RoadOnDemand`, `Aerial`, `AerialWithLabelsOnDemand`, `CanvasDark`, `CanvasLight`, `CanvasGray`.  |  
| Hidpi  |   | When `true`, high resolution tiles are requested. Default is `false`.  |  
| MaxZoom  |   | Maximum zoom level to request from server.  |  
| Print_MaxZoom  |   | Maximum zoom level to request from server when using Print function. Set this value to avoid blank map when printing maps at small scales, which exceed the resolutions provided by Bing Maps. Default is 19.  |

###### External-queries

# Example 1 - URL query with attribute parameters
## URL query with attribute parameters[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/External-queries/Example-1---URL-query-with-attribute-parameters.html#url-query-with-attribute-parameters)
The following is a real example based on an official address search service for Denmark which returns results as a GeoJSON feature collection. Note the parameter names and how they are specified in the URL. Note also in the URL we are specifying a projection for the result i.e. `srid=25832`, and therefore specifying the  of the data. It is recommended that a `<Projection>` is always provided.
Note this service also can dynamically compress the result, the portal can accept either `gzip` or `deflate` encodings therefore the `Accept-Encoding` request header is specified.

```
<HttpQuery name="externQuery1" username="Address search 1">
	<Url><![CDATA[https://dawa.aws.dk/adgangsadresser?q={searchText}&format=geojson&struktur=mini&srid=25832&fuzzy=true&kommunekode={kommuneKode}]]></Url>
	<RequestHeaders>
		<Header key="Accept-Encoding">gzip, deflate</Header>
	</RequestHeaders>
	<ResponseType>JSON</ResponseType>
	<Parameters>
		<Text>
			<Name>searchText</Name>
			<UserName>Adresse</UserName>
			<Required>true</Required>
			<MinLength>3</MinLength>
			<MaxLength>50</MaxLength>
		</Text>
		<Picklist>
			<Name>kommuneKode</Name>
			<UserName>Kommune</UserName>
			<Required>true</Required>
			<Options>
				<Option>
					<Key>0101</Key>
					<Value>København</Value>
				</Option>
				<Option>
					<Key>0147</Key>
					<Value>Frederiksberg</Value>
				</Option>
				<Option>
					<Key>0151</Key>
					<Value>Ballerup</Value>
				</Option>
			</Options>
		</Picklist>
	</Parameters>
        <Projection>EPSG:25832</Projection>
	<EnableTooltips>true</EnableTooltips>
	<FeatureUserNameFormatString>{betegnelse}</FeatureUserNameFormatString>
</HttpQuery>

```

# Example 2 - URL based query with geometry parameter
## URL based query with geometry parameter[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/External-queries/Example-2---URL-based-query-with-geometry-parameter.html#url-based-query-with-geometry-parameter)
This is similar to [Example 1](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/External-queries/Example-1---URL-query-with-attribute-parameters.html) however we are using a geometry field parameter. Note here that we are specifying a `<Projection>` for the resulting geometry and also the geometry parameter. They do not necessarily need to be the same, it depends on the service.
Drawing a polygon outside of the Danish borders will likely result in an error.

```
<HttpQuery name="externQuery2" username="Address search 2">
	<Url><![CDATA[https://dawa.aws.dk/adgangsadresser?polygon=[[{polygon}]]&format=geojson&struktur=mini]]></Url>
	<RequestHeaders>
		<Header key="Accept-Encoding">gzip, deflate</Header>
	</RequestHeaders>
	<ResponseType>JSON</ResponseType>
	<Projection>EPSG:4326</Projection>
	<Parameters>
		<Geometry>
			<Name>polygon</Name>
			<UserName>Draw polygon</UserName>
			<Required>true</Required>
			<GeometryType>Polygon</GeometryType>
			<Projection>EPSG:4326</Projection>
			<CoordinateFormatString>[{0},{1}]</CoordinateFormatString>
			<CoordinateSeparator>,</CoordinateSeparator>
		</Geometry>
	</Parameters>
	<EnableTooltips>true</EnableTooltips>
	<FeatureUserNameFormatString>{betegnelse}</FeatureUserNameFormatString>
</HttpQuery> 

```

# Example 3 - External WFS based query
## External WFS based query[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/External-queries/Example-3---External-WFS-based-query.html#external-wfs-based-query)
This example is using a geoserver based WFS service which returns various administrative areas for Denmark. Note the `Content-Type` request header is set as a `<RequestBody>` is being used. Also note that it is using a `<ResponseTransform>` to convert the GML response to which is returned into a GeoJSON feature collection. This is required to be registered with the portal. The contents of the transform are provided below.

```
<HttpQuery name="externQuery3" username="Lokal plan">
	<Url>https://geoserverpreprod.plandata.dk/geoserver/wfs</Url>
	<RequestBody><![CDATA[
<wfs:GetFeature xmlns:wfs="http://www.opengis.net/wfs/2.0" xmlns:fes="http://www.opengis.net/fes/2.0" xmlns:gml="http://www.opengis.net/gml/3.2" xmlns:pdk="http://www.plansystemdk.dk" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" service="WFS" version="2.0.0" xsi:schemaLocation="http://www.opengis.net/wfs/2.0 http://schemas.opengis.net/wfs/2.0/wfs.xsd http://www.opengis.net/gml/3.2 http://schemas.opengis.net/gml/3.2.1/gml.xsd">
<wfs:Query typeNames="pdk:theme_pdk_lokalplan_vedtaget_v">
<fes:Filter>
<fes:Intersects>
  <fes:ValueReference>geometri</fes:ValueReference>
  <gml:Polygon  gml:id="polygon.1" srsName="urn:ogc:def:crs:EPSG::25832">
	<gml:exterior>
	  <gml:LinearRing>
		<gml:posList>
			{polygon}
		</gml:posList>
	  </gml:LinearRing>
	</gml:exterior>
  </gml:Polygon>
</fes:Intersects>
</fes:Filter>
</wfs:Query>
</wfs:GetFeature>            
	]]></RequestBody>
	<RequestHeaders>
		<Header key="Accept-Encoding">gzip, deflate</Header>
		<Header key="Content-Type">application/xml</Header>
	</RequestHeaders>
	<ResponseType>XML</ResponseType>
	<ResponseTransform>lokalPlan</ResponseTransform>
        <Projection>EPSG:25832</Projection>
	<Parameters>
		<Geometry>
			<Name>polygon</Name>
			<UserName>Draw polygon</UserName>
			<Required>true</Required>
			<GeometryType>Polygon</GeometryType>
			<CoordinateFormatString>{0} {1}</CoordinateFormatString>
                        <Projection>EPSG:25832</Projection>
		</Geometry>
	</Parameters>
</HttpQuery>

```

## lokalPlan.xslt[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/External-queries/Example-3---External-WFS-based-query.html#lokalplanxslt)

```
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<xsl:stylesheet version="1.0" xmlns:xsl="http://www.w3.org/1999/XSL/Transform"
                xmlns:pdk="http://www.plansystemdk.dk"
                xmlns:wfs="http://www.opengis.net/wfs/2.0"
                xmlns:gml="http://www.opengis.net/gml/3.2">
    <xsl:output method="xml"/>
    <xsl:template match="/">
        <FeatureCollection>
            <Type>FeatureCollection</Type>
            <Features>
                <xsl:apply-templates select="descendant::wfs:member/pdk:theme_pdk_lokalplan_vedtaget_v" />
            </Features>
        </FeatureCollection>
    </xsl:template>
    <xsl:template match="pdk:theme_pdk_lokalplan_vedtaget_v">
        <Feature>
            <TypeName>Feature</TypeName>
            <UserName>Lokalplan Vedtaget <xsl:value-of select="pdk:planid"/></UserName>
            <Properties>
                <item>
                    <xsl:attribute name="key">Plan id</xsl:attribute>
                    <xsl:value-of select="pdk:planid" />
                </item>
                <item>
                    <xsl:attribute name="key">Plan nr</xsl:attribute>
                    <xsl:value-of select="pdk:plannr" />
                </item>
                <item>
                    <xsl:attribute name="key">Plan navn</xsl:attribute>
                    <xsl:value-of select="pdk:plannavn" />
                </item>
                <item>
                    <xsl:attribute name="key">Dato vedtaget</xsl:attribute>
                    <xsl:value-of select="pdk:datovedt" />
                </item>
                <item>
                    <xsl:attribute name="key">Link</xsl:attribute>
                    <xsl:value-of select="pdk:doklink"/>
                </item>
            </Properties>
            <Geometry>
                <xsl:apply-templates select="pdk:geometri/gml:MultiSurface" />
            </Geometry>
        </Feature>
    </xsl:template>
    <xsl:template match="gml:MultiSurface">
        <MultiPolygon>
            <Coordinates>
                <xsl:for-each select="descendant::gml:Polygon">
                    <Coordinates>
                        <xsl:apply-templates select="gml:outerBoundaryIs | gml:exterior"/>
                    </Coordinates>
                </xsl:for-each>
            </Coordinates>
        </MultiPolygon>
    </xsl:template>
    <xsl:template match="gml:Polygon">
        <Polygon>
            <Coordinates>
                <xsl:apply-templates select="gml:outerBoundaryIs | gml:exterior"/>
            </Coordinates>
        </Polygon>
    </xsl:template>
    <xsl:template match="gml:outerBoundaryIs | gml:exterior">
        <xsl:if test="gml:LinearRing">
            <xsl:for-each select="gml:LinearRing">
                <Coordinates>
                    <xsl:apply-templates select="gml:posList|gml:coordinates"/>
                </Coordinates>
            </xsl:for-each>
        </xsl:if>
        <xsl:if test="gml:Ring">
            <xsl:for-each select="gml:Ring">
                <Coordinates>
                    <xsl:for-each select="gml:curveMember">
                        <xsl:apply-templates select="gml:posList|gml:coordinates"/>
                    </xsl:for-each>
                </Coordinates>
            </xsl:for-each>
        </xsl:if>
    </xsl:template>
    <xsl:template match="gml:MultiCurve | gml:MultiLineString">
        <MultiLineString>
            <Coordinates>
                <xsl:for-each select="descendant::gml:LineString|descendant::gml:Curve|descendant::gml:Arc">
                    <Coordinates>
                        <xsl:apply-templates select="descendant::gml:posList|descendant::gml:coordinates"/>
                    </Coordinates>
                </xsl:for-each>
            </Coordinates>
        </MultiLineString>
    </xsl:template>
    <xsl:template match="gml:LineString | gml:Curve | gml:Arc">
        <LineString>
            <Coordinates>
                <xsl:apply-templates select="descendant::gml:posList|descendant::gml:coordinates"/>
            </Coordinates>
        </LineString>
    </xsl:template>
    <xsl:template match="gml:Point">
        <Point>
            <Coordinates>
                <xsl:apply-templates select="gml:pos|gml:coordinates"/>
            </Coordinates>
        </Point>
    </xsl:template>
    <xsl:template match="gml:coordinates">
        <xsl:call-template name="encodeCoordinates">
            <xsl:with-param name="coords" select="." />
            <xsl:with-param name="decimal" select="@decimal" />
            <xsl:with-param name="cs" select="@cs" />
            <xsl:with-param name="ts" select="@ts" />
        </xsl:call-template>
    </xsl:template>
    <xsl:template match="gml:posList">
        <xsl:call-template name="encodeCoordinates">
            <xsl:with-param name="coords" select="." />
            <xsl:with-param name="decimal" select="'.'" />
            <xsl:with-param name="cs" select="' '" />
            <xsl:with-param name="ts" select="' '" />
        </xsl:call-template>
    </xsl:template>
    <xsl:template match="gml:pos">
        <xsl:call-template name="encodeCoordinates">
            <xsl:with-param name="coords" select="." />
            <xsl:with-param name="decimal" select="'.'" />
            <xsl:with-param name="cs" select="' '" />
            <xsl:with-param name="ts" select="' '" />
        </xsl:call-template>
    </xsl:template>
    <xsl:template name="encodeCoordinates">
        <xsl:param name="coords" />
        <xsl:param name="decimal" select="'.'" />
        <xsl:param name="cs" select="','"/>
        <xsl:param name="ts" select="' '"/>
        <xsl:variable name="X" select="substring-before($coords, $cs)" />
        <xsl:if test="$X">
            <xsl:variable name="tmp" select="substring-after($coords, concat($X, $cs))" />
            <xsl:variable name="Y" select="substring-before(concat($tmp, $ts), $ts)" />
            <coord>
                <xsl:value-of select="concat(translate($X,$decimal,'.'), ',', translate($Y,$decimal,'.'))" />
            </coord>
            <xsl:call-template name="encodeCoordinates">
                <xsl:with-param name="coords" select="substring-after($tmp, concat($Y, $ts))" />
                <xsl:with-param name="decimal" select="$decimal" />
                <xsl:with-param name="cs" select="$cs" />
                <xsl:with-param name="ts" select="$ts" />
            </xsl:call-template>
        </xsl:if>
    </xsl:template>
</xsl:stylesheet>

```

## web.config[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/External-queries/Example-3---External-WFS-based-query.html#webconfig)

```
<webGIS>
   ...
   <transforms>
      ...
      <add name="lokalPlan" path="App_GlobalResources\Transforms\lokalPlan.xslt" />
   </transforms>

```

# Example 4 - Internal WFS based query
## Internal WFS based query[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/External-queries/Example-4---Internal-WFS-based-query.html#internal-wfs-based-query)
It is also possible to use NetWorks WFS services in the same way as external WFS services and in this way use them to run simple, ad-hoc spatial and/or attribute queries. Note that this example also uses a `<ResponseTransform>` however, this is registered in the portal by default. Note also if you are using OIDC with the WFS service then you will need to use the proxy to access the service as shown.

```
<HttpQuery name="externQuery4" username="Stations">
   <Url>proxy/networks/WfsElectricGINIUSANON/wfs</Url>
   <RequestBody><![CDATA[
      <GetFeature xmlns="http://www.opengis.net/wfs" service="WFS" version="1.1.0" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xsi:schemaLocation="http://www.opengis.net/wfs http://schemas.opengis.net/wfs/1.1.0/wfs.xsd">
         <Query typeName="ucgml:V_E_STATIO_32300_I_PT" srsName="EPSG:5678" xmlns:ucgml="http://www.intergraph.com/infrastructure/gml" xmlns:gml="http://www.opengis.net/gml">
            <Filter xmlns="http://www.opengis.net/ogc">
               <Within>
                  <PropertyName>G3E_GEOMETRY</PropertyName>
                  <gml:Polygon srsName="EPSG:5678"><gml:exterior><gml:LinearRing><gml:posList srsDimension="2">{polygon}</gml:posList></gml:LinearRing></gml:exterior></gml:Polygon>
               </Within>
            </Filter>
         </Query>
      </GetFeature>
   ]]></RequestBody>
   <RequestHeaders>
      <Header key="Content-Type">application/xml</Header>
   </RequestHeaders>
   <ResponseType>XML</ResponseType>
   <ResponseTransform>networksFeatureCollection</ResponseTransform>
   <Projection>EPSG:5678</Projection>
   <EditorName>networksEditor</EditorName>
   <EnableTooltips>true</EnableTooltips>
   <FeatureUserNameFormatString>{ToolTip}</FeatureUserNameFormatString>
   <Parameters>
      <Geometry>
         <Name>polygon</Name>
         <UserName>Draw polygon</UserName>
         <Required>true</Required>
         <GeometryType>Polygon</GeometryType>
         <CoordinateFormatString>{0} {1}</CoordinateFormatString>
         <Projection>EPSG:5678</Projection>
      </Geometry>
    </Parameters>
</HttpQuery>

```

# Example 5 - Transforming JSON result
## Transforming JSON result[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/External-queries/Example-5---Transforming-JSON-result.html#transforming-json-result)
This example is based on another Danish service that returns cadastral areas but not as a GeoJSON feature collection so it needs transformation.

```
<HttpQuery name="externQuery5" username="Cadastre Search">
	<Url><![CDATA[https://api.dataforsyningen.dk/jordstykker?q={searchText}&kommunekode={kommuneKode}&struktur=mini]]></Url>
	<ResponseType>JSONXML</ResponseType>
	<ResponseTransform>cadastreSearch</ResponseTransform>
	<Projection>EPSG:4326</Projection>
	<Parameters>
		<Text>
			<Name>searchText</Name>
			<UserName>Search value</UserName>
			<Required>true</Required>
			<MaxLength>100</MaxLength>
		</Text>
		<Picklist>
			<Name>kommuneKode</Name>
			<UserName>Kommune</UserName>
			<Required>true</Required>
			<Options>
				<Option>
					<Key>0101</Key>
					<Value>København</Value>
				</Option>
				<Option>
					<Key>0147</Key>
					<Value>Frederiksberg</Value>
				</Option>
				<Option>
					<Key>0151</Key>
					<Value>Ballerup</Value>
				</Option>
			</Options>
		</Picklist>
	</Parameters>    
	<EnableTooltips>true</EnableTooltips>
	<FeatureUserNameFormatString>{Tooltip}</FeatureUserNameFormatString>     
</HttpQuery>

```

## cadastreSearch.xslt[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/External-queries/Example-5---Transforming-JSON-result.html#cadastresearchxslt)

```
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<xsl:stylesheet version="1.0" xmlns:xsl="http://www.w3.org/1999/XSL/Transform">
    <xsl:strip-space elements="wkt"/>
    <xsl:template match="/">
        <FeatureCollection>
            <Type>FeatureCollection</Type>
            <Features>
                <xsl:apply-templates select="root/rootObject" />
            </Features>
        </FeatureCollection>
    </xsl:template>
    <xsl:template match="rootObject">
        <Feature>
            <UserName><xsl:value-of select="betegnelse" /></UserName>
            <Properties>
                <Property key="Matrikel Nr."><xsl:value-of select="matrikelnr" /></Property>
                <Property key="Ejerlav"><xsl:value-of select="ejerlavnavn" /> (<xsl:value-of select="ejerlavkode" />)</Property>
                <Property key="Tooltip"><xsl:value-of select="betegnelse" /></Property>
                <Property key="Link"><xsl:value-of select="href" /></Property>
            </Properties>
            <Geometry>
                <Point>
                    <Coordinates>
                       <xsl:value-of select="visueltcenter_x" />,<xsl:value-of select="visueltcenter_y" />
                    </Coordinates>
                </Point>
            </Geometry>
        </Feature>
    </xsl:template>
</xsl:stylesheet>

```

```
<webGIS>
   ...
   <transforms>
      ...
      <add name="cadastreSearch" path="App_GlobalResources\Transforms\cadastreSearch.xslt" />
   </transforms>

```

# External queries
## Overview[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/External-queries.html#overview)
The portal can support external queries from services accessible via HTTP(S) GET and POST requests and that return results as a GeoJSON feature collection or JSON/XML formats which can be transformed via XSLT into a GeoJSON feature collection, such as WFS services. Currently the portal does not support reading of paged results so the maximum size of the result set is limited to how many items the service can return in a single request.
## Defining an external query[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/External-queries.html#defining-an-external-query)
External queries must be defined in a section with the type set to `query`. Currently only one type of query is supported that is `<HttpQuery>`. For example:

```
    <Section type="query">
        <HttpQuery name="externQuery1" username="Address search 1">
            <Url><![CDATA[https://dawa.aws.dk/adgangsadresser?q={searchText}&format=geojson&struktur=mini&srid=25832&fuzzy=true]]></Url>
            <RequestHeaders>
                <Header key="Accept-Encoding">gzip, deflate</Header>
            </RequestHeaders>
            <ResponseType>JSON</ResponseType>
            <Projection>EPSG:25832</Projection>
            <Parameters>
                <Text>
                    <Name>searchText</Name>
                    <UserName>Adresse</UserName>
                    <Required>true</Required>
                    <MinLength>3</MinLength>
                    <MaxLength>50</MaxLength>
                </Text>
            </Parameters>
        </HttpQuery>
    </Section>

```

This example shows a simple GET query. When selected by the user they are shown a single field with the label `Adresse`. When the query is executed the value of the field is sent to the portal service with the name, `searchText`. The value is then substituted into the Url by replacing the text in curly brackets containing the name, 'searchText'. The value is formatted as defined by configuration on the parameters.
Like all configuration items the `HttpQuery` must have a name attribute which is unique from all other `HttpQuery` elements. It must also define a username attribute which is displayed to the user in the query dialog. In addition to these attributes the following elements can be defined.  
| Name  | Required  | Remarks  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| Url  | Y  | The full URL to the service. It is recommended that this value is contained within a CDATA tag.  |  
| AuthMode  | N  | If OIDC is enabled then set this to 'Anonymous' to prevent the an authorization header being sent with the request.  |  
| RequestBody  | N  | The POST body to be sent with the request. This should be specified within a CDATA tag.  |  
| RequestHeaders  | N  | Additional HTTP request headers to send with the request. Each header should be specified as a separate  element with a key attribute defined which is the header name. The value of the element is the header value.  |  
| ResponseType  | Y  | The type of the response. This can be JSON, XML or JSONXML (see below). If the service does not return GeoJSON directly then the result must be transformed.  |  
| ResponseTransform  | N  | The name of the transform as specified in the web.config file used to convert the result into GeoJSON.  |  
| EnableTooltips  | N  | If the results are added to the legend set this to True to enable tooltips for features in the results. Default if false. If this is set to true then remember to set FeatureUserNameFormatString.  |  
| FeatureNameFormatString  | N  | Can be used by extensions to the portal to differentiate between features coming from the source.  |  
| FeatureUserNameFormatString  | N  | Can be used to control the text being displayed in the feature selection panel and tooltips.  |  
| EditorName  | N  | If the resulting feature contains valid G3E_FNO and G3E_FID properties then setting this to a valid editor configuration will open the feature using the feature editor.  |  
| Projection  | N  | EPSG code specifying the projection in which geometry are returned in. If not specified it is assumed that they are returned in the maps projection.  |  
| Culture  | N  | Culture used when formatting numeric, date time field values and coordinate values into the Url or RequestBody. If not specified then the 'invariant' culture is used. Should be specified as a .NET culture name e.g. en-US, en-GB or fr-FR.  |  
NOTE if you specify a `<Projection>` then ensure that it is also defined in [coordsys.json](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/coordsys.json.html). If you specify a `<ResponseTransform>` then ensure that it is [registered](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/web.config-file/Transforms.html) with the portal.
## Defining a query with a POST body[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/External-queries.html#defining-a-query-with-a-post-body)
In addition to sending simple parameters via URLs it is also possible to send more complex parameters by specifying a POST body. For example:

```
   <HttpQuery name="externQuery4" username="Stations">
      <Url>proxy/networks/WfsElectricGINIUSANON/wfs</Url>
      <RequestBody><![CDATA[
        <GetFeature xmlns="http://www.opengis.net/wfs" service="WFS" version="1.1.0" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xsi:schemaLocation="http://www.opengis.net/wfs http://schemas.opengis.net/wfs/1.1.0/wfs.xsd">
            <Query typeName="ucgml:V_E_STATIO_32300_I_PT" srsName="EPSG:5678" xmlns:ucgml="http://www.intergraph.com/infrastructure/gml" xmlns:gml="http://www.opengis.net/gml">
                <Filter xmlns="http://www.opengis.net/ogc">
                <Within>
                   <PropertyName>G3E_GEOMETRY</PropertyName>
                   <gml:Polygon srsName="EPSG:5678"><gml:exterior><gml:LinearRing><gml:posList srsDimension="2">{polygon}</gml:posList></gml:LinearRing></gml:exterior></gml:Polygon>
                </Within>
                </Filter>
            </Query>
        </GetFeature>
      ]]></RequestBody>
      <RequestHeaders>
         <Header key="Content-Type">application/xml</Header>
      </RequestHeaders>
      ...
   </HttpQuery>

```

Note that when specifying a `<RequestBody>` the bodies mime type should also typically be provided in the request header `Content-Type`. Often used mime types are `application/json`, `application/xml` and `application/x-form-urlencoded`. Note that its not possible to send content of the type `multipart/form-data`.
## Defining parameters[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/External-queries.html#defining-parameters)
There can be defined the following types of parameter.
  * Text
  * Number
  * DateTime
  * Picklist
  * Geometry

Parameters are defined using elements containing one of the above texts.
Common to all parameters types are the following elements.  
| Name  | Required  | Remarks  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| Name  | Y  | The name to be replaced in the query Url or RequestBody. Value must not contain curly bracets.  |  
| UserName  | Y  | Label displayed in the query dialog next to the field.  |  
| Required  | N  | Set to 'true' if the parameter is required. Default is 'false'.  |  
### [](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/External-queries.html#section)  
| Name  | Required  | Remarks  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| MinLength  | N  | Minimum number of characters that must be entered in the field.  |  
| MaxLength  | N  | Maximum number of characters that can be entered.  |  
### [](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/External-queries.html#section-1)  
| Name  | Required  | Remarks  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| MinValue  | N  | Lowest value that can be entered in the field.  |  
| MaxValue  | N  | Highest value that can be entered in the field.  |  
| DecimalPlaces  | N  | Number of decimal places that the entered number will be rounded too. Default is zero.  |  
### [](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/External-queries.html#section-2)  
| Name  | Required  | Remarks  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| MinValue  | N  | Lowest value that can be entered in the field. Should be specified as an ISO date time.  |  
| MaxValue  | N  | Highest value that can be entered in the field. Should be specified as an ISO date time.  |  
| Format  | N  | A .NET style format string. By default dates are formatted as ISO date time strings. See <https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/standard/base-types/formatting-types> for more information.  |  
###  `<Picklist>`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/External-queries.html#picklist)  
| Name  | Required  | Remarks  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| Options  | Y  | List of picklist options.  |  
Picklist options should be specified as follows:

```
   <Picklist>
      <Name>kommuneKode</Name>
      <UserName>Kommune</UserName>
      <Required>true</Required>
      <Options>
         <Option>
            <Key>0101</Key>
            <Value>København</Value>
         </Option>
         <Option>
            <Key>0147</Key>
            <Value>Frederiksberg</Value>
         </Option>
         <Option>
            <Key>0151</Key>
            <Value>Ballerup</Value>
         </Option>

```

Where _key_ is the value to be substituted into the Url or RequestBody and _value_ is what is shown to the user.
###  `<Geometry>`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/External-queries.html#geometry)  
| Name  | Required  | Remarks  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| GeometryType  | Y  | The type of geometry. Can be Point, Polyline or Polygon.  |  
| CoordinateFormatString  | N  | Format string used to write each coordinate. Default is "{0},{1}" where {0} is X or longtitude and {1} is Y or latitude.  |  
| CoordinateSeparator  | N  | The character used to separate each coordinate. Default is _space_.  |  
| Projection  | N  | The projection the coordinate should be written in as an EPSG code. If not supplied coordinate will be written in the maps coordinate system.  |  
Typical coordinate formats and separators are
  * WKT

```
    <CoordinateFormatString>{0} {1}</CoordinateFormatString>
    <CoordinateSeparator>,</CoordinateSeparator>

```

  * GeoJSON

```
    <CoordinateFormatString>[{0},{1}]</CoordinateFormatString>
    <CoordinateSeparator>,</CoordinateSeparator>

```

  * GML v2

```
    <CoordinateFormatString>{0},{1}</CoordinateFormatString>
    <CoordinateSeparator> </CoordinateSeparator>

```

  * GML v3

```
    <CoordinateFormatString>{0} {1}</CoordinateFormatString>
    <CoordinateSeparator> </CoordinateSeparator>

```

If the query uses geographic coordinates in longitude, latitude (yx) order then in the coordinate format swap the order e.g. `{1},{0}`.
Note if you specify a `<Projection>` then ensure that it is also defined in [coordsys.json](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/coordsys.json.html).
### Example[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/External-queries.html#example)

```
        <HttpQuery name="externQuery2" username="Non functional fields example">
            <Url><![CDATA[http://localhost/result.xml?text={text}&number={number}&datetime={datetime}&picklist={picklist}&geometry={geometry}]]></Url>
            <ResponseType>XML</ResponseType>
            <Parameters>
                <Text>
                    <Name>text</Name>
                    <UserName>Text field</UserName>
                    <Required>true</Required>
                    <MinLength>3</MinLength>
                    <MaxLength>50</MaxLength>                    
                </Text>
                <Number>
                    <Name>number</Name>
                    <UserName>Number field</UserName>
                    <Required>true</Required>
                    <MinValue>0</MinValue>
                    <MaxValue>1000000</MaxValue>
                    <DecimalPlaces>0</DecimalPlaces>
                </Number>
                <DateTime>
                    <Name>datetime</Name>
                    <UserName>DateTime field</UserName>
                    <Required>true</Required>
                    <MinValue>2000-01-01T00:00:00Z</MinValue>
                    <MaxValue>2100-12-31T11:59:59Z</MaxValue>
                    <Format>MMMM dd, yyyy</Format>
                </DateTime>
                <Picklist>
                    <Name>picklist</Name>
                    <UserName>Picklist Field</UserName>
                    <Options>
                        <Option>
                            <Key>1</Key>
                            <Value>Foo</Value>
                        </Option>
                        <Option>
                            <Key>2</Key>
                            <Value>Bar</Value>
                        </Option>
                    </Options>
                </Picklist>
                <Geometry>
                    <Name>geometry</Name>
                    <UserName>Draw polygon</UserName>					
                    <Required>true</Required>
                    <GeometryType>Polygon</GeometryType>
                    <Projection>EPSG:4326</Projection>
		    <CoordinateFormatString>[{0},{1}]</CoordinateFormatString>
		    <CoordinateSeparator>,</CoordinateSeparator>
                </Geometry>
            </Parameters>
        </HttpQuery>

```

## Transforming XML and JSON results[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/External-queries.html#transforming-xml-and-json-results)
For services that do not return the result as a GeoJSON feature collection the result must be transformed into one before it can be used by the portal.
An example of parsing a GML result returned by a WFS service is provided [here](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/External-queries/Example-3---External-WFS-based-query.html). In addition an xslt transform called `networksFeatureCollection` is included with the portal for use with queries defined on the Networks WFS queries. Transform documents must convert resulting features into the following structure:

```
<FeatureCollection>
   <Type>FeatureCollection</Type>
   <Features>
      <Feature>
         <UserName>feature name</UserName>
         <Properties>
            <Property key="property name">property value</Property>
         </Properties>
	 <Geometry>
            <Point>
               <Coordinates>x,y</Coordinates>
            </Point>
	 </Geometry>
      </Feature>
      <Feature>
         <UserName>feature name</UserName>
         <Properties>
            <Property key="property name">property value</Property>
         </Properties>
	 <Geometry>
            <LineString>
               <Coordinates>
                  <Coordinate>x1,y1</Coordinate>
	          <Coordinate>x2,y2</Coordinate>
               </Coordinates>
            </LineString>
	 </Geometry>
      </Feature>
      <Feature>
         <UserName>feature name</UserName>
         <Properties>
            <Property key="property name">property value</Property>
         </Properties>
	 <Geometry>
            <Polygon>
               <Coordinates>
                  <Coordinates>
                     <Coordinate>x1,y1</Coordinate>
		     <Coordinate>x2,y2</Coordinate>
		     <Coordinate>x3,y3</Coordinate>
		     <Coordinate>x1,y1</Coordinate>
	          </Coordinates>
               </Coordinates>
            </Polygon>
	 </Geometry>
      </Feature>
   </Features>
</FeatureCollection>

```

The  is optional but is used to set the title of the editor in the portal. Coordinates must always be specified `x,y` or `longtitude,latitude`. Decimal places must be represented with a `.` character. Polyline/linestring geometry must always contain a minimum of two coordinates. Polygon geometry must always contain a minimum of four coordinates where the first equals the last. There can only be 0 to 1 geometries per feature.
How to register your own transform documents with the portal is described [here](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/web.config-file/Transforms.html). When defining your HttpQuery element you must then set the following properties, for example:

```
<HttpQuery>
   ...
   <ResponseType>XML</ResponseType>
   <ResponseTransform>yourTransformName</ResponseTransform>
</HttpQuery>

```

In addition to transforming XML formats it is also possible to do the same with JSON results by setting `<ResponseType>` to JSONXML. When JSONXML is set then Newtonsoft.JSON is used to convert the JSON to XML before applying the xslt transform. The root element is always written as `<root>`. Depending on whether the root of the JSON document is an object or an array there will either be one or many `<rootObject>` elements. JSON property names are written as XML elements and property values and as element values. Where the value is an array then the XML element is repeated, for example:

```
{
   items: [
      {
         prop1: 1,
         prop2: "Hello"
      },
      {
         prop1: 2,
         prop2: "Goodbye"
      }
   ]
}

```

Converts to:

```
<root>
   <rootObject>
      <items>
         <prop1>1</prop1>
         <prop2>Hello</prop2>
      </items>
      <items>
         <prop1>2</prop1>
         <prop2>Goodbye</prop2>
      </items>
   <rootObject>
</root>

```

```
[
   {
      "matrikelnr": "106", 
      "bbox": [1,2,3,4], 
      "ejerlav": { 
         "kode": 10051, 
         "navn": "Fredericksberg", 
         "href": "https://api.dataforsyningen.dk/jordstykker/10051/106"
      }
   }, 
   {
      "matrikelnr": "106", 
      "bbox": [1,2,3,4], 
      "ejerlav": {
         "kode": 10051, 
         "navn": "Fredericksberg", 
         "href": "https://api.dataforsyningen.dk/jordstykker/10051/106"
      }
   }
]

```

Converts to:

```
<root>
  <rootObject>
    <matrikelnr>106</matrikelnr>
    <bbox>1</bbox>
    <bbox>2</bbox>
    <bbox>3</bbox>
    <bbox>4</bbox>
    <ejerlav>
      <kode>10051</kode>
      <navn>Fredericksberg</navn>
      <href>https://api.dataforsyningen.dk/jordstykker/10051/106</href>
    </ejerlav>
  </rootObject>
  <rootObject>
    <matrikelnr>106</matrikelnr>
    <bbox>1</bbox>
    <bbox>2</bbox>
    <bbox>3</bbox>
    <bbox>4</bbox>
    <ejerlav>
      <kode>10051</kode>
      <navn>Fredericksberg</navn>
      <href>https://api.dataforsyningen.dk/jordstykker/10051/106</href>
    </ejerlav>
  </rootObject>
</root>

```

This XML result can then be transformed using an XSLT transform. An example of transforming JSON is provided [here](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/External-queries/Example-5---Transforming-JSON-result.html).

# Feature Editor
## Overview[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/Feature-Editor.html#overview)
In the portal a user can select between one or more 'workspaces'. A workspace defines the configuration for the client. In the workspace you can define one or more legends which contain layers from one or more map sources (eg. a map service or other web resource). Each map source can link to an editor configuration which defines how features selected from that source should be treated.
Currently configuration is limited to GTech features and you can configure:
  * The default dialog type for features that the user has the edit role for.
  * The toolbar for features that the user has the edit role for.
  * The default dialog type for features that the user does not have the edit role for.
  * The toolbar for features that the user does not have the edit role for.
  * The dialog type and toolbars for specific feature types.
  * For a dialog tab whether add and/or delete component is enabled.
  * List of specific tabs for a specific feature type
  * Whether to filter dialog tabs by G3E_FNO.

## Linking a map source to an editor configuration[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/Feature-Editor.html#linking-a-map-source-to-an-editor-configuration)
For any map source you specify the link to an editor configuration by using the  element eg.

```
<Section type="mapsource">
   <MapSourceType name="example">
      ...
      <EditorName>myEditorConfig</EditorName>
   </MapSourceType>
</Section>

```

This will then link to the following editor configuration.

```
<Section type="editor">
   <GtdwsEditor name="myEditorConfig">
   </GtdwsEditor>
</Section>

```

## Specifying whether to filter tabs by G3E_FID[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/Feature-Editor.html#specifying-whether-to-filter-tabs-by-g3e_fid)
By default tabs are _not_ filtered by G3E_FID which can improve performance as it is possible to cache the available tabs for a particular feature type. However if this behaviour is required then add an `<UseDialogFilter>` element and set the value to 'true'.

```
<GtdwsEditor name="myEditorConfig">
   <UseDialogFilter>true</UseDialogFilter>
</GtdwsEditor>

```

When deployed from the Admin Console, this automatically adds this element and sets it to true.
## Specifying the default dialog types and toolbars[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/Feature-Editor.html#specifying-the-default-dialog-types-and-toolbars)
Whether feature attributes can be edited or not is dependent on whether the current user has the edit role for the loaded feature. If they do then the default dialog type is 'Edit' otherwise it is 'Review'. These can be overriden as by specifying `<ReviewConfig>` element or `<EditConfig>` element as follows:

```
<Section type="editor">
   <GtdwsEditor name="myEditorConfig">
      <ReviewConfig>
         <Type>Review</Type>
      </ReviewConfig>
      <EditConfig>
         <Type>Edit</Type>
      </EditConfig>
   </GtdwsEditor>
</Section>

```

You can also redefine the toolbar for the feature editor using the same syntax as `<Function>` elements. For example:

```
<Section type="editor">
    <GtdwsEditor name="myEditorConfig">
        <ReviewConfig>
            <!-- <Type>Review</Type> -->
            <Config>
                <JProperty name="items">
                    <!--Remove edit buttons from menu-->
                    <JArray>
                        <JValue>editorreload</JValue>
                        <JValue>editoropendetails</JValue>
                        <JValue>tbfill</JValue>
                        <JValue>featurefit</JValue>
                        <JValue>close</JValue>
                    </JArray>
                </JProperty>
            </Config>
        </ReviewConfig>
        <EditConfig>
            <!-- <Type>Edit</Type> -->
            <Config>
                <JProperty name="items">
                    <JArray>
                        <JValue>editorreload</JValue>
                        <JValue>editoropendetails</JValue>
                        <JValue>tbfill</JValue>
                        <JValue>editorsaveattributes</JValue>
                        <JValue>editoraddcomponent</JValue>
                        <JValue>editordeletefeature</JValue>
                        <JValue>featurefit</JValue>
                        <JValue>close</JValue>
                    </JArray>
                </JProperty>
            </Config>
        </EditConfig>
    </GtdwsEditor>
</Section>

```

The default list of buttons for the editor toolbar is as follows:

```
<Config>
   <JProperty name="items">
      <JArray>
         <JValue>editorreload</JValue>
         <JValue>editoropendetails</JValue>
         <JValue>tbfill</JValue>
         <JValue>editoreditgeometry</JValue>
         <JValue>editorresetgeometry</JValue>
         <JValue>editorsavegeometry</JValue>
         <JValue>editorsaveattributes</JValue>
         <JValue>editoraddcomponent</JValue>
         <JValue>editordeletefeature</JValue>
         <JValue>featurefit</JValue>
         <JValue>close</JValue>
      </JArray>
   </JProperty>
</Config>

```

## Specifying the dialog types and toolbars for specific feature types[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/Feature-Editor.html#specifying-the-dialog-types-and-toolbars-for-specific-feature-types)
The dialog types and toolbars can be overridden for specific feature types by specifying and `<ReviewConfig>` and/or `<EditConfig>` as follows:

```
<Section type="editor">
    <GtdwsEditor name="myEditorConfig">
        <DialogTypes>
            <DialogType>
                <FNO>306,505</FNO>
                <ReviewConfig>
                    <Config>
                        ...
                    </Config>
                </ReviewConfig>
                <EditConfig>
                    <Config>
                        ...
                    </Config>
                </EditConfig>
            </DialogType>
            <DialogType>
                <FNO>349</FNO>
                <EditConfig>
                    <Type>Review</Type>
                </EditConfig>
            </DialogType>
        </DialogTypes>                
    </GtdwsEditor>
</Section>

```

The FNO element can contain a single G3E_FNO or a comma separated list of FNOs.
## Enabling add and delete component[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/Feature-Editor.html#enabling-add-and-delete-component)
By default add and delete component functions are disabled. It can be enabled for a dialog tab OR dialog tab _and_ feature type. To do this you must know the G3E_DTNO of the dialog tab _and_ the G3E_CNO of the component which is to be added (or deleted). The following example enables add and delete for all features with the tab '31021'.

```
<GtdwsEditor name="myEditorConfig">
   <TabsConfig>
      <DialogTab>
         <DTNO>31021</DTNO>
         <CNO>908</CNO>
         <AllowAdd>true</AllowAdd>
         <AllowDelete>true</AllowDelete>
      </DialogTab>
      <DialogTab>
         ...
       </DialogTab>
   </TabsConfig>
</GtdwsEditor>

```

## Specifying the available tabs for a feature type[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/Feature-Editor.html#specifying-the-available-tabs-for-a-feature-type)
By default all tabs for a dialog type will be presented to the user, however it is possible to limit these to a specific list. To do this you must know the G3E_DTNO of the dialog tabs you wish for to display. For example, the following will configure the feature editor to show two tabs for the feature type.

```
<GtdwsEditor name="myEditorConfig">
   <DialogTypes>
      <DialogType>
         <FNO>1</FNO>
         <!-- <ReviewConfig> and <EditConfig> are valid here too -->
         <Tabs>
            <DialogTab>
               <DTNO>123</DTNO>
            </DialogTab>
            <DialogTab>
               <DTNO>456</DTNO>
               <CNO>908</CNO>
               <AllowAdd>true</AllowAdd>
               <AllowDelete>true</AllowDelete>
            </DialogTab>
         </Tabs>
      </DialogType>
   </DialogTypes>
</GtdwsEditor>

```

It is also to enable add and delete component functions for a specific tab and feature type in this way.
## Deprecated settings[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/Feature-Editor.html#deprecated-settings)
The following will work but are not recommended anymore.
### Root for tab configuration[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/Feature-Editor.html#root-for-tab-configuration)
The element name `<DefaultTabs>` has been replaced with `<TabsConfig>`.
### Specifying the default dialog type[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/Feature-Editor.html#specifying-the-default-dialog-type)
The default dialog type is specified using the `<DefaultType>` element which must a child of a `<GtdwsEditor>` element. The type name is case sensitive. For example the following sets the default type to `Review`.

```
<GtdwsEditor name="myEditorConfig">
   <DefaultType>Review</DefaultType>
</GtdwsEditor>

```

### Specifying the dialog type for a feature type[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/Feature-Editor.html#specifying-the-dialog-type-for-a-feature-type)
In addition to the default type you can associated a different dialog type to specific feature types by mapping a features types G3E_FNO to a dialog type name. For example.

```
<GtdwsEditor name="myEditorConfig">
   <DefaultType>Review</DefaultType>
   <DialogTypes>
      <DialogType>
         <FNO>1</FNO>
         <Type>Edit</Type>
      </DialogType>
      <DialogType>
         <FNO>2</FNO>
         <Type>Custom Type</Type>
      </DialogType>
   </DialogTypes>
</GtdwsEditor>

```

# File location and loading
## Location[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/File-location-and-loading.html#location)
When the portal is deployed via NetWorks deployment tools (e.g. the Admin console) then the default location for workspaces is under:
`%ProgramData%\Intergraph\NetWorks\Portal\{Portal instance name}`
So, for example, if you are deploying a portal under the name `nwportal` then the workspace will be under:
`C:\ProgramData\Intergraph\NetWorks\Portal\nwportal`
The NetWorks deployment tools will create the workspace in a single file named as:
`Workspace.{Configuration name}.xml`
The link between the folder and portal is defined in the [web.config](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/web.config-file/Workspaces.html) file.
## Loading[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/File-location-and-loading.html#loading)
Workspaces are loaded and parsed when the Portal application pool is started or is recycled. Once loaded, the information is cached in memory.
When loading workspace files from a folder the portal will load all files with the '.xml' extension from the folder _and_ its sub folders, ordered by workspace file name, in ascending order. Where workspace or configuration item names are duplicated, the last read will take precedence.

# Google map source
## Important[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/Google-map-source.html#important)
Before using Google as a background map you should check whether you have a license to do so. We believe you need a 'Google Maps Premium Plan'.
##### Note
Using `<TileSize>` greater than allowed by your Google Maps license will result in misaligned tiles.
## Specifying a google map source[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/Google-map-source.html#specifying-a-google-map-source)
To add a google map source use the following.

```
<Section type="mapsource">
   … 
   <GoogleSource name="google" username="Google">
      <Key>…</Key>
      <CryptoKey>…</CryptoKey>
      <TileSize>…</TileSize>
