      <Attributions>Map data @Google <![CDATA[<a href="https://cloud.google.com/maps-platform/terms" target="_blank">Terms of use</a>]]>.</Attributions>
      <ImagerySet>…</ImagerySet>
      <Culture>…</Culture>
   </GoogleSource>

```

It can then be added to a legend as normal eg.

```
<Section type="maplegend">
   <Legend name="mylegend" username="My Legend">
      … 
      <SourceEntry>
         <SourceName>google</SourceName>
         <Visible>true</Visible>
         <DrawingPriority>1</DrawingPriority>
      </SourceEntry>
      … 

```

## Google source elements[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/Google-map-source.html#google-source-elements)
You should read <https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/maps-static/get-api-key> before configuring google maps in the Portal.  
| Name  | Required  | Remarks  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| Key  | Yes  | Should be set to your Google API key.  |  
| CryptoKey  | Yes  | Digital signature used to encrypt requests.  |  
| TileSize  | No  | Must be a multiples of 256 - 512, 1024, 2048. Default is 512.  |  
| ImagerySet  | No  | Can be roadmap (default), satellite, terrain or hybrid  |  
| Culture  | No  | ...  |  
| Attributions  | No  | Content to show as legal attributions for google maps. In order to display link as hyperlink, ![CDATA] syntax is required (see example above)  |  
## Changing the URL to Google maps static API[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/Google-map-source.html#changing-the-url-to-google-maps-static-api)
By default the portal will forward requests for map data to this URL
<https://maps.googleapis.com/maps/api/staticmap>
Typically you should not need to change it. However, if it is necessary then you can re-define the URL in the Portal's `web.config` file under the `<appSettings>` section as follows.

```
<add key="Google.StaticMapsApiUrl" value="https://maps.googleapis.com/maps/api/staticmap"/>

```

# Google Tiles Map Source
## Important[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/Google-Tiles-Map-Source.html#important)
Before using Google as a background map you should check whether you have a license to do so. You need a Google Cloud Account with Billing enabled
## Specifying a google tiles map source[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/Google-Tiles-Map-Source.html#specifying-a-google-tiles-map-source)

```
<GoogleTilesSource name="googleTiles" username="GoogleTiles">
     <Key>...</Key>
     <MapType>roadmap</MapType>
     <Language>en-US</Language>
     <highDpi>true</highDpi>
     <Scale>scaleFactor2x</Scale>
</GoogleTilesSource>

```

It can then be added to a legend as normal eg.

```
<SourceEntry>
   <SourceName>googleTiles</SourceName>
   <visible>false</visible>
</SourceEntry>

```

## Google Tiles source elements[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/Google-Tiles-Map-Source.html#google-tiles-source-elements)
You should read <https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/tile/get-api-key> before configuring google maps in the Portal.  
| Name  | Required  | Default Value  | Remarks  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| Key  | Yes  | -  | Should be set to your Google Tiles API key.  |  
| MapType  | No  | roadmap  | The type of base map  |  
| Language  | No  | en-US  | An IETF language tag for information displayed on the tiles  |  
| Region  | No  | US  | A Common Locale Data Repository (CLDR) region identifier that represents the user location.  |  
| ImageFormat  | No  | -  | The image format used for the map tiles (e.g. 'jpeg', or 'png').  |  
| Scale  | No  | -  | Scale for map elements ('scaleFactor1x', 'scaleFactor2x', or 'scaleFactor4x')  |  
| HighDpi  | No  | false  | Use high-resolution tiles.  |  
| LayerTypes  | No  | -  | The layer types added to the map (e.g. 'layerRoadmap', 'layerStreetview', or 'layerTraffic').  |  
| Overlay  | No  | false  | Display only the layerTypes and not the underlying mapType (only works if layerTypes is provided)  |  
| Styles  | No  | -  | Custom styles applied to the map.  |

# Loading extra scripts
The workspace XML file can contain an option section called 'scripts' which can be used to load either JavaScript or CSS files. For example:

```
<Section type="scripts">
   <Script name="sc1">
      <Url>http://muc-sgiv-ntst05/VectorServiceFonts/fonts.css</Url>
   </Script>
   <Script name="sc2">
      <Url>/mywebsite/turf.min.js</Url>
   </Script>
</Section>

```

The 'Url' can either be absolute or relative. It is recommended that URLs are relative or that files are on the same origin as the portal (i.e. same domain, port and protocol). However it is possible to load files from another origin if CORS is enabled for those files on the remote server.
To add references to scripts into workspace from the Admin Console use XML of the following form.

```
<add position="last" path="/config/Workspace[@name='default']/Section[@type='scripts']">
   <Script name="file1">
      <Url>/path/file1.js</Url>
   </Script>
   <Script name="file2">
      <Url>/path/file2.js</Url>
   </Script>
</add>

```

The name attribute is required by the application but is not used for anything in this context. The only requirement is that each name is unique for the list.
Scripts are loaded before the UI is initialized.

# Map Legend
## Overview[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/Map-Legend.html#overview)
In the portal, map legends combine map sources to generate the map. A workspace can define one or more legends so you can combine map sources in different ways. Legends are defined under `<Section type="maplegend">` for example.

```
    <Section type="maplegend">
        <Legend name="default" username="OSM">
            <OverviewLegendName>overview</OverviewLegendName>
            <View>
                <Projection>EPSG:3857</Projection>
                <Center>1378956.309,7505430.854</Center>
                <Resolution>0.6</Resolution>
            </View>
            <Entries>
                <SourceEntry>
                    <SourceName>osm</SourceName>
                    <Visible>true</Visible>
                </SourceEntry>
            </Entries>
        </Legend>
   ...

```

## Legend element[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/Map-Legend.html#legend-element)
The legend element is the root of a tree of 'entry' elements. A legend element has two attributes:
  * name - The internal name of the legend which must be unique for all legends.
  * username - The display text which is shown in the dropdown in the portals legend panel.

Both attributes are required.
The legend element can have the following child elements:  
| Element  | Required  | Remarks  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| IsDefault  |   | True or false. Used to determine the first legend to display on portal startup. Default is false.  |  
| Hidden  |   | True or false. Used to determine whether the legend should appear in the legend selection dropdown if more than one is defined. Default is false.  |  
| OverviewLegendName  |   | Links this legend to another which is used in the overview map function.  |  
| View  | Y  | Defines the map projection, start/home position and optionally the extent which can be viewed by the user.  |  
| Entries  | Y  | Defines the map legend tree of map sources.  |  
| Configuration  |   | NetWorks configuration name. If supplied overrides the configuration name specified in the workspace when generating Redline XML exports.  |  
| LegendNumber  |   | NetWorks legend settings number (G3E_LSNO). If supplied used to set the legend number attribute in in Redline XML exports.  |  
| LegendType  |   | Can be one of geographic, detail or schematic. Default is geographic. When multiple geographic legends are defined and the user switches between them the portal will attempt to maintain the map view position.  |  
| DetailId  |   | Indicates the identifier of the detail or schenatic.  |  
## View element[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/Map-Legend.html#view-element)
The view element can have the following child elements:  
| Element  | Required  | Remarks  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| Projection  | Y  | EPSG code of the maps projection  |  
| Resolution  | Y  | Initial map resolution.  |  
| Center  | Y  | Initial map center coordinate as comma separated numbers X,Y.  |  
| Extent  | N  | Maximum extent which can be viewed by the user. Defined as four numbers minx,miny,maxx,maxy.  |  
| MinResolution  | N  | The small map resolution and user can zoom in to.  |  
| MaxResolution  | N  | The largest map resolution a user can zoom out to.  |  
## Entries element[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/Map-Legend.html#entries-element)
The entries element can contain a list of three types of child elements. These are:
  * `<FolderEntry>` - Adds a folder to the legend to group child element elements together.
  * `<SourceEntry>` - Adds a map source to the legend. While it is valid to nest source entry elements it is not recommended as it will end up confusing for the user.
  * `<LayerEntry>` - For NetworksVectorSource, NetworksWMSSource and WMSSource defines which layers from these services are to be added to the map. A layer entry must be descended from a source entry.

Common to all entry elements are the following properties.  
| Element  | Required  | Remarks  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| Name  | Y  | Key for the entry. Should be unique within the legend.  |  
| UserName  | N  | Display text for the legend. Defaults to name.  |  
| Icon  | N  | URL to an icon image to display next to the text in the legend. URL can be absolute or relative.  |  
| IconCls  | N  | CSS class name that defines the icon to display next to the text in the legend. This is ignored if Icon is set.  |  
| Tooltip  | N  | Text to display when user mouses over the element in the legend panel. Can contain HTML elements. Defaults to UserName.  |  
| CheckVisible  | N  | Defines whether a visibility checkbox is displayed in the legend panel next to the text. Default is true.  |  
| Hidden  | N  | True or false if the legend entry is displayed in the legend panel or not. Default is false.  |  
| Expanded  | N  | True or false if the legend entry is initially expanded or not. Default is false.  |  
| Group  | N  | String identifier. When this legend entry is set to visible then any other legend entry with the same group identifier is set to not visible and vice versa, in the same way as radio buttons.  |  
| Entries  | N  | Contains a list of zero or more entry elements.  |  
These properties should be set as child elements to an entry element including name and user name e.g.

```
<Entries>
   ...
   <FolderEntry>
      <Name>Folder1</Name>
      <UserName>Basemap</UserName>
      <IconCls>x-fa fa-layer-group</IconCls>
      <CheckVisible>false</CheckVisible>
      <Expanded>true</Expanded>
      <Entries>
         <SourceEntry>
            <Name>OSM</Name>
            <SourceName>osm</SourceName>
            <IconCls>x-fa fa-image</IconCls>
            <Group>basemap-group</Group>
            <Visible>true</Visible>
         </SourceEntry>
         <SourceEntry>
            <Name>bingmaps</Name>
            <UserName>Bing</UserName>
            <SourceName>bingmaps</SourceName>
            <IconCls>x-fa fa-image</IconCls>
            <Group>basemap-group</Group>
         </SourceEntry>
         <SourceEntry>
            <Name>googlemaps</Name>
            <UserName>Google</UserName>
            <SourceName>googlemaps</SourceName>
            <IconCls>x-fa fa-image</IconCls>
            <Group>basemap-group</Group>
         </SourceEntry>
      </Entries>
   </FolderEntry>
</Entries>

```

## SourceEntry element[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/Map-Legend.html#sourceentry-element)
Source entry elements add map sources to the map. They can have the following properties:  
| Element  | Required  | Remarks  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| SourceName  | Y  | Name of the map source this entry will add to the map  |  
| AllLayers  | N  | For WMS or Networks Vector sources, if set to true then the portal will query the service for child entries to populate the legend with. Otherwise it is expected that they are already defined. For other map sources does nothing.  |  
| Visible  | N  | Initial visibility of the legend entry. Default is false. For WMS and Networks Vector sources then visibility is defined on child entries however this value will be used to set that for child entries if AllLayers is true.  |  
| Queryable  | N  | Default locatability of the legend entry. Default is false. For WMS and Networks Vector sources then locatability is defined on child entries however this value will be used to set that for child entries if AllLayers is true.  |  
| NonQueryable  | N  | If set to true this will prevent the source entry from becoming queryable/locatable, and will also override queryable and set it to false. See notes below.  |  
| DrawingPriority  | N  | Numeric value Used to sort sources when adding them to the map. By default sources are added to the map in the order they appear in the legend. So the bottom most source in the legend is added to the map last so this will appear on top. Default is 1.  |  
| Opacity  | N  | Value between 0 and 1 which defines how transparent data from the source is rendered. 0 for completely transparent, 1 for completely opaque. Default is 1.  |  
Note that opacity in this context is not the same as transparency. Opacity can be set to 1 but for where there is no map data can be still transparent.
Whether a source entry can be made queryable/locatable depends first on the type of map source the source entry represents. The following map source types cannot be made locatable/queryable:
  * `<WMTSSource>`
  * `<OSMSource>`
  * `<BingSource>`
  * `<GoogleSource>`

They will remain 'NonQueryable' regardless of what is specified in the workspace. For other map source types, including `<NetworksWMTSSource>`, NonQueryable will default to false. This will allow users to change whether that legend entry (and any child entries) are locatable in the map via the portal UI. If this behavior is not desired then setting NonQueryable to true will set the entry (and any child entries) to be not locatable/queryable and prevent the user from changing that property.
## LayerEntry element[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/Map-Legend.html#layerentry-element)
Layer entry elements define, for WMS and NetworksVector sources the layers to display in the map. They can have the following properties:  
| Element  | Required  | Remarks  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| Visible  | N  | Initial visibility of the legend entry. Default is false.  |  
| Queryable  | N  | Initial locatability of the legend entry. Default is false.  |  
| NonQueryable  | N  | If set to true this will prevent the source entry from becoming 'queryable', and will also override queryable and set it to false. See notes for SourceEntry elements.  |  
| StyleName  | N  | For WMS layers that define multiple named styles you can set the preferred layer style here.  |  
| Id  | N  | G3E_DCROWNO of the legend display control node. This value is required when the NetWorks Vector Service legend structure is manually configured in the workspace for correct function of setting Ad-hoc or Predefined Filter and other legend-related functions.  |  
For WMS layers Name must match the name of the WMS layer. For Vector Service layers Name of leaf nodes must match G3E_LENO of legend entry.
**Example**

```
<Section type="maplegend">
   <Legend name="default" username="All">
      ...
      <Entries>
         <SourceEntry>
            <SourceName>wms1</SourceName>
            <Name>wms1</Name>
            <DrawingPriority>15</DrawingPriority>
            <Queryable>true</Queryable>
            <Entries>
               <LayerEntry>
                  <Name>HIGH_VOLTAGE</Name>
                  <UserName>Hochspannung</UserName>
                  <Queryable>true</Queryable>
                  <Visible>true</Visible>
                  <StyleName>Red</StyleName>
               </LayerEntry>
               <LayerEntry>
                  <Name>MIDDLE_VOLTAGE</Name>
                  <UserName>Mittelspannung</UserName>
                  <Queryable>True</Queryable>
                  <Visible>true</Visible>
                  <StyleName>Yellow</StyleName>
               </LayerEntry>
               ...
            </Entries>
         </SourceEntry>

```

# Map sources
## Overview[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/Map-sources.html#overview)
Map sources define parameters which tell the Portal how to retrieve map data from a service (or other web resource). They are defined under `<Section type="mapsource">` in the workspace. Under this section you can define the following child elements.
  * `<BingSource>` - for Bing maps.
  * `<GoogleSource>` - for Google maps.
  * `<NetworksVectorSource>` - for the NetWorks Vector Service.
  * `<NetworksWMSSource>` - for NetWorks WMS services.
  * `<NetworksWFSSource>` - for NetWorks WFS services.
  * `<NetworksWMTSSource>` - for NetWorks WMTS services.
  * `<OSMSource>` - for OpenStreetMap or OpenStreetMap compatible tile sets.
  * `<WFSSource>` - for WFS services.
  * `<WMSSource>` - for WMS services.
  * `<WMTSSource>` - for WMTS services.

## Common Parameters[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/Map-sources.html#common-parameters)
The following are parameters that can be defined on every map source.  
| Name  | Required  | Remarks  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| name  | Y  | Unique identifier for the map source.  |  
| username  | N  | Display string for the map source. Defaults to name.  |  
| AuthMode  | N  | Defaults to the infrastructureAppAuthentication mode defined in web.config. See the notes below.  |  
| MinResolution  | N  | Minimum map resolution at which data from the source will be visible in the map. Default is 0.  |  
| MaxResolution  | N  | Maximum map resolution at which data from the source will be visible in the map. Default is +Infinity.  |  
| Projection  | N  | Projection which the source presents map data in expressed as an EPSG code e.g. EPSG:3857. Default is the map view projection.  |  
| Extent  | N  | The extent of the data provided by the map source defined as min, max coordinates in the sources projection. minx,miny,maxx,maxy.  |  
| Attributions  | N  | Short attribution or copyright text for the sources data. Can contain HTML elements.  |  
| Documentation  | N  | URL to a PDF document or other web resource which describes the map sources content. Can be relative or absolute.  |  
| ExtraParams  | N  | A list of key value pairs which will be appended to the query string to every request sent to the map source.  |  
| EditorName  | N  | If the map source returns features with valid GTech G3E_FNO and G3E_FID properties, e.g. from a GetFeatureInfo request, this can be set to the name of an editor configuration item in the editor section. If sete the portal will use the legacy Feature Editor to view attributes rather than the simple editor.  |  
| EnableTooltips  | N  | True to enable tooltips for features from this map source. Default is true for Networks Vector sources and false for WFS. Only applicable to Networks Vector and WFS sources.  |  
| FeatureNameFormatString  | N  | Can be used by extensions to the portal to differentiate between features coming from the source.  |  
| FeatureUserNameFormatString  | N  | Can be used to control the text being displayed in the feature selection panel and tooltips. Does not apply to Networks Vector sources as text for tooltips and feature user names is configured in the GTech database.  |  
Please note the following:
  * Map resolution is the ration from screen units (CSS pixel) and the map's projection's units e.g. meters. A map resolution of 1 means that one pixel is 1 square metre, 2 means that one pixel is 2 square meters and so on. This is a rough factor as pixels are generally not perfectly square and the operating system can also apply additional scaling factors when using high resolution displays.
  * If the projection of the data from the a map source is different than the projection defined for the legend it is part of, then you MUST specify a projection for the source.
  * If you set a projection you must ensure that the projections definition is in [coordsys.json](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/coordsys.json.html).
  * Projection _is_ case sensitive and must be written EPSG:_epsg code_ or it must exactly match an alias in [coordsys.json](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/coordsys.json.html).
  * Setting a projection on Bing, Google or Open street maps will have no affect as these services only produce data in EPSG:3857.
  * Setting a projection on a source that the underlying service does not support will often cause unexpected results or an error in the portal client.
  * If you define an extent then you must also define a projection.

**Example**

```
<...Source name="uniqueName" username="Display Text">
	<MinResolution>0.5</MinResolution>
	<MaxResolution>2.5</MaxResolution>
	<Projection>EPSG:5678</Projection>
	<Extent>>4350860.09,5319920.57,4628080.32,6098619.71</Extent>
	<Attributions><![CDATA[>&#169; <a href="https://hexagon.com/">Hexagon</a>]]></Attributions>
	<ExtraParams>
		<param key="Parameter name">Parameter value</param>
	</ExtraParams>
	<EditorName>default</EditorName>
</...Source>

```

## Format strings[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/Map-sources.html#format-strings)
Format strings are available for defining better labels for features which originate from an external (none NetWorks) map source. These are defined on a source by
  * FeatureNameFormatString
  * FeatureUserNameFormatString

They can be left null, set to a simple string or, they can be set to a string which includes curly braces surrounding a property name available from the feature. For example, consider the following feature returned by a service (shown as GeoJSON).

```
{
   type: "Feature",
   geometry: ...
   properties: {
      id: 12838,
      type: "Well",
      state: "Active"
   }
}

```

On the source the user name format string is defined as:

```
<FeatureUserNameFormatString>{type} - {id} : {state}</FeatureUserNameFormatString>

```

This will result in the user label or tooltip (if enabled) for the feature to be displayed as:
`Well - 12838 : Active`
This feature can also be used to display the tooltip for Networks WFS features e.g.

```
<FeatureUserNameFormatString>{ToolTip}</FeatureUserNameFormatString>

```

Note that the matching between the text in the curly braces and the features attribute/property names, is case sensitive.
## Re-projection of map sources[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/Map-sources.html#re-projection-of-map-sources)
Generally it is recommended that the map services published by NetWorks use the same projection as the database as this will give the most accurate positioning of data on the map and also the most accurate length and area calculation results. Where possible it is also recommended that external map data used in the portal also uses the same projection. Background data from Bing or Open Street Maps only comes in one projection, EPSG:3857. The client can re-project/transform the data to the maps projection but it can sometimes cause errors in the client. The current recommendation is that if this occurs is to set an extent on the map source which covers the area of interest or is slightly smaller than the map projections extent.
## Map sources and OpenID Connect[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/Map-sources.html#map-sources-and-openid-connect)
For WMS, WFS and WMTS services, the Portal makes requests directly to these services to find metadata and to request map data. When the Portal is configured to use Open ID Connect, then by default the portal will attach an [authorization](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Authorization) header to these requests. If the map services are external this can cause the service to return a 4xx error. In these cases you can define an AuthMode parameter on the map source to prevent it doing this i.e.

```
<...Source name="uniqueName" username="Display Text">
	<AuthMode>Anonymous</AuthMode>

```

# Networks Vector Source
## Specifying a NetWorks vector map source[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/Networks-Vector-Source.html#specifying-a-networks-vector-map-source)
To add a NetWorks Vector source use the following.

```
<Section type="mapsource">
   … 
   <NetworksVectorSource name="testvector" username="Vector test">
      <Attributions>&#169; Hexagon.</Attributions>
      <Lsno>7</Lsno>
      <Url>/VectorServiceNWTEST</Url>
      <EditorName>editorconfigname</EditorName>
   </NetworksVectorSource>

```

It can then be added to a legend as normal e.g.

```
<Section type="maplegend">
   <Legend name="mylegend" username="My Legend">
      … 
      <SourceEntry>
         <Name>sourceentryname</Name>
         <SourceName>testvector</SourceName>
         <Visible>true</Visible>
         <AllLayers>true</AllLayers>
         <DrawingPriority>20</DrawingPriority>
      </SourceEntry>
      … 

```

## Vector source elements[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/Networks-Vector-Source.html#vector-source-elements)  
| Name  | Required  | Type  | Remarks  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| Lsno  | Y  | int  | The G3E_LSNO of the legend  |  
| Url  | Y  | string  | The URL to the service. Can be absolute or relative.  |  
| PaperScale  |   | double  | Scaling factor styles as a double. By default this is looked up from the service.  |  
| Attribution  |   | string  | Attribution text for display on the map.  |  
| Projection  |   | string  | EPSG code for the projection in which map data is available. By default this is looked up from the service.  |  
| MinResolution  |   | double  | Smallest map resolution at which this source will be visible in a map.  |  
| MaxResolution  |   | double  | Largest map resolution at which this source will be visible in a map.  |  
| Extent  |   | double[]  | Map extent in which this source is visible in the map. Specify as a comma separated list of coordinates i.e. `minx,miny,maxx,maxy`  |  
| EditorName  |   | string  | Link to an editor configuration.  |  
| RenderMaskSymbols  |   | bool  | When `true`, mask symbols are rendered. Default is `false`.  |  
| EnableComponentTooltips  |   | bool  | If tooltips are enabled for this source and this is set to true then the application will attempt to fetch the tooltip for the selected geometry component (if configured) otherwise it will fetch the tooltip for the feature. Default is false.  |  
| MinimumLineWidth  |   | double  | Minimum width of rendered line in CSS pixels. Default is `0.5`. Higher values make hairline width lines more visible. Use `1` to match NetWorks Core Designer rendering.  |  
| RenderBuffer  |   | integer  | The buffer in pixels around the viewport extent used by the renderer when getting features from the vector source for the rendering or hit-detection. Recommended value: the size of the largest symbol, line width or label. Default is `100`.  |  
| ImageRatio  |   | double  | Ratio by which the rendered extent should be larger than the viewport extent. A larger ratio avoids cut images during panning, but will cause a decrease in performance. Default is 1.  |  
If EnableTooltips is true and on systems with configured formatted tooltips (G3E_FEATURE.G3E_IDENTIFIERVIEW), the Vector Service returns formatted feature tooltips. This may lead to slightly worse performance, because it includes a database call.
## Fonts[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/Networks-Vector-Source.html#fonts)
For labels and symbology to be displayed correctly in the portal fonts will need to be published onto a web server and the resulting CSS file linked to the portal. Publishing the required CSS files and TTF files is done by using a utility supplied with NetWorks and its usage is documented with the Vector Service. You should note the following.
  * If you intend to publish the portal publicly on the internet then ensure that you are not breaching the license terms associated with any fonts you are using in your styles.
  * To enable printing ensure that the fonts are installed on the server that the portal is installed on.
  * If you intend for the portal to only be used on the windows desktop then it is sufficient to publish only TTF. Otherwise you will need to publish both TTF and WOFF and run a one time conversion to convert the TTF files to WOFF format.

If you are using fonts that are licensed such that they cannot be published on a web server then it is possible manually modify the CSS file produced by the publish utility to map the font name to font files which are not limited by the license.
As an example of the process.
  1. Run the PublishFonts utility on your NetWorks server to generate the CSS and TTF files e.g.

```
C:\Program Files (x86)\Intergraph\NetWorks\Program\PublishFonts.exe -c GINIUS -o c:\Temp\VectorServiceFonts

```

  1. Copy the contents of `c:\Temp\VectorServiceFonts` to `c:\inetpub\wwwroot\VectorServiceFonts`.
  2. In your workspace file add an entry to the `scripts` section of your workspace xml file that points to the CSS file in your published folder e.g.

```
<Workspace name="default" username="Default">
   <DatabaseAlias>GINIUS</DatabaseAlias>
    <Section type="scripts">
       <Script name="sc1">
          <Url>/VectorServiceFonts/fonts.css</Url>
       </Script>
       ...
     </Section>
     ...

```

## Manually configuring the legend.[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/Networks-Vector-Source.html#manually-configuring-the-legend)
As with a WMS service you can manually configure the legend entries a user sees by manually specifying the entries in the workspace xml file. However there are some special rules.
  * Only leaf legend entries should be LayerEntry elements. Grouping entries should be FolderEntry elements.
  * The `<Name>` of a `LayerEntry` must be set to the G3E_LENO of the legend entry. FolderEntry names can be any string but should be unique within the legend.

For example, if I requested the legend directly from the Vector Service e.g.

```
http://localhost/myvectorservice/displaycontrol/7/dc

```

And this returns

```
{
    "dcrowno": "0",
    "level": 0,
    "children": [{
            "dcrowno": "100000000",
            "name": "Cadaster",
            "level": 0,
            "leafIndicator": 0,
            "children": [{
                    "dcrowno": "100001000",
                    "name": "Cad-Country",
                    "level": 0,
                    "leafIndicator": 0,
                    "children": [{
                            "dcrowno": "100001010",
                            "leno": "1000000",
                            "name": "Cad-Country - Inventory",
                            "level": 0,
                            "leafIndicator": 1,
                            "locatable": 0,
                            "displayMode": 1
                        },
                        ...
                    ]
                }, ...

}

```

Then in my workspace XML I could manually configure this as

```
<SourceEntry>
   <Name>electricvector</Name>
   <SourceName>myvectorservice</SourceName>
   <DrawingPriority>25</DrawingPriority>
   <Entries>
       <FolderEntry>
          <Name>anyuniquestring</Name> <!-- Can be a numeric string e.g. the dcrowno -->
          <UserName>Cadaster</UserName> 
          <Entries>
             <LayerEntry>
                <Name>1000000</Name> <!-- The leno -->
                <UserName>Cad-Country - Inventory</UserName>
                <Queryable>true</Queryable>
                <Visible>true</Visible>
             </LayerEntry>
          </Entries>
       </FolderEntry>
   </Entries>
</SourceEntry>

```

Here we have removed one of the levels and changed the default 'locability' to true by setting `<Queryable>` to true. Also note that here we only need to set `<Queryable>` and `<Visible>` on the `<LayerEntry>` elements.

# OSM Source
## Specifying an OpenStreetMap map source[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/OSM-Source.html#specifying-an-openstreetmap-map-source)
To add an OSM or OSM-compatible map source use the following.

```
<Section type="mapsource">
   … 
   <OSMSource name="osm" username="OpenStreetMap">
      <UrlTemplate>...</UrlTemplate>
   </OSMSource>

```

## OpenStreetMap source properties[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/OSM-Source.html#openstreetmap-source-properties)  
| Name  | Required  | Remarks  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| Attributions  | N  | The attributions text of the map.  |  
| UrlTemplate  | N  | Template for creating URL to an Open Street Maps service. Must include `{x}`, `{y}` or `{-y}`, and `{z}` placeholders. Defaults to `https://tile.openstreetmap.org/{z}/{x}/{y}.png`.  |  
| CrossOrigin  | N  | CrossOrigin value must be provided if you want to access pixel data with the Canvas renderer. Defaults to `anonymous`.  |  
| Opacity  | N  | A value between 0 and 1 that defines the opacity at which data from the map source is rendered in. Default to `1`.  |

# Overview Map
## Introduction[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/Overview-Map.html#introduction)
The portal supports viewing an overview map. This is activated by a toggle button which is typically located as the top most button in the right hand toolbar. Toggling the button the button displays a map with a secondary map view. In this view is a dotted rectangle which represents the extent of the main map view. This rectangle can be dragged to change the main view. Panning and/or zooming in the main map view updates the secondary map view.
## Changes to the workspace XML[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/Overview-Map.html#changes-to-the-workspace-xml)
First you must define one or more map sources for your overview map. For example you could use Open Street Maps. If you already are using Open Street Maps as a basemap then all well and good otherwise you must add it to your workspace XML file.

```
<Section type="mapsource">
   ...
   <OSMSource name="osm" username="OSM">
   </OSMSource>
   ...
</Section>

```

Second you must define a legend for your overview map. For example.

```
<Section type="maplegend">
   <Legend name="osm-overview" username="Overview">
      <Hidden>true</Hidden>
      <View>
         <Projection>EPSG:25832</Projection>
      </View>
      <Entries>
         <SourceEntry>
            <SourceName>osm</SourceName>
         </SourceEntry>
      </Entries>
   </Legend>
   ...

```

Here the '' is set to `true` so that it does not appear in the legend dropdown box. The legend name must be unique for all legends. For the view section of the legend you only need to define a projection but note that it **must** match the projection of your main legend(s). The map sources can be in other projections, for example here we are using Open Street Maps and that uses `EPSG:3857`.
Finally you then link your main legend to your overview map legend by setting 'OverviewLegendName' in it. For example.

```
   <Legend name="default" username="Default">
      <OverviewLegendName>osm-overview</OverviewLegendName>
      <View>
         <Projection>EPSG:25832</Projection>
         <Resolution>51.2</Resolution>
         <Center>642450,6133750</Center>
         <MaxResolution>2000</MaxResolution>
         <MinResolution>0.01</MinResolution>
      </View>
      <Entries>
         ...
      </Entries>
   </Legend>

```

# Print Templates
## Overview[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/Print-Templates.html#overview)
This guide is intended for system administrators to allow them to make add and modify print templates within the the Utility Portal. It is a prerequisite that administrators know what an XML file is and can modify them. It is also useful to know basic CSS but not required.
The portal comes with four print templates already defined. They are defined within a portal workspace. Typically they are included into a workspace file via an `<Import>` tag e.g.

```
<config>
  <Import>maplegends\osm.xml</Import>
  <Import>printtemplates\default.xml</Import>

```

They are then linked into an actual workspace via a print `<Section>` e.g.

```
    <Section type="print">
      <Template name="A4" />
      <Template name="A4_" />
      <Template name="A3" />
      <Template name="A3_" />
    </Section>

```

The file the template definitions are in by default here:
`portaldir\App_GlobalResources\Workspaces\printtemplates\default.xml`
You can create copies of this file as required. It is recommended that you quickly review the contents of this file or the copy in [Appendix B](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/Print-Templates.html#appendix-b) before you read further.
A print template defines a single page that contains a single viewport into which the map is rendered. The size of the viewport is defined by the templates margins and borders. Overlayed onto the viewport can be zero or more tables divided into cells that contain static images (e.g. logos), labels, auto text generated by the application and user text entered by the user. For example:
[![PrintPage.png](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/.attachments/PrintPage-eb1d94a1-ed9b-4c1c-afca-e6b4f7224e5e.png)](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/.attachments/PrintPage-eb1d94a1-ed9b-4c1c-afca-e6b4f7224e5e.png)
Print templates use millimetres throughout as their unit of measurement. For prints 1 pixel is approximately 0.26 mm. Similar to CSS, print templates use two data structures regularly.
  1. Box. The width of the sides of a box. This can be defined as a comma separated list of four floating point numbers top, right, bottom, left. Or two float point numbers that define top & bottom, left & right. Or one number which defines that all sides have the same width.
  2. BoxSize. The size of a rectangle. This is defined as two floating point numbers separated with a comma width, height.

Within a print template you can also define colors for various elements. This can be define as a known color name (see [Appendix A](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/Print-Templates.html#appendix-a)) or
  * `#FFFFFF` – A hexadecimal number containing 6 digits defining an RGB color code. `#` character must be first.
  * `#FFFFFFFF` – A hexadecimal number containing 8 digits defining an RGBA color code. `#` character must be first.
  * `255,255,255` – A comma separated list of 3 whole numbers between 0 and 255 defining an RGB color code.
  * `255,255,255,255` - A comma separated list of 4 whole numbers between 0 and 255 defining an RGBA color code. For the alpha channel (A) 0 is transparent and 255 is opaque.

When rendering text in a template you can define which font is to be used. This can be defined by using its name. The font must be installed on the server. The list of fonts available can typically be found under C:\Windows\Fonts.
## Template element[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/Print-Templates.html#template-element)
The is the root element of a print template definition and must be a child of a `<Section type="print">` element.  
It has two attributes both of which must be defined:
  * `name` – The internal name of the template. This is what the workspace uses to link to this definition. It can be any string but it is recommended that you use ASCII characters and digits with no spaces when defining a name. All print template definitions must have a unique name.
  * `username` – The display name of the template. This is what is shown to a user. It can be any string but it is recommended that it should be limited to 50 characters.

The template element can have the following child elements.  
| Name  | Required  | Type  | Remark  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| BorderColor  | N  | Color  | Color of the border. Default is black.  |  
| Borders  | N  | Box  | Width of the viewport border. Default is 0 i.e. no border.  |  
| Fields  | N  |   | List of plot header fields. See following section.  |  
| FontColor  | N  | Color  | Font color used by default in the template. Default is black.  |  
| FontFamily  | N  | String  | Name of the font used by default in the template. Default is Verdana.  |  
| FontSize  | N  | Number  | Optional. Default font size in mm.  |  
| Margins  | N  | Box  | Viewport margin width(s).  |  
| PageSize  | Y  | BoxSize  | Dimensions of the page in mm (width, height).  |  
| Tables  | N  |   | List of tables. See following section.  |  
##### Important
While the application does not enforce any limit on page size creating prints larger than A3 will require significant hardware resources and reconfiguration of your web server for it to work reliably. If you wish to use the print function to generate prints larger than A3 then its strongly recommended that you contact your software distributor first.
## Fields elements[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/Print-Templates.html#fields-elements)
Fields in a template define the list of fields shown in the portal when the user selects that template for printing e.g.

```
<Fields>
  <Field>
    <Name>notes</Name>
    <Label>Bemærkning</Label>
  </Field>
  <Field>
    <Name>printedby</Name>
    <Label>Udskrevet af</Label>
  </Field>
</Fields>

```

A field is defined by a `<Field>` element that must contain two child elements.  
| Name  | Required  | Type  | Remark  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| Name  | Y  | String  | Internal name of the field. Used by table cells to reference this field. Must be unique within the template.  |  
| Label  | Y  | String  | Text displayed to the user in the client.  |  
| MaxLength  | N  | Integer  | Maximum number of characters allowed to be input. Default is 100 characters.  |  
## Table element[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/Print-Templates.html#table-element)
Tables are panels which are overlayed onto the viewport. A table is built up within a template using a similar logic to defining a table within an HTML document. A table is split into one or more rows, a row is split into one or more cells. A cell can `span` across one or more rows and/or columns. For example.

```
<Table>
  <Position>BottomRight</Position>
  <Borders>0.5,0,0,0.5</Borders>
  <BorderColor>Black</BorderColor>
  <Rows>
    <Row>
      <Cell>
        <Type>label</Type>
        <Content>Udskrevet af</Content>
        <Width>25</Width>
        <Padding>2,0,0,2</Padding>
      </Cell>
      <Cell>
        <Type>fieldValue</Type>
        <Content>printedby</Content>
        <Width>50</Width>
        <Padding>2,0,0,2</Padding>
      </Cell>
      <Cell>
        <Type>image</Type>
        <Content>resources/images/logo.png</Content>
        <RowSpan>5</RowSpan>
        <Width>50</Width>
        <Padding>0,2,0,2</Padding>
      </Cell>
    </Row>

```

A `<Table>` element can have the following child elements that define its attributes.  
| Name  | Required  | Type  | Remark  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| BackgroundColor  | N  | Color  | Background color of the table. Default is white.  |  
| BorderColor  | N  | Color  | Color of the border. Defaults to the templates border color.  |  
| Borders  | N  | Box  | Outside border of the table. Defaults to 0 i.e. no border.  |  
| FontColor  | N  | Color  | Color of text within the table. Defaults to the templates font color.  |  
| FontFamily  | N  | String  | Font used to render text in the table. Defaults to the templates font.  |  
| FontSize  | N  | Number  | Font size in mm.  |  
| Position  | Y  | String  | Currently this can be set to TopLeft, TopRight, BottomLeft and BottomRight. The table will be rendered into that corner of the viewport.  |  
| Size  | N  | BoxSize  | Intended size of the table. The application will attempt to size the table but will overflow that size if it cannot.  |  
A table's contents is defined by adding `<Row>` elements under `<Rows>`. Under a `<Row>` element you can add one or more `<Cell>` elements. A `<Cell>` element defines the actual content to be rendered within a table.
A `<Cell>` element can have the following child elements that defines its attributes.  
| Name  | Required  | Type  | Remark  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| BackgroundColor  | N  | Color  | Background color of the cell. Default is table background color..  |  
| BorderColor  | N  | Color  | Color of the border. Defaults to the tables border color.  |  
| Borders  | N  | Box  | Outside border of the table. Defaults to 0 i.e. no border.  |  
| Content  | Y  | String  | See following.  |  
| ColumnSpan  | N  | Whole number  | Number of columns that this cell spans. Default is 1.  |  
| FontColor  | N  | Color  | Color of text within the table. Defaults to the tables font color.  |  
| FontFamily  | N  | String  | Font used to render text in the table. Defaults to the tables font.  |  
| FontSize  | N  | Number  | Font size in mm.  |  
| Format  | N  | String  | Formatting string to be applied to a value. Currently only used when `Type` is `autoValue`.  |  
| Height  | N  | Number  | Height of the cell in mm. Typically the application will calculate this for you.  |  
| Padding  | N  | Box  | Whitespace padding to be applied around the content of the cell.  |  
| RowSpan  | N  | Whole number  | Number of rows that this call spans. Default is 1.  |  
| Type  | Y  | String  | Currently this can be either `label`,`image`,`fieldValue` or `autoValue`. See following.  |  
| Width  | N  | Number  | Width of the cell in mm. Typically the application wil calculate this for you.  |  
| RightToLeft  | N  | bool  | specifies whether text should be written as Right-to-left (e.g. for arabic, hebrew)  |  
| CellVerticalAlignment  | N  | string  | provides options for different text vertical alignments (center, top, bottom), default is center  |  
| CellHorizontalAlignment  | N  | string  | provides options for different text horizontal alignments (left, right, center), default is left.  |  
A cell has two main attributes, `type` and `content`. The `type` attribute defines how the value of content is to be interpreted.
  * Type `label` The string in content is rendered as is, so if you write `foo` in content then on the print you will see the text `foo`.
  * Type `image` The string in content is interpreted as a file path to an image file. Images can be in JPEG or PNG formats. The application will look up that image file and render it into the cell. The file path can be absolute or relative to the portal directory. It is recommended that custom image files are not placed into existing folders but rather a new folder for example `portaldir\resources\custom`.
  * Type `fieldValue` The string on content must match the name of a field defined in the fields section of the template. The application will print the text entered by the user into the field onto the print.
  * Type `autoValue` In this case content can either be `date`, `scale` or `attributions`. If content is set to date then the servers datetime will be printed into the cell. Additionally you can specify a date format string to format the datetime further (see <https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/standard/base-types/custom-date-and-time-format-strings>). If content is set to scale then the scale selected by the user for the print will be printed into the cell.

## Appendix A – Color chart[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/Print-Templates.html#appendix-a--color-chart)
See <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Web_colors>.
## Appendix B – Sample template[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/Print-Templates.html#appendix-b--sample-template)

```
  <Section type="print">
    <Template name="A4" username="A4">
      <PageSize>210,297</PageSize>
      <Margins>10</Margins>      
      <Borders>0.5</Borders>
      <BorderColor>Black</BorderColor>
      <Fields>
        <Field>
          <Name>notes</Name>
          <Label>Bemærkning</Label>
        </Field>
        <Field>
          <Name>printedby</Name>
          <Label>Udskrevet af</Label>
        </Field>
      </Fields>
      <Tables>
        <Table>
          <Position>BottomRight</Position>
          <Borders>0.5,0,0,0.5</Borders>
          <BorderColor>Black</BorderColor>
          <Rows>
            <Row>
              <Cell>
                <Type>label</Type>
                <Content>Udskrevet af</Content>
                <Width>25</Width>
                <Padding>2,0,0,2</Padding>
              </Cell>
              <Cell>
                <Type>fieldValue</Type>
                <Content>printedby</Content>
                <Width>50</Width>
                <Padding>2,0,0,2</Padding>
              </Cell>
              <Cell>
                <Type>image</Type>
                <Content>resources/images/logo.png</Content>
                <RowSpan>5</RowSpan>
                <Width>50</Width>
                <Padding>0,2,0,2</Padding>
              </Cell>
            </Row>
            <Row>
              <Cell>
                <Type>label</Type>
                <Content>Bemærkning</Content>
                <RowSpan>2</RowSpan>
                <Padding>0,2,0,2</Padding>
              </Cell>
              <Cell>
                <Type>fieldValue</Type>
                <Content>notes</Content>
                <RowSpan>2</RowSpan>
                <Padding>0,2,0,2</Padding>
              </Cell>
            </Row>
            <Row></Row>            
            <Row>
              <Cell>
                <Type>label</Type>
                <Content>Skala</Content>
                <Padding>2,2,0,2</Padding>
              </Cell>
              <Cell>
                <Type>autoValue</Type>
                <Content>scale</Content>
                <Padding>2,2,0,2</Padding>
              </Cell>
            </Row>
            <Row>
              <Cell>
                <Type>label</Type>
                <Content>Dato</Content>
                <Padding>2</Padding>
              </Cell>
              <Cell>
                <Type>autoValue</Type>
                <Content>date</Content>
                <Format>dd/MM/yyyy H:mm</Format>
                <Padding>2</Padding>
              </Cell>
            </Row>
          </Rows>
        </Table>
      </Tables>
    </Template>
    <Template name="A4_" username="A4 (No header)">
      <PageSize>210, 297</PageSize>      
    </Template>
  </Section>

```

### Map attributions[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/Print-Templates.html#map-attributions)
### Text attributions[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/Print-Templates.html#text-attributions)
The map attributions are collected from each map source specified in the print. The particular attributions are merged into one text. This merged attribution can be placed to the print using cell type `autoValue` and its content set to `attributions`.
If you need a transparent background for attribution, you have to create a transparent table and set the background color for all other cells to white. An example of such a table is shown bellow.
[![2024-11-08_10h41_52.png](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/.attachments/2024-11-08_10h41_52-f84d801f-07ef-4d24-8847-a7f372156291.png)](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/.attachments/2024-11-08_10h41_52-f84d801f-07ef-4d24-8847-a7f372156291.png)

```
<Table>
    <Position>BottomRight</Position>
    <BorderColor>Black</BorderColor>
    <BackgroundColor>0,0,0,0</BackgroundColor>
    <Rows>
        <Row>
            <Cell>
                <Type>autoValue</Type>
                <Content>attributions</Content>
                <Padding>0,2,2,0</Padding>
                <ColumnSpan>3</ColumnSpan>
                <Borders>0,0,0.5,0</Borders>
                <HorizontalAlignment>right</HorizontalAlignment>
            </Cell>
        </Row>
        <Row>
            <Cell>
                <Type>label</Type>
                <Content>Printed by</Content>
                <Width>25</Width>
                <Padding>2,0,0,2</Padding>
                <Borders>0.5,0,0,0.5</Borders>
                <BackgroundColor>#FFFFFF</BackgroundColor>
            </Cell>
            <Cell>
                <Type>fieldValue</Type>
                <Content>printedby</Content>
                <Width>50</Width>
                <Padding>2,0,0,2</Padding>
                <Borders>0.5,0,0,0</Borders>
                <BackgroundColor>#FFFFFF</BackgroundColor>
            </Cell>
            <Cell>
                <Type>image</Type>
                <Content>assets/images/hxgn-logo-color.png</Content>
                <RowSpan>5</RowSpan>
                <Width>50</Width>
                <Padding>0,2,0,2</Padding>
                <Borders>0.5,0.5,0.5,0</Borders>
                <BackgroundColor>#FFFFFF</BackgroundColor>
            </Cell>
        </Row>
        <Row>
            <Cell>
                <Type>label</Type>
                <Content>Remarks</Content>
                <RowSpan>2</RowSpan>
                <Padding>0,2,0,2</Padding>
                <Borders>0,0,0,0.5</Borders>
                <BackgroundColor>#FFFFFF</BackgroundColor>
            </Cell>
            <Cell>
                <Type>fieldValue</Type>
                <Content>notes</Content>
                <RowSpan>2</RowSpan>
                <Padding>0,2,0,2</Padding>
                <BackgroundColor>#FFFFFF</BackgroundColor>
            </Cell>
        </Row>
        <Row></Row>
        <Row>
            <Cell>
                <Type>label</Type>
                <Content>Scale</Content>
                <Padding>2,2,0,2</Padding>
                <Borders>0,0,0,0.5</Borders>
                <BackgroundColor>#FFFFFF</BackgroundColor>
            </Cell>
            <Cell>
                <Type>autoValue</Type>
                <Content>scale</Content>
                <Padding>2,2,0,2</Padding>
                <Borders>0,0,0,0</Borders>
                <BackgroundColor>#FFFFFF</BackgroundColor>
            </Cell>
        </Row>
        <Row>
            <Cell>
                <Type>label</Type>
                <Content>Date</Content>
                <Padding>2</Padding>
                <Borders>0,0,0.5,0.5</Borders>
                <BackgroundColor>#FFFFFF</BackgroundColor>
            </Cell>
            <Cell>
                <Type>autoValue</Type>
                <Content>date</Content>
                <Format>dd/MM/yyyy H:mm</Format>
                <Padding>2</Padding>
                <Borders>0,0,0.5,0</Borders>
                <BackgroundColor>#FFFFFF</BackgroundColor>
            </Cell>
        </Row>
    </Rows>
</Table>

```

#### An example of attributions text in a separate table positioned bottom left[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/Print-Templates.html#an-example-of-attributions-text-in-a-separate-table-positioned-bottom-left)

```
<Table>
    <Position>BottomLeft</Position>
    <BackgroundColor>0,0,0,0</BackgroundColor>
        <Rows>
            <Row>
                <Cell>
                    <Type>autoValue</Type>
                    <Content>attributions</Content>
                    <Padding>2,0,2,2</Padding>
                </Cell>
            </Row>
        </Rows>
</Table>

```

#### Google Maps/ Map Tiles[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/Print-Templates.html#google-maps-map-tiles)
Print made with Google products such as Map or Maps Tiles needs to be done with the Google logo placed in the resulting print. This logo and its position need to be defined in the print template using a cell of type `image`.
[![2024-11-08_11h05_28.png](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/.attachments/2024-11-08_11h05_28-cf3b216c-a041-4cdf-9016-9a238e39ff66.png)](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/.attachments/2024-11-08_11h05_28-cf3b216c-a041-4cdf-9016-9a238e39ff66.png)

```
<Table>

# Sidebar panels
The sidebar is the region on the left hand side of the portal which consists of multiple panels arranged in a tab page. The sidebar is defined in the function section of the workspace file e.g.

```
<Function name="sidebar">
    <Config>
        <JProperty name="items">
            <JArray>
                <JValue>legend</JValue>
                <JValue>job</JValue>
                <JValue>areas</JValue>
                <JValue>features</JValue>
                <JValue>search</JValue>
		<JValue>cad</JValue>
                <JValue>trace</JValue>
                <JValue>redline</JValue>
                <JValue>print</JValue>
            </JArray>
        </JProperty>
    </Config>
</Function>

```

Each value represents a panel. Panels can be re-ordered or removed as required.
Its possible to add a one or more custom panels which load content into an iframe which fills the sidebar. The content should be a HTML page. Note that the iframe (and its content) will not be loaded until the tab is selected by the user unless you make it the first tab which is automatically opened by the client on initialization.
To add a panel use XML of the following form

```
<add position="last" path="/config/Workspace[@name='default']/Section[@type='function']/Function[@name='sidebar']/Config/JProperty[@name='items']/JArray">
   <JObject>
      <JProperty name="xtype"><JValue>iframepanel</JValue></JProperty>
      <JProperty name="title"><JValue>Test</JValue></JProperty>				
      <JProperty name="url"><JValue>/path/content.html</JValue></JProperty>
      <JProperty name="id"><JValue>mysidebarpaneluniqueid</JValue></JProperty>
   </JObject>
</add>

```

There are three attributes that must be set:
  1. xtype - This must always be set to 'iframepanel' as above.
  2. title - The text to display in the panels tab which can either be plain text or the key to a string resource.
  3. url - The link to the content. The URL can either be relative or absolute.

Optionally you can set an id property which can help to identify the panel when using scripts. The value of an id is any string but it needs to be unique across all potential side bar panels that could be added to avoid conflicts. The recommendation is to prefix the identifier with a value that represents your office. For example, I work for Hexagon S&I in the danish office so I would use 'hxgnsi-dk-mysidebarpanel'.

###### Structure

# Import
The `<Import>` element instructs the workspace loader to load workspace xml from other files which can then be referenced by workspaces in the current file. The intention is, if manually maintaining workspaces, to simplify maintenance by splitting configuration over multiple files. However there usage has been largely superseded, see the note below.
`<Import>` elements must be direct children of the document root element and are processed in the sequence they appear in a file. An `<Import>` must appear before any references to the content they include. The element must contain a valid file path. The file path can be either absolute or relative e.g.

```
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8" ?>
<config>
  <Import>..\printtemplates\default.xml</Import>
  ...

```

If the path is relative then it is relative to the location of the file being read.
##### Note
If the portal is configured to load workspace files from a folder then the import element is not required if the file to be imported has an `.xml` extension and is in the same folder or sub folder. If such cases the file will automatically be read regardless. See [File location and loading](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/File-location-and-loading.html) for more information.

# Section
A `<Section>` element is a container for individual configuration items. The type of item a section can contain is defined by the sections _type_ attribute. This attribute is required. `<Section>` elements can be either direct children of the document root element or direct children of `<Workspace>` elements.
The _type_ attribute can have the following values:
  * `editor` - Configuration for the legacy [feature editor](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/Feature-Editor.html).
  * `function` - Configures available [sidebar panels](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/Sidebar-panels.html) and [toolbars](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/Toolbars-and-buttons.html).
  * `maplegend` - Defines map [legends](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/Map-Legend.html).
  * `mapsource` - Configuration for [map sources](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/Map-sources.html).
  * `print` - Configures available [print templates](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/Print-Templates.html).
  * `plugins` - Configuration for Portal plugins.
  * `query` - Configuration of [external query](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/External-queries.html) services.
  * `scripts` - Additional [scripts](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/Loading-extra-scripts.html) or CSS files to load into the Portal client.

Each direct child element of a `<Section>` is referred to as a configuration item. The child element names are validated against the type attribute so, for example, it is not valid to place map sources under the `maplegend` section. All configuration items have two attributes:
  1. _name_ which is used as the unique key of the element within the section and is used to reference that item from other items.
  2. _username_ which is used as a display string in the Portal client when relevant.

For example:

```
   ...
   <Section type="editor">
      <GtdwsEditor name="default">
         <DefaultType>Edit</DefaultType>
      </GtdwsEditor>
   </Section>
   <Section type="maplegend">
      <Legend name="default" username="All (EPSG:5678)">
   ...

```

When multiple configuration items within a section contain the same name, the last one read will replace the previous one.
When multiple `<Section>` elements of the same _type_ exist then they are merged. Effectively configuration items from subsequent sections are added to the first and will overwrite existing ones if they have the same name.
## Referencing global configuration items[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/Structure/Section.html#referencing-global-configuration-items)
A `<Section>` that is defined as a direct child of the document root element is referred to as a _global_ section. The items contained within the section are _global_ configuration items.
A `<Section>` element that is a direct child of a `<Workspace>` can reference configuration items of a global `<Section>` of the same _type_. The intention is that a configuration items can be defined once and included in multiple workspaces.
Referencing can be done in one of two ways.
A `<Section>` can include all configuration items defined in a global section by specifying the _all_ attribute and setting it to `true` e.g.

```
<config>
   ...
   <!-- This is the global section -->
   <Section type="scripts">
      <Script name="sc1"><Url>/giniusfonts/giniusfonts.css</Url></Script>
      <Script name="sc2"><Url>/website/custom.js</Url></Script>
   </Section>
   ...
   <Workspace name="default">
      ...
      <!-- This is the workspace section -->
      <Section type="scripts" all="true"/>

```

In this case the workspace named `default` will include both script configuration items, `sc1` and `sc2`.
Alternatively a `<Section>` can contain a list of _named_ configuration items defined in the global section. This is done by adding configuration items with the same element name and name value e.g.

```
<config>
   ...
   <!-- This is the global section -->
   <Section type="scripts">
      <Script name="sc1"><Url>/giniusfonts/giniusfonts.css</Url></Script>
      <Script name="sc2"><Url>/website/custom.js</Url></Script>
   </Section>
   ...
   <Workspace name="default">
      ...
      <!-- This is the workspace section -->
      <Section type="scripts">
         <Script name="sc1" />
      </Section>

```

In this case only the script configuration item called `sc1` will be included in the workspace named `default`.

# Workspace
A `<Workspace>` element must be a direct child of the document root element. It has two required attributes.
  1. `name` The identifier for the workspace. It is used as part of the portal client URL so it should only contain ascii letters, digits and `-` or `_` characters.
  2. `username` The display name for the workspace.

Under the element there can be the following child elements.
  * `<Services>` List of Networks services URLs (e.g. Dialog, Analytical etc.).
  * `<DatabaseAlias>` Used together with the solution service to locate detail WMS services and other services (e.g. Dialog, Analytical) if not defined under `<Services>`.
  * `<GTechConfiguration>` Required by netplot, netexport and coordinate system services.
  * `<RequiresAuth>` and `<Claims>`. See [Workspace filtering](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/Workspace-filtering.html).
  * `<Settings>` See [Workspace settings](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/Workspace-settings.html).
  * `<Section>` Can occur multiple times with different type attributes.

Other than `<Section>` elements, other child elements should only occur once under a `<Workspace>` element.
**Examples**

```
  <Workspace name="default" username="Default">
    <DatabaseAlias>DBALIAS</DatabaseAlias>
    <GTechConfiguration>NETWORKS</GTechConfiguration>
    <Services>
       <SolutionService>NetworksSolutionService</SolutionService>
       <CoordinateSystemsService>NetworksCoordinateSystemService</CoordinateSystemsService>
       <DirectPlotService>NetPlot</DirectPlotService>
       <DirectExportService>NetExport</DirectExportService>
    </Services>
    ...

```

The above is the simplest example. URLs can be specified as absolute or relative. If relative as above then they are relative to the application base URL defined in the web.config file. Alternatively you can specify the URL to the NetWorks server by adding a `<ServicesBaseUrl>` element and relative URLs will be relative to that e.g.

```
  <Workspace name="default" username="Default">
    <DatabaseAlias>DBALIAS</DatabaseAlias>
    <GTechConfiguration>NETWORKS</GTechConfiguration>
    <Services>
       <ServicesBaseUrl>https://my.server.com</ServicesBaseUrl>
       <SolutionService>NetworksSolutionService</SolutionService>
       <CoordinateSystemsService>NetworksCoordinateSystemService</CoordinateSystemsService>
       <DirectPlotService>NetPlot</DirectPlotService>
       <DirectExportService>NetExport</DirectExportService>
    </Services>
    ...

```

For any services which are not defined the portal will query the Solution service for them.
##### Note
The Solution service does not return URLs for netplot, netexport or the Coordinate Systems Service. Alternatively, if no WMS services for detail/schematic legends are deployed you can define all the service URLs here and exclude the Solution service from the list e.g.

```
  <Workspace name="default" username="Default">
    <GTechConfiguration>NETWORKS</GTechConfiguration>
    <Services>
       <ServicesBaseUrl>https://my.server.com</ServicesBaseUrl>
       <AnalyticalService>AnalyticalService</AnalyticalService>
       <CoordinateSystemsService>NetworksCoordinateSystemService</CoordinateSystemsService>
       <DataTransferService>DataTransferService</DataTransferService>
       <DialogWebService>Gtdws</DialogWebService>
       <DirectExportService>NetExport</DirectExportService>
       <DirectPlotService>NetPlot</DirectPlotService>
       <DynamicWMSService>DynamicWMSService</DynamicWMSService>
       <JobService>JobService</JobService>
       <WorkService>http://localhost:9402/</WorkService>
    </Services>
    ...

```

Without the solution service the portal will not query it for service URLs. This can used to exclude functionality for users. For example, if you exclude the JobService element then job service functionality will not be available to users.
Note also that if the service is not on the [same origin](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Security/Same-origin_policy) as defined by the services base URL then you must specify the URL as an absolute URL. In the above example the work service is on a different port so it is specified as an absolute URL.

# Structure
Each workspace XML file contains a single root element `<config>`. Under the root element there can be:
  * One or more [<Import>](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/Structure/Import.html) elements.
  * One or more [<Section>](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/Structure/Section.html) elements.
  * One or more [<Workspace>](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/Structure/Workspace.html) elements.

# Toolbars and buttons
## Overview[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/Toolbars-and-buttons.html#overview)
There are multiple toolbars which can be configured by removing buttons or adding custom buttons.
  1. `toolbar` - The main toolbar position across the top of the map.
  2. `zoomtoolbar` - The secondary toolbar positioned at the bottom right hand corner of the map.
  3. `coordinatestoolbar`- The toolbar about the bottom of the map.
  4. `gtdwstoolbar` - The toolbar across the top of the (old) feature editor (optional).
  5. `featurepanel` - The toolbar at the top of the 'Features' sidebar panel.
  6. `resultsgrid` - Defines the toolbar at the top of the 'Search' sidebar panel, the toolbar above the results grid in the 'Query' dialog and the toolbar in the 'Trace results' dialog.
  7. `redlinetoolbar` - Defines the main toolbar in the 'Redline' sidebar panel (optional).

Toolbars are defined in the `function` section of the workspace file e.g.

```
<Function name="toolbar">
    <Config>
        <JProperty name="items">
            <JArray>
                <JValue>sidebarcollapse</JValue>
                <JValue>mapselectmenu</JValue>
                <JValue>maptooltip</JValue>
                <JValue>mapzoomextent</JValue>
                <JValue>maprotate</JValue>
                <JValue>maplock</JValue>
                <JValue>maphome</JValue>
                <JValue>mapgeographic</JValue>                        
                <JValue>query</JValue>
                <JValue>detailssearch</JValue>
                <JValue>menu</JValue>
            </JArray>
        </JProperty>
    </Config>
</Function>

```

The values are the default buttons. The button order can re-arranged and buttons can be removed. However buttons should not be moved from one toolbar to another.
## Optional toolbars[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/Toolbars-and-buttons.html#optional-toolbars)
Both the `gtdwstoolbar` and `redlinetoolbar` are optional configurations which are not included in the workspace by default. The contents of the `redlinetoolbar` can be completely redefined by adding the following to the `function` section of the workspace and changing it as required.

```
<Function name="redlinetoolbar">
    <Config>
        <JProperty name="items">
            <JArray>
                <JValue>redlineappend</JValue>
                <JValue>redlinesaveas</JValue>
                <JValue>redlinedeleteall</JValue>
                <JValue>redlineactivatecategory</JValue>
                <JValue>redlinefitall</JValue>
                <JValue>redlineplaceline</JValue>
                <JValue>redlineplacelinestring</JValue>
                <JValue>redlineplacefreehandlinestring</JValue>                        
                <JValue>redlineplacepolygon</JValue>
                <JValue>redlineplacecircle</JValue>
                <JValue>redlineplacerectangle</JValue>
                <JValue>redlineplacetext</JValue>
                <JValue>redlineplacesymbol</JValue>
                <JValue>redlineedit</JValue>
                <JValue>redlinegroupops</JValue>
            </JArray>
        </JProperty>
    </Config>
</Function>

```

The `gtdwstoolbar` has a set of mandatory buttons which cannot be removed, however, custom buttons can be added to the toolbar by adding a section like the following.

```
<Function name="gtdwstoolbar">
   <Config>
      <JProperty name="items">
         <JArray>
            <JObject>
		<JProperty name="xtype" type="string" value="actionbutton" />
		<JProperty name="iconCls" type="string" value="x-fa fa-bolt" />
		<JProperty name="tooltip" type="string" value="Test Action"/>
		<JProperty name="actionName" type="string" value="testaction"/>	
                <JProperty name="position" type="number" value="2"/>							
            </JObject>						
	</JArray>
      </JProperty>
   </Config>
</Function>

```

The position property allows you to place the button at a certain position amongst the mandatory buttons. For the `gtdwstoolbar` these mandatory buttons are:

```
[
   'editorreload',
   'editoropendetails',
   'tbfill',
   'editoreditgeometry',
   'editorresetgeometry',
   'editorsavegeometry',
   'editorsaveattributes',
   'editoraddcomponent',
   'editordeletefeature',
   'featurefit',
   'close'
]

```

## Custom buttons[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/Toolbars-and-buttons.html#custom-buttons)
In addition to the default buttons custom buttons can be added to the toolbars. There are three basic types of buttons which can be added to the portal clients toolbars. These are:
  1. Action buttons. When a user clicks on an action button a notification is published by the application which can be picked up via the [API](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/API/Notifications.html) and acted upon. Their state (e.g. enabled or not) can also be changed via the [API](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/API/%24NWP/toolbar.html).
  2. Link buttons. When clicked link buttons can be configured to open a URL in a new browser window/tab or open it within an iframe embedded on a floating window within the client.
  3. Draw button. This button can be configured to, on click, set the map to allow the user to draw a geometry of a specific type. Once the geometry is drawn then geometry is converted to GeoJSON and published as a notification by the application.

All buttons have the following properties:  
| Name  | Type  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| xtype  | {string}  | The type of the button  |  
| [icon]  | {string}  | Optional path to a graphics file. SVG is preferred. The icon should be sized to 24x24 pixels and be monochrome (color should be `#666`).  |  
| [iconCls]  | {string}  | Optional name of a CSS class which points to a font icon, instead of using an icon file.  |  
| [text]  | {string}  | Optional button label. Can either be text or key to a string resource. Not generally recommended, use the tooltip instead.  |  
| [tooltip]  | {string}  | Optional tooltip text. Can either be text or key to a string resource.  |  
| [visible]  | {boolean}  | Determines if the button is initially visible. Default is true.  |  
| [disabled]  | {boolean}  | Sets the button to be initially disabled. Default is false.  |  
| [position]  | {number}  | Optional. Allows you to specify the position at which a button is added. Only relevant for `gtdwstoolbar`.  |  
The types (xtype) of buttons available are:
### "actionbutton"[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/Toolbars-and-buttons.html#actionbutton)
Additional properties  
| Name  | Type  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| actionName  | {string}  | Name sent with the notification  |  
| [toggleGroup]  | {string}  | Enables buttons with the same toggle group to act as a radio button set.  |  
| [enableToggle]  | {boolean}  | If true allows the button to be a toggle button. If toggleGroup is set then this is automatically set to true.  |  
On click sends out the notification 'actionbuttonpress' with the following argument.  
| Name  | Type  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| data  | {Object}  |   |  
| data.name  | {string}  | Set to actionName.  |  
## "drawactionbutton"[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/Toolbars-and-buttons.html#drawactionbutton)
Additional properties  
| Name  | Type  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| actionName  | {string}  | Name sent with the notification.  |  
| drawMode  | {string}  | The draw mode to start.  |  
The draw mode can be set to either drawpoint, drawline, drawpolygon, drawrectangle or drawcircle. On click sets the map to the mode defined in drawMode. Once the user completes drawing the geometry sends of the notification 'drawactionbuttonpress' with the following argument.  
| Name  | Type  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| data  | {Object}  |   |  
| data.name  | {string}  | Set to actionName.  |  
| data.feature  | {Object}  | Set to the geometry as a GeoJSON feature.  |  
### "featureactionbutton"[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/Toolbars-and-buttons.html#featureactionbutton)
Additional properties  
| Name  | Type  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| actionName  | {string}  | Name sent with the notification  |  
| [enableOnFNOs]  | {number[]}  | Optional comma separated list of FNOs which when selected will enabled this button.  |  
| [disableOnFNOs]  | {number[]}  | Optional comma separated list of FNOs which when selected will disable this button.  |  
Button is only enabled when a feature is selected. On click sends out the notification 'featureactionbuttonpress' with the following argument.  
| Name  | Type  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| data  | {Object}  |   |  
| data.name  | {string}  | Set to actionName.  |  
| data.feature  | {Object}  | Currently selected features as GeoJSON feature.  |
