#### Placement

# Coordinates Toolbar
## Overview[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Placement/Coordinates-Toolbar.html#overview)
In a default configuration the coordinates toolbar has the following elements.
  1. Collapse/uncollapse toolbar
  2. Coordinate system picklist
  3. Coordinate field
  4. Copy coordinate
  5. Paste coordinate
  6. Select coordinate
  7. Center map
  8. Place coordinate
  9. Draw measuring line
  10. Draw measuring area
  11. Clear measure geometry and markers

The toolbar allows users to query geometry for their coordinates and place markers at precise coordinates. These markers can then be used to place other geometry such as redlines or feature geometry via the feature editor plugin.
## Coordinate system picklist[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Placement/Coordinates-Toolbar.html#coordinate-system-picklist)
The picklist display the list from the NetWorks Coordinate System Service. See [GetCoordSystemParameters](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Coordinate-System-Service/GetCoordSystemParameters.html). The picklist is only available if the service returns a coordinate system which matches the projection defined for the legend in the portal. Matching is done first on the attribute EPSGCrs returned by the service and then on Name. The EPSG code can be defined in the coordinate system editor delivered with the core product.
Changing the selection in the picklist will transform the coordinate from the previous coordinate system to the new one.
## Coordinate field[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Placement/Coordinates-Toolbar.html#coordinate-field)
The coordinate displayed is determined by the selection in the coordinate system picklist. If the picklist is not available then the coordinate display will be in the legends projection. The order of the coordinate (e.g. latitude, longitude or longitude, latitude) and how it is formatted can be altered via the settings dialog under 'Precision Coordinates'. Changes in the settings dialog are applied the next time the field is updated.
The field will by default automatically update when the map is moved or zoomed with the new center coordinate of the map view. This behavior can be switched on and off via the settings dialog.
Pressing ENTER in the coordinate field places a marker.
## Copy coordinate[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Placement/Coordinates-Toolbar.html#copy-coordinate)
The copy function is only available if the portal is running in a [secure context](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Security/Secure_Contexts) and the user has not otherwise disabled permissions to the clipboard, otherwise it will be disabled.
The copy function will copy the coordinate as displayed using coordinate number separator defined in the settings dialog.
## Paste coordinate[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Placement/Coordinates-Toolbar.html#paste-coordinate)
The paste function is only available if the portal is running in a [secure context](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Security/Secure_Contexts) and the user has not otherwise disabled permissions to the clipboard, otherwise it will be disabled.
For the paste to function correctly the coordinate text being pasted must use the decimal place and coordinate number separators defined in the settings dialog for 'Precision Coordinates'.
It is not possible to paste a coordinate if the decimal place and coordinate number separator used are the same character.
## Select coordinate[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Placement/Coordinates-Toolbar.html#select-coordinate)
This is a toggle button. While active, clicking on the map will update the coordinate field with the coordinate selected transformed to the selected coordinate system.
## Center map[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Placement/Coordinates-Toolbar.html#center-map)
This will center the map on the coordinate displayed in the field, transformed from the selected coordinate system to the map legends projection.
## Place coordinate[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Placement/Coordinates-Toolbar.html#place-coordinate)
This will place a marker at the coordinate displayed in the field, transformed from the selected coordinate system to the map legends projection. Markers can be snapped too allow for precise placement. If the selected coordinate system is the same as the legend then the coordinate displayed will that which is exported to, for example, redline XML.
Whether a coordinate label is shown with the marker or not is controlled via the settings dialog under 'Measure'. The coordinate label will contain the coordinate as displayed in the coordinate field.
## Draw measuring line[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Placement/Coordinates-Toolbar.html#draw-measuring-line)
This will switch the map to a mode allowing the user to place a polyline geometry with optionally segment length labels and a total length label at the last point. What labels are displayed are controlled via the settings dialog under 'Measure'.
Whether the lengths displayed are the geodesic length or projected length is also controlled via the settings dialog under 'Measure'.
The number of decimal places is controlled by the setting `measure.precision`. The decimal separator comes from the localized string `common.format.decimalSeparator` which is the default for the portal.
## Draw measuring area[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Placement/Coordinates-Toolbar.html#draw-measuring-area)
This will switch the map to a mode allowing the user to place a polygon geometry with optionally segment length labels and a total area label. What labels are displayed are controlled via the settings dialog under 'Measure'.
Whether the lengths and area are calculated using geodesic length or projected length is also controlled via the settings dialog under 'Measure'.
The number of decimal places is controlled by the setting `measure.precision`. The decimal separator comes from the localized string `common.format.decimalSeparator` which is the default for the portal.

# Snapping
Snapping allows the user to select vertices (coordinates) and/or edges (line segments) of existing geometry without needing to be pixel perfect with the positioning of their pointing device. When in snapping mode a small dot will appear by the cursor as the user moves the mouse cursor close to a geometry if a snapping point is available on that geometry the dot will automatically move to that point. Activating the pointing device (e.g. clicking the left mouse button) will select the point where the dot is.
Snapping is available for many functions in the portal including:
  * Draw measuring line or area
  * Draw or edit redlines
  * Feature Editor plugin place geometry
  * Select coordinate
  * Place print frame

The following geometry can be snapped too:
  * Redlines
  * Measuring geometry and coordinate markers
  * Geometry from the NetWorks Vector Service

Currently two types of snapping are available
  1. Snap to vertex. Will snap to point geometry, corners and end points of lines and corners in outlines of areas.
  2. Snap to edge. Will snap to any point on line segments between two vertices.

Snapping will occur while enabled and the geometry are visible Snapping can be enabled and disabled via the Settings dialog in the portal. Changes made in Settings are applied immediately and are saved between sessions.
The sensitivity of snapping can also be adjusted in the settings dialog by adjusting the number in 'Pixel tolerance'. The larger number the further away the geometry can be from the cursor for snapping to occur.

# Placement
This section details the tools and options for placing geometry in the portal.

#### Plugin-API

# Configuration
## Introduction[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Plugin-API/Configuration.html#introduction)
It is expected that the configuration of a plugin will be different from one hosting application to another. For example in the Portal the Feature Data Service is accessed via HTTP(S), so it requires a URL to the service to be configured. Whereas in Core Mobile it is part of the client application so it is not required.
Also the way configuration is encoded will also be different. On the portal the configuration will be encoded as part of the workspace XML, whereas in Core Mobile it will be encoded in a JSON file included in the package with the plugin itself.
However the structures for defining configuration will be common.
## Root configuration[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Plugin-API/Configuration.html#root-configuration)
At its root the configuration will be a single object with the following properties.  
| Property name  | Data type  | Required  | Remark  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| identifier  | string(100)  | No  | A unique value used to tie the configuration to a particular plugin. Defaults to typeIdentifier.  |  
| typeIdentifier  | string(100)  | Yes  | A unique value that identifies the functionality that the plugin provides. Defined by the plugin implementor.  |  
| path  | string(500)  | Yes  | Can be used to define the entry point into the plugin.  |  
| parameters  | JSON Object  | No  | Additional configuration parameters for the plugin e.g. customized settings, mappings etc.  |  
| services  | Enumerable  | No  | Configuration for each service.  |  
The identifier property is used to associate the configuration with a plugin instance and when passing messages to identify the source and potentially the target of a message. This will default to the typeIdentifier property however if there are multiple instances of the plugin hosted in the same client application then the administrator who is configuring the system will need to set it to a unique value.
The typeIdentifier property is used by the hosting application, and potentially other plugins, to identify what functionality the plugin provides. It is up to the plugin supplier to define and document the value it should be set to. Care should be taken when defining it that it does not clash with other plugins. Using a UUID string is recommended.
The path property defines the URL that will be applied to the iframe or WebView to load the plugin. It is (currently) envisaged that a plugin will have a single entry point and will request dynamic parameters, for example, current map selection from the hosting application after it has started.
The parameters property is made directly available to the plugin as a JSON _object_ (as opposed to an array or null value for example). From the perspective of the API it is a purely generic representation of a JSON object. It is up to the plugin supplier to define and document what structure (if any) it contains. It is recommended that the parameters when expressed as a JSON string is limited to 20KB to prevent overloading of the host applications memory.
The services property defines a list of service configurations as defined in the next section.
## Service configuration[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Plugin-API/Configuration.html#service-configuration)
The majority of functionality provided to a plugin is via client services and the services available to a plugin is defined in configuration. Each service configuration is a single object with the following properties.  
| Property name  | Data type  | Required  | Remark  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| identifier  | string(100)  | No  | Uniquely identifies the service for the plugin.  |  
| typeIdentifier  | string(100)  | Yes  | Defines the API that the service provides. Defined by the service implementor.  |  
| path  | string(500)  | No  | URL to the service if required.  |  
The identifier property is used by the plugin to call the service. It defaults to the service typeIdentifier so is not required to be set unless multiple instances of the same service are associated with the plugin.
The typeIdentifier property is used by the hosting application to identify what functionality the service provides. It is up to the service supplier to define and document the value it should be set to. Care should be taken when defining it that it does not clash with other services. Using a UUID string is recommended.
The path property is used for external services to define the URL to that service.

##### Host-interface

# IInternalPlatformInfo
## Overview[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Plugin-API/Host-interface/IInternalPlatformInfo.html#overview)
The platform information service returns information about the hosting application and the environment it is being executed in.

```
export interface IInternalPlatformInfo {
    /**
    * Return the name of the hosting application
    */
    readonly applicationName: string;
    /**
     * Return the version of the hosting application
     */
    readonly applicationVersion: string;
    /**
     * Return a set of tags which can help identify the underlying platform characteristics
     */
    readonly tags: Set<string>;
    /**
     * Returns a string representing the preferred language of the platform as defined by RFC 5646.
     */
    readonly language: string;
}

```

**NOTE** The result of applicationName is not well defined currently. This will be improved in future releases.
The property 'tags' is not currently used and may be removed or replaced in future releases.

# IInternalPluginConfig
## Overview[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Plugin-API/Host-interface/IInternalPluginConfig.html#overview)
The configuration plugin interface represents the configuration which has been supplied for the plugin. It is defined as follows.

```
export interface IInternalPluginConfig {
    /** The plugin identifier as defined by the system administrator. */
    readonly identifier: string;
    /** The plugin type identifier as defined by the plugin supplier. */
    readonly typeIdentifier: string;
    /** The plugins start up path */
    readonly path: string;
    /** The plugins parameters */
    readonly parameters: IObject;
    /** The list of services associated with the plugin. */
    readonly services: IInternalServiceConfig[];
}

```

The service configuration interface is defined as

```
export default interface IInternalServiceConfig {
    readonly identifier: string;
    readonly typeIdentifier: string;
    readonly path: string;
}

```

See the section on [configuration](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Plugin-API/Configuration.html) for more information about the properties and their usage.

# IInternalRequestFactory
## Overview[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Plugin-API/Host-interface/IInternalRequestFactory.html#overview)
The request factory gives access to the hosting application client services. It is based in part on the Fetch API available in modern browsers.
The request factory function takes a plugin identifier, a service identifier and a set of arguments and returns a request object. From the request object the service response can, asynchronously, be read.

```
export interface IInternalRequestFactory {
    (pluginId: string, serviceId: string, args: IInternalRequestArgs): IInternalRequest;
}

```

**NOTE:** That request body arguments and responses are limited to JSON objects.
### Request arguments[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Plugin-API/Host-interface/IInternalRequestFactory.html#request-arguments)

```
export interface IInternalRequestArgs {
    /**
    * The request path, appended to the services root path.
    * Equivalent to a HTTP path and query string. Uses the same encoding as that.
    */
    path: string;
    /**
     * The body of the request. Equivalent to an HTTP request body. If body is set to a javascript object and if no content-type header has been defined the one should
     * be added and set to 'application/json'.
     */
    body?: string | object;
    /**
     * The HTTP method that should be used.
     */
    method?: string;
    /**
     * HTTP headers as key value pairs. Defaults to GET unless a body is provided in which case POST.
     */
    headers?: { [key: string]: string }
    /**
     * If set to true then where relevant indicates to the host that it should cache the request response and if a response is already cached then it should return that rather than
     * making a request. It is the host that controls caching (if it caches at all). If body is set this argument is ignored.
     */
    cache?: boolean;
}

```

### Request object[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Plugin-API/Host-interface/IInternalRequestFactory.html#request-object)

```
export interface IInternalRequest {
    /** Return the requests response. */
    response(): Promise<IInternalResponse>;
    /** Abort the request. */
    abort(): void;
}

```

### Response object[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Plugin-API/Host-interface/IInternalRequestFactory.html#response-object)

```
export interface IInternalResponse {
    /**
     * Returns true if the request completed successfully
     */
    readonly ok: boolean;
    /**
     * Returns the numeric status value of the request
     */
    readonly status: number;
    /**
     * Return the response headers 
     */
    readonly headers: { [key: string]: string }
    /**
     * Parse the response body as json and return it.
     */
    json(): Promise<any>;
    /**
     * Return the response body as a string.
     */
    text(): Promise<string>;
}

```

The text() function is not currently be used and may be removed in future releases.

# IInternalStateManager
## Overview[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Plugin-API/Host-interface/IInternalStateManager.html#overview)
The state manager allows a plugin to store and retrieve state encoded as JSON against its own identifier and an arbitrary key.

```
export interface IInternalStateManager {
    /**
     * Returns the data associated with key. Returns null if no data is available.
     */
    get(pluginId: string, key: string): Promise<any>;
    /**
     * Store data and associate it with the value key. Overwrites existing data stored against key.
     */
    set(pluginId: string, key: string, data: any): Promise<boolean>;
    /**
     * Return true if data has been stored against key.
     */
    has(pluginId: string, key: string): Promise<boolean>;
    /**
     * Remove key and its associated data.
     */
    remove(pluginId: string, key: string): Promise<boolean>;
    /**
     * Clear all data
     */
    clear(pluginId: string): Promise<boolean>;
}

```

# IUserInfo
## Overview[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Plugin-API/Host-interface/IUserInfo.html#overview)
The user information interface provides the plugin information about the current user.

```
export interface IUserInfo {
    /**
     * Returns true if the current user is an anonymous user.
     */
    readonly isAnonymous: boolean;
    /**
     * Returns the user name
     */
    readonly name: string;
    /**
     * Returns the set of properties which have been published by the administrator (can be empty)
     */
    properties: Map<string, string>;
}

```

# Host interface
## Introduction[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Plugin-API/Host-interface.html#introduction)
The Host interface represents the client application to the plugin. Its primary purpose is to give the plugin access to the client services which the host defines. To get a reference to the host the following function must be called.
On HxGN NetWorks Core Portal:

```
$NWP.getPluginHost() : Promise<IInternalHost>

```

On HxGN NetWorks Core Mobile:

```
NWM.getPluginHost() : Promise<IInternalHost>

```

The host interface itself is defined as follows.

```
export interface IInternalHost {
    /**
     * Returns the plugins configuration
     */
    getConfiguration(pluginId: string): Promise<IInternalPluginConfig>;
    /**
     * Returns information about the platform the host is running on.
     */
    getPlatformInfo(): Promise<IInternalPlatformInfo>;
    /**
     * Returns information about the current user.
     */
    getUserInfo(): Promise<IUserInfo>;
    /**
     * Returns an object onto which plugin objects can add event listeners too.
     */
    getEventTarget(): Promise<IEventTarget>;
    /**
     * Returns the hosts state manager for plugins
     */
    getStateManager(): Promise<IInternalStateManager>;
    /**
     * Return whether the host is connected to networks services
     */
    isConnected(): Promise<boolean>;
    /**
     * Factory function to create requests.
     */
    createRequest: IInternalRequestFactory;    
}

```

The functions getConfiguration(), getPlatformInfo() and getUserInfo() return information to the plugin.
The function getEventTarget() is not currently used and will probably be removed and replaced with a different mechanism in future releases.
The function getStateManager() returns an API which allows a plugin to store and retrieve simple state information with the client application.
The function isConnected() is not currently used and may be modified or replaced in future releases.
The function createRequest is a function which allows the plugin to call services.
The interfaces returned by these function are described in more detail in their respective sections.

##### Services

# Common Interfaces
## IServiceResult[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Plugin-API/Services/Common-Interfaces.html#iserviceresult)
Standard result wrapper from services which indicates whether an operation was successful and optionally indicates the error if not.

```
export interface IServiceResult {
    /**
     * Indicates if the operation was successful 
     */
    success: boolean;
    /**
     * If the operation was not successful indicates to the plugin why not. 
     * It is assumed that the host will prompt the user with a message if necessary.
     */
    error?: IError;
}

```

```
export interface IError {
    /**
     * Error code. 
     */
    code: string;
    /**
     * Error detail (additional value or identifier). 
     */
    value?: string;
}

```

## IGeometryFeature[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Plugin-API/Services/Common-Interfaces.html#igeometryfeature)
Functionally equivalent to a GTech geometry component in a structure similar to a GeoJSON feature. Geometry is always defined using NetworksJson structures.

```
export interface IGeometryFeature {
    /**
     * Type identifier, always returns "NetworksFeature"
     */
    readonly type = "NetworksFeature";
    /**
     * Geometry expressed as a networks json geometry
     */
    readonly geometry: IGeometry;
    /**
     * Feature properties
     */
    readonly properties: IGeometryFeatureProperties;
}

```

```
export interface IGeometryFeatureProperties {
    /**
     * String formatted as {G3E_FID},{G3E_FNO},{G3E_CID},{G3E_CNO}
     * For new features fid and cid should be set to -1
     */
    ID?: string;
    /**
     * Style identifier
     */
    SNO?: number;
    /**
     * Is detail/schematic
     */
    detail?: boolean;
    /**
     * Detail/schematic identifier
     */
    DETAILID?: number;
    /**
     * Other properties
     */
    [propName: string]: number | string | boolean | null | undefined;
}

```

```
/**
 * Defines a networks json geometry. The properties of a geometry depend on the geometry type. See design specification for examples.
 */
export interface IGeometry {
    type: GeometryType;
}

```

# File storage
## Description[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Plugin-API/Services/File-storage.html#description)
Allows a plugin to maintain a collection of files which persists between sessions. It has the following functions.
NOTE: For hosts which are browser based, e.g. the Portal, the intention of this service is act as a wrapper around the Data Transfer Service. In this case the sid returned by "Create Storage" is in fact the tid return by the Data Transfer Service [BeginTransaction](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Data-Transfer-Service/BeginTransaction.html).
## Create Storage[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Plugin-API/Services/File-storage.html#create-storage)
Creates a new area for storage of files and returns its identifier
**Request arguments**  
| Name  | Value/Type  | Remarks  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| path  | "create"  |   |  
**Response json - ICreateStorageResult**

```
export interface ICreateStorageResult {
    /**
     * Indicates if the create operation was successful.
     */
    success: boolean;
    /**
     * Identifier for the storage.
     */
    sid?: string;
    /**
     * If the operation was not successful indicates to the plugin why not. 
     * It is assumed that the host will prompt the user with a message if necessary.
     */
    errorCode?: number;
}

```

## Add file[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Plugin-API/Services/File-storage.html#add-file)
Invokes an action in the host such as displaying a file selection dialog or opening a camera function. Once the action is completed the selected file(s) will be stored in storage identified by the supplied storage id parameter and the file names are returned.
**Request arguments**  
| Name  | Value/Type  | Remarks  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| path  | "addfile"  |   |  
| body  | IAddFileArgs  |   |  

```
export interface IAddFileArgs {
    /**
     * Storage identifier from create storage. 
     */
    sid: string; 
    /**
     * Optional message which the host can display to prompt the user. 
     * It is upto the host whether it uses the message or not.
     */
    message?: string;
    /**
     * List of file filters which the host can use to filter a file select dialog or directly open a camera function for example.
     * See https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Attributes/accept
     */
    accept?: string[];
    /**
     * Indicate to the host that the user should be allowed to select multiple files.
     */
    multiple?: boolean;
}

```

**Response json - IAddFileResult**

```
export interface IAddFileResult {
    /**
     * Indicates if the operation was successful 
     */
    success: boolean;
    /**
     * List of file names added.
     */
    fileNames?: string[];
    /**
     * If the operation was not successful indicates to the plugin why not. 
     * It is assumed that the host will prompt the user with a message if necessary.
     */
    errorCode?: number;
}

```

## Add JSON[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Plugin-API/Services/File-storage.html#add-json)
Takes a simple javascript object and converts it to a JSON string. Then writes that string to the specified file. If the file already exists then it should be replaced.
**Request arguments**  
| Name  | Value/Type  | Remarks  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| path  | "addjson"  |   |  
| body  | IAddJsonArgs  |   |  

```
export interface IAddJsonArgs {
    /**
     * Storage identifier from create storage. 
     */
    sid: string; 
    /**
     * The file name to store the json in. Must have a .json extension.
     */
    fileName: string;
    /**
     * The object to be converted to JSON. 
     */
    json: object;
}

```

**Response**

# FM Job
## Description[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Plugin-API/Services/FM-Job.html#description)
Allows the plugin to submit a collection of files from the plugins file storage service to the Networks feature transaction and job services. This service requires the host to be online and connected to networks services to function.
## Submit Job[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Plugin-API/Services/FM-Job.html#submit-job)
The precise workflow is dependent on the host application.
The submit job function takes one parameter `sid`. This is the storage id parameter returned from the file storage service when the create storage function is called and indicates the files to be submitted (via the [Work Service](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Features.html) to the [Feature Transaction](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Transaction-Service.html) and [Job Service](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Job-Service.html)(s). This will typically be done via the data transfer service.
There must be a file named _sid_ _request.json within the files to be submitted. This must be renamed to a specific file name and placed in a specific folder on the server i.e. `.well-known/request.json`. See the [Feature Editor detailed design specification](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Features/Interface-files.html) for more information. Also see [Data Transfer Service/UploadFile](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Data-Transfer-Service/UploadFile.html) for more information on uploading files into folders.
The file _sid_ _data.json is an intermediate file created by the plugin and can be ignored.
The other files should be uploaded to server without any path. Ideally they should be filtered and only files referenced by the `request.json` file uploaded. See the [Feature Editor detailed design specification](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Features/Interface-files.html) for more information on file fields.
If using the Data Transfer Service once all files have been uploaded. The service transaction should be committed with the following json, which triggers processing by the [Work Service](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Features.html).

```
{
   "type": "features",
   "process": true
}

```

The storage can then be discarded. See [Data Transfer Service/CommitTransaction](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Data-Transfer-Service/CommitTransaction.html) for more information.
**Request arguments**  
| Name  | Value/Type  | Remarks  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| path  | `submit?sid={sid}`  |   |  
**Response**
[IServiceResult](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Plugin-API/Services/Common-Interfaces.html#iserviceresult)
## Get List of Messages[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Plugin-API/Services/FM-Job.html#get-list-of-messages)
Wrapper for calling Data Transfer Service's [GetMessages endpoint](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Data-Transfer-Service/Messages/GetMessages.html). This response is used in a List of all Messages view. This service call does not have a required parameters, but as a part of a query string arguments plugin is able to send parameters for filtering, ordering, paging and value of a user to filter (see GetMessages documentation page for more information about arguments)
**Request arguments**  
| Name  | Value/Type  | Remarks  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| path  | `message/list[?filter={filter}&orderby=${orderby}&skip=${skip}&count=${count}&dbuser=${dbuser}&user=${user}]`  |   |  
**Response**
[IServiceResult](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Plugin-API/Services/Common-Interfaces.html#iserviceresult)
## Get List of Message Logs[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Plugin-API/Services/FM-Job.html#get-list-of-message-logs)
Wrapper for calling Data Transfer Service's [GetMessageLogs endpoint](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Data-Transfer-Service/Messages/GetMessageLogs.html). This response is used in a This service call takes one parameter `msgId`, which represents 'msgid' property of an actual Message, and user is also able to send as query string arguments parameters for paging (see GetMessageLogs documentation page for more information about arguments).  
| Name  | Value/Type  | Remarks  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| path  | `message/{msgId}/logs[?skip=${skip}&count=${count}]`  |   |  
**Response**
[IServiceResult](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Plugin-API/Services/Common-Interfaces.html#iserviceresult)
## Get state of Transaction[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Plugin-API/Services/FM-Job.html#get-state-of-transaction)
Wrapper for calling Data Transfer Service's [GetTransactionState endpoint](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Data-Transfer-Service/GetTransactionState.html). This call is used during Workset resubmission and resubmission of updated Workset JSON, to know if Transaction can/should be reverted and later submitted again. This call takes one argument `tid` which represents Transaction ID parameter of particular transaction.
**Request arguments**  
| Name  | Value/Type  | Remarks  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| path  | `transaction/{tid}/state`  |   |  
**Response**
[IServiceResult](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Plugin-API/Services/Common-Interfaces.html#iserviceresult)
## Revert Transaction[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Plugin-API/Services/FM-Job.html#revert-transaction)
Reverts the transaction to `OPEN` state. Wrapper for calling Data Transfer Service's [RevertTransaction endpoint](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Data-Transfer-Service/RevertTransaction.html). Takes one parameter `tid` which represents Transaction ID parameter of particular transaction.
**Request arguments** | Name | Value/Type | Remarks | |--|--|--| | path | `transaction/{tid}/revert` | | | method | POST | |
**Response**
[IServiceResult](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Plugin-API/Services/Common-Interfaces.html#iserviceresult)
## Commit Transaction[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Plugin-API/Services/FM-Job.html#commit-transaction)
Commits the Transaction. State of the Transaction will be set to `COMMITTED`. Wrapper for calling Data Transfer Service's [CommitTransaction endpoint](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Data-Transfer-Service/CommitTransaction.html). This endpoint is used for the resubmission of Workset, therefore body needs to be set exactly like the one specified in [Submit job](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Plugin-API/Services/FM-Job.html#submit-job).
**Request arguments**  
| Name  | Value/Type  | Remarks  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| path  | `transaction/{tid}`  |   |  
| method  | POST  |   |  
| body  | `{"type": "features", "process": true}`  |   |  
**Response json - IServiceResult**
## Read transaction file[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Plugin-API/Services/FM-Job.html#read-transaction-file)
Reads Transaction file which is shown is Show Workset JSON view. Wrapper for calling Data Transfer service's [GetTransactionFile enpoint](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Data-Transfer-Service/GetTransactionFile.html). Takes two mandatory parameters `tid`, which represents Transaction Id of particular transaction and `file` which represents the name of the file, and `path` which is optional and represents URL-encoded relatiove path to a file.
**Request arguments**  
| Name  | Value/Type  | Remarks  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| path  | `transaction/tid/file?file={file}[&path={path}]`  |   |  
**Response**
[IServiceResult](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Plugin-API/Services/Common-Interfaces.html#iserviceresult)
## Update message state[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Plugin-API/Services/FM-Job.html#update-message-state)
Updates the state of the message. Wrapper for calling Data Transfer's service [UpdateMessageState endpoint](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Data-Transfer-Service/Messages/UpdateMessageState.html). Takes two mandatory parameters `msgId` which represents the Message Id of message that is being updated and and `state` which represents new state of the message.
**Request arguments**  
| Name  | Value/Type  | Remarks  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| path  | `message/{msgId}/state/{state}`  |   |  
| method  | POST  |   |  
**Response**
[IServiceResult](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Plugin-API/Services/Common-Interfaces.html#iserviceresult)
## Upload request File[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Plugin-API/Services/FM-Job.html#upload-request-file)
Uploads update Workset JSON into Data Transfer service. Wrapper for calling Data Transfer Service's [UploadFile endpoint](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Data-Transfer-Service/UploadFile.html). Takes mandatory parameter `tid` which represents the Transaction Id of the Transaction the file is being uploaded into. The file itself is being sent within request body in a JSON format (serialized as string).
**Request arguments**  
| Name  | Value/Type  | Remarks  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| path  | `transaction/{tid}/file?file=request.json&path=.well-known`  |   |  
| method  | POST  |   |  
| body  | content of the file serialized into JSON string  |   |  
**Response**
[IServiceResult](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Plugin-API/Services/Common-Interfaces.html#iserviceresult)

# Interactive Placement
## Description[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Plugin-API/Services/Interactive-Placement.html#description)
Allows the plugin to invoke a geometry capture process and returns a geometry. It has the following functions.
## Supports[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Plugin-API/Services/Interactive-Placement.html#supports)
Returns a list of placement functions which are supported by the host. If the function is not supported the plugin calls it anyway then the host should return an 'aborted' IPlacement result.
**Request arguments**  
| Name  | Value/Type  | Remarks  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| path  | "supports"  |   |  
**Response json**

```
export interface ISupports {
    /**
     * Supports place geometry function
     */
    readonly placegeometry: boolean;
    /**
     * Supports edit geometry function
     */
    readonly editgeometry: boolean;
    /**
     * Other placement functions     
     */
    [name: string]: boolean;
}

```

## Place geometry[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Plugin-API/Services/Interactive-Placement.html#place-geometry)
The basic placement function which can be used as a fallback if other geometry placement techniques are not supported by a host. Actual functionality is dependent on the hosting application but it is roughly equivalent to the interactive placement technique implemented in G/Designer. Allows the user to place one or more instances of a particular geometry type. After placing each geometry the user should be given the opportunity to adjust or modify the geometry.
If the legend/map the geometry is drawn in is a detail or schematic legend then the returned geometry feature properties must include the legend LSNO and detail identifier so that it can be added to the correct map in the map features service.
**Request arguments**  
| Name  | Value/Type  | Remarks  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| path  | "placegeometry"  |   |  
| body  | IPlaceGeometryArgs  |   |  

```
export interface IPlaceGeometryArgs {
    /**
     * Layer geometry should be rendered in (if supported by host)
     */
    layerName: string;
    /**
     * The type of geometry to place
     */
    type: ComponentGeometryType;
    /**
     * Optional GTech style number. 
     */
    SNO?: number;
    /**
     * Optional label text for when placing labels. If supplying an initial text geometry then the text from that will be used in preference.
     */
    LBL?: string;
    /**
     * Optional label alignment
     */
    ALN?: AlignmentType;
    /**
     * Optional initial rotation in radians.
     */
    ROT?: number;
    /**
     * Allowed adjustments (if supported by the host). If left undefined this indicates that there should be no post placement adjustment.
     */
    adjustmentModes?: IAdjustmentModes;
}

```

```
export const ComponentGeometryType = {
    BoundaryGeometry: 'BoundaryGeometry',
    CompositePolygonGeometry: 'CompositePolygonGeometry',
    CompositePolylineGeometry: 'CompositePolylineGeometry',
    OrientedPointGeometry: 'OrientedPointGeometry',
    PolygonGeometry: 'PolygonGeometry',
    PolylineGeometry: 'PolylineGeometry',
    RasterGeometry: 'RasterGeometry',
    TextPointGeometry: 'TextPointGeometry'
} as const;
export type GeometryType = typeof GeomType[keyof typeof GeomType];

```

```
export interface IAdjustmentModes {
    move: boolean;
    moveAlong: boolean;
    moveAlongWithAngle: boolean;
    rotate: boolean;
    rotateAround: boolean;
    flipInverse: boolean;
    flip: boolean;
    moveAlongWithRelativeAngle: boolean;
}

```

**Response json**

```
export interface IPlacementResult extends IServiceResult {
    /**
     * The geometry placed. If no geometry placed then this will be an empty array.
     */
    readonly features: IGeometryFeature[];
    /**
     * Indicates that the user aborted placement. If the user aborts placement the geometry will be an empty array.
     */
    readonly aborted: boolean;
}

```

## Edit Geometry[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Plugin-API/Services/Interactive-Placement.html#edit-geometry)
Allows a user to _interactively_ adjust a single geometry.
**Request arguments**  
| Name  | Value/Type  | Remarks  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| path  | "editgeometry"  |   |  
| body  | IEditGeometryArgs  |   |  

```
export interface IEditGeometryArgs {
    /**
     * Layer geometry should be rendered in (if supported by host)
     */
    layerName: string;
    /** The geometry to edit */
    feature: IGeometryFeature;
    /**
     * Allowed adjustments (if supported by the host);
     */
    adjustmentModes?: IAdjustmentModes;
}

```

**Response json - IPlacementResult**
## Stop placement[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Plugin-API/Services/Interactive-Placement.html#stop-placement)
Notify the host that they should stop edit (or placement) and return the current geometry. In other words this is called when a user is satisfied with the current geometry.
**Request arguments**  
| Name  | Value/Type  | Remarks  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| path  | "stop"  |   |  
**Response json - IPlacementResult**
## Abort placement[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Plugin-API/Services/Interactive-Placement.html#abort-placement)
Notify the host that they should stop edit (or placement). This is called when the user wishes to cancel an edit or placement.
**Request arguments**  
| Name  | Value/Type  | Remarks  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| path  | "stop"  |   |  
**Response json - IServiceResult**

# Licensing
## Description[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Plugin-API/Services/Licensing.html#description)
Allows the plugin to query license status.
## Verify availability of a license[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Plugin-API/Services/Licensing.html#verify-availability-of-a-license)
Check if the license identified by name and version is currently available.
### Request[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Plugin-API/Services/Licensing.html#request)
#### Path[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Plugin-API/Services/Licensing.html#path)  
| Name  | Value/Type  | Remarks  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| path  | "verify"  |   |  
#### Query parameters[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Plugin-API/Services/Licensing.html#query-parameters)  
| Name  | Value/Type  | Mandatory  | Remarks  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| name  | string  | X  | License name  |  
| version  | string  | X  | License version. The value must exactly match the checked out version.  |  
#### Example[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Plugin-API/Services/Licensing.html#example)
`version?name=nwweb_portal&version=11.2401`
### Response[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Plugin-API/Services/Licensing.html#response)
[IServiceResult](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Plugin-API/Services/Common-Interfaces.html#iserviceresult). The `success` property contains the verification result.

# Map features
## Description[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Plugin-API/Services/Map-Features.html#description)
Allows a plugin to define one or more geometries to be drawn in the host applications maps. Geometry should be presented to the service as an array of [IGeometryFeature](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Plugin-API/Services/Common-Interfaces.html) objects.
If the detail property is set to false on a feature then it is recommended that host render the geometry in all open maps which are not details/schematics. Otherwise DETAILID will be set and the geometry should only be rendered in that detail/schematic.
The rendering service has the following functions.
## Configure[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Plugin-API/Services/Map-Features.html#configure)
Configure host and prepare it for rendering for geometries. This method needs to be called one time before any of the remaining ones. The primary purpose of this API is to provide a way how to pass style data from plugin to host and decouple the host from relying on a particular service instance.
**Request arguments**  
| Name  | Value/Type  | Remarks  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| path  | "configure"  |   |  
| body  | IConfigureArgs  |   |  

```
export interface IConfigureArgs {
    /**
     * If the host supports it specifies the layer into which the geometry should be renderered.
     */
    layer?: IMapLayer;
    /**
     * Style data, in format returned by Vector Service or FDS /style/map response.
     */
    styles?: any;
}

```

```
export interface IMapLayer {
    /**
     * Identifier for a layer/legend entry name
     */
    name: string;
    /**
     * Display name which can be used in a legend control
     */
    userName?: string;
}

```

## Draw features[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Plugin-API/Services/Map-Features.html#draw-features)
Draw the supplied set of geometry in all open maps. The host should track which plugin geometry come from so that the plugin only clears its own geometry. Alternatively it should place geometry in a layer which is only used by that plugin.
If the user opens a new map/legend after the render function has been called, the host should check to see if it should render any of the supplied geometry in that map.
**Request arguments**  
| Name  | Value/Type  | Remarks  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| path  | "drawfeatures"  |   |  
| body  | IDrawFeaturesArgs  |   |  

```
export interface IFeaturesArgs {
    /**
     * Collection of geometry to be processed.
     */
    features: IGeometryFeature[];
}

```

```
export interface IDrawFeaturesArgs extends IFeaturesArgs {
    /**
     * If the host supports it, specifies the layer into which the geometry should be renderered.
     */
    layerName: string;
    /**
     * If true remove all current geometry in the specified layer before rendering the newly supplied ones. Default is true.
     */
    replace?: boolean;
}

```

**Response json - IServiceResult**
## Fit features[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Plugin-API/Services/Map-Features.html#fit-features)
Fit the active map to the bounds of the specified features.
**Request arguments**  
| Name  | Value/Type  | Remarks  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| path  | "fitfeatures"  |   |  
| body  | IFitFeaturesArgs  |   |  

```
//Note extends IFeatureArgs
export interface IFitFeaturesArgs extends IFeaturesArgs {
    /**
     * Optionally highlight the geometry. Default is false.
     */
    highlight?: boolean;
}

```

**Response json - IServiceResult**
## Highlight features[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Plugin-API/Services/Map-Features.html#highlight-features)
Similar to fit features this function is used to highlight the supplied features. However it will not fit the map to those features.
Highlight is only maintained by the application until another geometry (or geometries) is highlighted in the application.
**Request arguments**  
| Name  | Value/Type  | Remarks  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| path  | "highlightfeatures"  |   |  
| body  | IHighlightFeaturesArgs  |   |  

```
//Note extends IFeatureArgs
export interface IHighlightFeaturesArgs extends IFeaturesArgs {
    /**
     * Clear any existing highlight. Default is true.
     */
    clearHighlight?: boolean;
}

```

**Response json - IServiceResult**
## Clear highlight[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Plugin-API/Services/Map-Features.html#clear-highlight)
Clear any highlighted geometry from the active map
**Request arguments**  
| Name  | Value/Type  | Remarks  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| path  | "clearhighlight"  |   |  
**Response json - IServiceResult**
## Clear[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Plugin-API/Services/Map-Features.html#clear)
Clear all geometry from the specified layer, or if not specified all layers created by the plugin.
**Request arguments**  
| Name  | Value/Type  | Remarks  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| path  | "clear[?layerName={string}]"  |   |  
**Response json - IServiceResult**
## Remove[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Plugin-API/Services/Map-Features.html#remove)
Clear rendered geometry from the specified layer and then remove that layer from all maps/legends. If a layer is not specified then do the same for all layers created by the plugin
**Request arguments**  
| Name  | Value/Type  | Remarks  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| path  | "remove[?layerName={string}]"  |   |  
**Response json - IServiceResult**

# Map selection
## Description[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Plugin-API/Services/Map-selection.html#description)
Allows a plugin to request that the application starts a map selection operation. This should allow the user to select a specific feature. Once selected the request will then return with a response with the feature key. Alternatively the user can choose to abort the selection operation in which case the request will return with a fail response.
## Select feature[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Plugin-API/Services/Map-selection.html#select-feature)
Starts the select operation. Optionally this operation can be filtered to only allow selection of features with particular FNOs.
**Request arguments**  
| Name  | Value/Type  | Remarks  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| path  | "selectfeature"  |   |  
| body  | ISelectFeatureFilter  |   |  

```
export interface ISelectFeatureFilter {
    /**
     * Set of fnos to allow updates too.
     */
    fnos?: number[];
    /**
     * Allow user to select multiple features in one operation (if application supports it)
     * Default is false.
     */
    multiple?: boolean;
}

```

**Response**
[IServiceResult](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Plugin-API/Services/Common-Interfaces.html#iserviceresult)

# Map window
## Description[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Plugin-API/Services/Map-window.html#description)
Allows the plugin to query the current map window parameters and update the current map window parameters.
## Get current window parameters[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Plugin-API/Services/Map-window.html#get-current-window-parameters)
Return the map parameters for the current map window.
**Request arguments**  
| Name  | Value/Type  | Remarks  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| path  | "getcurrent"  |   |  
**Response Json**

```
export interface IMapWindowParams {
    /**
     * The identifier of the current map panel if any. Used by a host application that support multiple map panels.
     */
    id?: string;
    /**
     * The identifier of the current legend if available.
     */
    legendId?: string;
    /**
     * The nominal NetWorks legend identifier (G3E_LSNO) as a whole number if available.
     */
    lsno?: number;
    /**
     * The associated NetWorks detail identifier (G3E_DETAILID) as a whole number, if applicable.
     */
    detailId?: number;
    /**
     * Detail reference. Set when its a new offline detail which is being displayed.
     */
    dref?: number;
    /**
     * The window extent in CS coordinates, formatted as [XMIN, YMIN, XMAX, YMAX].
     */
    bbox: number[];
    /**
     * The window size in (nominal) pixels as [WIDTH, HEIGHT].
     */
    size: number[];
    /**
     * Coordinate system identifier for bbox. Typically an EPSG:nnnn code.
     */
    coordinateSystem: string;
}

```

## Set map window parameters[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Plugin-API/Services/Map-window.html#set-map-window-parameters)
**Request arguments**  
| Name  | Value/Type  | Remarks  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| path  | "set"  |   |  
| body  | INetworksDetailWindowArgs  |   |  

```
export interface INetworksDetailWindowArgs {
    /**
     * Identifier for the map window if the client supports multiple map windows.
     */
    id?: string;
    /** Type discriminator */
    windowType: "networksdetail";
    /** Detail id */
    detailid: number;
    /** Detail user name */
    name: string;
    /** Detail/schematic discriminator */
    type: number;
    /** Legend identifier */
    lsno: number;
    /** Owner FNO */
    ownerfno: number;
}

```

NOTE
The `id` argument for map windows is reserved for future versions and is the identifier of the UI element which will display the map. Host applications that do not support multiple map panels will ignore it. If supplied and the host application supports it then the id must be valid or an error will be returned. If no `id` is supplied then the host application will use the 'current' map will be used. The definition of 'current' is left to the host application.
The `networksdetail` map window is defined by a legend number (G3E_LSNO) and a detail id (G3E_DETAILID), both of which must be valid for the operation to succeed.
**Response Json - IServiceResult**
