# Services
## Overview[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Plugin-API/Services.html#overview)
Client services implement the majority of the functionality available to plugins. They are implemented to resemble an HTTP based service in that you make a request by sending a path and optionally a (JSON) body, then asynchronously receive a response which is also a JSON object.
The following services are available to plugins.  
| Name  | Type id  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| Feature data  | hxgn.networks.fds  | Gives access to the [Feature Data Service](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Data-Service.html).  |  
| Interactive placement  | hxgn.networks.ipts  | Invokes geometry placement in the host application and returns the resulting geometry.  |  
| Map features  | hxgn.networks.mapfeatures  | Allows the plugin to supply a set of geometry features to render in the hosts map.  |  
| Map selection  | hxgn.networks.mapselection  | Allows the plugin to start a map select operation and return the results to the plugin.  |  
| Map window  | hxgn.networks.mapwindow  | Allows the plugin to switch map legends.  |  
| File storage  | hxgn.networks.storage  | Allows the plugin to manage a collection of files.  |  
| FM Job  | hxgn.networks.fm-job  | Allows the plugin to submit Feature Editor workset together with any hyperlink files to the work service.  |  
| Resource  | hxgn.networks.resource  | Retrieves localized string resources from the host.  |  
| [Licensing](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Plugin-API/Services/Licensing.html)  | hxgn.networks.licensing  | License verification API. _Note:_ All requests return `true` in Portal.  |

# Plugin API
## Introduction[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Plugin-API.html#introduction)
User Interfaces are expensive to develop and test and it costs more to train users to use a User interface. Therefore there is an obvious advantage for everyone if we can develop modular user interfaces (UI plugins) which can be used in multiple hosting applications.
The plugin API is an API which is common to both HxGN NetWorks Core Portal and HxGN NetWorks Core Mobile clients. The API is designed to allow a UI plugin to be hosted in either client without modification.
A plugin is defined as a UI component created using HTML, CSS and JavaScript/Typescript which can be executed in a browser iframe or WebView component.
The plugin API consist of three main parts:
  1. [Configuration](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Plugin-API/Configuration.html) that defines a standard way of configuring a plugin.
  2. [Host interface](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Plugin-API/Host-interface.html) which gives access to a set of common functions on the hosting client, in particular the services.
  3. [Services](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Plugin-API/Services.html) which implement the basic functionality for the plugin.

The most important part here is the services. It is these which bridge the dichotomy between the Portal which is an online client and Core Mobile, an offline one.
**NOTE:** The Plugin API is subject to further development and change in future releases. Some of these changes may be breaking.

# Portal
## Overview[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Portal.html#overview)
Networks Portal is a browser based GIS client which gives users access to the functionality available in NetWorks Web Services such as viewing map data, editing features and running analyses. In addition it can be configured to give users access to external map and query services such as OGC services. Networks Portal has multiple points of configuration and its functionality can be extended via several APIs.

#### Query

# Configure query category shown by default
Set Portal setting `query.defaultCategoryACNO` to `G3E_ACNO` of default query category (defined in table `G3E_ANALYSISCATEGORY`) which should be preselected when the Query dialog is opened. If not configured, the query categories are not sorted and the ordering is determined by the response from the Analytical Service.
## See also[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Query/Configure-query-category-shown-by-default.html#see-also)
  * [Settings](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Settings.html)
  * [Deployment customization](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Administration-Console/Deployment-customization.html)

# External queries
## Overview[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Query/External-queries.html#overview)
If configured, users can execute queries which are based on external search and map services such as WFS. For the user external queries function in the same way as gtech searches/finds. They can be saved to My Queries and the results can be exported to Excel or added to the map and legend.
See [configuration of external queries](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/External-queries.html).
In addition to ordinary text fields and pick lists external queries can be configured with the following fields:
  * Date time fields - Value can be entered via the date picker or entered via the keyboard in the format configured for the locale. These fields can be configured to only accept a range of dates.
  * Numeric fields - Value must only be numbers and if configured to accept decimal places the decimal point character for the locale. These fields can be configured to only accept a range of values.
  * Geometry fields - These fields can be configured to accept a point, polyline or polygon.

In addition it is possible to limit the number of characters a user can enter into a text field and also require a certain number of characters.
For geometry fields there are three buttons on the right hand side of the field. Click the first button collapses the query dialog and switches the map to accept drawing of the geometry type configured for the field. Once the user completes drawing the geometry the query dialog is expanded again and a green tick is displayed in the field. If the user does not complete drawing the geometry (for example, they switch to map select mode) then they must expand the dialog and start again. The second button on the field will fit the map to the geometry if defined. The third button will clear the field.

# Save query
# Overview
Users can save the currently entered field values of the selected query to a query under the category 'My Queries', by using the save button. In this way if they wish to re-run the same query multiple times they do not need to re-enter the values. When the user presses the save button they are presented with a small dialog where they can name the new query, the dialog is pre-populated with a unique name based on the selected query name. If the user specifies a name that already exists, then the portal will automatically append a number in brackets to make it unique before saving, for example:
![image.png](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/.attachments/image-7db058ce-f5d8-4dd6-92de-bb223fbe2f90.png)
To re-execute a saved query the user should select the category 'My Queries' and then select the query they wish to execute from the list below. Once selected they should click/tap the search button or press the enter key to execute it.
Note the following:
  * It is not possible to save the selected Area of Interest with a query. This must be selected each time before the query is re-executed.
  * It _is_ possible to save an item under 'My Queries' under a new name.
  * Query items are saved on the client, not the server.

# Query
## Overview[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Query.html#overview)
The query dialog consists of multiple functions. At the top left is a dropdown which the user can select the category of query they wish to execute. The available categories are:
  * Find Component - Lists configured gtech find by component searches.
  * Find Feature - Lists configured gtech find feature searches.
  * Quick Find - Lists configured gtech quick reference searches.
  * Simple Query - Lists configured gtech simple attribute queries.
  * External Query - Lists queries based on external services configured in the portal workspace.
  * My Queries - Lists queries/searches with values already entered by the user and saved.

The main toolbar contains the following buttons:
![save.svg](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/.attachments/save-448a8f41-1036-42cd-9560-4df004ff4572.svg) Executes the selected query and returns the result in the bottom grid.
![cancel-edit.svg](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/.attachments/cancel-edit-06b8a954-9552-4601-abc0-3849d00ba782.svg) Clears any values from the query parameter fields.
![save.svg](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/.attachments/save-87884cb8-f7e7-4d7e-994e-0846abb17d99.svg) Save the selected query and its field values to My Queries.
![trash.svg](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/.attachments/trash-dbea136b-b034-4d7c-bfd7-3fad52cd2aff.svg) If a query from the category My Queries is selected, this button will remove it.
![delete.svg](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/.attachments/delete-e0c799f3-4ba6-44b4-8886-99b3bfde2912.svg) Closes the dialog.
The results grid toolbar contains the following buttons:
![edit-property.svg](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/.attachments/edit-property-25e4370e-9784-427b-b8ed-b81c1ae09ce5.svg) Toggle button. If highlighted then clicking on an item in the results grid will open it in an editor.
![zoom-to-3.svg](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/.attachments/zoom-to-3-675428cc-a40d-40f6-91bf-912f36342b17.svg) Toggle button. If highlighted then clicking on an item in the results grid will fit the map to it.
![excel-logo.svg](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/.attachments/excel-logo-eca222a2-4cb1-4d75-912b-35137c16a5b8.svg) Exports the currently loaded query results to an excel spreadsheet.
![legend-append.svg](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/.attachments/legend-append-3efeccfd-5382-4ea6-8332-e33e6d350d2c.svg) Adds the currently loaded query results to the map and legend.
![trash.svg](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/.attachments/trash-dbea136b-b034-4d7c-bfd7-3fad52cd2aff.svg) Clears the currently loaded query results.
Note that the maximum amount of rows that can be exported to excel or added to the map is defined by the system administrator. Pressing the enter key will also execute the selected query, if any. Pressing the escape key will close the dialog.

#### Redlines

# Categories
## Overview[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Redlines/Categories.html#overview)
When redlines are created, they are automatically associated with a category. A category is an represents a group of related redlines which share a set of default styles. For more information about the technical details of categories see the article 'Redline XML Document' in the NetWorks Core Admin Help, however, also note the [differences between Portal and Designer](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Redlines/Differences-to-Designer-Analyst.html).
Only one category can be active at any time. Users can switch between categories in the user interface using the **Activate Redline Category** function. Switching to a different category will reset all style settings to those associated with the newly selected category. When importing redlines from WKT, GML or Networks Portal GeoJSON created by earlier versions of the Portal, they will be associated with the active category.
Importing a redlines file that contains categories that are not one of the default categories, will add those categories to the list of available categories until the end of the users session.
Users can choose to show or hide redlines associated to a particular category via the legend tab by checking or unchecking the box next to the category name under 'Redline' folder.
## Defining default categories[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Redlines/Categories.html#defining-default-categories)
By default a single category is defined by the portal settings. See
  * [Style Properties](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Settings/Style-Properties.html)
  * [Redline](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Settings/Redline.html)

This can be overridden by making a `categories.xml` file available to the portal. This file is a redlines XML document, the same as used by Designer to configure default redline categories. See the NetWorks Core Admin Help for more information about this file. To make it available to the portal do one of the following
  1. Define a folder path in the portal workspace file under Settings/RedlinesCategoriesFilePath. See [Workspace settings](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/Workspace-settings.html) for more details.

OR
  1. Place a `categories.xml` file together with the workspace in the same folder. See [Workspace folders](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/web.config-file/Workspaces.html) for more information about workspace folders. Note the file must be called `categories.xml`. If there are multiple folders and multiple `categories.xml` files then only the first file found will be used.

## Style mapping[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Redlines/Categories.html#style-mapping)
_Note:_ Make sure the color value specified in any *Color property is added in settings, otherwise Portal won't be able to recognize the color name, for more info, please take a look in [Redline settings](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Settings/Redline.html)
The style properties defined by Redline XML map to the portal [style properties](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Redlines/Style-property-reference.html) as follows:  
| Redline XML name  | Portal name  | Remarks  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| LineColor  | strokeColor  |   |  
| LineTranslucency  | strokeOpacity  |   |  
| LineStyle  | strokeDashStyle  |   |  
| LineWidth  | strokeWidth  |   |  
| FillColor  | fillColor  |   |  
| FillTranslucency  | fillOpacity  |   |  
| FillStyle  |   | Only solid fills are supported in the portal.  |  
| FillHatch  |   | Not mapped.  |  
| FontColor  | fontColor  |   |  
| FontTranslucency  | fontOpacity  |   |  
| FontName  | fontFamily  |   |  
| FontSize  | fontSize  |   |  
| FontStyle  | fontStyle  |   |  
| SymbolColor  | fontColor  |   |  
| SymbolTranslucency  | fontOpacity  |   |  
| SymbolFontName  | fontFamily  | Font must be specified in the settings. See [Redline settings](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Settings/Redline.html)  |  
| SymbolFontCharset  |   | Not mapped.  |  
| SymbolSize  | fontSize  |   |  
| SymbolValue  | text  | Only for redline symbol features.  |  
| TextValue  | text  | Only for redline text features.  |  
| ViewScaleDependent  | scaleDependent  | In the portal this is a boolean.  |  
| MapScale  |   | This is converted to feature '__resolution'.  |  
| TextBox  |   | Not mapped.  |  
| StartSymbol  |   | Not mapped.  |  
| EndSymbol  |   | Not mapped.  |

# Differences to Designer-Analyst
## Differences to Designer-Analyst[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Redlines/Differences-to-Designer-Analyst.html#differences-to-designer-analyst-1)
The section is included to highlight the current differences between redline functionality as implemented in the Portal with respect to that in a, non customized, installation of Designer-Analyst. In particular it highlights the things that are not currently supported in the Portal.
Currently there is no support for:
  * Hatch fills.
  * Arc geometry.
  * Scale dependent line/outline widths.

Currently there is only limited support for:
  * Ellipses. Only circles are supported.
  * Rectangles. Rectangles are captured as polygons.
  * Text boxes.

UI Differences:
  * No 'Text Box' check box for text geometry.
  * No text and symbol alignment pick lists.
  * No text or symbol transparency pick lists.

Portal only features:
  * Segment labels
  * Total length label
  * Total area label
  * Total outline length label
  * Coordinate label

# NetWorks Portal GeoJSON
## Overview[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Redlines/NetWorks-Portal-GeoJSON.html#overview)
By default the portal exports redlines in 'NetWorks Portal GeoJSON' format. This is based on [GeoJSON](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7946) with some specific differences.
  1. The coordinate reference system for coordinates in a NetWorks Portal GeoJSON file is defined by the legend the redlines are exported from. It is not currently encoded into the file.
  2. A set of four named properties which are documented in this article.

## Properties[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Redlines/NetWorks-Portal-GeoJSON.html#properties)
The properties specific to 'NetWorks Portal GeoJSON' are placed under the `properties` member of a feature object e.g.

```
{
   "type": "Feature",
   "geometry": {
      "type": "LineString",
      "coordinates": [[4502428.417007837, 5924225.121863357],...]
   },
   "properties": {
      "__style": {
         "strokeDashstyle": "solid",
         "strokeWidth": 2,
         "strokeColor": "#FF0000",
         "strokeOpacity": 0.9,
         "enableSegmentLength": false,
         "enableTotalLength": false,
         "enableArrows": false,
         "enableAngle": false,
         "fontFamily": "Calibri",
         "fontSize": 14,
         "fontOutlineColor": "#FFFFFF",
         "fontOutlineWidth": 3,
         "rotateWithView": true,
         "scaleDependent": false
      },
      "__category": "_Default",
      "__rotation": 0,
      "__featureType": "line",
      "__resolution": 1.841,
      "__zindex": 0
   }
}

```

The properties are as follows:  
| Name  | Required  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| `__category`  | N  | The name of the associated category as a string.  |  
| `__featureType`  | N  | Redline feature type identifier.  |  
| `__group`  | N  | The group name the feature is associated with as a string.  |  
| `__style`  | N  | Style properties for display. See [Style property reference](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Redlines/Style-property-reference.html).  |  
| `__resolution`  | N  | Map resolution that the feature was last placed at.  |  
| `__rotation`  | N  | Rotation applied to the geometry.  |  
| `__zindex`  | N  | The zindex of the feature as an integer value greater or equal to zero.  |  
## Feature type[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Redlines/NetWorks-Portal-GeoJSON.html#feature-type)
The `__featureType` property can be set to one of the values defined in the following table. Each type is associated with a specific GeoJSON geometry type. If its associated with another geometry type then the file is invalid.  
| Feature type  | Geometry type  | Notes  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| `circle`  | `Polygon`  | On import the extent of the associated polygon is calculated and a circle is created centered in the extent with the diameter set to the largest of the extent width or height. On export circles are split into multiple straight line segments.  |  
| `label`  | `Point`  | Equivalent to a Redline XML text.  |  
| `line`  | `LineString`  |   |  
| `point`  | `Point`  | Equivalent to a Redline XML symbol.  |  
| `polygon`  | `Polygon`  |   |  
| `rectangle`  | `Polygon`  |   |  
## Group[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Redlines/NetWorks-Portal-GeoJSON.html#group)
Features can only be grouped with other features within the same category.
## Rotation[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Redlines/NetWorks-Portal-GeoJSON.html#rotation)
Rotation is applied directly to `label` and `point` feature types and is also used for label decorations on line and polygons such as segment length labels. Rotation is specified in radians. Positive values are clockwise from the nominal vertical up direction. How rotation is applied depends on the style. See notes on rotate with view in [Style property reference](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Redlines/Style-property-reference.html).
## Resolution[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Redlines/NetWorks-Portal-GeoJSON.html#resolution)
Resolution is applied directly to `label` and `point` feature types if the style is scale dependent. It is similarly used for label decorations on line and polygons such as segment length labels. If resolution is not defined than scale dependent styles will have no effect. Resolution is defined as the number of CRS units per nominal pixel e.g. meters per pixel.
## Z-index[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Redlines/NetWorks-Portal-GeoJSON.html#z-index)
Features can only be z indexed relative to other features within the same category. Categories can be z-index in the Portal via the Legend UI. Z indexes will be overwritten by the application as data is modified.

# Style property reference
## Style property reference[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Redlines/Style-property-reference.html#style-property-reference-1)
Redline style properties are used to style both redline and measure geometry. Style properties offer a more limited way of styling geometry than what can be done in a modern browser but are more compatible with Designer-Analyst redlines.
See [Style properties](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Settings/Style-Properties.html) for the default style properties delivered with the portal.
Style properties are defined as simple JavaScript or JSON objects with a flat list of properties. For example in the Portals settings.js file the measuring line style can be defined as:

```
    // Measuring line style
    measureLine: {
        enableSegmentLength: true,
        enableTotalLength: true,
        strokeColor: '#ff00ff',
        strokeDashstyle: 'dot',
        strokeOpacity: 1.0,
        strokeWidth: 2,
        fontFamily: 'Calibri',
        fontSize: 14,
        textAlign: 'left',
        textBox: true,
        textBoxPadding: [2, 2, 2, 2],
        textBoxFillColor: '#ffffff',
        textBoxFillOpacity: 1.0,
        fontOutlineColor: '#ff00ff',
        fontOutlineWidth: 1.0,
        textOffsetX: 9,
        textOffsetY: -9,
        scaleDependent: false,
        rotateWithView: true
    }

```

The full list of properties together with the default values if not otherwise defined are as follows:  
| Name  | Default  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| enableAngle  | `false`  | Whether angle decorator is enabled. Only applies to polyline geometry.  |  
| enableArea  | `false`  | Whether area label decorator is enabled. Only applies to polygon geometry.  |  
| enableArrows  | `false`  | Whether arrows decorator is enabled. Only applies to polyline geometry.  |  
| enableCoordinate  | `false`  | Whether coordinate label decorator is enabled. Only applies to point geometry  |  
| enableSegmentLength  | `false`  | Whether segment length label decorator is enabled. Only applies to polyline and polygon geometry.  |  
| enableTotalLength  | `false`  | Whether total line/outline length label decorator is enabled. Only applies to polyline and polygon geometry.  |  
| fillColor  |   | Fill color for polygons of all types as a hexadecimal RGB code e.g. `'#FF0000'`.  |  
| fillOpacity  |   | Fill opacity for polygons of all types as a number between 1 and 0 where 1 is fully opaque and 0 is fully transparent.  |  
| fontColor  | _strokeColor_  | Color for text or symbols as a hexadecimal RGB code e.g. `'#FF0000'`.  |  
| fontFamily  | `'sans-serif'`  | The font family to be used for symbol and text geometry and any decorative text.  |  
| fontOpacity  | _strokeOpacity_  | Opacity for text or symbol as a number between 1 and 0 where 1 is fully opaque and 0 is fully transparent.  |  
| fontOutlineColor  |   | If defined, defines the color of either the text box outline OR the text outline. A hexadecimal RGB code e.g. `'#FF0000'`.  |  
| fontOutlineOpacity  | _fontOpacity_  | The opacity of the text box or text outline as a as a number between 1 and 0 where 1 is fully opaque and 0 is fully transparent.  |  
| fontOutlineWidth  | `1`  | The width of the text box or text outline.  |  
| fontSize  | `12`  | Size of the font in CSS pixels.  |  
| fontStyle  |   | The style of the font. Can be `'normal'`, `'bold'`, `'italic'` or `'bold italic'`.  |  
| pointRadius  | `1`  | Radius of backstop point style.  |  
| rotateWithView  | `false`  | Whether to rotate the text or symbol with the view. Can be `true` or `false`.  |  
| scaleDependent  | `false`  | Whether the text or symbol is scaled with the view. Can be `true` or `false`.  |  
| strokeDashstyle  | `'solid'`  | Dash style for lines or outlines. Can be `'solid'`, `'dash'`, `'dot'`, `'dashdot'` or `'dashdotdot'`.  |  
| strokeWidth  | `1`  | Width of a line or outline in CSS pixels.  |  
| strokeColor  | `'#000000'`  | Color of a line or outline as a hexadecimal RGB code e.g. `#FF0000`.  |  
| strokeOpacity  | `1`  | Opacity of a line or outline as a number between 1 and 0 where 1 is fully opaque and 0 is fully transparent.  |  
| textAlign  | `'center'`  | Defines the horizontal text alignment. Can be `'left'`, `'right'` or `'center'`.  |  
| textBaseline  | `'alphabetic'`  | Defines the vertical text alignment. Can be `'alphabetic'`, `'top'`, `'middle'` or `'bottom'`.  |  
| text  |   | The text or symbol to be displayed.  |  
| textBox  | `false`  | Defines whether a text or symbol is drawn in a text box. Can be `true` or `false`.  |  
| textBoxFillColor  |  _fillColor_ > _strokeColor_  | Fill color for text boxes as a hexadecimal RGB code e.g. `#FF0000`.  |  
| textBoxFillOpacity  |  _fillOpacity_ > _strokeOpacity_  | Fill opacity for text boxes as a number between 1 and 0 where 1 is fully opaque and 0 is fully transparent.  |  
| textBoxPadding  | `[1, 1, 1, 1]`  | Padding in CSS pixels [top, right, bottom, left].  |  
| textOffsetX  |   | Text or symbol X offset in CSS pixels. A positive value will shift the text right.  |  
| textOffsetY  |   | Text or symbol Y offset in CSS pixels. A positive value will shift the text down.  |  
## Rotate with view[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Redlines/Style-property-reference.html#rotate-with-view)
The `rotateWithView` property determines how a label or symbol angle changes when the map is rotated. If `true` then the angle of the label or symbol maintains its angle with respect to the map. If `false` then its angle is maintained with respect to the screen.
For example, if you were to start with a map which is not rotated and place a label, it would appear horizontal with respect to the screen. This is the default starting position for all labels and symbols regardless of screen rotation. Now if you rotate the label 90 degrees anti clockwise it would appear as
![label-rotated.svg](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/.attachments/label-rotated-0d60ab1b-cb81-4be8-89c6-d6fc4e96d9b3.svg)
If `rotateWithView` is set to `true` and you now rotate the map 90 degrees clockwise, it will now appear horizontally e.g.
![label-not-rotated.svg](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/.attachments/label-not-rotated-2c283f77-ee9c-4f10-b4f0-bd64582489d0.svg)
If, however, `rotateWithView` is set to `false` then the label will still appear as placed e.g.
![label-rotated.svg](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/.attachments/label-rotated-0d60ab1b-cb81-4be8-89c6-d6fc4e96d9b3.svg)
And no matter how you rotate the map it will maintain that orientation with respect to the screen.
## Text alignment[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Redlines/Style-property-reference.html#text-alignment)
Text and symbol alignment is specified using two separate values in the Portal. These map to the values used by Designer-Analyst as follows:  
| Alignment  | textBaseline  | textAlign  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| Bottom Center  | bottom  | center  |  
| Bottom Left  | bottom  | left  |  
| Bottom Right  | bottom  | right  |  
| Center Center  | middle  | center  |  
| Center Left  | middle  | left  |  
| Center Right  | middle  | right  |  
| Left Baseline  | alphabetic  | left  |  
| Top Center  | top  | center  |  
| Top Left  | top  | left  |  
| Top Right  | top  | right  |

# Upload redlines to server
In the **Save Redlines File** sub panel, there is a button labelled **Upload**. The upload function works by generating the redlines file and then, rather than downloading it to the users file system, uploads it to the Data Transfer Service.
This button is only shown if setting `redlines.showUploadButton` is set to true (see See [Settings documentation](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Settings.html)).
In order for this functionality to work, the Data Transfer Service must be [deployed](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Data-Transfer-Service/Deployment.html) and [configured](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Data-Transfer-Service/Configuration.html)
See [Data Transfer Service documentation](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Data-Transfer-Service/Upload.html) for details on how to find the uploaded file.

#### Results-tables

# Add results to legend
## Overview[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Results-tables/Add-results-to-legend.html#overview)
After a query or analysis is executed, the geometries of the features in the result set can be added to the current legend as a dynamic layer.
## Main workflow[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Results-tables/Add-results-to-legend.html#main-workflow)
  1. Execute the query or analysis.
  2. Click on the **Add query results to legend** button (![add-query-to-legend-icon.png](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/.attachments/add-query-to-legend-icon-684929d0-638d-40de-9edb-a82c2ad7557e.png))
  3. Portal loads geometries of the features in the result set from the server and adds a new entry into the legend.

## Additional workflows[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Results-tables/Add-results-to-legend.html#additional-workflows)
### Fit result extents in map[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Results-tables/Add-results-to-legend.html#fit-result-extents-in-map)
  1. Find the results legend entry in the legend.
  2. Right click and select **Fit**.
  3. Portal changes the map view to fit all geometries in the result set.

### Remove query results from legend[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Results-tables/Add-results-to-legend.html#remove-query-results-from-legend)
  1. Find the results legend entry in the legend.
  2. Right click and select **Remove**.
  3. Portal removes the entry from legend and map view

## Restrictions[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Results-tables/Add-results-to-legend.html#restrictions)
  * This functionality is only available when a **Vector Service** source is defined in the Portal workspace.
  * Adding results to detail or schematic legends is always restricted to geometries from given legend.
  * The maximum number of feature records that can be added to the legend is restricted to a configured amount (see [web.config file](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/web.config-file.html)).
  * The portal renders only simplified symbology for features, i.e. simple polygons and lines. Circles are shown instead of point and text geometries.

# Configure buttons
The available buttons for results grids are configured via  elements. Toolbar buttons are configured under a property called items similar to previous releases. Table quick action buttons are configured under a property called actioncolumns.
## Features Panel[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Results-tables/Configure-buttons.html#features-panel)
The features panel is configured by a  element named featurepanel, which is by default defined as follows.

```
<Function name="featurepanel">
   <Config>
      <JProperty name="items">
         <JArray>
            <JValue>featureeditonclick</JValue>
            <JValue>featurefitonclick</JValue>
            <JValue>featureappendselection</JValue>
            <JValue>featureshowselected</JValue>
            <JValue>featureshowrelated</JValue>
            <JValue>featuremeasure</JValue>
            <JValue>widget.tbfill</JValue>
            <JValue>removeall</JValue>
         </JArray>
      </JProperty>
      <JProperty name="actioncolumns">
         <JArray>
            <JValue>detailsaction</JValue>
            <JValue>editaction</JValue>
            <JValue>fitaction</JValue>
         </JArray>
      </JProperty>
   </Config>
</Function>

```

## Search, Query and Trace results[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Results-tables/Configure-buttons.html#search-query-and-trace-results)
The search, query and trace results tables are all configured by the  element named resultsgrid which is by default configured as follows.

```
<Function name="resultsgrid">
   <Config>
      <JProperty name="items">
         <JArray>
            <JValue>featureeditonclick</JValue>
            <JValue>featurefitonclick</JValue>
            <JValue>resultexportexcel</JValue>
            <JValue>resultaddtolegend</JValue>
            <JValue>removeall</JValue>
         </JArray>
      </JProperty>
      <JProperty name="actioncolumns">
         <JArray>
            <JValue>detailsaction</JValue>
            <JValue>editaction</JValue>
            <JValue>fitaction</JValue>
         </JArray>
      </JProperty>
   </Config>
</Function>

```

# Download results as Excel
## Overview[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Results-tables/Download-results-as-Excel.html#overview)
After a query or analysis is executed, the geometries of the features in the result set can be added to the current legend as a dynamic layer.
## Main workflow[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Results-tables/Download-results-as-Excel.html#main-workflow)
  1. Execute the query or analysis.
  2. Click on the **Export to excel** button
  3. While the export is in progress the results table will show busy.
  4. Once the export is complete the excel spreadsheet will automatically download.

## Restrictions[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Results-tables/Download-results-as-Excel.html#restrictions)
  * The attributes exported are defined by the query/analysis and can't be configured.
  * The maximum number of feature records that can be added to the legend is restricted to a configured amount (see [web.config file](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/web.config-file.html)).

# Results tables
Results tables are part of the Portal Features and Search sidebar panels, the Query dialog results and the Trace results browser.

#### Security

# HTTP Header Configuration
Deploying the Portal and Web Services does not change the optional HTTP response headers which Internet Information Services (IIS) publishes. Neither does the Portal or any NetWorks Web Services require any custom headers to function correctly. Custom headers that are published by IIS can be viewed, edited and removed by using, for example, Microsoft's Internet Information Services (IIS) Manager. See for <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/iis/configuration/system.webserver/httpprotocol/customheaders/> for information on how to modify custom HTTP headers. It is left to the system Administrator to determine which HTTP headers should or should not be published.
In addition to custom headers Internet Information Services by default adds a header called `Server` which indicates to clients what HTTP server is being used. This can be disabled by modifying the web.config file and adding the attribute `removeServerHeader="true"` to the configuration/system.webServer/security/requestFiltering element e.g.

```
<configuration>
   ...
   <system.webServer>
        ...
        <security>
            <requestFiltering removeServerHeader="true">
                <hiddenSegments>
                    <add segment="OpenIdConfig.json" />
                </hiddenSegments>
                <requestLimits maxQueryString="32768" />
            </requestFiltering>
        </security>   
        ...
   </system.webServer>
   ...
</configuration>

```

The example is based on the default Portal web.config file. See this article for more information <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/iis/configuration/system.webserver/security/requestfiltering/> .
Another header which Internet Information Services adds by default is `X-ASPNet-Version` which indicates to clients what version of .NET is being used. This can be disabled by modifying the web.config file and adding the attribute `enableVersionHeader="false"` to the configuration/system.web/httpRuntime element e.g.

```
<configuration>
   ...
   <system.web>
      ...
      <httpRuntime targetFramework="4.8" maxQueryStringLength="32768" maxUrlLength="65536" requestValidationMode="2.0" enableVersionHeader="false" />
   </system.web>
   ...
</configuration>

```

The example is based on the default Portal web.config file. See this article for more information <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.web.configuration.httpruntimesection?view=netframework-4.8.1> .
Administrators may wish to consider adding the following custom headers for enhanced client security:  
| Name  | Remarks  |  
| --- | --- |  
| X-Content-Type-Options  | A marker used by the server to indicate that the MIME types advertised in the Content-Type headers should be followed and not be changed. See <https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/X-Content-Type-Options>.  |  
| X-Frame-Options  | Used to indicate whether a browser should be allowed to render a page in a , ,  or . See <https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/X-Frame-Options>.  |  
| Referrer-Policy  | Controls how much referrer information (sent with the Referer header) should be included with requests. See <https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Referrer-Policy>.  |  
## Content Security Policies[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Security/HTTP-Header-Configuration.html#content-security-policies)
Currently the Portal does not support Content Security Policies. Support for them is actively being worked on for a future release.

# Restrict access to Portal by role
## Overview[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Security/Restrict-access-to-Portal-by-role.html#overview)
Similar to G/Designer and G/NetViewer, when OpenID Connect is used, the Portal can be configured to restrict access only to users with a certain role encoded in a claim. Users without the specified role are denied access to the Portal and a HTTP 403 Forbidden response is returned.
This can be configured for the entire portal, for specific workspaces or both.
## Configure restriction for portal[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Security/Restrict-access-to-Portal-by-role.html#configure-restriction-for-portal)
In a deployed Portal _web.config_ , set the following properties under `<appSettings>`:  
| Name  | Description  | Expected value  | Default  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| OIDC.RestrictByRole  | When `true`, turns role restriction on.  | true, false  | false  |  
| OIDC.ValidRoles  | Semicolon-separated list of valid roles.  | Role or list of roles, separated by `;`  | Networks-Portal  |  
| OIDC.RoleClaim  | Name of claim which contains the role. The claim must be registered in RequiredClaims (see [Authentication](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/web.config-file/Authentication.html)).  | Name of claim  | role  |  
**Example**
Configuration of role restriction:

```
<appSettings>
    <add key="OIDC.RestrictByRole" value="true"/>
    <add key="OIDC.ValidRoles" value="Networks-Portal"/>
    <add key="OIDC.RoleClaim" value="role"/>
</appSettings>

```

## Configure restriction for a portal workspace[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Security/Restrict-access-to-Portal-by-role.html#configure-restriction-for-a-portal-workspace)
The instructions for configuration workspace restrictions are documented [here](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/Workspace-filtering.html).

# Server components and operating system
The portal is built on .NET framework 4.8 running in Internet Information Services on the Windows operating system. It is up to the system administrator to ensure that these components are up to date and the latest security patches from Microsoft are installed e.g. Windows Update is run regularly on the server.
In addition organization should ensure to upgrade to the latest version of Portal and Web Services as soon as reasonably possible. This ensures the latest and most secure components are installed on the organizations servers.

# Use OpenID Code Authorization Code flow
To setup NetWorks Portal to use the OpenID Connect **authorization code** flow, set the `ResponseType` property in **OpenIdConfig.json** to `code`.
To enable **PKCE** , set property `UsePkce` to `true`. Default is `false`.
**Example**

```
{
  "Issuer": "https://oidcserver:8443/auth/realms/realm1",
  "ClientId": "hsi",
  "ClientSecret": ".........",
  "RedirectUri": "https://portalserver.com/networksportal",
  "Scope": "openid",
  "ResponseType": "code",
  "UsePkce": true
}

```

## See also[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Security/Use-OpenID-Code-Authorization-Code-flow.html#see-also)
  * [Authorization code flow in OpenID Connect specification](https://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-core-1_0.html#CodeFlowSteps)
  * [OpenID Connect explained](https://connect2id.com/learn/openid-connect)

#### State-management

# Browser caching
## Overview[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/State-management/Browser-caching.html#overview)
All major browsers can and will cache the results of server requests to avoid re-fetching information that has not changed and in that way speed up the users experience. The portal also makes use of this mechanism to avoid unnecessary reloads of static files (e.g. scripts and css files) and also some metadata such as vector service legend trees and style definitions.
Browser caching only applies to files or service results loaded using HTTP GET and requires an ETag or Last-Modified header to be returned by the HTTP server or service. Whether a file or data is cached (and how it is cached) is controlled by the browser itself. This can be frustrating if you wish to force the client to load new versions of a particular file or result. Caching can be controlled to a larger extent by two mechanisms.
  1. Setting up [cache expiration](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/iis/configuration/system.webserver/staticcontent/clientcache) headers within IIS.
  2. Modifying the [query string/parameters](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Learn/Common_questions/What_is_a_URL) sent with a request.

The portal uses both of the above mechanisms to control caching.
## Static caching[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/State-management/Browser-caching.html#static-caching)
The portal uses a parameter called 'ver' to each file that can be statically cached. This can be seen in the browser tools networks window, for example:

```
http://myserver.com/NwPortal/classic/app.js?ver=11.01.2201.00XXX

```

The value of this parameter comes from the file classic.json or modern.json depending on whether the desktop or mobile client is being loaded and is set to the release version number. Typically you do not need modify this value. However it should be noted that the same parameter is applied to files loaded from the list of [scripts and/or css files](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace/Loading-extra-scripts.html) specified in a workspace. It is often a good idea to specify your own parameter in the URL in the script element, for example:

```
<Section type="scripts">
   <Script name="sc1">
      <Url>/nwfonts/fonts.css?myver=1.0</Url>
   </Script>
</Section>

```

In this way if you change the file and require users to load the new version then you edit the workspace and modify the parameter. Restart the portal app pool as required and when users start the portal they will download your updated file.
Note that if the file you are loading contains a reference to another file then you will need to apply the same practice to the URLs in that file, for example:

```
@font-face {
  font-family: "Intergraph ISO"; 
  font-weight: normal; 
  font-style: normal; 
  font-display: block;
  src: url("./fonts/igriso.ttf?d1f55b") format("truetype");
}

```

If cache expiration headers are setup for the portal then they will be applied to static files but not service results.
## Metadata caching[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/State-management/Browser-caching.html#metadata-caching)
The portal can be configured to cache metadata from GTech and external services such as WMS capabilities. By default this is disabled and should only be enabled when the portal is running in anonymous mode (i.e. when OIDC is not enabled). Caching is defined in the web.config file by the attribute cacheExpiration defined on the  element e.g.

```
...
<webGIS cacheExpiration="0">
...

```

If set to 0 then caching is disabled. Setting it to a positive number defines how long data is to be cached in minutes.
When caching metadata requests the portal uses a parameter called 'ts'. For example:

```
http://myserver.com/NwPortal/default/services/legend/vectorserviceentry?name=vector1&G3E_LSNO=7&ts=1657733610153

```

The value for the parameter is the timestamp of the last saved date for the workspace. One way of notifying the client to changes in vector service metadata is to modify the workspace (can be be just a comment) and to restart the portal app pool as required. In addition to this the portal returns a cache control header which will cause the portal to reload the metadata after a set period.
If the portal is running in anonymous mode then performance can be improved by setting cacheExpiration to 12 hours e.g.

```
...
<webGIS cacheExpiration="720">
...

```

# Cookies
## Cookies[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/State-management/Cookies.html#cookies-1)
Cookies are used when open id connect is enabled and are necessary for the correct functioning of the portal. They are used to enable page navigation and to secure access to NetWorks services.  
| Name  | Type  | Expires  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| queryString  | HTTP  | Session  | Used for page navigation.  |  
| workspaceName  | HTTP  | Session  | Used for page navigation.  |  
| _authentication_  | HTTP  | Session  | The name of the authentication cookie can vary with the open id provider and can be split across multiple cookies e.g. '.AspNet.Cookies, .AspNet.CookiesC1 & .AspNet.CookiesC2'.  |

# IndexedDB
## IndexedDB[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/State-management/IndexedDB.html#indexeddb-1)
[IndexedDB](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/IndexedDB_API) is a standard browser API for storing large amounts of data on the client. The portal creates an indexeddb database the first time the user loads the portal named '422861d6-f7c0-40b6-89c4-8242aefbb3d2'. The reason for using a GUID to name the database is to avoid naming clashes with other web sites/applications on the same origin.
The database contains the following object stores:  
| Name  | Primary Key  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| configitem  | id  | Cache for workspace configuration loaded from the server.  |  
| legendentry  | id  | Contains configuration for map source entries user has added to the map e.g. analysis results and attached CAD files.  |  
| legendstate  | id  | Contains legend state saved by the user.  |  
| savedquery  | id  | Contains query definitions saved by the user.  |  
| setting  | key, workspace  | Contains setting values for settings overriden by the user.  |  
| state  | key, workspace  | Contains the current state of the portal e.g. legend state.  |  
| vectorresult  | id  | Contains the snapshots of analysis service results.  |  
| workspace  | id  | Cache for loaded workspaces.  |  
Portal plugins can modify data in these tables but they should never modify the structure of the database or add stores to it. In these cases they should create their own indexeddb database and work with that.
The objects stored in the object stores all have a similar structure, that being a javascript object with one or more key properties and a property called 'value' which contains the actual data.
Note that indexeddb should not be confused with 'Web SQL' as these are two functionally separate APIs.
## configitem[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/State-management/IndexedDB.html#configitem)
Required object properties:  
| Name  | Type  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| workspace  | string  | Workspace name.  |  
| section  | string  | Config section type.  |  
| name  | string  | Config item name.  |  
The combination of workspace, section and name must be unique.
## legendentry[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/State-management/IndexedDB.html#legendentry)
Required object properties:  
| Name  | Type  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| workspace  | string  | Workspace name.  |  
| value.legend  | string  | Legend name.  |  
## legendstate[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/State-management/IndexedDB.html#legendstate)
Required object properties:  
| Name  | Type  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| workspace  | string  | Workspace name.  |  
| value.userName  | string  | User name.  |  
The combination of workspace and value.userName must be unique.
## savedquery[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/State-management/IndexedDB.html#savedquery)
Required object properties:  
| Name  | Type  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| workspace  | string  | Workspace name.  |  
| value.userName  | string  | User name.  |  
The combination of workspace and value.userName must be unique.

The combination of workspace and key must be unique.

The combination of workspace and key must be unique.

The combination of workspace, resultId, detailId and g3e_lsno must be unique.

# Portal reset
The Portal main toolbar contains, by default, a menu function for resetting the Portal. This function will delete the associated indexeddb database, clear localStorage and force the portal to re-read the default configuration from the server again. This function will remove the following types of data from the browser.
  * Redlines
  * User settings
  * Saved legend settings
  * Saved queries
  * Cached query and analysis results
  * Attached CAD files
  * Submitted and completed NetPlot jobs.
  * Submitted and completed NetExport jobs.

It will not remove files and cookies cached by the browser. To do this the browsers clear data functionality will need to be used.

# Window.localStorage
## Window.localStorage[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/State-management/Window.localStorage.html#windowlocalstorage-1)
[Window.localStorage](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/localStorage) is a standard browser API which allows storage of limited amounts of data which will persist between sessions. Within the portal it is used to persist user interface settings between sessions such as the feature editor position and size and the side bars collapsed status. Local storage behaves the same as a hash table or map using string keys. All setting keys used by the portal are prefixed with 'Hxgn.', for example:

```
> localStorage
< Storage {...}
   Hxgn.detailssearchwindow: "o%3Awidth%3Dn%253A350%5Eheight%3Dn%253A550%5Emax..."
   Hxgn.editor.: "o%3Awidth%3Dn%253A653.6000366210938%5Eheight%3Dn%253A534.3999633789062%5Emax..."
   Hxgn.editor.gtdws.WestPanel: "o%3Aweight%3Dn%253A-10"
   Hxgn.editor.gtdws.tabPanel: "o%3Acolumns%3Da%253Ao%25253Aid%25253Ds%2525253Ah1"
   Hxgn.querywindow: "o%3Awidth%3Dn%253A600%5Eheight%3Dn%253A500%5Emaximized%3Db%253A0%5..."
   Hxgn.search.queryPanel.northPanel: "o%3Aweight%3Dn%253A20"
   Hxgn.search.queryPanel.westPanel: "o%3Aweight%3Dn%253A-10"
   Hxgn.sidebarpanel: "o%3Awidth%3Dn%253A351.1999816894531%5Eweight%3Dn%253A-10%5Ecollapsed%3Db%253A0"
  length: 8[[Prototype]]: Storage

```

Other web sites and/or portal plugins on the same origin as the portal can also make use of localStorage, as long as the keys they use are not prefixed with 'Hxgn.' (case sensitive).

# Cost - constraint trace markers settings
Cost-constraint trace displays markers on map. Style of these markers is taken from [style settings](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Settings/Styles.html) where you can find styles values specified as json under `trace.circle`.
These values are used to render markers and can be customized:  
| Setting  | Description  | Example value  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| trace.circle.fill.color  | Color of the marker, in rgba array format [red,green,blue,opacity]  | [0, 255, 0, 0.3]  |  
| trace.circle.stroke.color  | Color of the marker's border, in rgba array format [red,green,blue,opacity]  | [0, 255, 0, 1]  |  
| trace.circle.stroke.width  | Width of marker's border  | 3  |  
| trace.circle.radius  | Radius of the marker  | 10  |

## Modifying the web site[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Web-site-contents.html#modifying-the-web-site)
When the portal is redeployed using Networks deployment tools then the web site folder and all files in it will be deleted and a new folder created. Therefore any files added or modified after deployment will be removed. The Networks deployment do however contain tools to reapply changes to the portal web site.
Generally it is not recommended that, aside from modifying the files under 'settings' that you add, modify or remove files in the web site. Normally it is simpler to deploy additional HTML, CSS, scripts, services etc. in separate virtual directories or applications on the same web server.
If it is necessary add files to the web site then it is strongly recommended that they are placed into folders or sub folders that you create and not to place files directly into existing folders. This will make it much simpler to move your additions when updating to a newer version of the portal.

# Workset Monitor UI
## Introduction[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Workset-Monitor-Plugin/Workset-Monitor-UI.html#introduction)
This document describes the main elements of the Workset Monitor UI. The plugin is displayed within a rectangular frame and is designed to work in portrait mode i.e. the height of the rectangle is greater than its width from the users perspective.
The general layout of the plugin is such that at the the toolbar is always placed at the top and at least one status bar at the bottom. The status bar may be configured to display multiple lines of text. In between the toolbar(s) and status bar(s) is a panel which allow the user to perform a set of functions. Depending on where the user is within a Workset Monitor workflow the panel can be switched to another panel.
## Panels[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Workset-Monitor-Plugin/Workset-Monitor-UI.html#panels)
### Workset List[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Workset-Monitor-Plugin/Workset-Monitor-UI.html#workset-list)
When the plugin is initially started this is the first panel to be displayed. The panel constains a table displaying the worksets which have been submitted by the user previously . It also gives the user access to the following functions:
  * Filter - at the very top of the panel there is so-called "Filter row", which allows user to filter based on `State` (available states to filter are localized equivalents of `Queued`, `In Progress`, `Success`, `Error` and `Cancelled`), which allows multiple choices from picklist, `Configuration` and `User` (text fields). The field `Filter` dynamically generates the actual SQL-like filter string that is being sent to the server, and can be manually altered by user. NOTE: there is no two-way binding, once the eventual field value is altered, the other filter fields are not adjusted accordingly.
  * Open Message Detail - By clicking on the item from the list, Message Detail panel is being open.
  * Re-submit - it is possible to re-submit one or more Worksets. This button becomes available only in case one or more items are selected.
  * Set success state - This sets the status of selected Worksets to `SUCCESS`. This function should only be available if one or more Worksets are selected.
  * Set cancelled state. This sets the status of selected Worksets to `CANCELLED`. This function should only be available if one or more Worksets are selected.
  * View logs. This function is only available if exactly one Workset is selected. This opens `View Logs panel` and show log messages of particular Workset.

The table is scrollable in both the X and Y axis as required. It displays job id, description, state. Paging toolbar is shown at the bottom of the page if returned number of worksets is larger than specified number of items per page.
### Workset Detail[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Workset-Monitor-Plugin/Workset-Monitor-UI.html#workset-detail)
The Workset Detail panel displays read-only detail information about the Workset. It also gives the user access to the following functions:
  * View logs - similar functionality as View Logs from Workset List panel
  * Workset JSON - This opens View Request JSON panel and shows Workset's `request.json` body.

### View Logs[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Workset-Monitor-Plugin/Workset-Monitor-UI.html#view-logs)
The Workset Logs panel shows error code/error detail combination of logs for the selected Workset if any logs are available, otherwise user is notified that no logs are available
### Workset JSON[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Workset-Monitor-Plugin/Workset-Monitor-UI.html#workset-json)
The Workset JSON panel shows raw unformatted `request.json` body of the Workset. The user is able to manually edit the request.json body and submit the change.
##### Note
Since Data Transfer Service is doing periodic clean up of transactions, if Transaction is no longer on a disk, Request JSON body cannot be found and read, therefore user is notified that Request JSON body is not available.

# Workset Monitor Plugin
## Introduction[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Workset-Monitor-Plugin.html#introduction)
The Workset Monitor is a web application used for administrative purposes of monitoring the submitted [Feature Editor](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Feature-Editor.html) worksets from various clients.
Workset Monitor is developed as a NetWorks Portal plug-in (using the same architecture as Feature Editor). Workset Monitor communicates with Data Transfer Service, which uses the central NetWorks database to store information on submitted worksets.
Configuration and architecture information can be found under [Workset Monitor](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Feature-Editor/Workset-Monitor.html).
## Functionality and Use Cases[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Workset-Monitor-Plugin.html#functionality-and-use-cases)
### 1. Display list of worksets[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Workset-Monitor-Plugin.html#1-display-list-of-worksets)
The system displays a list of all worksets submitted through Data Transfer Service. The user has options to filter the list by:
  * State (queued, in progress, success, error, cancelled)
  * Configuration name
  * User (identification of user, who submitted the workset)

### 2. Display workset details[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Workset-Monitor-Plugin.html#2-display-workset-details)
The system displays, on user request, details of a submitted workset, including:
  * request content
  * processing results (job identifier, feature and component identifiers)
  * errors from processing

### 3. Edit workset[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Workset-Monitor-Plugin.html#3-edit-workset)
The system allows display and editing of the JSON representation of the workset request, in order to fix data related issues. The modified request is saved to the original DTS transaction, reverted to open state.
### 4. Resubmit workset[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Workset-Monitor-Plugin.html#4-resubmit-workset)
The system allows repeated submitting of a workset (or multiple worksets).
### 5. Set workset processing status[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Workset-Monitor-Plugin.html#5-set-workset-processing-status)
The system allows the user to set the status of a workset explicitly to Cancelled or Success. This allows manual clean-up of worksets, which would be otherwise stuck in an error state.
### 5. Periodic clean-up[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Workset-Monitor-Plugin.html#5-periodic-clean-up)
The system periodically runs a clean-up process (DTS internal scheduled processing or Oracle job), which deletes or moves obsolete records (i.e. records in specific states, which weren’t changed in the last N days).
