#### Administration-Console

# Attach vector file configuration
## Overview[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Administration-Console/Attach-vector-file-configuration.html#overview)
NetWorks Portal supports the workflow ad-hoc attach of vector files (AutoCAD - DWG, DXF, Microstation - DGN, or Shapefiles). This requires the upload of the files, their conversion to DDC and rendering using Dynamic WMS. As such this workflow requires deployment and proper configuration of the Data Transfer Service, Work Service and Dynamic WMS Service.
The following diagram depicts the situation after deployment and the configuration parameters which need to point to the same locations.
[![AttachCAD_configuration_v01.svg](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/.attachments/AttachCAD_configuration_v01-3944b45e-ac63-4d2d-876d-e33b3f563a5e.svg)](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/.attachments/AttachCAD_configuration_v01-3944b45e-ac63-4d2d-876d-e33b3f563a5e.svg)
##### Note
Follow HxGN NetWorks Core Administrator's Guide related to configuration parameters (e.g. `SHPComponentNumber`, `SHPFeatureNumber`) needed for usage of tools **PublishCADFiles.exe** and **PublishShapeToDDC.exe**.
## Configuration[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Administration-Console/Attach-vector-file-configuration.html#configuration)
### Uploaded files[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Administration-Console/Attach-vector-file-configuration.html#uploaded-files)
**Data Transfer Service** stores uploaded files into a folder on the disk. This value is configured using **Root folder for committed transactions**.
**Work Service** looks for uploaded vector files to be processed. Its configuration parameter **Path to storage folder for uploaded files** must be set the same value as in **Root folder for committed transactions** of the Data Transfer Service.
## Converted files[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Administration-Console/Attach-vector-file-configuration.html#converted-files)
**Dynamic WMS Service** looks for folders with DDC files on a disk folder. This value is configured using **Path to root folder of DDC storage**.
**Work Service** places DDC files converted from uploaded vector sources to disk folder. This value is configured using **Path to storage folder for Dynamic WMS Service**
## Portal[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Administration-Console/Attach-vector-file-configuration.html#portal)
NetWorks Portal finds the service instances to be used in the Attach vector workflow using two modes:
  * Discovery Portal uses the NetWorks Solution Service to discover the location (URL) of the services.
  * Configuration URLs of the services are explicitly configured in the Portal's **web.config** file under the **webGIS** element as **dataTransferServiceUrl** , **dynamicWMSUrl** and **workServiceUrl** entries, e.g.:

```
<webGIS GTechConfiguration="NETWORKS">
    <dataTransferServiceUrl path="https://server.com/DataTransferService" />
    <dynamicWMSUrl path="https://server.com/DynamicWMSService" />
    <workServiceUrl path="http://localhost:9400/" />
    <!-- ... -->
</webGIS>

```

For deployments with OpenID Connect, Data Transfer Service and Dynamic WMS Service must be also registered under **proxyUrls**. Example:

```
<proxyUrls>
  <add name="datatransfer" path="https://server.com/DataTransferService" />
  <add name="dynamicwms" path="https://server.com/DynamicWMSService" />
</proxyUrls>

```

##### Important
When deploying Portal using Administration Console, make sure the Data Transfer Service and Dynamic WMS Service are deployed before deploying the Portal instance. Otherwise the automatic deployment for Portal will not discover and register the **proxyUrls**.
## Parameter mapping[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Administration-Console/Attach-vector-file-configuration.html#parameter-mapping)
Mapping of Administration console parameters to service parameter names is in the following table.  
| Service  | Parameter in Console  | Parameter in Configuration  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| Data Transfer Service  | Root folder for committed transactions  | [transactionStore:committed](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Data-Transfer-Service/Configuration.html)  |  
| Work Service  | Path to storage folder for uploaded files  | [ConvertCAD:InputPath](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Configuration.html)  |  
| Work Service  | Path to storage folder for Dynamic WMS Service  | [ConvertCAD:OutputPath](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Configuration.html)  |  
| Dynamic WMS Service  | Path to root folder of DDC storage  | [Storage:Root](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Dynamic-WMS-Service/Configuration.html)  |

# Common deployment settings
Common settings for deployment can be stored in an INI file named **DeploymentConfig.ini** , located in the same folder as **NetWorksDeployedServices.xml**. The default location is `%ProgramData%\Intergraph\NetWorks\DeployedServices\`.
## Properties[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Administration-Console/Common-deployment-settings.html#properties)  
| Name  | Description  | Value if missing  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| ServiceDeployment:Hostname  | Host name to be used in host part of the URL when deploying Portal.  | Current machine name (environment variable `COMPUTERNAME`).  |  
| ServiceDeployment:DefaultWebSite  | Name of IIS web site to which services are deployed.  | Default Web Site  |  
| ServiceDeployment:Fonts:Preload  | Switch indicating whether font preload links should be included in `index.html` file.  | `false`  |  
| ServiceDeployment:Fonts:SourceFolder  | Folder used as a source for font files during deployment.  | System default fonts folder  |  
| ServiceDeployment:Fonts:Formats  | Comma separated list of font formats processed during deployment. Allowed values: `truetype`, `opentype`, `woff`, `woff2`.  | `truetype`  |  
| ServiceDeployment:Fonts:CrossOrigin  | Content of the crossorigin attribute on preload fonts `<link>` element  | `anonymous`  |  
| TNS_ADMIN  | Oracle TNS_ADMIN setting. When present, some services (Vector, Dynamic WMS, Data Transfer, Work Service) use this value unless it's overridden in the service instance configuration.  |   |  
| ClientIdClaim  | If set, the claim is used to identify user actions in the database. See [User identifier in database operations](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Data-Access/User-identifier-in-database-operations.html).  |   |  
| NetworksVectorSource:RenderMaskSymbols  | Deploy Portal with mask symbol rendering for Vector Service sources. Allowed values: `true`, `false`.  | `true`  |  
| IIS_AppPool_AlwaysRunning  | When `true`, the app. pool is set as _AlwaysRunning_. Allowed values: `true`, `false`.  | `false`  |  
| IIS_AppPool_IdleTimeout  | Idle timeout for the app. pool. Set to `00:00:00` to disable the idle timeout. Format: `HH:MM:SS`.  |   |  
| IIS_AppPool_DisableOverlappingCycle  | Set to `true` to disable overlapping app. pool cycle. Allowed values: `true`, `false`.  | `false`  |  
| IIS_Application_EnablePreload  | Set to `true` to enable preload of the app. by IIS. Allowed values: `true`, `false`.  | `true`  |  
## File formatting[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Administration-Console/Common-deployment-settings.html#file-formatting)
See [ServiceConfig.ini](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Configuration/How-service-locates-configuration-files/ServiceConfig.ini.html) for formatting rules.
## Example[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Administration-Console/Common-deployment-settings.html#example)

```
; Common deployment properties
ServiceDeployment:Hostname=web.mycompany.com
ServiceDeployment:DefaultWebSite=mycompany.com
TNS_ADMIN=c:\Oracle\tns
ClientIdClaim=email

```

# Definition of Coordinate systems
**Overview**
Administration Console modules use file `CRSConfig_v2.xml` to determine the definition of the coordinate system when deploying services and Portal. The file is located in the NetWorks Program folder.
When a NetWorks configuration uses a coordinate system not present in this file, deployment might fail.
A cache of previously used coordinate system definitions is kept at `%ProgramData%Intergraph\NetWorks\EpsgDefinitions\`. The content of this folder can be removed or updated, if update to coordinate system definition is needed.
**Workaround**
Edit the `CRSConfig_v2.xml` file and add missing coordinate system definition.
**Example**

```
<category name="Czech Republic">
  <code name="S-JTSK / Krovak" value="EPSG:5513">
    <axes>
      <axis>
        <dir>south</dir>
        <label>Y</label>
      </axis>
      <axis>
        <dir>west</dir>
        <label>X</label>
      </axis>
    </axes>
    <south>47.73</south>
    <north>51.06</north>
    <west>12.09</west>
    <east>22.56</east>
    <attributes>+proj=krovak +lat_0=49.5 +lon_0=24.83333333333333 +alpha=30.28813972222222 +k=0.9999 +x_0=0 +y_0=0 +ellps=bessel +towgs84=589,76,480,0,0,0,0 +units=m +no_defs </attributes>
    <isGeographic>false</isGeographic>
    <unit>
      <name>metre</name>
      <value>1</value>
    </unit>
  </code>
</category>

```

# Deploy services as always running
Command line deployment tools can configure services hosted in IIS as always running, i.e. their app. pools are not terminated after a period of inactivity. This setting can improve perceived startup times, at the expense of higher memory usage.
This configurable is application to all IIS hosted services, i.e. all services except for services hosted as Windows services (Work Service, Deltas Service), which are started by default.
## How to configure[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Administration-Console/Deploy-services-as-always-running.html#how-to-configure)
This setting requires manual configuration in the `%ProgramData%Intergraph\NetWorks\DeployedServices\NetWorksDeployedServices.xml` file.
These parameters can be added to the XML element with the properties of the service (e.g. `<NetWorksPortal>` or `<WMS>`).  
| Name  | Data type  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| IIS_AppPool_AlwaysRunning  | boolean  | When `True`, the app. pool is set as _AlwaysRunning_.  |  
| IIS_AppPool_IdleTimeout  | timespan  | Idle timeout for the app. pool. Set to `00:00:00` to disable the idle timeout.  |  
| IIS_Application_EnablePreload  | boolean  | Set to `True` to enable preload of the app. by IIS.  |  
## Example - set WMS as Always running[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Administration-Console/Deploy-services-as-always-running.html#example---set-wms-as-always-running)

```
<WMS InstanceName="WmsElectricDetailsGINIUSANON"
     ...
     IIS_AppPool_AlwaysRunning="True"
     IIS_AppPool_IdleTimeout="00:00:00" 
     IIS_Application_EnablePreload="True" 
/>

```

##### Deployment-customization

# Customization file syntax
## Organization[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Administration-Console/Deployment-customization/Customization-file-syntax.html#organization)
The customization file is an XML file. It's root element is always `<configuration>`. The configuration element can contain 0 or more of the following elements which define what to modify:  
| Name  | Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
| `<serviceConfig>`  | Contains XML modifications to instance **ServiceConfig.xml** file.  |  
| `<settings>`  | Contains modifications to the **Portal settings** or **ServiceConfig.ini** file.  |  
| `<web.config>`  | Contains XML modifications to instance **web.config** file.  |  
| `<workspace>`  | Contains XML modifications to **Portal workspace** files. The attribute `name` can be used to specify the workspace files which defaults to `default`.  |  
Each element can be present 0 or more times. The modifications they define are applied in the order they are presented in the file, from top to bottom.
Where a name attribute is defined on a `<workspace>` element then the value of the attribute is matched to the value of the name attribute of an `<add>` element in the portals [web.config](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/web.config-file/Workspaces.html) file defining a workspace file or folder. If no match is found then no customizations are applied. If the name corresponds to a workspace folder and that folder contains multiple XML files then the customizations will be applied to each XML file.
### Example[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Administration-Console/Deployment-customization/Customization-file-syntax.html#example)

```
<configuration>
  <web.config>
     <!--XML modifications for web.config file-->
  </web.config>
  <serviceConfig>
     <!-- XML modifications for ServiceConfig.xml file-->
  </serviceConfig>
  <settings target='ServiceConfig.ini'>
     <!-- ServiceConfig.ini  modifications -->
  </settings>
  <settings>
     <!--Portal settings modifications-->
  </settings>
  <workspace>
     <!--XML modifications (for workspace file(s) referenced by name='default')-->
  </workspace>
  <workspace name="workspace1">
     <!--XML modifications for workspace file(s) referenced by name='workspace1'-->
  </workspace>
</configuration>

```

Under `<serviceConfig>`, `<web.config>` or `<workspace>` elements zero or more XML operation elements can be defined. Under `<settings>` elements can be defined zero or more `<setting>` elements.
## XML Operations[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Administration-Console/Deployment-customization/Customization-file-syntax.html#xml-operations)
Valid XML operations are **add** , **addattribute** , **change** , and **delete** defined by XML elements of the same name placed directly under the element which defines the XML to modify.
All operations elements require a **path** attribute. The **path** specifies an XML **element** or XML **attribute** in the XML file where the operation is to be performed. If the path matches multiple nodes in the XML document, the operation is performed on all of them.
Path is specified using the [XPath](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/XPath) language.
For example:

```
<configuration>
   <workspace>
      <add path="/config/Workspace[@name='default']/Section[@type='print']" position="last">
         <Template name="MyA4">
            <!-- Print template content -->
         </Template>
      </add>
   </workspace>
</configuration>

```

### add[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Administration-Console/Deployment-customization/Customization-file-syntax.html#add)
Adds new XML content to the target file relative to the element(s) defined by path. For example:

```
<add path="path to a xml element goes here" position="see below for values">
   <!-- XML content to add is defined here -->
</add>

```
  
| Attribute  | Required  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| path  | Y  | Specifies affected element(s) in the file.  |  
| position  | Y  | Specifies where to add the new content relative to path.  |  
Allowed values for position  
| Value  | Behavior  |  
| --- | --- |  
| first  | Add content as the first child of XML element.  |  
| last  | Add content as the last child of XML element.  |  
| before  | Add content as a sibling before the XML element.  |  
| after  | Add content as a sibling after the XML element.  |  
For example, to add a new print template to the default workspace:

```
<add path="/config/Workspace[@name='default']/Section[@type='print']" position="last">
  <Template name="MyA4" />
</add>

```

### addattribute[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Administration-Console/Deployment-customization/Customization-file-syntax.html#addattribute)
Add an attribute to the element(s) defined by path.  
| Attribute  | Required  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| path  | Y  | Specifies affected element(s) in the file.  |  
| name  | Y  | Name of the added attribute.  |  
| namespace  | N  | XML namespace (not prefix) of the added attribute.  |  
The content of the `<addattribute>` element defines the attributes value. It should be text only and is required.
For example, to add a new attribute to an XML element:

```
<addattribute path="/config/Workspace[@name='default']" name="mycustomtag">My custom workspace</addattribute>

```

### change[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Administration-Console/Deployment-customization/Customization-file-syntax.html#change)
Change the content of the element(s) defined by path, replace the element(s) defined by path **or** change the value of the attribute(s) defined by path.  
| Attribute  | Required  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| path  | Y  | Specifies affected element(s) in the file.  |  
| mode  | N  | Replacement mode for XML elements. Default is `content`.  |  
Allowed values for mode.  
| Value  | Behavior  |  
| --- | --- |  
| content  | Replace the content of the element(s) defined by path with the content of the `<change>` element.  |  
| replace  | Replace the element(s) defined by path with the content of the `<change>` element.  |  
The content of a `<change>` element can be any valid XML, however, if changing an attribute value then the content _must_ be plain text only as XML attribute can only contain text.
Example 1: Replace the _contents_ (i.e. inner XML) of an XML element in target document with content of the `<change>` XML element.

```
<change path="/config/Section[@type='maplegend']/Legend/View">
  <Projection>EPSG:3857</Projection>
  <Center>4500105,5708299</Center>
  <Resolution>52.87</Resolution>
</change>

```

Example 2: Replace an _element_ (i.e. outer XML) in target document with the content of the `<change>` element.

```
<change path="/config/Section[@type='maplegend']/Legend/View" mode="replace">
  <View>
    <Projection>EPSG:3857</Projection>
    <Center>4500105,5708299</Center>
    <Resolution>52.87</Resolution>
  </View>
</change>

```

Example 3: Change an XML element value, e.g. the default edit mode to `Review`:

```
<change path="/config/Section[@type='editor']/GtdwsEditor[@name='networksEditor']/DefaultType">Review</change>

```

Example 4: Change an XML attribute value:

```
<change path="/config/Section[@type='maplegend']/Legend/@username">My custom legend</change>

```

### delete[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Administration-Console/Deployment-customization/Customization-file-syntax.html#delete)
Delete the element(s) defined by path.
The **path** must specify an **element** in the file.
For example to remove the redlines tab from the portal:

```
<delete path="/config/Workspace[@name='default']/Section[@type='function']/Function[@name='sidebar']/Config/JProperty/JArray/JValue[text()='redline']"/>

```

## Portal settings[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Administration-Console/Deployment-customization/Customization-file-syntax.html#portal-settings)
Portal [settings](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Settings.html) settings can be changed by adding a `<settings>` element under the  root element. For example:

```
<settings>
  <setting name="setting name" value="setting value"/>
</settings>

```

The `<settings>` can contain zero or more `<setting>` elements which must defined the following attributes.  
| Attribute  | Required  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| name  | Y  | The name of the setting to change.  |  
| value  | Y  | The new value of the setting.  |  
For example, to change the highlight color to green:

```
<configuration>
  <settings>
    <setting name="styles.highlight.circle.fill.color" value="[0, 255, 0, 0.3]" />
    <setting name="styles.highlight.circle.stroke.color" value="[0, 255, 0, 1]" />
    <setting name="styles.highlight.fill.color" value="[0, 255, 0, 0.3]" />
    <setting name="styles.highlight.stroke.color" value="[0, 255, 0, 0.7]" />
  </settings>
</configuration>

```

## ServiceConfig.ini[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Administration-Console/Deployment-customization/Customization-file-syntax.html#serviceconfigini)
Settings in the service configuration [ServiceConfig.ini](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Configuration/How-service-locates-configuration-files/ServiceConfig.ini.html) file can be changed by defining a `<settings>` element under the root `<configuration>` element. The attribute **target** must be set to the value `ServiceConfig.ini`.
If the setting already exists in the file, the _last occurrence_ is replaced with the new value. Otherwise, a new line is added to the end of the file.
> **Note** The -s parameter must be specified on the command line to the _RunCustomization.exe_ tool.

```
<settings target="ServiceConfig.ini">
  <setting name="setting name" value="setting value"/>
</settings>

```

Example:

```
<configuration>
  <settings target="ServiceConfig.ini">
    <setting name="UseDefaultIdentity" value="False" />
  </settings>
</configuration>

```

## See also[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Administration-Console/Deployment-customization/Customization-file-syntax.html#see-also)
  * [XML terminology](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Administration-Console/Deployment-customization/XML-terminology.html)
  * [Examples](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Administration-Console/Deployment-customization/Examples.html)

# Customization from folder
## Workflow[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Administration-Console/Deployment-customization/Customization-from-folder.html#workflow)
When using the Administration Console to edit a service or Portal in the Service Deployment Module, specify a path to a folder instead of a path to a single customization XML file.
When deploying a service or Portal, the Administration Console will apply customizations from all `*.xml` files in the folder, as well as run any custom scripts defined in `*.cmd` and `*.bat` files. By default, the customizations are applied in the order defined by file names.
It is possible to force explicit order (and filtering) by creating a text file name `.order` in the folder. The `.order` file should contain list of file names in the order in which they should be applied.
## Example[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Administration-Console/Deployment-customization/Customization-from-folder.html#example)
The folder `C:\customizations\` contains the necessary customization XML and scripts. Specify this path in the Administration Console.
File system:

```
C:/
    customizations/
        .order
        AddOn1.xml
        BoundingBoxFixes.xml
        settings_custom.js
        CopySettings.cmd

```

In this example, `settings_custom.js` will be ignored as it has a '.js' extension.
**.order** file contents:

```
BoundingBoxFixes.xml
CopySettings.cmd
AddOn1.xml

```

Administration console will apply `BoundingBoxFixes.xml` first, then run the `CopySettings.cmd` script and finally apply `AddOn1.xml`.
## Windows scripts[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Administration-Console/Deployment-customization/Customization-from-folder.html#windows-scripts)
When executing a `.bat` or `.cmd` script, the script will be executed using the same file privileges as those being used to run the Administration Console. The working directory for the script will be set to the deployed service or Portal instance's root directory. It is therefore possible to use relative file paths within a batch script. The physical path to the deployed service or Portal instance is also passed in as a command line parameter of the script. For example the following script would, if used when deploying a Portal, copy the `settings_custom.js` file into the deployed Portal instance.

```
copy /y c:\customizations\settings_custom.js .\settings\

```

# Examples
## Modify Portal settings and workspace[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Administration-Console/Deployment-customization/Examples.html#modify-portal-settings-and-workspace)

```
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8" ?>
<configuration>

  <!-- Change the highlight color to green -->
  <settings>
    <setting name="styles.highlight.circle.fill.color" value="[0, 255, 0, 0.3]" />
    <setting name="styles.highlight.circle.stroke.color" value="[0, 255, 0, 1]" />
    <setting name="styles.highlight.fill.color" value="[0, 255, 0, 0.3]" />
    <setting name="styles.highlight.stroke.color" value="[0, 255, 0, 0.7]" />
  </settings>

  <workspace>
    <!-- Delete the base map -->
    <delete path="/config/Section[@type='maplegend']/Legend[@name='default']/Entries/SourceEntry[./SourceName='osm']" />

    <!-- Change the name of the WMS (change attribute value) -->
    <change path="/config/Section[@type='mapsource']/WMSSource[@name='wms0']/@username">
      Electric Design Legend
    </change>

    <!-- Remove all the print templates and replace them with MyA4 -->
    <change path="/config/Workspace[@name='default']/Section[@type='print']">
      <Template name="MyA4" />
    </change>

    <!-- Change the editor to review mode (change element value) -->
    <change path="/config/Section[@type='editor']/GtdwsEditor[@name='networksEditor']/DefaultType">Review</change>

    <!-- Change the default parameters of map view by replacing the content of the <View> element -->
    <change path="/config/Section[@type='maplegend']/Legend/View">
      <Projection>EPSG:3857</Projection>
      <Center>4500105,5708299</Center>
      <Resolution>52.87</Resolution>
    </change>

    <!-- Change the default parameters of map view by replacing the <View> element completely -->
    <change path="/config/Section[@type='maplegend']/Legend/View" mode='replace'>
      <View>
        <Projection>EPSG:3857</Projection>
        <Center>4500105,5708299</Center>
        <Resolution>52.87</Resolution>
      </View>
    </change>

  </workspace>

</configuration>

```

## Modification of Portal web.config[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Administration-Console/Deployment-customization/Examples.html#modification-of-portal-webconfig)
Register explicit URLs for services:

```
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<configuration>
  <web.config>
    <add path="/configuration/webGIS" position="first">
      <dialogWebServiceUrl path="http://server/GtdwsGINIUSANON" />
    </add>
    <add path="/configuration/webGIS" position="first">
      <analyticalWebServiceUrl path="http://server/AnalyticalServiceGINIUSANON" />
    </add>
    <add path="/configuration/webGIS" position="first">
      <jobWebServiceUrl path="http://server/JobServiceGINIUSANON" />    
    </add>
    <add path="/configuration/webGIS" position="first">
      <workServiceUrl path="http://localhost:9400/" />
    </add>
    <add path="/configuration/webGIS" position="first">
      <dynamicWMSUrl path="http://server/DynamicWMSServiceGINIUSANON" />
    </add>
    <add path="/configuration/webGIS" position="first">
      <dataTransferServiceUrl path="http://server/DataTransferServiceGINIUSANON" />    
    </add>    
  </web.config>
</configuration>

```

## Set explicit geographic bounding box for OGC service[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Administration-Console/Deployment-customization/Examples.html#set-explicit-geographic-bounding-box-for-ogc-service)

```
<configuration>
  <serviceConfig>
    <add path="/ucServiceConfiguration/providers/provider/providerSettings" position="last">
      <setting name="GeographicBoundingBox" value="-180.0,-85.0511,180.0,85.0511" />
    </add>
  </serviceConfig>
</configuration>

```

## Change URL of proxy in Portal web.config[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Administration-Console/Deployment-customization/Examples.html#change-url-of-proxy-in-portal-webconfig)
Text:

```
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8" ?>
<configuration>
	<web.config>
		<change path="/configuration/webGIS/proxyUrls">http://localhost/networksProxy</change>
	</web.config>
</configuration>

```

## Attribute change: set path to Portal workspace[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Administration-Console/Deployment-customization/Examples.html#attribute-change-set-path-to-portal-workspace)

```
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<configuration>
  <web.config>
    <change path="/configuration/webGIS/workspaces/add[@name='default']/@path">
      App_GlobalResources\Workspaces\NetWorks\Workspace.NETWORKS-external.xml
    </change>
  </web.config>
</configuration>

```

## Add new XML element[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Administration-Console/Deployment-customization/Examples.html#add-new-xml-element)
In case you want to change the whole XML Element, either combine Delete + Add methods described here, or in some case, if applicable, use change Attribute for attributes
### Add[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Administration-Console/Deployment-customization/Examples.html#add)

```
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<configuration>
  <web.config>
    <add path="/configuration/webGIS/services" position="last">
      <add name="engineeringplotting" type="Hexagon.Ginius.EP.WebGIS.HttpHandlers.APIHandler, Hexagon.Ginius.EP.WebGIS"/>
    </add>
  </web.config>
</configuration>

```

### Delete[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Administration-Console/Deployment-customization/Examples.html#delete)

```
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<configuration>
  <web.config>
    <delete path="/configuration/webGIS/services/add[@name='netplot']" />
  </web.config>
</configuration>

```

## Add settings to ServiceConfig.ini[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Administration-Console/Deployment-customization/Examples.html#add-settings-to-serviceconfigini)

```
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8" ?>
<configuration>
  <settings target="ServiceConfig.ini">
    <setting name="UseDefaultIdentity" value="False" />
    <setting name="LCID" value="0009" />
  </settings>
</configuration>

```

# Set extra configuration parameters
## Overview[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Administration-Console/Deployment-customization/Set-extra-configuration-parameters.html#overview)
Administration Console writes only specific configuration parameters to configuration files when deploying services. Not all configuration parameters have their UI element.
For services which use configuration based on [**instance.ini** and **ServiceConfig.ini**](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Configuration.html) it is possible to setup automatic configuration of extra parameters during deployment.
## How to configure[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Administration-Console/Deployment-customization/Set-extra-configuration-parameters.html#how-to-configure)
Administration Console keeps track of configured services in file **%PROGRAMDATA%\Intergraph\NetWorks\DeployedServices\NetWorksDeployedServices.xml**.
Each service has a record on the first level, e.g.:

```
<VectorService 
  InstanceName="VectorService1" 
  IsInSolution="True" 
  IsDeployed="True" 
  InstanceId="e0b353d6-35c3-4e2f-a413-57d92150897f"
  InstanceDescription="" 
  ...
/>

```

To add an extra parameter which should be written to **ServiceConfig.ini** , add this parameter to the service XML element. Replace all `:` (colon) characters in parameter name with `__` (double underscore).
**Example**
Vector Service parameters `UseDefaultIdentity` and `infrastructureServiceAuthentication:Parameters:RequiredClaims` can be configured for automatic configuration upon deployment.

```
<VectorService 
  InstanceName="VectorService1" 
  IsInSolution="True" 
  IsDeployed="True" 
  InstanceId="e0b353d6-35c3-4e2f-a413-57d92150897f"
  InstanceDescription="" 
  ...
  UseDefaultIdentity="false" 
  infrastructureServiceAuthentication__Parameters__RequiredClaims="gtechnologyDBConnect,g3e_role" 
/>

```

# XML terminology
XML contains **elements** and **attributes**. An **element** can have zero or more **attributes**.
For example, _Workspace_ is an XML element while _name_ and _username_ are XML attributes.

```
<Workspace name="default" username="Default">

```

XML **elements** can also have **content**. Content can be one or more XML **elements** or plain text.
In the following example, the _Section_ element has XML content while the _DefaultType_ element has plain text content.

```
<Section>
  <Legend />
  <Legend />
</Section>
<DefaultType>Edit</DefaultType>

```

XML **attributes** must have a plain text **value**.
For example, the **value** of the _name_ **attribute** is default.

```
<Workspace name="default" username="Default">

```

# Deployment customization
## Overview[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Administration-Console/Deployment-customization.html#overview)
NetWorks Administration Console can process customization XML files defined for each deployed service or Portal. The files are processed immediately after deployment or redeployment of the instance. The files can be used to modify (where applicable):
  * `web.config` file
  * `ServiceConfig.xml` file
  * `ServiceConfig.ini` file
  * Portal workspace file
  * Portal settings

In addition to the customization XML files it is also possible to execute `.bat` or `.cmd` script files immediately after service or Portal deployment to further customize the deployment.
## Configuration[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Administration-Console/Deployment-customization.html#configuration)
NetWorks Administration Console allows configuration of a customization path in the **Enable Custom Configurations** text box. The path may be either of the following:
  * Path to single customization XML file
  * [Path to folder with customization files](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Administration-Console/Deployment-customization/Customization-from-folder.html)

Where a path to a folder is defined then all customization XML files in the folder will be processed and all script files in the folder will be executed.
## See also[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Administration-Console/Deployment-customization.html#see-also)
  * [Customization file syntax](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Administration-Console/Deployment-customization/Customization-file-syntax.html)
  * [Examples](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Administration-Console/Deployment-customization/Examples.html)

# Export data to Excel configuration
## Overview[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Administration-Console/Export-data-to-Excel-configuration.html#overview)
NetWorks Portal supports the workflow ad-hoc attach of vector files (AutoCAD - DWG, DXF, Microstation - DGN, or Shapefiles). This requires the upload of the files, their conversion to DDC and rendering using Dynamic WMS. As such this workflow requires deployment and proper configuration of the Data Transfer Service, Work Service and Dynamic WMS Service.
NetWorks Portal supports export of tabular data to Microsoft Excel. This requires the upload of files, their conversion to Excel and download. As such this workflow requires deployment and proper configuration of the Data Transfer Service and Work Service.
The following diagram depicts the situation after deployment and the configuration parameters which need to point to the same locations.
[![ExportData_configuration_v01.svg](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/.attachments/ExportData_configuration_v01-b8d050b8-d626-4029-b20d-0beb82b52b25.svg)](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/.attachments/ExportData_configuration_v01-b8d050b8-d626-4029-b20d-0beb82b52b25.svg)
## Configuration[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Administration-Console/Export-data-to-Excel-configuration.html#configuration)
**Data Transfer Service** stores uploaded files into a folder on the disk and provides access to exported data file. This value is configured using **Root folder for committed transactions**.
**Work Service** looks for uploaded vector files to be processed. Its configuration parameter **Path to storage folder for Export Data files** must be set the same value as in **Root folder for committed transactions** of the Data Transfer Service.
## Portal[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Administration-Console/Export-data-to-Excel-configuration.html#portal)
NetWorks Portal finds the service instances to be used in the Export Data workflow using two modes:
  * Discovery Portal uses the NetWorks Solution Service to discover the location (URL) of the services.
  * Configuration URLs of the services are explicitly configured in the Portal's [Workspace](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/Workspace.html) file under the `<Services>` element as **DataTransferService** and **WorkService** entries, e.g.:

For deployments with OpenID Connect, Data Transfer Service must be also registered under **proxyUrls** in Portal [web.config file](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Configuration/web.config-file.html). Example:

```
<proxyUrls>
  <add name="datatransfer" path="https://server.com/DataTransferService" />
</proxyUrls>

```

##### Important
When deploying Portal using Administration Console, make sure the Data Transfer Service is deployed before deploying the Portal instance. Otherwise the automatic deployment for Portal will not discover and register the **proxyUrls**.
## Parameter mapping[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Administration-Console/Export-data-to-Excel-configuration.html#parameter-mapping)
Mapping of Administration console parameters to service parameter names is in the following table.  
| Service  | Parameter in Console  | Parameter in Configuration  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| Data Transfer Service  | Root folder for committed transactions  | [transactionStore:committed](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Data-Transfer-Service/Configuration.html)  |  
| Work Service  | Path to storage folder for Export Data files  | [ExportData:StoragePath](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Configuration.html)  |

# Override default host name when deploying services
**Requirement**
Use different hostname in URLs when deploying services and Portal.
**Workflow**
An optional appSetting `ServiceDeployment:Hostname` can be configured to override the default behavior in [**DeploymentConfig.ini**](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Administration-Console/Common-deployment-settings.html). If the setting is not present (i.e. equal to null or empty string), the deployment process uses the original behavior.
When the setting is in use, it overrides also the host name configured in IIS for https binding.
**Note**
When this value is changed, the Portal workspace in Administration Console must be reconfigured for this change to apply. Remove and add the NetWorks sources again and redeploy the Portal.

# Preload fonts when deploying Portal
## Issue description[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Administration-Console/Preload-fonts-when-deploying-Portal.html#issue-description)
When using Portal to view geometry data using Vector Service, label and symbol font files are referenced using a CSS file, which is loaded asynchronously after Portal startup, once the particular font is requested for rendering. Due to internal synchronization in browser, the first map which is rendered after opening Portal may not yet have the fonts downloaded, which may result in rendering of symbols and labels using the default system font. Zooming or panning the map a couple of seconds after opening Portal resolves the issue.
## Manual solution[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Administration-Console/Preload-fonts-when-deploying-Portal.html#manual-solution)
Web pages may instruct the browser to load fonts and other resources in advance, before they are actually used by putting a `<link>` element into the `<head>` block of the page.
_Example_

```
 <link rel="preload" href="vectorfonts/fonts/MySymbolFont.ttf?ff1298" crossorigin="anonymous" as="font">

```

## Automated solution[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Administration-Console/Preload-fonts-when-deploying-Portal.html#automated-solution)
Deployment of NetWorks Portal can include the preload elements for fonts used for label and symbol rendering into the Portal `index.html` page. This functionality is not enabled by default.
### Workflow[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Administration-Console/Preload-fonts-when-deploying-Portal.html#workflow)
  * Follow [Common deployment settings](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Administration-Console/Common-deployment-settings.html) and configure settings with prefix `ServiceDeployment:Fonts:` to enable this functionality.
  * Deploy or redeploy Portal instance(s) after changing the configuration.

##### Services-Deployment

# Data Transfer Service
When deploying Data Transfer Service instance, set these parameters:
  * **Definition**  
Select **Data Transfer Service**.
  * **InstanceName** uniquely identifies the deployed service instance. This value is used as the application name in the IIS. The following fields populate when you enter an Instance Name:
    * Application Pool Name
    * Physical Path
    * Virtual Path
    * Default Database User Name
    * Default Database Password
  * _Optional_ **Instance Description** is optional user description of this instance.
  * **Application Pool Name** is the name of the IIS application pool. This value is typically derived from InstanceName.
  * Select the **Application Pool Identity** from the drop-down list. If **SpecificUser** is selected, enter your network credentials in **Application Pool User Name** and **Application Pool Password**.
  * _Optional_ : Select a **Logging Level**.
  * _Optional_ : Select **CORS Enabled** and enter **CORS Origins**.  
See the **Cross Origin Resource Sharing** in the NetWorks Administrator Guide topic for more information.
  * Set the **TNS_ADMIN** value to path of the folder containing **tnsnames.ora** file to allow the service locate Oracle instances.
  * **Root folder of the physical package storage**  
Set to a path of a disk folder which contains the packages published by this service instance.
  * **Root folder for open transactions**  
Set to a path of a disk folder which will contain the upload transaction in open state (non completed uploads).
  * **Root folder for committed transactions**  
Set to a path of a disk folder which will contain the upload transaction in committed state (completed uploads).
  * _Optional_. **Claim to be used as user's role**  
Name of claim in OpenID Connect JWT token which is used to determine the roles of the user in the Direct role assignment mode. See [Authorization in Data Transfer Service](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Data-Transfer-Service/Authorization.html) for details.
  * _Optional_. **Concurrent Licenses Used**  
Set this value to a number greater than zero when using the Per-Request licensing mode. The number entered here specifies the number of licenses checked out by this service instance and also the maximum number of concurrently served requests.

## Related topics[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Administration-Console/Services-Deployment/Data-Transfer-Service.html#related-topics)

  * [Upload](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Data-Transfer-Service/Upload.html)

# Dynamic WMS Service
When deploying Dynamic WMS Service instance, set these parameters:
  * **Definition**  
Select **Dynamic WMS Service**.
  * **InstanceName** uniquely identifies the deployed service instance. This value is used as the application name in the IIS. The following fields populate when you enter an Instance Name:
    * Application Pool Name
    * Physical Path
    * Virtual Path
    * Default Database User Name
    * Default Database Password
  * _Optional_ **Instance Description** is optional user description of this instance.
  * **Application Pool Name** is the name of the IIS application pool. This value is typically derived from InstanceName.
  * Select the **Application Pool Identity** from the drop-down list. If **SpecificUser** is selected, enter your network credentials in **Application Pool User Name** and **Application Pool Password**.
  * _Optional_ : Select a **Logging Level**.
  * _Optional_ : Select **CORS Enabled** and enter **CORS Origins**. See the **Cross Origin Resource Sharing** in the NetWorks Administrator Guide topic for more information.
  * Set the **TNS_ADMIN** value to path of the folder containing **tnsnames.ora** file to allow the service locate Oracle instances.
  * **Path to root folder of DDC storage**  
Set to a path of a disk folder which contains storage of DDC files published as Dynamic WMS Sources. See [Storage](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Dynamic-WMS-Service/Storage.html) for more information.
  * **Number of minutes to keep DDC source in memory after last access**  
Set to a number of minutes which the DDC is kept in memory after last request. The DDC is unloaded from memory if there was no request to this Dynamic WMS source within the last configured number of minutes. Setting to a higher value improves performance, because DDC files are kept loaded in memory, but increases memory usage.
  * **Period (minutes) in which the expired sources are checked**  
Internal timeout for checking Dynamic WMS sources which are not in use.
  * _Optional_. **Concurrent licenses Used**  
Set this value to a number greater than zero when using the Per-Request licensing mode. The number entered here specifies the number of licenses checked out by this service instance and also the maximum number of concurrently served requests.

# Work Service
When deploying Work Service instance, set these parameters:
  * **Definition**  
Select **Work Service**.
  * **InstanceName** uniquely identifies the deployed service instance. This value is used as the application name in the IIS. The following fields populate when you enter an Instance Name:
    * Application Pool Name
    * Physical Path
    * Virtual Path
    * Default Database User Name
    * Default Database Password
  * _Optional_ **Instance Description** is optional user description of this instance.
  * **Application Pool Name** is not used.
  * Select the **Application Pool Identity** from the drop-down list. If **SpecificUser** is selected, enter your network credentials in **Application Pool User Name** and **Application Pool Password**.
  * _Optional_ : Select a **Logging Level**.
  * _Optional_ : Select **CORS Enabled** and enter **CORS Origins**.  
See the **Cross Origin Resource Sharing** in the NetWorks Administrator Guide topic for more information.
  * Set the **TNS_ADMIN** value to path of the folder containing **tnsnames.ora** file to allow the service locate Oracle instances.
  * **Path to storage folder for CAD conversion uploaded files**  
Set to a path of a disk folder which contains the uploaded vector files, ready for conversion to DDC. See also [Attach vector file configuration](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Administration-Console/Attach-vector-file-configuration.html).
  * **Path to storage folder for Dynamic WMS Service**  
Set to a path of a disk folder to which the converted DDC files are copied. See also [Attach vector file configuration](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Administration-Console/Attach-vector-file-configuration.html).
  * **Path to temporary folder for intermediate files**  
Path of a disk folder for temporary files.
  * **Path to storage folder for Export Data files**  
Set to a path of a disk folder which contains the uploaded JSON files, ready for Export Data to Excel. This is typically the same folder as **storage folder for CAD conversion uploaded files** , as both uses the same instance of **Data Transfer Service**.
  * _Optional_. **Number of parallel workers (Concurrent licenses used)**  
Set this value to a number greater than zero when using the **Per-Request licensing** mode. The number entered here specifies the number of licenses checked out by this service instance and also the maximum number of concurrently served requests.
  * **Endpoint URL**  
Specify URL address at which the REST API of this Work Service Instance is accessible. Use format `http://localhost:<tcp port>`. The `<tcp port>` value must be a number in the 1024-65535 range which is not in used by other services. The default is _9400_. When there are more Work Service instances deployed, each instance must use a different port number.

# WMTS Sites Designer
# GetCapabilities URL in Metadata
For WMTS site to work correctly in NetWorks, the `G3E_WMTSSITES.G3E_CAPABILITIES_URL` must be correctly set up to contain GetCapabilities request in either REST or KVP form. This can be achieved using `DesignerWMTS.StoreFullCapabilitiesUrl` parameter in UCConsole.exe.config :

```
<appSettings>
    ...
    <add key="DesignerWMTS.StoreFullCapabilitiesUrl" value="true" />
</appSettings>

```

With this setting set to true, when defining service URL: ![image.png](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/.attachments/image-10a783d7-b58e-459c-b816-0a47b1b764ed.png) GetCapabilities query will be added to your WMTS URL: ![image.png](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/.attachments/image-aac00ab1-7e78-4ee2-bbf5-975d305565b5.png)
This can be reverted to previous behavior by setting the value to false or by omitting the setting from configuration file.

#### CIM-Export

##### Installation

# Installing CIM data model
CIM data model is not by-default installed together with NetWorks. To install the CIM data model, follow these instructions:
  1. Run NetWorks Upgrade Wizard This step will remove previous CIM data model (if existed).
  2. Using Oracle SQL*Plus, run script `PLSQL\CIM\Install.sql` and pass a single parameter - path to folder, where logs should be stored.

**Example**

```
cd "C:\Program Files (x86)\NetWorks\PLSQL\CIM\"
sqlplus user/password@alias @Install.sql C:\temp\logs\

```

# Migrating from previous CIM data model versions
CIM Export metadata and data model in NetWorks 02.00.1903 to 02.00.2112 (GPC versions) is not fully compatible with CIM Export in NetWorks 11.01.2201 (ISC) and newer versions. ESC NetWorks versions are not affected, as they removed the support for the original mode in version 02.00.2001.
To upgrade the existing CIM Export metadata, it is necessary to perform manual steps.
## Before upgrade[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/CIM-Export/Installation/Migrating-from-previous-CIM-data-model-versions.html#before-upgrade)
Export or preserve by other means (e.g. Microsoft Excel) all data from tables:
  * G3E_OMSEXPORTLIST
  * GAONET_CIMCLASS
  * GAONET_CIMFEATURE
  * GAONET_CIMFEATURATTR
  * GAONET_CIMMULTIPLIER
  * GAONET_CIMPROPERTY
  * GAONET_CIMSEQ
  * GAONET_CIMUNIT
  * GAONET_CIMVALUEGROUP
  * GAONET_CIMVALUEMAP
  * GAONET_CIMWATERMARKS

## During database upgrade[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/CIM-Export/Installation/Migrating-from-previous-CIM-data-model-versions.html#during-database-upgrade)
The Upgrade Wizard removes the original CIM Export data model, including the metadata configuration.
## After upgrade[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/CIM-Export/Installation/Migrating-from-previous-CIM-data-model-versions.html#after-upgrade)
### Install the CIM Export data model[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/CIM-Export/Installation/Migrating-from-previous-CIM-data-model-versions.html#install-the-cim-export-data-model)
Follow [Installing CIM data model](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/CIM-Export/Installation/Installing-CIM-data-model.html).
## Delete default metadata[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/CIM-Export/Installation/Migrating-from-previous-CIM-data-model-versions.html#delete-default-metadata)
Remove all rows from the CIM Export metadata tables using the following script:

```
DELETE FROM GAONET_CIMFEATUREATTR;
DELETE FROM GAONET_CIMFEATURE;
DELETE FROM GAONET_CIMWATERMARKS;
DELETE FROM GAONET_CIMVALUEMAP;
DELETE FROM GAONET_CIMVALUEGROUP;
DELETE FROM GAONET_CIMMULTIPLIER;
DELETE FROM GAONET_CIMSEQ;
DELETE FROM GAONET_CIMUNIT;
DELETE FROM GAONET_CIMPROPERTY;
DELETE FROM GAONET_CIMCLASS;
COMMIT;

```

### Import metadata[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/CIM-Export/Installation/Migrating-from-previous-CIM-data-model-versions.html#import-metadata)
Import the saved metadata back to GAONET_CIM* tables. Map columns by their names. Leave defaults for the columns which did not exist in the original model.
  * GAONET_CIMCLASS
  * GAONET_CIMFEATURE
  * GAONET_CIMFEATURATTR
  * GAONET_CIMMULTIPLIER
  * GAONET_CIMPROPERTY
  * GAONET_CIMSEQ
  * GAONET_CIMUNIT
  * GAONET_CIMVALUEGROUP
  * GAONET_CIMVALUEMAP
  * GAONET_CIMWATERMARKS

Configure [CIM Export parameters](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/CIM-Export/Reference/CIM-Export-parameters.html) using original settings from G3E_OMSEXPORTLIST.
### Add missing feature class metadata[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/CIM-Export/Installation/Migrating-from-previous-CIM-data-model-versions.html#add-missing-feature-class-metadata)
Update CIM class identifier in attribute mapping. Execute the following PL/SQL block:

```
UPDATE GAONET_CIMFEATUREATTR A
   SET A.GAO_CCNO = (SELECT GAO_CCNO FROM GAONET_CIMFEATURE WHERE GAO_CFNO = A.GAO_CFNO)
 WHERE A.GAO_CCNO IS NULL;
 
COMMIT;

```

### Update types in GAONET_CIMCLASS[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/CIM-Export/Installation/Migrating-from-previous-CIM-data-model-versions.html#update-types-in-gaonet_cimclass)
To maintain legacy processing, it is necessary to map the CIM class implementation types to a legacy dll. Execute the following statement in the database:

```
UPDATE GAONET_CIMCLASS 
   SET GAO_TYPE = REPLACE(GAO_TYPE,'GTechCIM:', 'GTechCIMLegacy:') 
 WHERE GAO_TYPE LIKE 'GTechCIM:%'
   AND (GAO_TYPE LIKE '%.ACLineSegment'
    OR  GAO_TYPE LIKE '%.Breaker'
    OR  GAO_TYPE LIKE '%.EnergyConsumer'
    OR  GAO_TYPE LIKE '%.Fuse'
    OR  GAO_TYPE LIKE '%.Recloser'
    OR  GAO_TYPE LIKE '%.Sectionalizer'
    OR  GAO_TYPE LIKE '%.ShuntCompensator'
    OR  GAO_TYPE LIKE '%.Switch');

COMMIT;

```

### Reset sequences[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/CIM-Export/Installation/Migrating-from-previous-CIM-data-model-versions.html#reset-sequences)
Execute the following PL/SQL block:

```
SET SERVEROUTPUT ON
DECLARE
  PROCEDURE RESET_SEQUENCE(PTABLE IN VARCHAR2, PKEY IN VARCHAR2)
  AS
    NMAXVAL NUMBER;
  BEGIN
    DBMS_OUTPUT.PUT_LINE(PTABLE);
    EXECUTE IMMEDIATE 'SELECT MAX(' || PKEY || ') FROM ' || PTABLE INTO NMAXVAL;
    IF (NMAXVAL IS NOT NULL) THEN  
      DBMS_OUTPUT.PUT_LINE('Resetting sequence to ' || TO_CHAR(NMAXVAL+1));
      EXECUTE IMMEDIATE 'ALTER SEQUENCE ' || PTABLE || '_SEQ RESTART START WITH ' || TO_CHAR(NMAXVAL+1);
    END IF;
  END;
BEGIN
  RESET_SEQUENCE('GAONET_CIMCLASS', 'GAO_CCNO');
  RESET_SEQUENCE('GAONET_CIMPROPERTY', 'GAO_CPNO');
  RESET_SEQUENCE('GAONET_CIMFEATURE', 'GAO_CFNO');
  RESET_SEQUENCE('GAONET_CIMFEATUREATTR', 'GAO_CFANO');
  RESET_SEQUENCE('GAONET_CIMVALUEGROUP', 'GAO_CVGNO');
  RESET_SEQUENCE('GAONET_CIMVALUEMAP', 'GAO_CVMNO');
END;
/

```

### Refresh metadata tables[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/CIM-Export/Installation/Migrating-from-previous-CIM-data-model-versions.html#refresh-metadata-tables)
Follow steps in [Metadata changes](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/CIM-Export/Reference/Metadata-changes.html).

# Uninstalling CIM data model
To uninstall the CIM data model, follow these instructions:
  1. Using Oracle SQL*Plus, run script `PLSQL\CIM\Uninstall.sql` and pass a single parameter - path to folder, where logs should be stored.

**Example**

```
cd "C:\Program Files (x86)\NetWorks\PLSQL\CIM\"
sqlplus user/password@alias @Uninstall.sql C:\temp\logs\

```

##### Mapping

# CIM Class implementation types
These .NET types can be specified in [GAONET_CIMCLASS.GAO_TYPE](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/CIM-Export/Reference/Metadata-tables/GAONET_CIMCLASS.html).
## GTechCIM:GTechnology.CommonInformationModel.Standard[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/CIM-Export/Mapping/CIM-Class-implementation-types.html#gtechcimgtechnologycommoninformationmodelstandard)
Implements generic metadata-driven export for any CIM class. The list of available properties for given CIM class is determined from [GAONET_CIMPROPERTY](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/CIM-Export/Reference/Metadata-tables/GAONET_CIMPROPERTY.html). Actual CIM class is determined at runtime from [GAONET_CIMFEATURE.GAO_CCNO](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/CIM-Export/Reference/Metadata-tables/GAONET_CIMFEATURE.html) or dynamically using the `sup:CIMClass` special property (see [Special CIM properties](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/CIM-Export/Mapping/Special-CIM-properties.html)).
The property mapping follows rules defined in [Object and property mapping](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/CIM-Export/Mapping/Property-mapping.html). Object identification follows [CIM Object Identification](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/CIM-Export/Mapping/CIM-Object-Identification.html).
## GTechCIM:GTechnology.CommonInformationModel.Singleton[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/CIM-Export/Mapping/CIM-Class-implementation-types.html#gtechcimgtechnologycommoninformationmodelsingleton)
Implements the same logic as `GTechCIM:GTechnology.CommonInformationModel.Standard`, but prevents from exporting the same CIM object ID multiple times within one export.
Typical uses are export of CIM objects not based on feature instances (like `cim:BaseVoltage`), which are usually based on actual attribute data. Only the first instance of the object with given ID is written to the CIM XML file, others are suppressed.
## GTechCIM:GTechnology.CommonInformationModel.{CIMClass}[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/CIM-Export/Mapping/CIM-Class-implementation-types.html#gtechcimgtechnologycommoninformationmodelcimclass)
The original CIM export model used strongly typed .NET implementation class for each CIM class. This model is now obsolete, but it still available for use.

# CIM Object Identification
## Object identification[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/CIM-Export/Mapping/CIM-Object-Identification.html#object-identification)
Each object requires a unique ID, based on a GUID. Most of these GUIDs must be constructed in such a way that we can extract values - primarily the G3E_FID - from them when the XML is consumed and the same GUID should be repeatedly constructed for the same object instance. This means that all GUIDs must be constructed from provided data, rather than use randomly generated GUIDs, in order to guarantee uniqueness and repeatability.
The GUID (`00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000`) can be split into the following named parts:  
| Data1  | Data2  | Data3  | Data4a  | Data4b  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| 00000000  | 0000  | 0000  | 0000-0000  | 00000000  |  
**Parts and their purposes**  
| Part  | Length  | Common purpose  | Default (dec)  | Default (hex)  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| Data1  | 32 bits - 8 hex digits  | No special usage  | -1  | ffffffff  |  
| Data2  | 16 bits - 4 hex digits  | Main differentiator for object type  | 1  | 1  |  
| Data3  | 16 bits - 4 hex digits  | Secondary differentiator  | 1  | 1  |  
| Data4a  | 32 bits - 8 hex digits  | Secondary object identification (in compound keys, e.g. sequence number of Terminal)  | -1  | ffffffff  |  
| Data4b  | 32 bits - 8 hex digits  | Primary object identification (e.g. G3E_FID, connectivity node id)  | -1  | ffffffff  |  
Data2 is used to distinguish the main classes of GUID that we need to generate. Some of these classes will have sub-classes that must be further identified - we use Data3 for that. Data2 and Data3 typically contain an enumeration value.
Data1, Data4a and Data4b contains either a -1 (0xFFFFFFFF) or a value obtained from a NUMBER(9, 0) database value, such as G3E_FID. Data4b is the primary identifier field; the others will be used when that is not sufficient to guarantee uniqueness.
Data4b contains the "primary" identifying value - either a FID, a node ID, or a generated value.  
Data4a and Data1 are used when we need to further qualify Data4b.
### Base Object[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/CIM-Export/Mapping/CIM-Object-Identification.html#base-object)
These are the "main" CIM objects generated from a feature instance.

```
Data1 = -1 (0xFFFFFFFF)         
Data2 = 1 (indicates FID-based)         
Data3 = 1 (indicates main object or no further sub-classing)            
Data4a = -1 (0xFFFFFFFF)            
Data4b = G3E_FID            

```
  
| G3E_FID  | rdf:ID  |  
| --- | --- |  
| 1030009  | _ffffffff-0001-0001-ffff-ffff**000fb779**  |  
**IMPORTANT**
The following information is included for reference and backward-compatibility only. Since the introduction of metadata-driven export, the construction of object IDs and object reference IDs is fully customizable via [GAONET_CIMFEATUREATTR](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/CIM-Export/Reference/Metadata-tables/GAONET_CIMFEATUREATTR.html).
### Terminal[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/CIM-Export/Mapping/CIM-Object-Identification.html#terminal)
These objects use their owner's FID, but need to be distinguished from that owner. We also need to distinguish between the two possible Terminal objects that can be owned by a ConductingEquipment instance.

```
Data1 = -1 (0xFFFFFFFF)         
Data2 = 1 (indicates FID-based)         
Data3 = 2 (indicates Terminal)         
Data4a = 1 or 2 (Terminal number)
Data4b = FID            

```
  
| G3E_FID  | Terminal  | rdf:ID  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| 1030009  | 1  | _ffffffff-0001-**0002** -0000-0001**000fb779**  |  
| 1030009  | 2  | _ffffffff-0001-**0002** -0000-0002**000fb779**  |  
### ConnectivityNode[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/CIM-Export/Mapping/CIM-Object-Identification.html#connectivitynode)
These use the node ID value as the primary identity.

```
Data1 = -1 (0xFFFFFFFF)         
Data2 = 2 (indicates node ID-based)         
Data3 = 1 (indicates main object or no further sub-classing)            
Data4a = -1 (0xFFFFFFFF)            
Data4b = node ID            

```
  
| Connectivity node ID  | rdf:ID  |  
| --- | --- |  
| 10636  | _ffffffff-**0002** -0001-ffff-ffff**0000298c**  |  
| 18409  | _ffffffff-**0002** -0001-ffff-ffff**000047e9**  |  
### BaseVoltage 1[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/CIM-Export/Mapping/CIM-Object-Identification.html#basevoltage-1)
BaseVoltage object created for each unique voltage level. The voltage value is mapped to numeric unique identifier(e.g. identifier 110000 for 110kV).

```
Data1 = -1 (0xFFFFFFFF)         
Data2 = 3 (indicates CIM data type object of BaseVoltage)           
Data3 = 1 (indicates main object or no further sub-classing)            
Data4a = -1 (0xFFFFFFFF)            
Data4b = Voltage value (in V) - e.g. 110000 => 0001adb0         

```

Voltage _ffffffff-**0003** -0001-ffff-ffff**0001adb0**
### CimDataType/Location[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/CIM-Export/Mapping/CIM-Object-Identification.html#cimdatatypelocation)
CimDataType objects are objects such as Location that are generated for each unique value of some attribute  
in the database.

```
Data1 = -1 (0xFFFFFFFF)         
Data2 = 4 (indicates CIM data type object of Location)          
Data3 = 1 (indicates main object or no further sub-classing)            
Data4a = -1 (0xFFFFFFFF)            
Data4b = generated unique ID (internal sequence)            

```

1 Unique ID (generated) _ffffffff-0004-0001-ffff-ffff00000001
### VoltageLevel[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/CIM-Export/Mapping/CIM-Object-Identification.html#voltagelevel)
VoltageLevel (EquipmentContainer) within a Substation. The ID contains G3E_FID of the owning Substation  
and the mapped ID of the BaseVoltage in Data4a.

```
Data1 = -1 (0xFFFFFFFF)         
Data2 = 5 (indicates CIM data type object of VoltageLevel)          
Data3 = 1 (indicates main object or no further sub-classing)            
Data4a = BaseVoltage ID (from internal sequence)            
Data4b = FID    

```

1 Substation G3E_FID + Voltage level _ffffffff-0005-0001-0000-0001000fb779
### PSRType[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/CIM-Export/Mapping/CIM-Object-Identification.html#psrtype)
PowerSystemResource.PSRType, created for each unique PSRType encountered during export.  
PSRType integer key should be mapped from source value to the 2^32-1 range (e.g. using value map)

```
Data1 = -1 (0xFFFFFFFF)         
Data2 = 6 (indicates CIM data type object of PSRType)           
Data3 = 1 (indicates main object or no further sub-classing)            
Data4a = -1 (0xFFFFFFFF)            
Data4b = PSRType integer key            

```

1 Mapped integer key _ffffffff-0006-0001-ffff-ffff00000001

These objects use their owner's FID, but need to be distinguished from that owner. We also need to distinguish between the two possible PowerTransformerEnd objects that can be owned by a PowerTransformer instance.

Data1 = -1 (0xFFFFFFFF)         
Data2 = 1 (indicates FID-based)         
Data3 = 6 (indicates PowerTransformerEnd)         
Data4a = 1 or 2 (sequence number of the transformer end)
Data4b = FID
