### Custom Classes[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/CIM-Export/Mapping/CIM-Object-Identification.html#custom-classes)
Custom classes are used in three instances:
  1. A custom class must be defined for each instance of a repeating component  
configured for export.
  2. Non-CIM attributes defined for a class are placed in a custom class.  
(But, the software will generate non-CIM attributes that act as if they are CIM attributes.  
Those are for internal purposes and are not mapped in metadata.)
  3. Stand-alone non-CIM objects.
Data1 = Value of GDR_CIM_REF_PROPERTY.GDR_CIM_PROP_CLNO  
Data2 = 1 (indicates FID-based)  
Data3 = 5 (indicates custom class)  
Data4a = generated unique ID (internal sequence)  
Data4b = FID of owner

1029639 G3E_FID _00000001-0001-0005-0000-0004000fb607

# Feature to CIM class mapping
NetWorks features can be mapped to CIM class instances in two ways in [GAONET_CIMFEATURE](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/CIM-Export/Reference/Metadata-tables/GAONET_CIMFEATURE.html).
  * To primary component of the feature class.
  * To any component of a feature class.

## Feature class to CIM class[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/CIM-Export/Mapping/Feature-to-CIM-class-mapping.html#feature-class-to-cim-class)
Specify **G3E_FNO** which is mapped to a CIM class (via **GAO_CCNO** , reference to [**GAONET_CIMCLASS.GAO_CCNO**](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/CIM-Export/Reference/Metadata-tables/GAONET_CIMCLASS.html). This maps instances of the primary attribute component of the feature to the CIM class instances.
This is the primary mapping record for a feature. It is used to populate the staging table and to track feature changes for incremental exports.
**Conditions**
  * Fields **GAO_CNO** and **GAO_FMNR** must remain NULL.
  * Field **GAO_FILTER** is not applied.

Set **GAO_ORDINAL** to value lower than `0` to prevent the feature mapping from being written to the CIM export XML file. The staging table is populated for this **G3E_FNO** , which is necessary when there are other rows for given G3E_FNO, with **GAO_CNO** and **GAO_FMNR** filled in.
### Example[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/CIM-Export/Mapping/Feature-to-CIM-class-mapping.html#example)  
| GAO_CFNO  | GAO_OMSELNO  | GAO_FNO  | GAO_CCNO  | GAO_ORDINAL  | GAO_CNO  | GAO_FMNR  | GAO_FILTER  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| 1  | 1  | 306  | 1  | 1  |   |   |   |  
### Attribute mapping[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/CIM-Export/Mapping/Feature-to-CIM-class-mapping.html#attribute-mapping)
You may use any attribute from the primary attribute component or other non-repeating components of the feature in attribute mapping.
## Feature component[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/CIM-Export/Mapping/Feature-to-CIM-class-mapping.html#feature-component)
Map any feature component (non-repeating or repeating) to a CIM class. Each instance of the component is mapped to a CIM class instance (after applying **GAO_FILTER** and other primary filtering conditions).
  * Fields **GAO_CNO** and **GAO_FMNR** must be filled in.
  * **GAO_FMNR**
  * Condition specified in **GAO_FILTER** is applied to the component specified in **GAO_CNO** when reading data from the component. You may used only field names used in the component or a SQL subquery.
  * Another record for given **GAO_FNO** must exists in **GAONET_CIMFEATURE** with **GAO_CNO** and **GAO_FMNR** set to `NULL`. This is important for population of the staging table for given **G3E_FNO**.

### Example[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/CIM-Export/Mapping/Feature-to-CIM-class-mapping.html#example-1)  
| GAO_CFNO  | GAO_OMSELNO  | GAO_FNO  | GAO_CCNO  | GAO_ORDINAL  | GAO_CNO  | GAO_FMNR  | GAO_FILTER  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| 2  | 1  | 306  | 20  | 2  | 306  | CONSEG_LV_TERMINAL  | NODE1 IS NOT NULL AND NODE1 <> 0  |  
### Attribute mapping[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/CIM-Export/Mapping/Feature-to-CIM-class-mapping.html#attribute-mapping-1)
You may use any attribute from the component specified in **GAONET_CIMFEATURE.GAO_CNO** or any other components. CIM Export creates a SELECT statement with a **LEFT JOIN** from the main component (**GAONET_CIMFEATURE.GAO_CNO**) to other components, joined by **G3E_FID** on both sides.

```
SELECT {attributes}
  FROM (SELECT * 
         FROM {MAIN_COMPONENT}  
        WHERE G3E_FNO = {GAONET_CIMFEATURE.GAO_FNO} 
          AND G3E_CNO = {GAONET_CIMFEATURE.GAO_CNO} 
       /* AND {GAONET_FEATURE.GAO_FILTER} */) a

  LEFT JOIN {COMPONENT1} c1
         ON c1.G3E_FID = a.G3E_FID
        AND c1.G3E_CNO = {G3E_CNO of joined component}
  ...
WHERE a.G3E_FID IN (SELECT G3E_FID 
                      FROM {Staging Table for G3E_FNO}) 

```

# Property mapping
## Value[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/CIM-Export/Mapping/Property-mapping.html#value)
Simple value property.

```
<cim:Conductor.length>296.477</cim:Conductor.length>

```

**Mapping**
Map source value to property with GAO_PROPERTYTYPE = `Value`, e.g. `cim:Conductor.length`.
## Value reference[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/CIM-Export/Mapping/Property-mapping.html#value-reference)
Value reference property. Typically used for referencing enum and code list values.

```
<cim:SynchronousMachine.operatingMode rdf:resource="http://iec.ch/TC57/2016/CIMschema-cim17#SynchronousMachineOperatingMode.generator" />

```

**Mapping**
Map source value to property with GAO_PROPERTYTYPE = `ValueReference`, e.g. `cim:SynchronousMachine.operatingMode`.
## Object reference[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/CIM-Export/Mapping/Property-mapping.html#object-reference)
Property with reference to another CIM object instance. Construct the object ID by mapping the individual ID parts using the special `{ObjectReferenceProperty}::ID.DataX` properties (see [Special CIM properties](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/CIM-Export/Mapping/Special-CIM-properties.html)). Each of the ID parts expects an Integer (32-bit or 16-bit) value.

```
<cim:Terminal.ConductingEquipment rdf:resource="#_ffffffff-0001-0001-ffff-ffff000fc0df"/>

```

**Mapping**
Map one or more properties with GAO_PROPERTYTYPE = `IDPart` related to the CIM object property to an attribute which produces an integer value, used to construct the ID of the referenced object. The prefix of the CIM property is the name of the object reference property (e.g. `cim:Terminal.ConductingEquipment::ID.Data4b`).
**Example**
`cim:Terminal.ConductingEquipment::ID.Data4b` is mapped to attribute which produces integer value `1032415` (e.g. G3E_FID).
CIM Export produces GUID with the following structure (default values for Data1-Data4a are applied):
(-1, 1, 1, -1, **1032415**) = `ffffffff-0001-0001-ffff-ffff000fc0df`
## Repeating object reference[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/CIM-Export/Mapping/Property-mapping.html#repeating-object-reference)
The same logic as for Object reference. Repeating instances of the object reference property can be achieved by mapping the ID parts properties (one or more) to a comma separated list of integer values. The number of comma separated values in each property must be either:
  * 1 - This value is used in all repeated instances.
  * N - N instances of the object property are produced.

```
<cim:Terminal.ConductingEquipment rdf:resource="#_ffffffff-0001-0002-ffff-ffff00000001"/>
<cim:Terminal.ConductingEquipment rdf:resource="#_ffffffff-0001-0002-ffff-ffff00000002"/>
<cim:Terminal.ConductingEquipment rdf:resource="#_ffffffff-0001-0002-ffff-ffff00000004"/>

```

**Example**
`cim:Terminal.ConductingEquipment::ID.Data3` is mapped to constant value `2`. `cim:Terminal.ConductingEquipment::ID.Data4b` is mapped to attribute which produces string value `1,2,4`.
CIM Export produces IDs with the following structure:
(-1, 1, **2** , -1, **1**) = `ffffffff-0001-0002-ffff-ffff00000001`
(-1, 1, **2** , -1, **2**) = `ffffffff-0001-0002-ffff-ffff00000002`
(-1, 1, **2** , -1, **4**) = `ffffffff-0001-0002-ffff-ffff00000004`
Default values for Data1, Data2 and Data4b are applied.
## Compound value[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/CIM-Export/Mapping/Property-mapping.html#compound-value)
Compound values are structured CIM properties. The name of the CIM property contains at least one forward slash `/`, which divides the hierarchy structure.
**Note**
Repeating compound attributes or compounds types with repeating parts are not supported.

```
<cim:Location rdf:about="#_ffffffff-0004-0143-ffff-ffff000fac41">
  <cim:Location.type>Pole</cim:Location.type>
  <cim:Location.mainAddress>
    <cim:streetDetail>
      <cim:number>12</cim:number>
      <cim:name>Main street</cim:name>
    </cim:streetDetail>
    <cim:status>
      <cim:value>Valid</cim:value>
    </cim:status>
  </cim:Location.mainAddress>
</cim:Location>

```

**Mapping**
Map attribute values to compound value properties, e.g. `cim:Location.mainAddress/cim:streetDetail/cim:name`. CIM Export creates the output compound structure from all non-NULL properties.
The structure above can be created by the following mapping:
`cim:Location.mainAddress/cim:streetDetail/cim:number` is mapped to attribute producing value `12`. `cim:Location.mainAddress/cim:streetDetail/cim:name` is mapped to attribute producing value `Main street`. `cim:Location.mainAddress/cim:status/cim:value` is mapped to attribute producing value `Valid`.
## Data type value (mapped to XML attribute)[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/CIM-Export/Mapping/Property-mapping.html#data-type-value-mapped-to-xml-attribute)
CIM properties mapped to XML attributes are similar to Compound values. The property name ends with `/@{property-name}`, e.g. `cim:BaseVoltage.nominalVoltage/@unit`.
Typical usage is for Data types (e.g. _Voltage_ or _ActivePower_), which may have alternative `unit` or `multiplier` attribute values.

```
<cim:BaseVoltage.nominalVoltage unit="V" multiplier="k">1</cim:BaseVoltage.nominalVoltage>

```

**Mapping**
Map values like for Value properties.
The structure above can be exported by the following mapping:
`cim:BaseVoltage.nominalVoltage/@unit` is mapped to value `V`. `cim:BaseVoltage.nominalVoltage/@multiplier` is mapped to value `k`.
## Constant value[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/CIM-Export/Mapping/Property-mapping.html#constant-value)
If you want to map a constant value to a CIM attribute, use the following method:
  * Define a mapping in **GAONET_CIMVALUEGROUP** with **GAO_MISSINGOPERATION** set to `Constant`.
  * Define a single row for this value group in **GAONET_CIMVALUEMAP** , with **GAO_TOVALUE** set to the desired constant.
  * Use this value group in **GAONET_CIMFEATUREATTR.GAO_CVGNO** , with arbitrary attribute from the source component as the source.

**Example metadata**
Mapping for constant value `1`.
GAONET_CIMVALUEGROUP  
| GAO_CVGNO  | GAO_USERNAME  | GAO_TABLE  | GAO_MISSINGOPERATION  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| 101  | Constant-1  |   | Constant  |  
GAONET_CIMVALUEMAP  
| GAO_CVMNO  | GAO_CVGNO  | GAO_FROMVALUE  | GAO_TOVALUE  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| 10101  | 101  |   | 1  |

# Special CIM properties
The CIM properties described below have special purpose.
## sup:ID.DataX[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/CIM-Export/Mapping/Special-CIM-properties.html#supiddatax)
The properties in this group can be used to construct customized [object ID](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/CIM-Export/Mapping/CIM-Object-Identification.html).  
| Name  | Type  | Description  | Default value  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| sup:ID.Data1  | Integer (32-bit)  | Data1 part of object ID  | -1  |  
| sup:ID.Data2  | Integer (16-bit)  | Data2 part of object ID  | 1  |  
| sup:ID.Data3  | Integer (16-bit)  | Data3 part of object ID  | 1  |  
| sup:ID.Data4a  | Integer (32-bit)  | Data4a part of object ID  | -1  |  
| sup:ID.Data4b  | Integer (32-bit)  | Data4b part of object ID  | -1  |  
## {ObjectReferenceProperty}::ID.DataX[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/CIM-Export/Mapping/Special-CIM-properties.html#objectreferencepropertyiddatax)
The properties in this group can be used to construct customized [ID of an referenced object](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/CIM-Export/Mapping/CIM-Object-Identification.html) in a CIM property. The properties are defined as complementary to properties of with GAO_PROPERTYTYPE = `'ObjectReference'` (see [GAONET_CIMPROPERTY.GAO_PROPERTYTYPE](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/CIM-Export/Reference/Metadata-tables/GAONET_CIMFEATUREATTR.html)). Placeholder `{ObjectReferenceProperty}` references the CIM object property name, e.g. `cim:ConductingEquipment.BaseVoltage`.  
| Name  | Type  | Description  | Default value  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| {ObjectReferenceProperty}::ID.Data1  | Integer (32-bit)  | Data1 part of referenced object ID  | -1  |  
| {ObjectReferenceProperty}::ID.Data2  | Integer (16-bit)  | Data2 part of referenced object ID  | 1  |  
| {ObjectReferenceProperty}::ID.Data3  | Integer (16-bit)  | Data3 part of referenced object ID  | 1  |  
| {ObjectReferenceProperty}::ID.Data4a  | Integer (32-bit)  | Data4a part of referenced object ID  | -1  |  
| {ObjectReferenceProperty}::ID.Data4b  | Integer (32-bit)  | Data4b part of referenced object ID  | -1  |  
## sup:CIMClass[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/CIM-Export/Mapping/Special-CIM-properties.html#supcimclass)
The `sup:CIMClass` property can be mapped to an attribute which contains a dynamic name of the CIM class to be mapped to this feature instance.
Since the introduction of the GAO_CNO/GAO_FMNR mechanism to [GAONET_CIMFEATURE](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/CIM-Export/Reference/Metadata-tables/GAONET_CIMFEATURE.html), there are now more options how to perform subclassing when generating CIM features, which are superior to using `sup:CIMClass`.

# Mapping
When mapping NetWorks feature data to CIM classes and properties, consider the following:
**1. How CIM object IDs are constructed**
See [CIM Object Identification](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/CIM-Export/Mapping/CIM-Object-Identification.html).
This is important especially for "virtual" objects which are not typically based on feature instances (e.g. BaseVoltage, VoltageLevel, ConnectivityNode).
**2. What is the source of data for mapping**
You can map from feature primary and non-repeating components or map any component. For component based mappings, subclassing is possible by further data filtering via [**GAONET_CIMFEATURE.GAO_FILTER**](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/CIM-Export/Reference/Metadata-tables/GAONET_CIMFEATURE.html).
See [Feature to CIM class mapping](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/CIM-Export/Mapping/Feature-to-CIM-class-mapping.html).
**3. What attributes are mapped**
There are multiple types of attributes in CIM, which need to be mapped:
  * Value (simple) attributes
  * Value reference - e.g. enum values
  * Object reference - referenced object IDs must be constructed from available data
  * Repeating object reference
  * Compound values

See [Property mapping](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/CIM-Export/Mapping/Property-mapping.html) and [Special CIM properties](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/CIM-Export/Mapping/Special-CIM-properties.html).

##### Reference

# CIM Export parameters
Table **[GAONET_CIMPARAMETER](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/CIM-Export/Reference/Metadata-tables/GAONET_CIMPARAMETER.html)** can be used to configure export-wide parameters.
### Well known parameters[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/CIM-Export/Reference/CIM-Export-parameters.html#well-known-parameters)  
| Name  | Description  | Mand.  | Default value  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| ExportName  | Name of the export.   
This value is used by the export runtime to identify the export and determine GAO_OMSELNO.  | Y  |   |  
| OutputLocation  | Output location for the export. Allowed formats: directory=, registry=. For Registry, the path is determined as String value **OMSExportPath** under Registry path `<key>`.  | Y  |   |  
| xmlns:cim  | CIM XML namespace (content of xmlns:cim)  |   | http://iec.ch/TC57/2016/CIM-schema-cim17#  |  
| xml:base  | Content of xml:base  |   | urn:uuid:  |  
| RecordsPerFile  | Number of records (objects) exported per single file  |   | 300000  |  
| FileSplitMode  | File splitting mode. Allowed values: **G3E_FNO** - Each G3E_FNO is exported into separate file(s), **None** - export all features into one file or files  |   | G3E_FNO  |  
| RdfIdentifierMode  | XML attribute used for RDF ID. Allowed values: **rdf:about** , **rdf:ID**  |   | rdf:about  |  
| ExportIDAsmRID  | Export rdf:ID as cim:IdentifierObject.mRID. Allowed values: **true** or **1** - Export, **false** or other value - don't export rdf:ID automatically  |   | false  |  
| xmlns:hex  | If defined and the value is non-empty, **xmlns:hex** is added to CIM documents and **hex:** properties are exported. To suppress export of hex: properties, set value to NULL.  |   | hex  |  
| xmlns:custom  | If defined and the value is non-empty, **xmlns:custom** is added to CIM documents. To suppress adding xmlns:custom to CIM document, set value to NULL.  |   | custom  |  
| xmlns:debug  | If defined and the value is non-empty, **xmlns:debug** is added to CIM documents. To suppress adding xmlns:debug to CIM document, set value to NULL.  |   |   |  
| PreProcess  | PL/SQL block to execute before the export in the same Oracle session. If the string contains `:fidquery`, the command line FIDQuery parameter is passed in. Example: `BEGIN PACKAGE1.PREPROCESS(:fidquery); END;`.  |   |   |  
| PostProcess  | PL/SQL block to execute after the export in the same Oracle session. If the string contains `:fidquery`, the command line FIDQuery parameter is passed in. Example: `BEGIN PACKAGE1.POSTPROCESS(:fidquery); END;`.  |   |   |

# CIMExport.exe
**CIMExport.exe** is the main executable used to export data from NetWorks database to CIM XML format.
## Command line parameters[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/CIM-Export/Reference/CIMExport.exe.html#command-line-parameters)
**CIMExport.exe** Login=`<user/password@alias>`; Configuration=`<configuration name>`; ErrorLogFile=`<errors logfile>`; [Full=`Y|N`;] [DiagLogFile=`<diagnostics logfile>`;] [ProgressLogFile=`<progress logfile>`;] [LCID=`<LCID>`;] [ExportName=`<ExportName>`;] [RefreshStaging=`Y|N`;] [DeleteStaging=`Y|N`;] [FIDQuery=`<query>`;] [DeletedQuery=`<query>`]
**IMPORTANT** The order of parameters Login, Configuration, `ErrorLogFile` is important!  
| Option  | Required  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| Login  | Y  | Connection string in format user/password@alias, where alias is the TNS name or EZCONNECT string.  
Accepts also connection string encrypted using _GTEncTool.exe_.  |  
| Configuration  | Y  | NetWorks configuration  |  
| ErrorLogFile  | Y  | Path to log file for reporting errors  |  
| Full  |   |  `Y` = Full export or partial export (when FIDQuery is specified),   
`N` = Incremental export.  
Default is `N`.  |  
| DiagLogFile  |   | Path to diagnostics log file  |  
| ProgressLogFile  |   | Path to progress log file  |  
| LCID  |   | Locale identifier (e.g. `0009`)  |  
| ExportName  |   | Name of the export definition, as defined in GAONET_CIMPROPERTY, GAO_NAME=ExportName. When not specified, 'Default' is assumed  |  
| RefreshStaging  |   | Y = Refresh data in staging tables (normal processing).   
N = Don't refresh data in staging tables (used for debug). Default is `Y`.  |  
| DeleteStaging  |   | Y = Delete data from staging tables after export.   
N = Don't delete data from staging tables (used for debug). Default is `Y`.  |  
| FIDQuery  |   | SELECT statement used to retrieve list of G3E_FNO, G3E_FID pairs to be exported.   
Used for partial export of data. Applicable only when _Full_ is set to `Y`.  |  
| DeletedQuery  |   | SELECT statement used to retrieve list of deleted features.   
Used for [Partial incremental export of data](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/CIM-Export/Reference/Partial-incremental-export-of-data.html). Applicable only when _Full_ is set to `Y`.  |  
_Modes of operation_  
| Full  | FIDQuery  | DeletedQuery  | Result  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| Y  | present  |   | Partial export of data based on FIDQuery.  |  
| Y  | present  | present  | Partial incremental export of selected data based on FIDQuery and DeletedQuery)  |  
| Y  |   |   | Full export of data  |  
| N  |   |   | Incremental export of data based on differences between previous full export and changes in GDT_TABLEMODLOG.  |

# Metadata changes
After changes in CIM export metadata, it is necessary to update GAONET_CIM*OPTABLEs, using one of the following methods:
  * Publish NetWorks metadata
  * Execute the following command in database:

```
EXEC GAONET_CIMFEATURE_PKG.CreateOptimizedTable;
EXEC GAONET_CIMFEATUREATTR_PKG.CreateOptimizedTable;
COMMIT;

```

**Note**
CIMExport.exe reads metadata tables directly from database, not from published metadata files.
**Important**
If you changed the GAONET_CIMFEATURE.GAO_CFNO values (new rows, deleted rows), it is necessary to delete rows from the GAONET_CIMWATERMARKS table, otherwise the export might crash.

# Metadata support objects
The metadata support objects allow easier population of CIM metadata tables using object names instead of numbers (primary keys).
  * [GAONET_CIMFEATURE_INS](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/CIM-Export/Reference/Metadata-support-objects/GAONET_CIMFEATURE_INS.html)
  * [GAONET_CIMFEATUREATTR_INS](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/CIM-Export/Reference/Metadata-support-objects/GAONET_CIMFEATUREATTR_INS.html)

Support views for retrieval of metadata information
  * [GAONET_CIMCLASS_INFO](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/CIM-Export/Reference/Metadata-support-objects/GAONET_CIMCLASS_INFO.html) - List of CIM classes with inheritance hierarchy
  * [GAONET_CIMPROPERTY_INFO](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/CIM-Export/Reference/Metadata-support-objects/GAONET_CIMPROPERTY_INFO.html) - List of CIM class attributes (own and inherited)

# Partial incremental export of data
To run CIMExport.exe in partial incremental export mode, specify command line parameter `Full=Y` and both **FIDQuery** and **DeletedQuery**.
The objects provided in DeletedQuery will be exported under (example):

```
<dm:DifferenceModel>
    <dm:reverseDifferences>

        <!-- deleted objects - example -->

        <cim:Substation rdf:about="#_00000001-0002-0003-0001-000400000457">
        </cim:Substation>

    </dm:reverseDifferences>
</dm:DifferenceModel>

```

## DeletedQuery[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/CIM-Export/Reference/Partial-incremental-export-of-data.html#deletedquery)
The DeletedQuery parameter expects a SELECT statement which delivers list of delected CIM objects. The statement expects these column names:  
| Name  | Data type  | Required  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| CIM_CLASS  | VARCHAR2  | Yes, if G3E_FNO is not present in the query.  | Name of the CIM class to export for this row (e.g. `cim:Substation`).  |  
| G3E_FNO  | NUMBER(5)  | Yes, if CIM_CLASS not present in the query.  | G3E_FNO of the feature. Used to determine the CIM class name from GAONET_CIMFEATURE_OPTABLE where GAO_FMNR and GAO_CNO are null.  |  
| G3E_FID  | NUMBER(9)  |   | G3E_FID of the feature. If present and DATA1-DATA4B are empty, used to construct the rdf:ID or rdf:about of the CIM object instance.  |  
| DATA1  | NUMBER(9)  |   | Data1 part of the rdf:ID. When missing or NULL, default is `-1`.  |  
| DATA2  | NUMBER(9)  |   | Data2 part of the rdf:ID. When missing or NULL, default is `1`.  |  
| DATA3  | NUMBER(9)  |   | Data3 part of the rdf:ID. When missing or NULL, default is `1`.  |  
| DATA4A  | NUMBER(9)  |   | Data4a part of the rdf:ID. When missing or NULL, default is `-1`.  |  
| DATA4B  | NUMBER(9)  |   | Data4b part of the rdf:ID. When missing or NULL, default is `-1`.  |  
For meaning of DATA1-DATA4B, see [CIM Object Identification](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/CIM-Export/Mapping/CIM-Object-Identification.html).
**Note** It is the duty of the designer of the system (not CIM Export) to collect all necessary data required for the DeletedQuery, e.g. using triggers on tables. The stored data must preserve all information used to determine the CIM class from feature data.
## Modes of operation[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/CIM-Export/Reference/Partial-incremental-export-of-data.html#modes-of-operation)
### CIM class determined by G3E_FNO[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/CIM-Export/Reference/Partial-incremental-export-of-data.html#cim-class-determined-by-g3e_fno)
For simple mappings, where each G3E_CNO is mapped to exactly one CIM class, the DeletedQuery may look like:

```
SELECT G3E_FNO, G3E_FID 
  FROM <table or view with deleted objects> 
 WHERE <optional condition>

```

CIM Export will determine the CIM class from the G3E_FNO by looking into GAONET_FEATURE_OPTABLE. It looks for a row with given G3E_FNO, where GAO_FMNR and GAO_CNO are null (i.e. no subclassing based on data filter or CIM instances created from non-primary attribute components).
### Explicit CIM class and identifier parts[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/CIM-Export/Reference/Partial-incremental-export-of-data.html#explicit-cim-class-and-identifier-parts)
For complex cases where one NetWorks feature maps to multiple CIM object instances, the DeletedQuery should deliver all information necessary for export: CIM class name and parts of the rdf:ID (or rdf:about), see [CIM Object Identification](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/CIM-Export/Mapping/CIM-Object-Identification.html).

```
  SELECT CIM_CLASS, G3E_FID, DATA1, DATA2, DATA3, DATA4A, DATA4B 
    FROM <table or view with deleted objects> 
   WHERE <optional condition>
ORDER BY <ordering>

```

**Example data**  
| CIM_CLASS  | G3E_FID  | DATA1  | DATA2  | DATA3  | DATA4A  | DATA4B  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| cim:Substation  | 1027199  | NULL  | NULL  | NULL  | NULL  | NULL  |  
| cim:ACLineSegment  | 1568126  | NULL  | NULL  | NULL  | NULL  | 1568126  |  
| cim:Terminal  | 1568126  | NULL  | 1  | 2  | NULL  | 1568126  |  
| cim:Terminal  | 1568126  | NULL  | 2  | 2  | NULL  | 1568126  |  
Output

```
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<?iec61970-552 version="2.0"?>
<rdf:RDF xmlns:rdf="http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#"
  xmlns:cim="http://iec.ch/TC57/2016/CIMschema-cim17#"
  xmlns:md="http://iec.ch/TC57/61970-552/ModelDefinition/1#"
  xmlns:dm="http://iec.ch/TC57/61970-552/DifferenceModel/1#"
  xml:base="urn:uuid:">
  <dm:DifferenceModel>
    <dm:forwardDifferences>
      <!-- Inserts and Updates based on FIDQuery -->
    </dm:forwardDifferences>

    <dm:reverseDifferences>
      <cim:Substation rdf:about="#_ffffffff-0001-0001-ffff-ffff000fac7f">
      </cim:Substation>
      <cim:ACLineSegment rdf:about="#_ffffffff-0001-0001-ffff-ffff0017ed7e">
      </cim:ACLineSegment>
      <cim:Terminal rdf:about="#_ffffffff-0001-0002-ffff-ffff0017ed7e">
      </cim:Terminal>
      <cim:Terminal rdf:about="#_ffffffff-0002-0002-ffff-ffff0017ed7e">
      </cim:Terminal>
    </dm:reverseDifferences>
  </dm:DifferenceModel>
</rdf:RDF>

```

### Force export of data in incremental mode[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/CIM-Export/Reference/Partial-incremental-export-of-data.html#force-export-of-data-in-incremental-mode)
By specifying the DeletedQuery on the command line, it is possible to force CIMExport to export data in incremental mode (`<dm:DifferenceModel>`), even if no deleted data will be exported. The DeletedQuery can contain a statement which delivers at least G3E_FNO and G3E_FID columns, but returns 0 rows.
Example

```
SELECT 0 AS G3E_FNO, 0 AS G3E_FID FROM DUAL WHERE 0 = 1

```

##### Troubleshooting

# Specified cast is not valid
## Symptoms[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/CIM-Export/Troubleshooting/Specified-cast-is-not-valid.html#symptoms)
CIM Export reports error _Specified cast is not valid_ when exporting data.
## Possible cause[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/CIM-Export/Troubleshooting/Specified-cast-is-not-valid.html#possible-cause)
CIM Export uses Oracle data access components, which work with less precision of numeric data types than ORACLE allows.
**Example**
Oracle table or view contains NUMBER value: `0.00545664563426562546264343656456004584`. This exceeds the precision limits of numeric processing of CIM Export.
## Workaround[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/CIM-Export/Troubleshooting/Specified-cast-is-not-valid.html#workaround)
Make sure the NUMBER values which are exported do not exceed 28 significant decimal digits. Use views with `ROUND(value, N)` to format the numeric values.

# CIM Export
## Overview[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/CIM-Export.html#overview)
Export of NetWorks model for electrical networks to CIM XML representation.
Related standards:
  * IEC 61970-301: Common information model (CIM) base
  * IEC 61970-452: CIM static transmission network model profiles 
    * Core Equipment Profile
  * IEC 61970-552: CIMXML Model exchange format
  * IEC 61968-11: Common information model (CIM) extensions for distribution
  * IEC 61968-13: CIM RDF Model exchange format for distribution
  * IEC 62361-100: CIM profiles to XML schema mapping

#### Configuration

# Common Service Configuration Parameters
## Data Access[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Configuration/Common-Service-Configuration-Parameters.html#data-access)
NetWorks Core configuration and database.
###  `ConnectionInfo`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Configuration/Common-Service-Configuration-Parameters.html#connectioninfo)
NetWorks connection string in `user/password@CONFIGURATION` format.  
Accepts values encrypted using `GTEncTool.exe`.
###  `FileUNCPath`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Configuration/Common-Service-Configuration-Parameters.html#fileuncpath)
Explicitly configured FileUNCPath. When present, FileUNCPath is located using this value and the configuration in Registry is ignored.
###  `LCID`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Configuration/Common-Service-Configuration-Parameters.html#lcid)
LCID to use when reading metadata. If not specified, it is determined from current session (locale of the user under which the IIS app. pool or service is running).  
Example: `0009`
## Oracle[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Configuration/Common-Service-Configuration-Parameters.html#oracle)
###  `TNS_ADMIN`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Configuration/Common-Service-Configuration-Parameters.html#tns_admin)
Oracle TNS_ADMIN parameter, path to folder with `tnsnames.ora`. Mandatory on systems where TNS_ADMIN is not available as environment variable.
###  `ConnectionStrings:default`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Configuration/Common-Service-Configuration-Parameters.html#connectionstringsdefault)
Oracle Connection String template. The parameter can be used to specify special connection properties. See [Oracle documentation](https://docs.oracle.com/en/database/oracle/oracle-database/21/odpnt/featConnecting.html#GUID-0CFEB161-68EF-4BC2-8943-3BDFFB878602).  
Example: `Self Tuning=False;Incr Pool Size=1;`
## Coordinate System[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Configuration/Common-Service-Configuration-Parameters.html#coordinate-system)
###  `CoordinateSystem:Code`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Configuration/Common-Service-Configuration-Parameters.html#coordinatesystemcode)
EPSG code of the coordinate system.  
Example: `EPSG:3857`
###  `CoordinateSystem:Proj4String`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Configuration/Common-Service-Configuration-Parameters.html#coordinatesystemproj4string)
Proj4 string for the coordinate system. This value is used by the clients of the service.
## Coordinate System Service[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Configuration/Common-Service-Configuration-Parameters.html#coordinate-system-service)
###  `CoordinateSystemServiceUri`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Configuration/Common-Service-Configuration-Parameters.html#coordinatesystemserviceuri)
URI of NetWorks Coordinate System Service. Default: `http://localhost/NetWorksCoordinateSystemService/`
## Authentication[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Configuration/Common-Service-Configuration-Parameters.html#authentication)
###  `infrastructureServiceAuthentication:Mode`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Configuration/Common-Service-Configuration-Parameters.html#infrastructureserviceauthenticationmode)
Authentication mode. Allowed values:
  * `Bearer` = OpenID Connect.
  * `Anonymous` = Anonymous (default).

###  `infrastructureServiceAuthentication:Parameters:RequiredClaims`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Configuration/Common-Service-Configuration-Parameters.html#infrastructureserviceauthenticationparametersrequiredclaims)
Required claims expected in Bearer token. Comma separated list. Include `gtechnologyDBConnect` claim to match role-restriction behavior of NetWorks.
###  `infrastructureServiceAuthentication:Parameters:EnableCaching`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Configuration/Common-Service-Configuration-Parameters.html#infrastructureserviceauthenticationparametersenablecaching)
Enable caching of user identities. When `true` (default), identities are cached and the OIDC UserInfo endpoint is called only once per unique identity if required claims are missing. When `false`, UserInfo endpoint is called on each request when required claims are missing.
###  `infrastructureServiceAuthentication:Parameters:CacheTimeoutMinutes`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Configuration/Common-Service-Configuration-Parameters.html#infrastructureserviceauthenticationparameterscachetimeoutminutes)
Number of minutes to keep identities in cache (before reaching to user info endpoint again). Default: `60`.
###  `RequireGTechnologyDBConnect`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Configuration/Common-Service-Configuration-Parameters.html#requiregtechnologydbconnect)
When set to `true`, `gtechnologyDBConnect` claim is required and the default connection string is never used. Applies only when authentication is set to OpenID Connect. Default is `false`.
###  `UseDefaultIdentity`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Configuration/Common-Service-Configuration-Parameters.html#usedefaultidentity)
In Anonymous mode, the default user's roles are used to restrict access to metadata and data. When set to `false`, default user's identity is not used an role restrictions are not applied. Default is `true`.
## Encoding[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Configuration/Common-Service-Configuration-Parameters.html#encoding)
Parameters related to explicit configuration of text encoding in specific parts of processing.
###  `DDC:TextPointEncoding`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Configuration/Common-Service-Configuration-Parameters.html#ddctextpointencoding)
Encoding of TextPoint text data in DDC files. Allowed values are well-known encoding monikers like `utf-8` or `iso-8859-1`. See [List of encodings](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.text.encoding#list-of-encodings). Default is `iso-8859-1`.
This configuration parameter can be also specified using environment variable `NW_DDC_TEXT_POINT_ENCODING`.
###  `CCMEncoding`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Configuration/Common-Service-Configuration-Parameters.html#ccmencoding)
Text encoding of CCM file. When not present, defaults to the current system ANSI encoding (if available), otherwise to UTF-8. For allowed values see [List of encodings](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.text.encoding#list-of-encodings).
## CORS[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Configuration/Common-Service-Configuration-Parameters.html#cors)
###  `IsCorsEnabled`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Configuration/Common-Service-Configuration-Parameters.html#iscorsenabled)
Enable [CORS (Cross-Origin Resource Sharing)](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/CORS) responses from the service. Allowed values: `true`, `false`. Default: `false`.
###  `Origins`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Configuration/Common-Service-Configuration-Parameters.html#origins)
Enter the client names that should have access to the service. Use a full path to the computer starting with `http://` or `https://`. Multiple clients can be specified by separating with commas. You can allow access by any client by specifying `*` as the `Origins` value.
##### Caution
Only add the names of computers to the CORS Origins list if the computer is running a web application or service that calls the service directly. Clients running web browsers that connect to those web applications or services do not need to be added to the CORS Origins list.
Setting the CORS Origins value to `*` poses a potentially serious security risk and is not recommended.
###  `Methods`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Configuration/Common-Service-Configuration-Parameters.html#methods)
Comma separated list of HTTP verbs for which CORS response is allowed. Use `*` to enable CORS for all verbs.

# Configuration System
For details on how to format configuration files, see [Configuration in ASP.NET Core](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/aspnet/core/fundamentals/configuration/)

# ConfigurationProperties.txt file
**ConfigurationProperties.txt** is a text file used to provide additional properties for NetWorks configurations.
It is always located in the same folder as the **ConnectionConfigurationMap.ccm** file.
## Format[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Configuration/ConfigurationProperties.txt-file.html#format)
**ConfigurationProperties.txt** uses the same formatting as **ConnectionConfigurationMap.ccm**.
Each line is formatted as `<key>`=`<value>`; Line starting `CONFIGURATION_NAME` starts a section of properties for the configuration specified in `<value>`. All subsequent lines are properties of this configuration.
Empty lines are ignored.
## Example[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Configuration/ConfigurationProperties.txt-file.html#example)

```
CONFIGURATION_NAME=GINIUS;
DELTASDIRECTORY=C:\Intergraph\Deltas\GINIUS;
CONFIGURATION_NAME=GINIUSD;
DELTASDIRECTORY=C:\Intergraph\Deltas\GINIUS;
CONFIGURATION_NAME=NETWORKS;
DELTASDIRECTORY=C:\Intergraph\Deltas\NETWORKS; 

```

## Well known properties[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Configuration/ConfigurationProperties.txt-file.html#well-known-properties)  
| Name  | Description  | Expected value  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| CONFIGURATION_NAME  | NetWorks configuration  |   |  
| DELTASDIRECTORY  | Path to folder where .deltas files are exported  | Path (C:\Folder) or UNC path (\server\share)  |

# Environment LCID override
## Overview[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Configuration/Environment-LCID-override.html#overview)
NetWorks uses LCID from current culture to determine the location of published metadata files. Some regional format settings (e.g. `English (Germany`) are bound to cultures with `LOCALE_CUSTOM_UNSPECIFIED` (0x1000, or 4096) LCID, resulting in incorrect `0000` metadata subfolder.
## Solution[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Configuration/Environment-LCID-override.html#solution)
To allow the user to use these regional settings and NetWorks to work properly, it is possible to set `NW_LCID` environment variable to the desired value. If it is specified, LCID from this variable is used instead of the one from current culture.
## Example[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Configuration/Environment-LCID-override.html#example)
Set the variable to use English metadata:

```
set NW_LCID=0009

```

##### How-service-locates-configuration-files

# ServiceConfig.ini
## Rules[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Configuration/How-service-locates-configuration-files/ServiceConfig.ini.html#rules)
  * Each line is `<key>`=`<value>`
  * Lines starting with `;` are comments

## Example configuration file[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Configuration/How-service-locates-configuration-files/ServiceConfig.ini.html#example-configuration-file)

```
ConnectionInfo=user/password@NETWORKS
LCID=0009
  
;; Default pre-loaded legend G3E_LSNO
G3E_LSNO=7
  
;; Alternative FileUNCPath. If specified, FileUNCPath is NOT read from Registry.
;FileUNCPath=

;; Use these values to specify DDC location directly, bypassing FileUNCPath and CCM mechanism 
;MetadataPath=
;DDCPath=
  
Deltas:RefreshMinutes=5

GeoJSON:UseVertexReduction=true
  
CoordinateSystem:Code=EPSG:3857
CoordinateSystem:Proj4String=

```

# ServiceConfig.json
## Rules[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Configuration/How-service-locates-configuration-files/ServiceConfig.json.html#rules)
  * Top level properties are mapped to parameter names
  * Parameters with `:` are split to next level objects (e.g. `Deltas:RefreshMinutes` - see example below)
  * All string values must be enclosed in `"`
  * All `\` characters in strings must be escaped as `\\`

## Example configuration file[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Configuration/How-service-locates-configuration-files/ServiceConfig.json.html#example-configuration-file)

```
{
    "ConnectionInfo": "user/password@NETWORKS",
    "LCID": "0009",
    "G3E_LSNO": "7",
    "Deltas": { 
       "RefreshMinutes": "5" 
    },
    "GeoJSON": { 
        "UseVertexReduction": "true" 
     },
    "CoordinateSystem": { 
      "Code": "EPSG:3857" 
    }
}

```

# ServiceConfig.xml
## Rules[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Configuration/How-service-locates-configuration-files/ServiceConfig.xml.html#rules)
  * Root element name is not important
  * Each element on 1st level is mapped to a parameter name
  * Parameters with `:` in name are split to parent-child elements (e.g. `Deltas:RefreshMinutes` - see below)

## Example configuration file[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Configuration/How-service-locates-configuration-files/ServiceConfig.xml.html#example-configuration-file)

```
<settings>
  <ConnectionInfo>user/password@NETWORKS</ConnectionInfo>
  <LCID>0009</LCID>
  
  <!-- Default pre-loaded legend G3E_LSNO -->
  <G3E_LSNO>7</G3E_LSNO>
  
  <!-- 
    Alternative FileUNCPath. If specified, FileUNCPath is NOT read from Registry.
  -->
  <FileUNCPath></FileUNCPath>

  <!-- 
    Use these values to specify DDC location directly, bypassing FileUNCPath and CCM mechanism 
  -->
  <MetadataPath></MetadataPath>
  <DDCPath></DDCPath>
  
  <!-- Deltas options -->
  <Deltas>
    <RefreshMinutes>5</RefreshMinutes>
  </Deltas>
  
  <GeoJSON>
    <UseVertexReduction>true</UseVertexReduction>
  </GeoJSON>
  
  <CoordinateSystem>
    <Code>EPSG:3857</Code>
    <Proj4String></Proj4String>
  </CoordinateSystem>
  
</settings>

```

# How service locates configuration files
## Workflow[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Configuration/How-service-locates-configuration-files.html#workflow)
Services use the following logic when searching for configuration files:
  1. [Determine service instance](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Configuration/How-services-determine-service-instance.html)
  2. If service instance is not configured, configuration files are loaded from the same directory as the .exe.
  3. If service instance is configured, configuration files are loaded from `c:\ProgramData\Intergraph\NetWorks\ServiceInstances\{SERVICE_INSTANCE}`

## Configuration file[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Configuration/How-service-locates-configuration-files.html#configuration-file)
Configuration parameters can be specified in JSON, XML and INI formats using **ServiceConfig.json** , **ServiceConfig.xml** or **ServiceConfig.ini** files. If there are is more than one configuration file specified, the priority is JSON (lowest), XML, INI (highest).
The default file for service configuration [ServiceConfig.ini](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Configuration/How-service-locates-configuration-files/ServiceConfig.ini.html) file.
## Technical notes[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Configuration/How-service-locates-configuration-files.html#technical-notes)
Services uses .NET Core configuration system. For details on how to format configuration files, see [Configuration in ASP.NET Core](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/aspnet/core/fundamentals/configuration/?view=aspnetcore-3.1)

# How services determine service instance
## Overview[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Configuration/How-services-determine-service-instance.html#overview)
Services can be configured using two modes:
A. No service instance name Service instance name is not configured. Configuration files are always loaded from the directory which contains the .exe or .dll.
B. Service instance name configured Service instance name determines the location of the configuration files. This mode allows separation of the binary files from configuration.
## Workflow[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Configuration/How-services-determine-service-instance.html#workflow)
Service checks for service instance name in this order. Files are always expected in the same directory as the main .exe or .dll.
  1. `instance.ini`
  2. `instance.xml`
  3. `instance.json`
  4. Environment variable `NW_SERVICE_INSTANCE`
  5. Command line parameter `SERVICE_INSTANCE`

## Examples[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Configuration/How-services-determine-service-instance.html#examples)
### instance.ini[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Configuration/How-services-determine-service-instance.html#instanceini)

```
SERVICE_INSTANCE=DeltasNETWORKS

```

### instance.json[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Configuration/How-services-determine-service-instance.html#instancejson)

```
{
  "SERVICE_INSTANCE": "DeltasNETWORKS"
}

```

### instance.xml[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Configuration/How-services-determine-service-instance.html#instancexml)

```
<settings>
  <SERVICE_INSTANCE>DeltasNETWORKS</SERVICE_INSTANCE>
</settings>

```

### Environment variable[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Configuration/How-services-determine-service-instance.html#environment-variable)

```
set NW_SERVICE_INSTANCE=DeltasNETWORKS
Hxgn.Intergraph.GTechnology.Deltas.ServiceHost.exe

```

### Command line[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Configuration/How-services-determine-service-instance.html#command-line)

```
Hxgn.Intergraph.GTechnology.Deltas.ServiceHost.exe --SERVICE_INSTANCE=DeltasNETWORKS

```

# Configuration
This topic contains all information on general configuration of services.
## Overview[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Configuration.html#overview)
Deployed NetWorks services use two configuration systems.
[![NetWorks_configuration_overview_v01.svg](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/.attachments/NetWorks_configuration_overview_v01-84794a42-8126-49ce-b9df-c777861e3d66.svg)](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/.attachments/NetWorks_configuration_overview_v01-84794a42-8126-49ce-b9df-c777861e3d66.svg)
### Type 1: web.config and ServiceConfig.xml[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Configuration.html#type-1-webconfig-and-serviceconfigxml)
Runtime configuration is stored in service deployment folders in files **web.config** , **ServiceConfig.xml**.
Logging is configured via **NLog.config**.
OpenID Connect via **OpenIdConfig.json**.
### Type 2: instance.ini and ServiceConfig.ini[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Configuration.html#type-2-instanceini-and-serviceconfigini)
File **instance.ini** in the service deployment folder contains the **InstanceName** of the service (as **SERVICE_INSTANCE**).
Runtime configuration is stored in service instance configuration folders under **%PROGRAMDATA%\Intergraph\NetWorks\ServiceInstances\\{InstanceName}** , in file **ServiceConfig.ini**.
Logging is configured via **NLog.config**. ETW logging can be optionally configured via file **logging.json**.
OpenID Connect via **OpenIdConfig.json**.
### Coordinate System Service[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Configuration.html#coordinate-system-service)
This service has no instance configuration.
## Related topics[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Configuration.html#related-topics)
  * [How service locates configuration files](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Configuration/How-service-locates-configuration-files.html)
  * [Diagnostics](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Diagnostics.html)

#### Data-Access

##### Dynamic-filtering

###### Configuration

# NWG_DYNAMICREGION
Assignment of groups (OIDC claims) to dynamic regions.  
| Column  | Data type  | NULL  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| GWS_GDRNO  | NUMBER(9)  | No  | Primary key.  |  
| GWS_GROUP  | VARCHAR2(100)  | No  | Identifier of a group of dynamic regions. The OIDC claim value is mapped to this identifier.  |  
| GWS_REGION  | VARCHAR2(100)  | No  | Identifier of dynamic region. The value is used for attribute-based filtering.  |  
| GWS_WRITE  | NUMBER(1)  | No  | Read/Write flag. 0=Read only. 1=Read/Write  |  
| GWS_DESCRIPTION  | VARCHAR2(100)  | No  | User description.  |  
| GAO_EDITDATE  | DATE  | Yes  | Date of last modification  |  
**Important** The table must be registered as a picklist and published with metadata.
Example of G3E_PICKLIST record:  
| G3E_PNO  | G3E_USERNAME  | G3E_TABLE  | G3E_KEYFIELD  | G3E_VALUEFIELD  | G3E_ORDERBYKEY  | G3E_PUBLISH  | G3E_ADDITIONALPUBLISHFIELDS  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| 90001  | Dynamic filtering  | NWG_DYNAMICREGION  | GWS_GDRNO  | GWS_GROUP  | GWS_GDRNO  | 1  | GWS_REGION, GWS_WRITE  |

# Dialog Web Services
## Overview[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Data-Access/Dynamic-filtering/Dialog-Web-Services.html#overview)
In GTDWS, dynamic filtering must be implemented in methods, which:
  * read feature instance data
  * update feature data
  * delete feature

> **Note** Feature creation is not restricted beyond the existing role-based restriction. The region gets typically populated after the feature is created (by a FI), which is done outside of the current database transaction and requires re-reading of the feature data **after** is was created.
## Mechanism[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Data-Access/Dynamic-filtering/Dialog-Web-Services.html#mechanism)
Unlike Vector Service, GTDWS works with database and component tables, not published component views. To restrict access to features based on region, each RW operation must be accompanied by a SQL condition, filtering the list of allowed G3E_FID values for the region.
The list of regions is evaluated in the web service from OIDC claims and passed in to the database session using the `NWG_CONTEXT` package. `NWG_GTDWS` reads the context value and (if present), constructs dynamic filtering condition using the metadata in [NWG_DYNAMICFILTERATTR_OPTABLE](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Data-Access/Dynamic-filtering/Metadata/NWG_DYNAMICFILTERATTR_OPTABLE.html).
Example:

```
SELECT ... 
  FROM COMMON_N
 WHERE G3E_FNO = :G3E_FNO 
   AND G3E_FID = :G3E_FID
   AND CLLI IN ('REGION1', 'REGION2')

```

## Configuration[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Data-Access/Dynamic-filtering/Dialog-Web-Services.html#configuration)
The dynamic region filtering is configured via `web.config` file of the deployed Dialog Web Services instance. appSetting keys used to configure dynamic filtering:  
| Parameter  | Mandatory  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| DynamicFiltering:MembershipClaimName  | Y  | Name of OIDC claim which contains group assigned to user (access level is RO or determined from MappingTable).  |  
| DynamicFiltering:MembershipClaimNameRW  |   | Name of OIDC claim which contains group assigned to user for read-write operations (access level is RW).  |  
| DynamicFiltering:MembershipIdSeparator  |   | Separator character used as delimiter of groups in claim.  |  
| DynamicFiltering:MappingTable  |   | Name of metadata table which contains list of groups and regions.  |  
| DynamicFiltering:MappingTableGroupColumn  |   | Name of column in metadata table which identifies the group.  |  
| DynamicFiltering:MappingTableRegionColumn  |   | Name of column in metadata table which identifies the region.  |  
| DynamicFiltering:MappingTableWriteColumn  |   | Name of column in metadata table which identifies the access level (0=Read only, 1=Read/write). Optional. When not present, all access is treated as read-only.  |  
| DynamicFiltering:MappingFile  |   | Path to JSON file with group to region mapping. Alternative to MappingTable with higher precedence.  |  
### Example[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Data-Access/Dynamic-filtering/Dialog-Web-Services.html#example)

```
  <appSettings>
    <add key="DynamicFiltering:MembershipClaimName" value="dynamic_role" />
    <add key="DynamicFiltering:MappingTable" value="NWG_DYNAMICREGION" />
    <add key="DynamicFiltering:MappingTableGroupColumn" value="GWS_GROUP" />
    <add key="DynamicFiltering:MappingTableRegionColumn" value="GWS_REGION" />
    <add key="DynamicFiltering:MappingTableWriteColumn" value="GWS_WRITE" />
  </appSettings>

```

**Important**
The claims configured in `DynamicFiltering:MembershipClaimName` must be added to the list of RequiredClaims in `web.config`, unless they are automatically added to the access token by the OIDC provider.
Example:

```
  <infrastructureServiceAuthentication mode="Bearer">
    <parameters>
      <add key="OpenIdConfigFile" value="~/OpenIdConfig.json" />
      <add key="RequiredClaims" value="gtechnologyDBConnect,dynamic_role" />
      <add key="EnableCaching" value="False" />
    </parameters>
  </infrastructureServiceAuthentication>

```

# Vector Service
## Mechanism[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Data-Access/Dynamic-filtering/Vector-Service.html#mechanism)
The list of regions is determined from the OIDC claim identified by setting `DynamicFiltering:MembershipClaimName` when request arrives. The filtering condition on field specified in setting `DynamicFiltering:FilterColumn` is evaluated in the pipeline when reading data from published component views.
> **Important** The filtering attribute must be published in **all** component views for all filtered features.
## Configuration[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Data-Access/Dynamic-filtering/Vector-Service.html#configuration)  
| Parameter  | Mandatory  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| DynamicFiltering:FilterColumn  | Y  | Name of column to use in filtering.  |  
| DynamicFiltering:MembershipClaimName  |   | Name of OIDC claim which contains group assigned to user (access level is RO or determined from MappingTable).  |  
| DynamicFiltering:MembershipIdSeparator  |   | Separator character used as delimiter of groups in claim.  |  
| DynamicFiltering:MappingTable  |   | Name of metadata table which contains list of groups and regions.  |  
| DynamicFiltering:MappingTableGroupColumn  |   | Name of column in metadata table which identifies the group.  |  
| DynamicFiltering:MappingTableRegionColumn  |   | Name of column in metadata table which identifies the region.  |  
| DynamicFiltering:MappingFile  |   | Path to JSON file with group to region mapping. Alternative to MappingTable with higher precedence.  |  
**Important**
The claims configured in `DynamicFiltering:MembershipClaimName` must be added to the list of RequiredClaims in `web.config`, unless they are automatically added to the access token by the OIDC provider.
### Example 1 - Metadata based group to region assignment[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Data-Access/Dynamic-filtering/Vector-Service.html#example-1---metadata-based-group-to-region-assignment)
Claim `group` is used as source of assignment of user to groups in published picklist table `NWG_DYNAMICREGION`. Values in `GWS_REGION` are used to filter data rows by field `CLLI`.
Partial `ServiceConfig.ini`.

```
infrastructureServiceAuthentication:Parameters:RequiredClaims=gtechnologyDBConnect,group
DynamicFiltering:FilterColumn=CLLI
DynamicFiltering:MembershipClaimName=group
DynamicFiltering:MappingTable=NWG_DYNAMICREGION
DynamicFiltering:MappingTableGroupColumn=GWS_GROUP
DynamicFiltering:MappingTableRegionColumn=GWS_REGION

```

With this configuration, the Vector Service adds a dynamic condition when reading data from published component views, e.g.:

```
CLLI IN ('AT', 'DE')

```

### Example 2 - File based group to region assignment[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Data-Access/Dynamic-filtering/Vector-Service.html#example-2---file-based-group-to-region-assignment)
Claim `group` is used as source of assignment of user to groups in published file `C:\groups.txt`. Values in `GWS_REGION` are used to filter data rows by field `CLLI`.
Partial `ServiceConfig.ini`.

```
infrastructureServiceAuthentication:Parameters:RequiredClaims=gtechnologyDBConnect,group
DynamicFiltering:FilterColumn=CLLI
DynamicFiltering:MembershipClaimName=group
DynamicFiltering:MappingFile=C:\groups.txt

```

`C:\groups.txt` example:

```
Group1,CZ
Group1,SK
Group2,AT
Group2,DE

```

# Dynamic filtering
## Requirements[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Data-Access/Dynamic-filtering.html#requirements)
  * Services should allow access only to data regions assigned to the currently logged-in user.
  * A single user can have multiple regions assigned for read-only access and another set assigned for read-write access.
  * Filtering of data regions is based on attribute value.

## User-to-data-region mapping[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Data-Access/Dynamic-filtering.html#user-to-data-region-mapping)
Dynamic filtering requires that all access is authorized using OpenID Connect (OIDC). Each user has a set of claims available in access token or from the OIDC /userinfo endpoint.
User has assignment to an access group in claims.

```
{
   "regions": "Group1"
}

```

A mapping exists in another source (database, configuration file), which maps the group name to list of regions.
**Example**  
| Group  | Region  | Write  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| Group1  | AT  | 0  |  
| Group1  | DE  | 0  |  
| Group1  | CZ  | 1  |  
| Group1  | SK  | 1  |  
| Group2  | SK  | 1  |  
| Group3  | CZ  | 1  |  
Services use this information to translate group membership to regions.
List of regions is used in dynamic filtering conditions.
Example:

```
CLLI IN ('AT', 'DE', 'CZ', 'SK')

```

## Availability[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Data-Access/Dynamic-filtering.html#availability)
Dynamic filtering based on feature attributes is available only for:
  * Vector Service
  * Dialog Web Services

# Require gtechnologyDBConnect when OpenID Connect is used
Configurable option **RequireGTechnologyDBConnect** (true/false) can be set for NetWorks Services.
When **true** , _gtechnologyDBConnect_ must be present among the current user claims and it must match the current configuration and application (NetWorks) or the current configuration and must not have application specifier. It is not possible to use the default connection string defined for the service.
For configuration `CONFIGURATION`, these are valid _gtechnologyDBConnect_ claims (example):
  * `user/password@CONFIGURATION:NetWorks`
  * `user/password@CONFIGURATION`

When **false** , _gtechnologyDBConnect_ is not required. When missing, the default connection string is used. This is the default behavior.
The setting can be manually configured in:
**ServiceConfig.xml** for WMS, WFS and JobService.
Example

```
<providerSettings>
    <setting name="RequireGTechnologyDBConnect" value="true" /> 
</providerSettings>

```

**web.config** (under `<appSettings>`) for other services (Analytical, Dialog Web Service).
Example

```
<appSettings>
    <add key="RequireGTechnologyDBConnect" value="true" /> 
</appSettings>

```

**ServiceConfig.ini** for Vector, Data Transfer, Work Service (typically located under `c:\ProgramData\Intergraph\NetWorks\ServiceInstances\{instanceName}`
Example

```
RequireGTechnologyDBConnect=true

```

# User identifier in database operations
## Overview[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Data-Access/User-identifier-in-database-operations.html#overview)
Clients (like NetWorks Portal) use OpenID Connect for authentication and authorization of users. Requests from Portal to other services are make in the context of the logged in user by passing an authorization token (typically a JWT), which provides the identity of the interactive user to the service. When the service makes a connection to the database, the end user is typically mapped to an Oracle user using the `gtechnologyDBConnect` claim. In case when multiple OIDC users are mapped to the same Oracle user, the identity of the interactive user may not be established during the Oracle session.
## Passing end user identifier to database[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Data-Access/User-identifier-in-database-operations.html#passing-end-user-identifier-to-database)
NetWorks Web Services running in OpenID Connect (OIDC) mode are capable of extracting a configurable claim (attribute) from the claims of current user and pass this information to the Oracle session using the `DBMS_SESSION.SET_IDENTIFIER` procedure. During the processing of the request this identifier is available to Oracle procedures and triggers via `V$SESSION.CLIENT_IDENTIFIER` or can be retrieved from `SYS_CONTEXT('USERENV','CLIENT_IDENTIFIER')`. After completing the request, NetWorks services reset the identifier by calling `DBMS_SESSION.CLEAR_IDENTIFIER`.
### Limitations[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Data-Access/User-identifier-in-database-operations.html#limitations)
  * Oracle limits the CLIENT_IDENTIFIER to 64 bytes.

## Configuration[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Data-Access/User-identifier-in-database-operations.html#configuration)
Parameter `ClientIdClaim` in the service configuration. The value if this parameter is the name of the claim, available in OIDC access token or from the OIDC UserInfo endpoint.
##### Note
If the claim identified by `ClientIdClaim` is not available in access token, the claim name must be added to `RequiredClaims`.
### ASP.NET Core Services[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Data-Access/User-identifier-in-database-operations.html#aspnet-core-services)
This workflow applies to: _Vector Service, Feature Data Service, Feature Transaction Service, Data Transfer Service, Work Service._
  * Add parameter `ClientIdClaim` to _ServiceConfig.ini_.
  * Add claim name to `infrastructureServiceAuthentication:Parameters:RequiredClaims` if it is only available from OIDC UserInfo.

**Example**

```
ClientIdClaim=email
infrastructureServiceAuthentication:Parameters:RequiredClaims=gtechnologyDBConnect,email

```

### Owin services[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Data-Access/User-identifier-in-database-operations.html#owin-services)
This workflow applies to: _Analytical Service, Job Service, Feature Model Service, Vector Tile Service._
  * Add parameter `ClientIdClaim` to `web.config` under `<appSettings>`.
  * Add claim name to `RequiredClaims` under `<infrastructureServiceAuthentication>`.

**Example**
_web.config_

```
  <appSettings>
    <add key="ConnectionInfo" value="user/pwd@CONFIG" />
    <!-- ... -->
    <add key="ClientIdClaim" value="email" />
  </appSettings>

  <infrastructureServiceAuthentication mode="Bearer">
    <parameters>
      <add key="OpenIdConfigFile" value="~/OpenIdConfig.json" />
      <add key="RequiredClaims" value="gtechnologyDBConnect,email" />
      <add key="EnableCaching" value="False" />
    </parameters>
  </infrastructureServiceAuthentication>

```

### OGC Services[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Data-Access/User-identifier-in-database-operations.html#ogc-services)
This workflow applies to: _WMS, WFS, WMTS._
  * Add parameter `ClientIdClaim` to `ServiceConfig.xml`.

**Example**
_ServiceConfig.xml_

```
<ucServiceConfiguration>
  <providers>
    <provider category="wms" name="gtechnology" type=".\bin\Intergraph.GTechnology.OGCProviders.dll;Intergraph.GTechnology.OgcProviders.Wms.GTWmsProvider">
      <providerSettings>
        <setting name="ConnectionInfo" value="user/pwd@CONFIG" />
        <setting name="ServiceNumber" value="7" />
        <!-- ... -->
        <setting name="ClientIdClaim" value="email"/>
      </providerSettings>
    </provider>

```

_web.config_

```
  <infrastructureServiceAuthentication mode="Bearer">
    <parameters>
      <add key="OpenIdConfigFile" value="~/OpenIdConfig.json" />
      <add key="RequiredClaims" value="gtechnologyDBConnect,email" />
      <add key="EnableCaching" value="False" />
    </parameters>
  </infrastructureServiceAuthentication>

```

# Diagnostics
## Overview[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Diagnostics.html#overview)
New services and components use **ETW** ([Event Tracing for Windows](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/etw/about-event-tracing)) to collect events from the runtime.
ETW is a high-performance event tracing mechanism internally used also by .NET Framework and other libraries. It's core features are:
  * Event production, event collection and event serialization are decoupled
  * Produces semantic logs (not strings)
  * High performance - when turned off, the performance penalty is close to zero
  * Can be turned on and off remotely (e.g. logman)
  * Part of .NET Framework and .NET Core (no need to reference 3rd party libraries)

## Configuration[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Diagnostics.html#configuration)
Listening to ETW events is configured using `logging.json` file, which is expected at the same location as other service configuration files.
For command line tools, check the documentation of the tool for location of the file.
### logging.json format[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Diagnostics.html#loggingjson-format)

```
{
  "ETW": {
    "Sources": [
      {
        "Name": "<Event source name 1>",
        "Level": "<Level 1>",
        "Keywords": "<Keywords 1>"
      }, {
        "Name": "<Event source name 2>",
        "Level": "<Level 2>",
        "Keywords": "<Keywords 2>"
      },

     ...
    ]
  }
}

```
  
| Parameter  | Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
| Name  | ETW event source name or regular expression for matching the ETW event source name.  |  
| Level  | Threshold for event collection. When not specified, defaults to **Error**. [List of allowed values](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.diagnostics.tracing.eventlevel)  |  
| Keywords  | Flags for ETW event source keywords to track. When not specified, defaults to **All keywords**.   
This value can be used to turn on/off collection of certain events for a single source. Compute this value as a sum of `Keyword` value for all tracked Keywords for the ETW event source.  |  
## Default configuration[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Diagnostics.html#default-configuration)
If `logging.json` is not present, the default configuration is to track high-level activities at the level which is specified for logging output in log writer (by default: NLog).

```
{
  "ETW": {
    "Sources": [
      {
        "Name": "Intergraph-Diagnostics-Activities",
        "Level": "Verbose",
        "Keywords": 3
      }
    ]
  }
}

```

## Catching errors from all Hxgn sources[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Diagnostics.html#catching-errors-from-all-hxgn-sources)
Beginning with version 11.01.2201, services are deployed by default with the following `logging.json` configuration. This ensures that all Warnings and Errors from all Intergraph- and Hxgn- ETW sources are logged into the logs. The Level for `Intergraph-Diagnostics-Activities` is configured to use the same level as the primary logging output (typically `NLog.config`).

```
{
  "ETW": {
    "Sources": [
      {
        "Name": "Intergraph-Diagnostics-Activities",
        "Level": "Error",
        "Keywords": "3"
      },
      {
        "Name": "Intergraph-.*",
        "Level": "Warning"
      },
      {
        "Name": "Hxgn-.*",
        "Level": "Warning"
      }
    ]
  }
}

```
