# Licensing
## Overview[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Licensing.html#overview)
Beginning with version 02.00.2101, some NetWorks services support two licensing modes in combination with CC licenses:
  * **Per Service**  
One license is checked-out for each running instance of the service.
Number of concurrently served requests is not limited (only by hardware). This mode was used by all service (except for Map Server) in the previous version and it still available for all services.
  * **Per Request**  
One license is checked-out for each concurrently served request.
Example: Service instance with 1 per-request license can execute only 1 request at a time. Other requests wait in queue.
Each service instance needs to be configured with the number of licenses which it checks-out at startup time. If a service checks-out less than the configured amount of licenses from the license server, it continues with the maximum available amount (if greater than 0). If the request queue contains more than configured limit of requests, the service returns HTTP status 503 (Service Unavailable).

### Workflow[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Licensing.html#workflow)  
|   | Per Service  | Per Request  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| Check-out event  | Arrival of first request  | Service startup  |  
| Number of licenses checked out  | 1  | Configured value `MaxConcurrentRequests` or `ConcurrentLicensing:MaxConcurrentRequests`.  |  
| Concurrency restrictions  | None  | Number of concurrent requests at a time is limited.  |  
## Services[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Licensing.html#services)
Per Request licensing mode is applicable to services in the following table.  
| Component  | Per Service license name  | Per Request license name  | Configuration type  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| Analytical Service  | nwweb_analytical  | nwweb_analytical_c  | A  |  
| Dialog Web Service Read  | nwweb_dialogread  | nwweb_dialogread_c  | A  |  
| Dialog Web Service Write  | nwweb_dialogwrite  | nwweb_dialogwrite_c  | A  |  
| Job Service - Read  | nwweb_jobsview  | nwweb_jobsview_c  | A  |  
| Job Service - Manage  | nwweb_jobsmanage  | nwweb_jobsmanage_c  | A  |  
| Data Transfer Service  | nwweb_datatransfer  | nwweb_datatransfer_c  | B  |  
| Dynamic WMS  | nwweb_dynamicwms  | nwweb_dynamicwms_c  | B  |  
| Feature Data Service  | nwweb_fds  | nwweb_fds_c  | B  |  
| Feature Transaction Service  | nwweb_fts  | nwweb_fts_c  | B  |  
| Vector Service  | nwweb_vector  | nwweb_vector_c  | B  |  
| Work Service  | nwweb_work  | nwweb_work_c  | B  |  
## Configuration[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Licensing.html#configuration)
**Per Service** licensing does not require any special configuration.
**Per Instance** licensing requires setting of parameter **Concurrent licenses used** during deployment via Administration Console to a value greater than zero. The sum of **Concurrent licenses used** for all deployed services should be less or equal to the licenses available.
### Configuration type A[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Licensing.html#configuration-type-a)
Number of licenses is configured in **web.config** file of the deployed instance under `<appSettings>` as **MaxConcurrentRequests** setting.
Optional parameter **RequestQueueLimit** can be used to limit the queue of waiting requests. Default is 1000.

```
  <appSettings>
    <add key="MaxConcurrentRequests" value="5" />
    <add key="MaxConcurrentRequestsWrite" value="2" />
    <add key="RequestQueueLimit" value="100" />
  </appSettings>

```

##### Note
Some services (Dialog Web Service, Job Service) require two kinds of licenses (read-only operations, read-write operations). To check-out different number of licenses for the read-write operations, set also the `MaxConcurrentRequestsWrite` parameter.
### Configuration type B[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Licensing.html#configuration-type-b)
Number of licenses in configured in **ServiceConfig.ini** file of the service as parameter **ConcurrentLicensing:MaxConcurrentRequests**.
Optional parameter **ConcurrentLicensing:RequestQueueLimit** can be used to limit the queue of waiting requests. Default is 1000.

```
ConcurrentLicensing:MaxConcurrentRequests=2
ConcurrentLicensing:RequestQueueLimit=100

```

## Related topics[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Licensing.html#related-topics)
  * [How service locates configuration files](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Configuration/How-service-locates-configuration-files.html)

##### Metadata-tables

# NWG_CONTEXTPROPERTY
## Description[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Reference/Metadata-tables/NWG_CONTEXTPROPERTY.html#description)
Mapping of user properties and properties available in the Oracle context when updating feature attributes. The user properties are typically claims available in from OpenID Connect provider.
## Columns[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Reference/Metadata-tables/NWG_CONTEXTPROPERTY.html#columns)  
| Name  | Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
| GWS_CPNO  | Row identifier.  |  
| GWS_PROPERTYNAME  | The name of the context property. See [Property naming](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Reference/Metadata-tables/NWG_CONTEXTPROPERTY.html#property-naming) for details.  |  
| GWS_SOURCETYPE  | Type of source value. Allowed values: `Claim`, `Environment`. See [Source types](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Reference/Metadata-tables/NWG_CONTEXTPROPERTY.html#source-types).  |  
| GWS_SOURCE  | Source of the property. Depends on the GWS_SOURCETYPE property. For `Claim`, name of the claim retrieved from the identity provider. For `Environment`, allowed values are: `deviceid`.  |  
| GWS_EDITDATE  | Date the record was created or last edited.  |  
### Property naming[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Reference/Metadata-tables/NWG_CONTEXTPROPERTY.html#property-naming)
The property name is an arbitrary identifier. Beginning with version 11.01.2402, it can be used to encode the processing mode for the property when mapping it to the feature attribute.
The property name can optionally be followed by two underscore characters (`__`) and a set of optional flags (`IUCF`). The order of the flags is **important**. If missing, the default processing mode is `IUC`, i.e. the attribute is updated on inserts and updates of the component and a component row is created if it does not exist already.  
| Flag  | Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
| `I`  | Map the property when inserting new component instance.  |  
| `U`  | Map the property when updating existing component instance.  |  
| `C`  | Create component instance if does not exist yet.  |  
| `F`  | Force mapping of the property to an attribute even if the value for the attribute was provided explicitly.  |  
Examples:
  * `DEVICEID__IUC` - Property named `DEVICEID`, which is mapped when inserting or updating a component. The component is created if it does not exist yet on the feature.
  * `EMAIL__IF` - Property named `EMAIL`, mapped only when inserting a new component. The value is mapped even if a value for the attribute was already provided. The component is not automatically created.

### Source types[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Reference/Metadata-tables/NWG_CONTEXTPROPERTY.html#source-types)
####  `Claim`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Reference/Metadata-tables/NWG_CONTEXTPROPERTY.html#claim)
Used to map claims provided by the identity provider. Specify the name of the claim in `GWS_SOURCE`.
####  `Environment`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Reference/Metadata-tables/NWG_CONTEXTPROPERTY.html#environment)
Used to retrieve various values related to environment and current context. Allowed values are listed in the following table.  
| Name  | Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
| `deviceid`  | When used in [Feature Editor](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Feature-Editor.html) context, this value contains unique device identifier from which the workset originated.  |  
## NWG_CONTEXTPROPERTY_OPTABLE[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Reference/Metadata-tables/NWG_CONTEXTPROPERTY.html#nwg_contextproperty_optable)
Optimized table for `NWG_CONTEXTPROPERTY`. The table is populated by package `NWG_CONTEXTPROPERTY_PKG`.
## Columns[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Reference/Metadata-tables/NWG_CONTEXTPROPERTY.html#columns-1)  
| Name  | Source table  | source field  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| GWS_CPMNO  | NWG_CONTEXTPROPERTY  | GWS_CPMNO  |  
| G3E_FNO  | NWG_CONTEXTPROPERTY  | G3E_FNO  |  
| G3E_ANO  | NWG_CONTEXTPROPERTY  | G3E_ANO  |  
| GWS_CPNO  | NWG_CONTEXTPROPERTY  | GWS_CPNO  |  
| GWS_EDITDATE  |   | SYSDATE  |

# NWG_CTXPROPERTYMAP
## Description[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Reference/Metadata-tables/NWG_CTXPROPERTYMAP.html#description)
Mapping of context properties (see [NWG_CONTEXTPROPERTY](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Reference/Metadata-tables/NWG_CONTEXTPROPERTY.html)) to feature attributes. The mapping is used when updating feature attributes through Dialog Web Service API.

# NWG_GENERALPARAMETER
Table contains general processing parameters for Feature Editor workflows.  
| Column  | Description  | Type  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| NWG_GPNO  | Primary key for this table  | NUMBER(9)  |  
| NWG_NAME  | Parameter name  | VARCHAR2(100)  |  
| NWG_VALUE  | Parameter value  | VARCHAR2(1000)  |  
| NWG_PUBLISH  | When 1, parameter value is published through API.  | NUMBER(1)  |  
| NWG_APPLICATION  | Application for which this configuration parameter is applicable. Bitmask: 8=NetWorks Portal, 16=Core Mobile. When `NULL`, the parameter applies to all applications. Setting this value to a non-`NULL` value is valid only for rows where `NWG_PUBLISH` is set to `1`, i.e. to parameters applied in the client applications.   
  
**Note** Combinations of `NWG_NAME` and `NWG_APPLICATION` must yield unique parameters for all applications.  | NUMBER(9)  |

Parameter names can be templates, with placeholders enclosed in `{}`. When configuring, replaced placeholders by actual values (e.g. for template `style/{G3E_FNO}/{G3E_CNO}` use `style/306/5643`).
## Configurable parameters for [Feature Editor](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Feature-Editor.html)[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Reference/Metadata-tables/NWG_GENERALPARAMETER.html#configurable-parameters-for-feature-editor)
##### Important
All parameters in this section should be published (NWG_PUBLISH=1).  
| Name or name template  | Description  |   |   |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| AllowedJobClasses  | Comma separated list of job classes (G3E_JCNO) to show in the Create Job command. When not specified or empty, all values from the defined picklist are displayed.  |   |   |  
| DefaultJobClass  | Override of default job class (G3E_JCNO) defined in the dialog type used to create new jobs (see parameter `NewJobDialogType`).  | style/{G3E_FNO}/{G3E_CNO}  | Override for style number (G3E_SNO) used for rendering of component identified by {G3E_FNO} and {G3E_CNO}.   
  
If not configured, the default style for placement of the component is used (style from default style rule row of the G3E_SRNO from the placement metadata of the component).  |  
| NewJobDialogType  | Dialog type used to create new jobs after submitting a workset. When not specified, defaults to `G3E_NEWJOB`.  
Configure this value when you need to create new jobs with default values for job attributes which are not present in the Feature Editor UI.  |   |   |  
| EditJobDialogType  | Dialog type used when updating job attributes after submitting a workset or detaching a workset from a job.  |   |   |  
| dialogtype/{G3E_FNO}/edit  | Override of dialog type for editing attributes of feature type {G3E_FNO}. When not specified, defaults to `Edit`.  |   |   |  
| dialogtype/{G3E_FNO}/review  | Override of dialog type for reviewing attributes of feature type {G3E_FNO}. When not specified, defaults to `Review`.  |   |   |  
| style/{G3E_FNO}/{G3E_CNO}  | Override the default style to use for geometries of feature type {G3E_FNO} and component type {G3E_CNO}. The value is the G3E_SNO of the desired style.  |   |   |  
| Validation:RequiredAttribute  | Severity of required attribute validation. Allowed values: `Error`, `E`, `Warning`, `W`, `Info`, `I`. Default is `Warning`.  |   |   |  
| Validation:RequiredComponent  | Severity of required component validation. Allowed values: `Error`, `E`, `Warning`, `W`, `Info`, `I`. Default is `Warning`.  |   |   |  
## Configurable parameters for Feature Editor [hyperlink processing](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Transaction-Service/ProcessTransactions/Hyperlink-mapping.html)[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Reference/Metadata-tables/NWG_GENERALPARAMETER.html#configurable-parameters-for-feature-editor-hyperlink-processing)
All parameters should be set as not-published (NWG_PUBLISH=0).  
| Name or name template  | Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
| HyperlinkFilter  | Regular expression for file references and hyperlinks (`"f"` values) in [ProcessTransactions](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Transaction-Service/ProcessTransactions.html)) requests, which are mapped using _HyperlinkPathTemplate_ and/or _HyperlinkValueTemplate_. If not present, all hyperlinks are processed.  |  
| HyperlinkPathTemplate  | Template string for mapping of file references in transactions to physical paths. The result of the evaluation is used by Work Service Features workload to copy the file from transaction to folder to the destination. When not present, physical paths are not mapped, and no files are copied.  
  
The purpose of this configuration is to allow different values for physical file storage (when file attachment is stored to permanent location) and value stored in attribute.  
  
For usage see [Hyperlink mapping](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Transaction-Service/ProcessTransactions/Hyperlink-mapping.html).  |  
| HyperlinkValueTemplate  | Template string for mapping of file references in transactions to attribute values. If not present, file references are stored in attribute values without change.  
  
For usage see [Hyperlink mapping](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Transaction-Service/ProcessTransactions/Hyperlink-mapping.html).  |

# NWG_PROCESSSELECTION
Defines the information presented in **New Feature** window of Feature Editor. This window presents a hierarchical list of processes (feature and placement configurations) available to the user. The structure of this table is based on G3E_PLACEMENTSELECTION, which is used by HxGN NetWorks Core Designer. NWG_PROCESSSELECTION will be used by other clients to avoid interference with G3E_PLACEMENTSELECTION.
_Hint_
To populate this table with the same content as G3E_PLACEMENTSELECTION, run script `\GTDWS\FeatureEditor\utils\PopulateNWG_PROCESSSELECTION.sql` located under HxGN NetWorks Web Services installation folder.  
| Column  | Description  | Type  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| NWG_PSROWNO  | Primary key for this table  | NUMBER(9)  |  
| NWG_PROCESSNAME  | Unique name of this process. Only applicable to rows which have G3E_PCNO or G3E_FNO populated. This value is stored together with data to identify the source process if the same G3E_PCNO or G3E_FNO is referenced multiple times.  | VARCHAR2(80)  |  
| NWG_TYPE  | Type of the process. Allowed values are: Create, Edit, Delete, Replace. When set to Edit, Delete or Replace, G3E_PCNO must be NULL and G3E_FNO identifiers the type of feature.  
  
**Not used.**  | VARCHAR2(50)  |  
| NWG_DIALOGTYPE  | Type of the dialog to present to the user. The value is a filter for G3E_DIALOG.G3E_TYPE.  
  
If not specified, value Placement is used for processes of type Create where G3E_FNO is specifed, Edit for Edit. If G3E_PCNO is specified, the dialog type defaults to G3E_PLACEMENTCONFIGURATION_OPTABLE.G3E_CONFIGURATIONNAME (any row with given G3E_PCNO).  
  
**Not used.**  | VARCHAR2(80)  |  
| NWG_REPEATING  | When set to 1, the process should be repeated until user break. Default is 0, non-repeating.  
  
**Not used.**  | NUMBER(1)  |  
| NWG_PCNO  | Placement configuration associated with this item in the tree. Only applicable if this item is a placement configuration. If this value is populated, G3E_FNO is Null.  | NUMBER(9)  |  
| NWG_FNO  | Feature associated with this item in the tree. Only applicable if this item is a feature. If this value is populated, G3E_PCNO is Null.  | NUMBER(5)  |  
| NWG_USERNAME  | Text displayed in the Process selection tree view. This field is localized.  | VARCHAR2(80)  |  
| NWG_DESCRIPTION  | Long description of the process. This field is localized.  | VARCHAR2(1000)  |  
| NWG_LEVEL  | Level of item in the tree. One is a root or top level.  | NUMBER(9)  |  
| NWG_ORDINAL  | Order of item in tree construction.  | NUMBER(9)  |  
| NWG_LOCALECOMMENT  | String describing the fields within the table that are to be localized and how they are to be used within the application. For information only.  | VARCHAR(240)  |  
| NWG_ICON  | Reference to an icon resource. The value is a symbolic reference, resolved at the client to a physical resource.  | VARCHAR2(240)  |  
| NWG_ROLE  | Name of the database role the user must have to enable the object control. If the user has the role, the specific feature is displayed on the New Feature control.  | VARCHAR2(128)  |  
| NWG_APPLICATION  | Application in which this configuration should be displayed. Bitmask. 8=NetWorks Portal, 16=Core Mobile  | NUMBER(9)  |  
| NWG_EDITDATE  | Date the record was created or last edited.  | DATE  |  
## NWP_APPLICATION filtering logic[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Reference/Metadata-tables/NWG_PROCESSSELECTION.html#nwp_application-filtering-logic)
  * Filtering by NWP_APPLICATION applies at any level.
  * Filter on a folder (non-leaf) node, if it does not match, causes the whole subtree to be invisible. If matches, filtering on child nodes applies recursively.
  * Filter on a leaf node affects only the leaf node.

### Example 1[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Reference/Metadata-tables/NWG_PROCESSSELECTION.html#example-1)

```
Electric (NULL)
   General (NULL)
       Inventory (NULL)
          Ele-Station (8)
          Ele-Station M (16)

```

Electric, General and Inventory nodes will be visible on all clients. Ele-Station only in Portal, Ele-Station M only in Core Mobile.
### Example 2[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Reference/Metadata-tables/NWG_PROCESSSELECTION.html#example-2)

```
Electric (8)
   General (NULL)
       Inventory (NULL)
          Ele-Station (NULL)

```

Electric and all its children will be visible only in Portal.
### Example 3[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Reference/Metadata-tables/NWG_PROCESSSELECTION.html#example-3)

```
Electric (NULL)
   General (NULL)
       Inventory (8)
          Ele-Station (NULL)
       Inventory M (16)
          Ele-Station M (NULL)

```

Electric and General will be visible in all clients. Inventory and Ele-Station will be visible only in Portal. Inventory M and Ele-Station M will be visible only in Core Mobile.
### Example 4[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Reference/Metadata-tables/NWG_PROCESSSELECTION.html#example-4)

```
Electric (24)
   General (24)
       Inventory (8)
          Ele-Station (8)
       Inventory M (16)
          Ele-Station M (16)

```

Electric and General will be visible in all clients. Inventory and Ele-Station will be visible only in Portal. Inventory M and Ele-Station M will be visible only in Core Mobile.

##### PL-SQL-Packages

# NWG_CONTEXT
## Description[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Reference/PL-SQL-Packages/NWG_CONTEXT.html#description)
Package `NWG_CONTEXT` handles setting and retrieval of properties from/to Oracle context `NWG_CONTEXT_CTX`. The package is used by Dialog Web Services to set the properties for the session and retrieve the properties when updating feature attributes.

#### Security

# Password Vault Service support
NetWorks services support [Password Vault Service](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Password-Vault-Service.html) for storage and retrieval of credentials as an alternative to passing `gtechnologyDBConnect` in the OpenID Connect access token claims.
## Owin-based services[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Security/Password-Vault-Service-support.html#owin-based-services)
This workflow applies to: **WMS, WFS, WMTS, Analytical, Dialog Web Service, Job Service, Feature Model Service, Vector Tile Service**.
  * In **web.config** file of the deployed service, configure the URL of the PasswordVaultService by setting the key `PasswordVaultUrl` in the infrastructureServiceAuthentication section.

```
  <infrastructureServiceAuthentication mode="Bearer">
    <parameters>
      <add key="OpenIdConfigFile" value="~/OpenIdConfig.json" />
      <add key="RequiredClaims" value="gtechnologyDBConnect" />
      <add key="EnableCaching" value="True" />
      <add key="PasswordVaultUrl" value="https://server/PasswordVault" />
    </parameters>
  </infrastructureServiceAuthentication>

```

## ASP.NET Core based services[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Security/Password-Vault-Service-support.html#aspnet-core-based-services)
This workflow applies to: **Vector Service, Data Transfer Service, Dynamic WMS Service, Work Service, Feature Data Service, Feature Transaction Service**.
  * Find the **ServiceConfig.ini** of the service, typically under _C:\ProgramData\Intergraph\NetWorks\ServiceInstances{InstanceName}_
Configure PasswordVault URL by adding parameter `infrastructureServiceAuthentication:Parameters:PasswordVaultUrl` to the file:
Example:

```
infrastructureServiceAuthentication:Parameters:PasswordVaultUrl=https://server/PasswordVault?configuration=PROD

```

## Password Vault Service URL[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Security/Password-Vault-Service-support.html#password-vault-service-url)
The configured Password Vault Service URL should contain all necessary query parameters which are necessary for correct resolution of credentials in the context of this service. When processing tokens with `gtechnologyDBConnect` claims, Password Vault Service expects query parameter `configuration` with current NetWorks configuration and (optional) parameter `application` with the application name as configured in the `gtechnologyDBConnect` claim (e.g. `NetWorks-Portal`).
**Example**
The Password vault service can resolve credentials for multiple NetWorks configurations and application types. The currently configured service uses configuration `PRODUCTION` and the application type is `NetWorks`.
`https://server/PasswordVault?configuration=PRODUCTION&application=NetWorks`

# Support for Azure AD with claims mapping
When using Azure AD with claims mapping functionality, login attempts in Portal and service requests fail on `IDX10501: Signature validation failed. Unable to match key`. This is due to the fact that tokens issued with claims mapping are signed with a different key. Azure AD exposes a standard OIDC metadata at the default OIDC metadata endpoint `{issuer}/.well-known/openid-configuration` and a customized set of OIDC metadata at endpoint `{issuer}/.well-known/openid-configuration?appid={appid}`, where `{appid}` is the application identifier provided by the Azure AD.
To enable usage of Azure AD with claims mapping, add the parameter `appid` with its value (a GUID) to the Extra Parameters using the **All Applications Wizard**. The `ExtraParams` section must be configured in `OpenIdConfig.json`
## Examples[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Security/Support-for-Azure-AD-with-claims-mapping.html#examples)
### Portal OpenIdConfig.json[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Security/Support-for-Azure-AD-with-claims-mapping.html#portal-openidconfigjson)

```
{
  "Issuer": "https://sts.windows.net/11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555/v2.0/",
  "ClientId": "00000000-aaaa-bbbb-cccc-dddddddddddd",
  "ClientSecret": "xyz....",
  "RedirectUri": "https://myserver/Portal",
  "Scope": "openid",
  "ResponseType": "code",
  "ExtraParams": {
    "appid": "00000000-aaaa-bbbb-cccc-dddddddddddd"
  },
  "RequireHttps": false
}

```

### Service OpenIdConfig.json[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Security/Support-for-Azure-AD-with-claims-mapping.html#service-openidconfigjson)

```
{
  "Issuer": "https://sts.windows.net/11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555/v2.0/",
  "ExtraParams": {
    "appid": "00000000-aaaa-bbbb-cccc-dddddddddddd"
  }
}

```

## See also[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Security/Support-for-Azure-AD-with-claims-mapping.html#see-also)
  * <https://blogs.aaddevsup.xyz/2019/05/understanding-azure-ad-token-signing-certificate-kid/>

  * [Authorize access to web applications using OpenID Connect and Azure Active Directory](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/active-directory/azuread-dev/v1-protocols-openid-connect-code)

#### Services

##### Analytical-Service

# Report mapping for cost-constrained traces
##### Important
This configuration is now obsolete. For configuration of OTDR traces, see documentation for metadata table **GAONET_PARAMETER**.
* * *
Cost-constrained (formerly OTDR) traces require selection of NetWorks report to produce outputs, typically a list of marker points.
Each trace definition can have a marker placement interface assigned either indirectly (as G3E_RPNO value) or directly (as G3E_RINO and G3E_RIARGNO for marker and geo point computation).
The mapping can be configured in `appSettings` section of the **web.config** of a deployed Analytical Service instance:

```
<appSettings>
    <!-- Template for Cost-Constained (OTDR) trace report OR interfaces mapping -->
    <!-- For each G3E_TRACEID either Report or ComputeMarkersInterfaces mapping is needed -->
    <!--
    <add key="Trace.{G3E_TRACEID}.Report" value="{G3E_RPNO}" />
    <add key="Trace.{G3E_TRACEID}.ComputeMarkersInterfaces" value="{ComputeMarkerLocationRINO},{ComputeMarkerLocationRIARGNO},{GeoPointRINO},{GeoPointRIARGNO}" />
    -->
</appSettings>

```

**Example - indirect mapping by G3E_RPNO**

```
<appSettings>
    <add key="Trace.305.Report" value="300" />
    <add key="Trace.505.Report" value="500" />
</appSettings>

```

**Example - direct mapping by G3E_RINO and G3E_RIARGGNO**

```
<appSettings>
    <add key="Trace.305.ComputeMarkersInterfaces" value="1058,3001058,1059,3002200" />
    <add key="Trace.505.ComputeMarkersInterfaces" value="1058,5001058,1059,5002200" />
</appSettings>

```

##### Coordinate-Systems-Service

###### Deployment

# Command line deployment
The Coordinate System Service can be semi-automatically deployed and undeployed from the command line using the [DeployCoordinateSystemService.exe](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Coordinate-Systems-Service/Deployment/DeployCoordinateSystemService.exe.html) tool.
There is a single version of Coordinate System Service deployed automatically when running the NetWorks Configuration Wizard. Typically, there is no need to deploy additional instances.
**Workflow - deployment**
  1. Start a command prompt (`cmd.exe`) as _Administrator_
  2. Navigate to NetWorks Program folder e.g. `cd c:\Program Files (x86)\Intergraph\NetWorks\Program\`
  3. Deploy the service instance by executing `DeployCoordinateSystemService.exe`

**Workflow - undeployment**
  1. Start a command prompt (`cmd.exe`) as _Administrator_
  2. Navigate to NetWorks Program folder e.g. `cd c:\Program Files (x86)\Intergraph\NetWorks\Program\`
  3. Undeploy the service instance by executing `DeployCoordinateSystemService.exe -u`

**Workflow - redeployment**
  1. Start a command prompt (`cmd.exe`) as _Administrator_
  2. Navigate to NetWorks Program folder e.g. `cd c:\Program Files (x86)\Intergraph\NetWorks\Program\`
  3. Redeploy the service instance by executing `DeployCoordinateSystemService.exe -r`

# DeployCoordinateSystemService.exe
## Purpose[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Coordinate-Systems-Service/Deployment/DeployCoordinateSystemService.exe.html#purpose)
Command line tool which enables redeployment of NetWorks Coordinate System Service.
## Usage[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Coordinate-Systems-Service/Deployment/DeployCoordinateSystemService.exe.html#usage)

```
DeployCoordinateSystemService.exe [-i <instance-name>] [-u | --undeploy] 
    [-r | --redeploy] [--package-path <package path>]

```

### Options[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Coordinate-Systems-Service/Deployment/DeployCoordinateSystemService.exe.html#options)
  * **`-i <instance-name>`**  
When not specified, defaults to`NetWorksCoordinateSystemService`.
  * **`-u|--undeploy`**  
Undeploy the service.
  * **`-r|--redeploy`**  
Redeploy the service (undeploy followed by deploy).
  * **`--package-path <package path>`**  
Alternative location of the Service Templates folder.

## Return value[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Coordinate-Systems-Service/Deployment/DeployCoordinateSystemService.exe.html#return-value)  
| Value  | Meaning  |  
| --- | --- |  
| 0  | Success  |  
| 1  | Invalid parameters  |  
| 2  | Error during deployment  |  
## Configuration[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Coordinate-Systems-Service/Deployment/DeployCoordinateSystemService.exe.html#configuration)
You can edit the parameters of the default deployed Coordinate System Service in the file `DeployCoordinateSystemService.exe.config`.
## Logging[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Coordinate-Systems-Service/Deployment/DeployCoordinateSystemService.exe.html#logging)
Logging is configured in the file `DeployCoordinateSystemService.exe.NLog.config`. By default, the tool logs at Trace level to Console, at Error level to NetWorks logs folder.

# Deployment
The default instance of Coordinate System Service is automatically deployed when running NetWorks Configuration Wizard.
It creates IIS application pool `NetWorksCoordinateSystemServicePool` and application `NetWorksCoordinateSystemService`. Other NetWorks services on the machine are preconfigured to use this instance.
  * [Command line deployment](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Coordinate-Systems-Service/Deployment/Command-line-deployment.html)

# Coordinate Systems Service
## Overview[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Coordinate-Systems-Service.html#overview)
The Coordinate Systems Service is a web service which provides coordinate systems information and coordinate transformation functionality for other Networks services.
[![CoordinateSystemsService_Architecture_v1.png](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/.attachments/CoordinateSystemsService_Architecture_v1-60d95335-f5ce-4d40-9213-25e0030bbfd7.png)](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/.attachments/CoordinateSystemsService_Architecture_v1-60d95335-f5ce-4d40-9213-25e0030bbfd7.png)
## Details[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Coordinate-Systems-Service.html#details)
The service is based on a modern framework (ASP.NET Core) and is deployed into IIS. Key requirement is **performance** : low latency and high throughput. Default protocol is REST (JSON over HTTP).
It is expected that only a single instance of this service is deployed on a single server, typically by the NetWorks Configuration Wizard.
## Mode of operation[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Coordinate-Systems-Service.html#mode-of-operation)
  * After startup Service reads published metadata and caches in-memory all definitions of coordinate systems used by the configurations together with some predefined coordinates systems (e.g. EPSG:4326).
  * Runtime Service provides stateless API for the other services.

## Coordinate system information[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Coordinate-Systems-Service.html#coordinate-system-information)
Information on coordinate systems is read from published metadata. The coordinate system definitions in database can be overridden by CSF files in `\CSF` folder located in the Coordinate System Service deployment location.
Intergraph Common Coordinate System configuration is stored in `Program\Config` folder in the NetWorks installation folder location.
## API surface[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Coordinate-Systems-Service.html#api-surface)
  * Get list of configured CS
  * Convert projection coordinates to geographic (and reverse)
  * Convert geographic to projection coordinates (and reverse)
  * Convert geographic to database CS (and reverse)
  * Get details of configuration CS for given NetWorks configuration
  * Get details of database CS for given NetWorks configuration
  * Transform points from CS1 to CS2
  * Get CS unit of measure
  * Get CS units per meter
  * Get EPSG code of CS specified by NAME (from G3E_GCOORDSYSTEM_OPTABLE table)
  * Get EPSG code of CS (specified by values of G3E_GCOORDSYSTEM_OPTABLE structure)
  * Get EPSG code of CS by looking at CSF files in CSF folder
  * Validate CS and check if EPSG code exists (get CS moniker from G3E_GCOORDSYSTEM_OPTABLE structure, try to get EPSG code from moniker)
  * Check similarity (identity) of two CS definitions
  * Get Configuration CS
  * Get Database CS
  * Load CS from storage (G3E_GCOORDSYSTEM_OPTABLE)
  * Load CS by EPSG code
  * Load CS from CSF file

##### Data-Transfer-Service

# Authorization
DTS uses role-based authorization to restrict access to published packages. Authorization process relies on OpenID Connect. Each request is accompanied by a transparent JWT access token which contains user claims. Claims not present in the access token are retrieved from the OIDC _user info_ endpoint.
There are multiple options how to define the roles of the user requesting access.
## A. Direct role assignment[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Data-Transfer-Service/Authorization.html#a-direct-role-assignment)
Roles of the user are extracted from the OIDC **access token** from a claim specified in [Configuration](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Data-Transfer-Service/Configuration.html). The default is **role**.
## B. Direct role assignment with role mapping[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Data-Transfer-Service/Authorization.html#b-direct-role-assignment-with-role-mapping)
As A, but the OIDC roles are mapped to other set of roles defined in a configuration file (see [Configuration](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Data-Transfer-Service/Configuration.html), parameter `roleMapping:file`).
Example:
OIDC access tokens returns `Electric` and `Water` in **role** claim.
The DTS configuration has a role map in JSON file:

```
{
  "Electric": ["ELECTRICITY_R", "ELECTRICITY_RW"],
  "Water":    ["WATER_R", "WATER_RW"],
  "Heat":     ["HEATING_R", "HEATING_RW"]
}

```

This means the user can access all packages with access roles defined for `ELECTRICITY_R`, `ELECTRICITY_RW`, `WATER_R`, `WATER_RW`.
## C. gtechnologyDBConnect[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Data-Transfer-Service/Authorization.html#c-gtechnologydbconnect)
Standard mode used by NetWorks products. The user's claims contain a **gtechnologyDBConnect** claim, with connection strings to NetWorks databases (array of strings formatted as `user/password@configuration[:application]`).
The list of roles is determined by reading the list of user's roles from the Oracle database.

# CleanUp process
## Summary[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Data-Transfer-Service/CleanUp-process.html#summary)
DTS CleanUp process is a background process that serves as maintenance job for obsolete transactions and messages. It is an integral part of the service itself and it only runs when the service is running, i.e. restarting IIS or application pool doesn't automatically start the CleanUp process, unless it is deployed as [always running](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Administration-Console/Deploy-services-as-always-running.html). Arbitrary request to DTS is needed to start it. Each CleanUp cycle runs two separate tasks:
  * Clean up of obsolete transactions
  * Clean up of obsolete monitoring messages

## Configuration[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Data-Transfer-Service/CleanUp-process.html#configuration)
Details are provided on [Configuration](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Data-Transfer-Service/Configuration.html) page.
### Period[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Data-Transfer-Service/CleanUp-process.html#period)
The period is common for all tasks and is configured in `transactionStore:CleanUpOptions:MaintenancePeriodInMinutes` property.
### Clean up of obsolete transactions[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Data-Transfer-Service/CleanUp-process.html#clean-up-of-obsolete-transactions)
`transactionStore:CleanUpOptions:DaysToKeepOpenTransactions` and `transactionStore:CleanUpOptions:DaysToKeepCommitedTransactions` are used to configure the days to keep the transactions in store.
### Clean up of obsolete monitoring messages[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Data-Transfer-Service/CleanUp-process.html#clean-up-of-obsolete-monitoring-messages)
Set of paired `monitor:CleanUp:Rules:{ordinal}:Condition` and `monitor:CleanUp:Rules:{ordinal}:Action` properties are used to define clean up rules for monitoring messages.

# Configuration
## Common Parameters[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Data-Transfer-Service/Configuration.html#common-parameters)
  * [Authentication](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Configuration/Common-Service-Configuration-Parameters.html#authentication)
  * [Data Access](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Configuration/Common-Service-Configuration-Parameters.html#data-access)
  * [Oracle](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Configuration/Common-Service-Configuration-Parameters.html#oracle)
  * [Encoding](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Configuration/Common-Service-Configuration-Parameters.html#encoding)
  * [CORS](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Configuration/Common-Service-Configuration-Parameters.html#cors)

## Specific Parameters[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Data-Transfer-Service/Configuration.html#specific-parameters)
###  `infrastructureServiceAuthentication:ClientId`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Data-Transfer-Service/Configuration.html#infrastructureserviceauthenticationclientid)
OIDC Client Id for the client. Published in WebFinger response.
###  `infrastructureServiceAuthentication:WebAuthenticatorUri`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Data-Transfer-Service/Configuration.html#infrastructureserviceauthenticationwebauthenticatoruri)
URI of the Web Authenticator service used by clients as a proxy to actual OIDC provider login. The value is published in WebFinger response as link with `rel`=`web_authenticator`.
###  `packageStore:root`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Data-Transfer-Service/Configuration.html#packagestoreroot)
Root folder of the physical package storage. Environment variable references via `%VAR%` are allowed. **Required**.
###  `roleMapping:roleClaim`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Data-Transfer-Service/Configuration.html#rolemappingroleclaim)
Name of claim to be used as user's role. Default: `role`.
###  `roleMapping:file`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Data-Transfer-Service/Configuration.html#rolemappingfile)
Path to role mapping file. Environment variable references via `%VAR%` are allowed.
###  `transactionStore:open`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Data-Transfer-Service/Configuration.html#transactionstoreopen)
Root folder of physical storage for open transactions. The path should be on a local (fast) drive. Environment variable references via `%VAR%` are allowed. **Required**.
###  `transactionStore:committed`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Data-Transfer-Service/Configuration.html#transactionstorecommitted)
Root folder of physical storage for committed transactions. The path should be on a local (fast) drive. Environment variable references via `%VAR%` are allowed. **Required**.
###  `transactionStore:CleanUpOptions:MaintenancePeriodInMinutes`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Data-Transfer-Service/Configuration.html#transactionstorecleanupoptionsmaintenanceperiodinminutes)
Period in minutes to run CleanUp job, which removes obsolete transactions. When not defined or 0, transactions are kept undefinitelly. See also [CleanUp process](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Data-Transfer-Service/CleanUp-process.html).
###  `transactionStore:CleanUpOptions:DaysToKeepOpenTransactions`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Data-Transfer-Service/Configuration.html#transactionstorecleanupoptionsdaystokeepopentransactions)
Number of days to keep unfinished open transactions. Default: `30`.
###  `transactionStore:CleanUpOptions:DaysToKeepCommitedTransactions`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Data-Transfer-Service/Configuration.html#transactionstorecleanupoptionsdaystokeepcommitedtransactions)
Number of days to keep committed transactions. Default: `90`.
###  `discovery:links:{ordinal}:rel`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Data-Transfer-Service/Configuration.html#discoverylinksordinalrel)
Type of link discoverable from WebFinger endpoint. Used to publish link to License Service (rel = `licensing`). Replace `{ordinal}` with 0-based ordinal of link when configured in INI file.
###  `discovery:links:{ordinal}:href`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Data-Transfer-Service/Configuration.html#discoverylinksordinalhref)
Link discoverable from WebFinger endpoint. Used to publish link to License Service (rel = `licensing`). Replace `{ordinal}` with 0-based ordinal of link when configured in INI file.
###  `postProcessing:WorkServiceUri`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Data-Transfer-Service/Configuration.html#postprocessingworkserviceuri)
URI to deployed Work Service, where configured workload is executed as post process.
###  `postProcessing:Rules:{ordinal}:Filter`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Data-Transfer-Service/Configuration.html#postprocessingrulesordinalfilter)
SQL-like filter condition to match property values in the root element of the commit message. The condition may contain operators `=`, `<>`, `>`, `<`, `>=`, `<=`, `()`, `AND`, `OR`, `NOT`, `IS NULL`, string (enclosed in apostrophes) and numeric literals. JSON boolean literals are mapped to string constants `'true'` and `'false'`. Property names are matched in case-insensitive mode. To match property `"field"` in JSON with string value `ABC` set Filter to `field = 'ABC'`. Replace `{ordinal}` with 0-based ordinal of link when configured in INI file.
###  `postProcessing:Rules:{ordinal}:Property`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Data-Transfer-Service/Configuration.html#postprocessingrulesordinalproperty)
Applies together with Value only when Filter is not specified. Property name in commit message to check. Replace `{ordinal}` with 0-based ordinal of link when configured in INI file.
###  `postProcessing:Rules:{ordinal}:Value`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Data-Transfer-Service/Configuration.html#postprocessingrulesordinalvalue)
Applies together with Property only when Filter is not specified. Value that must this property have to trigger postprocessing. Replace `{ordinal}` with 0-based ordinal of link when configured in INI file.
###  `postProcessing:Rules:{ordinal}:Workload`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Data-Transfer-Service/Configuration.html#postprocessingrulesordinalworkload)
Workload to execute, when the _property_ and _value_ matches. Replace `{ordinal}` with 0-based ordinal of link when configured in INI file.
###  `postProcessing:Rules:{ordinal}:Stop`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Data-Transfer-Service/Configuration.html#postprocessingrulesordinalstop)
Boolean flag. When `true`, processing of rules stops if this rule evaluates to true. Default is `false`, i.e. processing continues on next rule after a match.
###  `postProcessing:Rules:{ordinal}:Ordinal`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Data-Transfer-Service/Configuration.html#postprocessingrulesordinalordinal)
Ordinal of the rule. If not specified, rules are evaluated in the order as specified in the configuration file.
###  `postProcessing:Rules:{ordinal}:Track`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Data-Transfer-Service/Configuration.html#postprocessingrulesordinaltrack)
Boolean flag. When `true`, the message is tracked in database via the [Monitoring](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/NetWorks-internal/Design-Documents/Managed-Redlines/Server-Processing/Monitoring.md) subsystem.
## Workset Monitor[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Data-Transfer-Service/Configuration.html#workset-monitor)
It is possible to configure [parameters for Workset Monitor](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Reference/Metadata-tables/NWG_GENERALPARAMETER.html) directly in the service configuration. If specified, parameters in the service configuration override parameters in metadata.
## Example[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Data-Transfer-Service/Configuration.html#example)
ServiceConfig.ini

```
Origins=*
Methods=*
IsCorsEnabled=True
packageStore:root=C:\DTS\packages
transactionStore:open=C:\DTS\open
transactionStore:committed=C:\DTS\committed
TNS_ADMIN=C:\app\tns\
ConnectionInfo=3sycet3LD5KF+4i6ge6EFxTXzIu9kSDSIZknst2OgHu15lliPvZPrgcfq8atvOd3

discovery:links:0:rel=test
discovery:links:0:href=http://test1.com

infrastructureServiceAuthentication:Mode=Anonymous
infrastructureServiceAuthentication:Parameters:RequiredClaims=gtechnologyDBConnect
infrastructureServiceAuthentication:Parameters:EnableCaching=true
infrastructureServiceAuthentication:Parameters:CacheTimeoutMinutes=60

postProcessing:WorkServiceUri=http://localhost:9400
postProcessing:Rules:0:Property=trigger
postProcessing:Rules:0:Value=export
postProcessing:Rules:0:Workload=ExportData
postProcessing:Rules:0:Stop=true

postProcessing:Rules:1:Filter= "trigger = 'features' AND run='true'"
postProcessing:Rules:1:Workload=features
postProcessing:Rules:1:Track=true

```

Postprocessing rule 0 matches JSON document:

```
{
    "trigger": "export",
}

```

Postprocessing rule 1 matches JSON document:

```
{
    "trigger": "features",
    "run": "true"
}

```

or

```
{
    "trigger": "features",
    "run": true
}

```

## OpenIdConfig.json[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Data-Transfer-Service/Configuration.html#openidconfigjson)
OpenID Connect configuration.

```
{
  "Issuer": "http://localhost:8080/auth/realms/NetWorks",
  "Audience": "",
  "RequireHttps": false,
  "ValidateIssuer": true,
  "ValidateAudience": false,
  "ValidateLifetime": false,
  "ClockSkewMinutes": 5
}

```
  
| Setting  | Description  | Mandatory  | Default  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| Issuer  | URL of the OIDC Identity Provider  | Y  |   |  
| Audience  | Expected audience.  |   |   |  
| RequireHttps  | When false, HTTPS is not required for communication with OIDC  |   | true  |  
| ValidateIssuer  | When `true`, Issuer in token is validated against the configured value  |   | false  |  
| ValidateAudience  | When `true`, Audience in token is validated against the configured value  |   | false  |  
| ValidateLifetime  | When `true`, token expiration is validated  |   | false  |  
| ClockSkewMinutes  | Difference in minutes when allowed when validating token expiration  |   | 0  |

###### Deployment

# Manual deployment
## Workflow[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Data-Transfer-Service/Deployment/Manual-deployment.html#workflow)
  1. Create folder on the disk for the service instance. This will be referred to as `SERVICEDIR` in following text.
  2. Unzip the contents of the service template folder containing `Hxgn.NetWorks.DataTransferService.WebHost.exe` to `SERVICEDIR`.
  3. [Configure the service](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Data-Transfer-Service/Configuration.html).
  4. Open IIS Manager
  5. Create app. pool in IIS Manager with the following properties: 
     * Name: `DataTransferServicePool`)
     * .NET CLR Version: _No Managed Code_
     * Managed Pipeline Mode: _Integrated_
     * Identity: Use account which has access to the physical storage folders
  6. Create application under `Default Web Site` (or other site) 
     * Alias: `DataTransferService`)
     * Application Pool: Use pool created above
     * Physical path: Use actual `SERVICEDIR` value
  7. The API is available at `http://{server}/{appName}` (e.g. `http://server1/DataTransferService`).

## Related topics[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Data-Transfer-Service/Deployment/Manual-deployment.html#related-topics)
  * [Software requirements](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Data-Transfer-Service/Deployment/Software-requirements.html)

# Software requirements
  * Windows Server 2016 or newer
  * IIS
  * [.NET Core Runtime 8.0](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download)
##### Important
Install the **Hosting bundle** , not just .NET Core runtime for Desktop applications.
  * NetWorks configuration: 
    * Registry key: `KEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\Intergraph\GFramme\02.00\Path`
    * String value `FileUNCPath` under the key points to folder, which contains `FileUNCPaths.xml` file
    * On the disk: `FileUNCPaths.xml` which points to a valid location of `ConnectionConfigurationMap.ccm` file

# Package storage
Exported packages are stored in a physical disk location accessible to the DTS (local disk or share).
## Structure[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Data-Transfer-Service/Package-storage.html#structure)

```
<package 1 version 1>/
    package.json
    .ready
    files/
        <content files>

<package 1 version 2>/
    package.json
    .ready
    files/
        <content files>

<package 2 version 1>/
    package.json
    .ready
    files/
        <content files>
...

```

Package folders can be also hierarchical. DTS checks for all folders in the subtree. Each folder with **package.json** and **.ready** is considered a package folder.
### Example - flat[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Data-Transfer-Service/Package-storage.html#example---flat)

```
ELECTRIC_LV_ALL_20200801085500/
    package.json
    package.cs.json
    package.de.json
    files/
        ABCD.vec
        Attributes.sqlite

ELECTRIC_LV_ALL_20200911085500/ 
    package.json
    package.cs.json
    package.de.json
    .ready
    files/
        ABCD.vec
        Attributes.sqlite
...

WATER_ALL_20200911085500/ 
    package.json
    package.cs.json
    package.de.json
    .ready
    files/
        WATER_50501.vec
        WATER_50502.vec
        WATER_50601.vec
        Attributes.sqlite
...

```

### Example - hierarchical[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Data-Transfer-Service/Package-storage.html#example---hierarchical)

```
ELECTRIC_LV_ALL/
    20200801085500/
        package.json
        package.cs.json
        package.de.json
        files/
            ABCD.vec
            Attributes.sqlite

    20200911085500/ 
        package.json
        package.cs.json
        package.de.json
        .ready
        files/
            ABCD.vec
            Attributes.sqlite

WATER_ALL/
    20200911085500/ 
        package.json
        package.cs.json
        package.de.json
        .ready
        files/
            WATER_50501.vec
            WATER_50502.vec
            WATER_50601.vec
            Attributes.sqlite
...

```

## package.json[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Data-Transfer-Service/Package-storage.html#packagejson)
**package.json** is the manifest file for a published package. A package is a named set of exported data (vector data, attribute data, legend definitions).
Each package has these attributes:  
| Name  | Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
| id  | Unique alpha-numeric name of the package version (e.g. `ELECTRIC_LV_20200801085500`), typically created from `package` and timestamp of export formatted as `yyyyMMddHHmmss`. The `id` must be limited to values valid for regular expression `^[0-9a-zA-Z_]+$`. The `id` value should be sortable - higher values  |  
| package  | Identifier of the export package. Used to track different versions of the same export package.  |  
| type  | Type of the package. Values are recognized by the client applications (e.g. `nwcmsubset`, `redlinewftemplate`, `redline`)  |  
| timestamp  | Date and time of when the package was published, formatted as `yyyyMMddHHmmss`.  |  
| description  | User name of the package. Can be localized to multiple languages via `package.{language}.json`.  |  
| roles  | List of roles which can access this package.  |  
| version  | Version of the package defined by the application. The value is not used by the service (has no impact on processing).  |  
### Example[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Data-Transfer-Service/Package-storage.html#example)
package.json

```
{
  "id": "ELECTRIC_LV_ALL_20200801T085500",
  "package": "ELECTRIC_LV_ALL",
  "type": "nwcmsubset",
  "timestamp": "20200801085500",
  "description": "Electricity Low Voltage - All regions",
  "roles": [
    "ELECTRICITY_R"
  ],
  "version": "1.0"
}

```

package.cs.json

```
{
  "description": "Elektřina - Nízké napětí - Všechny regiony",
}

```

## .ready[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Data-Transfer-Service/Package-storage.html#ready)
An empty file named **.ready** is placed into each folder with a prepared export once the export is complete and ready to be downloaded by clients. Package folders without the **.ready** are not processed by the MDS.
The purpose of the **.ready** file is to:
  * Notify DTS that a package is completely exported, to avoid interference during export
  * Signalize that a package is already obsolete, but still present on disk - when the file is deleted.

# Triggering Post Processing
## Overview[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Data-Transfer-Service/Triggering-Post-Processing.html#overview)
Data Transfer Service can be configured to trigger desired workload on [Work Service](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service.html) upon committing the transaction. This is then triggered by setting defined property to desired value in commit request body and work data are returned to the user (workload and wid) to be able to query the result. Multiple workloads can be triggered by single commit.
## Configuration[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Data-Transfer-Service/Triggering-Post-Processing.html#configuration)
In Data Transfer Service [Configuration](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Data-Transfer-Service/Configuration.html), **postProcessing** section is used to configure:
  * WorkServiceUri - URI to deployed Work Service, where configured workload is executed
  * Rules - set of rules to apply, consisting of: 
    * Property - property in commit message to check
    * Value - value that must this property have
    * Workload - workload to execute

WorkServiceUri can be configured in Administration Console. Individual rules must be configured manually.
### Example:[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Data-Transfer-Service/Triggering-Post-Processing.html#example)

```
"postProcessing": {
    "WorkServiceUri": "http://localhost:5000",
    "Rules": [
        {
            "Property": "trigger",
            "Value": "export",
            "Workload": "ExportData"
        },
        {
            "Property": "trigger",
            "Value": "backup",
            "Workload": "backup"
        },
        {
            "Property": "notify",
            "Value": "yes",
            "Workload": "notify"
        }
    ]
}

```

## Workflow[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Data-Transfer-Service/Triggering-Post-Processing.html#workflow)
Upon commit, all rules are checked, and all that matches are executed.
### Example:[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Data-Transfer-Service/Triggering-Post-Processing.html#example-1)
POST `http://localhost:5010/transaction/1jswknrkyllhul44le4fagz3qg9419nl`

```
{
    "package" : "pkg1",
    "type" : "type",
    "trigger" : "export",
    "notify" : "no"
}

```

From configuration example, first rule will match and **ExportData** workflow will be executed. Transaction ID (**tid** = 1jswknrkyllhul44le4fagz3qg9419nl) will be passed to Work Service to identify the transaction.
### Response:[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Data-Transfer-Service/Triggering-Post-Processing.html#response)

```
{
    "success": true,
    "tid": "1jswknrkyllhul44le4fagz3qg9419nl",
    "postProcess": [
        {
            "workload": "ExportData",
            "wid": "0mgr71rj4hop96rao24pzeba3e44rfzf"
        }
    ]
}

```

Response contains information about all triggered post processes. Each consists of both **workload** executed and **wid** (work ID) of the work. This allows the user to query Work Service for result.
## Authorization[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Data-Transfer-Service/Triggering-Post-Processing.html#authorization)
When authorization is required, authorization header from request to Data Transfer Service is passed to subsequent Work Service reques.

# Upload
Data Transfer Service provides API for uploading of arbitrary files from the clients to server. The processing is based on transactions, which involve upload of multiple files and an atomic commit or rollback transaction.
No restrictions are placed on the number or types, names or content of files uploaded or the directory structure created when uploading. Data Transfer Service does not perform any postprocessing and relies on other services to process the uploaded files.
## Workflow[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Data-Transfer-Service/Upload.html#workflow)
When a clients wants to upload one or more files to the server, the workflow is:
  * Call [BeginTransaction](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Data-Transfer-Service/BeginTransaction.html) to open a transaction and retrieve transaction identifier (`tid`).
  * Call [UploadFile](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Data-Transfer-Service/UploadFile.html) for each file it wants to upload.
  * Call [CommitTransaction](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Data-Transfer-Service/CommitTransaction.html) to complete the transaction.

Alternatively, the client may call [RollbackTransaction](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Data-Transfer-Service/RollbackTransaction.html) to abandon a previously opened transaction.
## Configuration[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Data-Transfer-Service/Upload.html#configuration)
See [Configuration](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Data-Transfer-Service/Configuration.html), parameters `transactionStore.open` and `transactionStore.committed`.
## Physical storage[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Data-Transfer-Service/Upload.html#physical-storage)
The transactional system uses two physical locations for open transactions and completed transactions. The **open** transactions storage contains transactions which are currently active and were not committed or rolled back yet. The **committed** transactions storage contains transactions where were committed.
The directory structure is based on the `tid`.
  * First level is determined from characters 1 and 2 of the `tid`.
  * Second level is determined from characters 3 and 4 of the `tid`.
  * Third level is the `tid` and the folder contains file `package.json` with metadata about the transaction and folder named **files** , which contains all files uploaded to the transaction.

**Example**
`tid` is `ns0im266d799odjv8vg5woy91fmbej12`
Client uploads files `data.xml` and `scan.pdf` to the root (`path` is empty) and file `screenshot1.jpg` to folder `screenshots`. Uploaded files are stored in the `files` folder.

```
<open>/
    ns/
        0i/
            ns0im266d799odjv8vg5woy91fmbej12/
                package.json
                files/
                    data.xml
                    scan.pdf
                    screenshots/
                        screenshot1.jpg

```

Once the transaction is committed, the same structure is moved to the committed transaction storage and removed from open transaction storage.
## Transaction log[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Data-Transfer-Service/Upload.html#transaction-log)
To keep track of transactions which were completed, a special folder named `transactionlog` is created in the committed storage root. Files with name pattern `yyyy-MM-dd.log` are created in this folder (one for each day). Each file contains list of `tids` and timestamp of their commit. This file is intended for usage by processing software which consumes the uploaded transactions to determine which transactions were added.
### Example[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Data-Transfer-Service/Upload.html#example)

```
<committed>/
    transactionlog/
        2020-10-29.log
        2020-10-30.log
        2020-10-31.log

```

Contents of the log file:

```
d0emizdsgzt14wmav2rtrw6s7qku07oo 2020-10-29T15:46:00.565
ns0im266d799odjv8vg5woy91fmbej12 2020-10-29T15:46:34.059

```

# Data Transfer Service
The Data Transfer Service (DTS) is a web service which provides REST API for file download and upload for NetWorks Portal, HxGN NetWorks Core Mobile app and other applications.
## Architecture[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Data-Transfer-Service.html#architecture)
### Transactional file transfer[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Data-Transfer-Service.html#transactional-file-transfer)
Transactional part of the REST API allows transactional upload of files from the client to server. This workflow is used in: upload files from Portal in the Attach Vector files workflow, upload of redlines files from NetWorks Portal and HxGN Core Mobile app. Uploaded files are stored on the server in folder structure (see [Upload - physical storage](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Data-Transfer-Service/Upload.html)). Data Transfer Service can be configured to automatically trigger post processing of uploaded data in [Work Service](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service.html). See [Triggering Post Processing](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Data-Transfer-Service/Triggering-Post-Processing.html).
[![WorkService_Architecture_AttachCAD_v03.svg](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/.attachments/WorkService_Architecture_AttachCAD_v03-63cdd89f-7790-4a5b-86ab-9bc9400653cf.svg)](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/.attachments/WorkService_Architecture_AttachCAD_v03-63cdd89f-7790-4a5b-86ab-9bc9400653cf.svg)
### Package distribution[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Data-Transfer-Service.html#package-distribution)
The Data Transfer Service is accessible on the Intranet or over the Internet. It provides access to the published data packages over the REST API. This functionality is in use by HxGN NetWorks Core Mobile.
[![DataTransferService_Architecture_v04.svg](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/.attachments/DataTransferService_Architecture_v04-53104268-0aad-4170-98a2-93b1a76d0c82.svg)](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/.attachments/DataTransferService_Architecture_v04-53104268-0aad-4170-98a2-93b1a76d0c82.svg)
### API surface[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Data-Transfer-Service.html#api-surface)
  * Get list of published data packages
  * Get details of a published data package
  * Download data package files
  * Upload one or more files in a transaction

###### Deployment

# Command line deployment
The Deltas Service can be semi-automatically deployed and undeployed from the command line using [DeployDeltasService.exe](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Deltas-Service/Deployment/DeployDeltasService.exe.html) tool.
## Workflow - deployment[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Deltas-Service/Deployment/Command-line-deployment.html#workflow---deployment)
  1. Create or edit service instance in **NetWorksDeployedServices.xml**.

NetWorks keeps track of service instances in XML file `c:\ProgramData\Intergraph\NetWorks\DeployedServices\NetWorksDeployedServices.xml`.
To register a new instance of the Deltas Service, open the file in a text editor (e.g. Notepad) and add new element under the `<NetWorksDeployedServices>` element, e.g.:

```
<DeltasService InstanceName="DeltasServiceINSTANCE1" 
               IsInSolution="False" 
               InstanceId="DeltasServiceINSTANCE1"
               Definition="Deltas Service" 
                />

```

### Additional parameters[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Deltas-Service/Deployment/Command-line-deployment.html#additional-parameters)  
| Name  | Description  | Mandatory  | Default Value  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| InstanceName  | Unique name of the service instance.  | Y  |   |  
| IsInSolution  | Flag. Must be set to `False`  | Y  |   |  
| InstanceId  | GUID of the instance  | Y  |   |  
| Definition  | Service definition  | Y  | Deltas Service  |  
| ConnectionInfo  | NetWorks connection string formatted as `user/password@configuration`.   
Accepts values encrypted using `GTEncTool.exe`.  | Y  |   |  
| PhysicalPath  | Path to folder where the service will be deployed. The value can contain environment variable placeholders via `%variable%` convention.  | Y  |   |  
| UserName  | Windows service account user name. When not specified, the built-in `NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM` is used. Special accounts `NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM`, `NT AUTHORITY\NetworkService`, `NT AUTHORITY\LocalService` are supported (use empty string for Password).  
**Note**  
The account must have access to the published metadata and data files.  |   |   |  
| Password  | Windows service account Password. Accepts values encrypted using `GTEncTool.exe`.  |   |   |  
| LCID  | Locale identifier for metadata access. When not specified, the default locale of the account is used  |   |   |  
| Deltas__FetchTimeout  | Period in which the service checks for new Deltas in database, in minutes.  |   | 10  |  
| CoordinateSystemServiceUri  | URL of the NetWorks Coordinate System Service  |   | http://localhost/NetworksCoordinateSystemService/  |  
| TNS_ADMIN  | Path to folder containing Oracle `tnsnames.ora` file.  |   |   |  
| LoggingType  | Default logging level. Allowed values: `Error`, `Warn`, `Info`, `Trace`.  |   | Error  |  
### Example[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Deltas-Service/Deployment/Command-line-deployment.html#example)

```
<DeltasService 
   InstanceName="DeltasServiceINSTANCE1" 
   IsInSolution="False" 
   InstanceId="DeltasServiceINSTANCE1" 
   Definition="Deltas Service"  
   ConnectionInfo="user/password@CONFIGURATION" 
   PhysicalPath="%SystemDrive%\inetpub\wwwroot\VectorServiceINSTANCE1" 
   UserName="" 
   Password="" 
   LCID="0009"
   LoggingType="Error" 
 />

```

  1. Start **Command Prompt** (`cmd.exe`) **as Administrator**
  2. Navigate to NetWorks Program folder, typically `cd c:\Program Files (x86)\Intergraph\NetWorks\Program\`
  3. Deploy the service instance by executing `DeployDeltasService.exe -i <service instance>`

## Workflow - undeployment[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Deltas-Service/Deployment/Command-line-deployment.html#workflow---undeployment)
  1. Create or edit service instance in **NetWorksDeployedServices.xml** as in **Workflow - deployment**
  2. Start **Command Prompt** (`cmd.exe`) **as Administrator**
  3. Navigate to NetWorks Program folder, typically `cd c:\Program Files (x86)\Intergraph\NetWorks\Program\`
  4. Deploy the service instance by executing `DeployDeltasService.exe -i <service instance> -u`

# DeployDeltasService.exe
## Purpose[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Deltas-Service/Deployment/DeployDeltasService.exe.html#purpose)
Command line tool which enables redeployment of NetWorks Deltas Service.
## Usage[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Deltas-Service/Deployment/DeployDeltasService.exe.html#usage)
**DeployDeltasService.exe** -i ]
### Options[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Deltas-Service/Deployment/DeployDeltasService.exe.html#options)
**-i** Service Instance Name as specified in NetWorksDeployedServices.xml, attribute InstanceName.
**-u** **--undeploy** Undeploy the service.
**-r** **--redeploy** Redeploy the service (undeploy followed by deploy).
**--package-path** Alternative location of the Service Templates folder.
## Return value[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Deltas-Service/Deployment/DeployDeltasService.exe.html#return-value)  
| Value  | Meaning  |  
| --- | --- |  
| 0  | Success  |  
| 1  | Invalid parameters  |  
| 2  | Error during deployment  |  
## Configuration[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Deltas-Service/Deployment/DeployDeltasService.exe.html#configuration)
### Logging[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Deltas-Service/Deployment/DeployDeltasService.exe.html#logging)
File **DeployDeltasService.exe.NLog.config**. By default, the tool logs at Trace level to Console, at Error level to NetWorks logs folder.

# Manual deployment
## Workflow[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Deltas-Service/Deployment/Manual-deployment.html#workflow)
  1. Create folder on the disk for the service instance. This will be referred to as `SERVICEDIR` in following text.
  2. Unzip the contents of the service template folder containing `Hxgn.Intergraph.GTechnology.Deltas.ServiceHost.exe` to `SERVICEDIR`.
  3. [Configure the service](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Deltas-Service/Configuration.html).
  4. Start PowerShell as **Administrator**
  5. Execute this command to register the new service. Replace `${SERVICEDIR}` by the actual path to `SERVICEDIR`. Replace `<SERVICE_INSTANCE>` in the command with the actual service instance name.

```
New-Service -Name "NetWorksDeltasService<SERVICE_INSTANCE>" -BinaryPathName "${SERVICEDIR}\Hxgn.Intergraph.GTechnology.Deltas.ServiceHost.exe" -Description "NetWorks Deltas Service <SERVICE_INSTANCE>" -StartupType Automatic

```

  1. Start the service using the following: Replace `<SERVICE_INSTANCE>` in the command with the actual service instance name.

```
Start-Service NetWorksDeltasService<SERVICE_INSTANCE>

```
