# Diagnostics
The service uses **ETW** ([Event Tracing for Windows](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/etw/about-event-tracing)) to produce and collect events during runtime.
**NLog** is used to write events to log files. It is configured using `Hxgn.Intergraph.GTechnology.Deltas.ServiceHost.NLog.config`, which is expected at the same location as other configuration files.
## How to turn on tracing[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Deltas-Service/Diagnostics.html#how-to-turn-on-tracing)
  * Locate the file `Hxgn.Intergraph.GTechnology.Deltas.ServiceHost.NLog.config`
  * Open the file in a text editor (e.g. Notepad)
  * Set the log level for `file` output to `Trace`

```
<logger name="*" minlevel="Trace" writeTo="file" />

```

  * Save the file
  * Restart the app. pool for the service
  * Execute diagnosed workflow
  * Check the log file (by default under `c:\ProgramData\Intergraph\NetWorks\Logs\`)

## Related topics[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Deltas-Service/Diagnostics.html#related-topics)
  * [ETW Listener configuration](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Diagnostics.html)
  * [ETW Event Sources](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Diagnostics/ETW-Event-Sources.html)

# Deltas Service
**Overview**
Deltas Service is a Windows Service running unattended in the background. It periodically checks the database for new Deltas in `MODIFICATIONLOG` and publishes `.deltas` files into configured `DELTASDIRECTORY` (see [ConfigurationProperties.txt](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Configuration/ConfigurationProperties.txt-file.html)).
A single Deltas Service processes Deltas for a single configuration only. To process multiple configurations, multiple instances must be deployed.
The Deltas export runs periodically. The default period is 10 minutes, it can be configured in the Deltas Service configuration.
In the following text, HWM means High Watermark = maximum MODIFICATIONNUMBER.
**Workflow**
  1. Read **Deltas HWM** from the latest `.deltas` file (if exists).
  2. Read **Database HWM** from database.
  3. Read **Published DDC HWM**
  4. If **Deltas HWM** >= **Database HWM** , exit. `.deltas` is up-to-date.
  5. Read deltas from database starting at **Published DDC HWM**
  6. Export temporary `.deltas` file
  7. Perform coordinate transformation to configuration coordinate system over temporary `.deltas` file.
  8. Build Quad Tree and key indexes over temporary `.deltas` file.
  9. Write final `.deltas` file to `DELTASDIRECTORY`
  10. Write `.deltaslock` file to `DELTASDIRECTORY`
  11. Remove obsolete `.deltas` and `.deltaslock` files from `DELTASDIRECTORY`

**.deltas file**
The `.deltas` file contains exported Deltas, i.e. complete component view records which where written to MODIFICATIONLOG after last DDC data publish.
**File naming**
`<CONFIGURATION>_<MAX_MODIFICATIONNUMBER>.deltas`
  * `<CONFIGURATION>` is the NetWorks configuration name for which the Deltas are exported
  * `<MAX_MODIFICATIONNUMBER>` is the maximum database MODIFICATIONNUMBER processed when exporting Deltas.

**File content**
The `.deltas` file is a binary file, which contains several types of records.  
| Name  | Magic number  | Min  | Max  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| File header  | FHDR  | 1  | 1  | File header  |  
| Layer header  | LAYR  | 0  | *  | Layer header  |  
| Layer field  | FELD  | 0  | *  | Layer field descriptor  |  
| Data row  | DATA  | 0  | *  | Layer data row  |  
| Quad Tree  | QTRE  | 0  | *  | Layer quad tree  |  
| Key Index  | KIDX  | 0  | *  | Layer key index (index-by pointers to DATA rows)  |  
| End of file  | EOFT  | 1  | 1  | End of file marker  |  
**Note** `.deltas` file contents can be examined using **DumpDeltas.exe** utility.
**.deltaslock file**
The `.deltaslock` file is a marker file indicating that the `.deltas` file with the same name (before extension) is ready for usage.
Conversely, if the `DELTASDIRECTORY` contains only a `.deltas` file, but no `.deltaslock`, the `.deltas` should not be used.
**Requirements**
The Deltas Service depends on NetWorks **Coordinate System Service** to perform coordinate transformations. For best performance, both services should run on the same machine.
**Related topics**
  * [ConfigurationProperties.txt file](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Configuration/ConfigurationProperties.txt-file.html)
  * [How service locates configuration files](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Configuration/How-service-locates-configuration-files.html)

##### Dialog-Web-Services

# Data access optimization
## Overview[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Dialog-Web-Services/Data-access-optimization.html#overview)
Dialog Web Services reads feature data via PL/SQL. This process makes extensive use of metadata tables and dynamically generated SQL statements. Performance of selected workflows can be improved by generating a PL/SQL package (`NWG_DATAACCESS`) with the SQL statements in advance. This avoids the cost of accessing metadata at runtime and hard-parsing of SQL by the database.
This optimization improves the performance of Feature Explorer in NetWorks Portal.
##### Note
This workflow is designed to support production environments with stable metadata.
## How it works[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Dialog-Web-Services/Data-access-optimization.html#how-it-works)
Package `NWG_GTDWS` looks in to configuration in table `NWG_RELATEDFEATURES` (optimized table `NWG_RELATEDFEATURES_OPTABLE`). If specified records are present, it uses the configured PL/SQL function to retrieve data instead of the default ones.
Optimized reading applies to (`GWS_TYPE` in parentheses):
  * Related features (`*`)
  * Detail and schematic windows (`DetailsAndSchematics`)
  * Feature labels (`FeatureLabels`)

## Configuration workflow[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Dialog-Web-Services/Data-access-optimization.html#configuration-workflow)
  * **Generate`NWG_DATAACCESS` package body**
Execute `EXEC NWG_DATAACCESSGEN.GenerateDataAccess;` in database.
If any errors occur during this step, review the NWG_DATAACCESS package body and fix issues in metadata (e.g. label rule referencing missing column).
> **Important** This step must be executed repeatedly after every change in metadata related to: relationships, details and schematics, features and feature labels (tooltips).
  * **Register optimized functions in`NWG_RELATEDFEATURES`**
Run the following script:

```
DECLARE
  nCount NUMBER;
  nRfno NUMBER;
BEGIN
  DELETE FROM NWG_RELATEDFEATURES WHERE GWS_FNO IS NULL AND GWS_TYPE IN ('*', 'DetailsAndSchematics', 'FeatureLabels');
  SELECT MAX(GWS_RFNO)+1 INTO nRfno FROM NWG_RELATEDFEATURES;

  nRfno := NVL(nRfno, 0);

  INSERT INTO NWG_RELATEDFEATURES(GWS_RFNO, GWS_TYPE, GWS_USERNAME, GWS_TRAVERSALFUNCTION) VALUES (nRfno, '*', 'All Relationships', 'NWG_DATAACCESS.GetRelatedFeatures');
  INSERT INTO NWG_RELATEDFEATURES(GWS_RFNO, GWS_TYPE, GWS_USERNAME, GWS_TRAVERSALFUNCTION) VALUES (nRfno + 1, 'DetailsAndSchematics', 'Details And Schematics', 'NWG_DATAACCESS.GetDetailOrSchematicWindNames');
  INSERT INTO NWG_RELATEDFEATURES(GWS_RFNO, GWS_TYPE, GWS_USERNAME, GWS_TRAVERSALFUNCTION) VALUES (nRfno + 2, 'FeatureLabels', 'Feature Labels', 'NWG_DATAACCESS.GetFeatureLabel');

  NWG_RELATEDFEATURES_PKG.CreateOptimizedTable;
  COMMIT;

  -- Reset internal state of NWG_GTDWS to force reload of configuration
  EXECUTE IMMEDIATE 'ALTER PACKAGE NWG_GTDWS COMPILE BODY';
END;

```

Expected result:  
| GWS_RFNO  | GWS_FNO  | GWS_TYPE  | GWS_USERNAME  | GWS_TRAVERSALFUNCTION  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| 0  | (NULL)  | *  | Relationships  | NWG_DATAACCESS.GetRelatedFeatures  |  
| 1  | (NULL)  | DetailsAndSchematics  | Details And Schematics  | NWG_DATAACCESS.GetDetailOrSchematicWindNames  |  
| 2  | (NULL)  | FeatureLabels  | Feature Labels  | NWG_DATAACCESS.GetFeatureLabel  |  

## Revert configuration to original[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Dialog-Web-Services/Data-access-optimization.html#revert-configuration-to-original)
  * **Reset configuration**
To remove the optimizations, return the configuration in NWG_RELATEDFEATURES to default state.
Execute the following:

```
DECLARE
  nCount NUMBER;
  nRfno NUMBER;
BEGIN
  DELETE FROM NWG_RELATEDFEATURES WHERE GWS_FNO IS NULL AND GWS_TYPE IN ('*', 'DetailsAndSchematics', 'FeatureLabels');
  SELECT MAX(GWS_RFNO)+1 INTO nRfno FROM NWG_RELATEDFEATURES;

  nRfno := NVL(nRfno, 0);

  INSERT INTO NWG_RELATEDFEATURES(GWS_RFNO, GWS_TYPE, GWS_USERNAME, GWS_TRAVERSALFUNCTION) VALUES (nRfno, '*', 'All Relationships', 'NWG_GTDWS.getRelatedFeaturesAll');

  NWG_RELATEDFEATURES_PKG.CreateOptimizedTable;
  COMMIT;

  -- Reset internal state of NWG_GTDWS to force reload of configuration
  EXECUTE IMMEDIATE 'ALTER PACKAGE NWG_GTDWS COMPILE BODY';
END;

```

Expected result:  
| GWS_RFNO  | GWS_FNO  | GWS_TYPE  | GWS_USERNAME  | GWS_TRAVERSALFUNCTION  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| 0  | (NULL)  | *  | Relationships  | NWG_GTDWS.getRelatedFeaturesAll  |

# Disable searching in OtherPaths when downloading files
**Overview**
The Dialog Web Service File download API looks for files in paths defined under  in the FileUNCPaths.xml file, if the file is specified by a relative address and/or can't be found at the default location.
**Configuration**
To turn searching in  off for a deployed Dialog Web Services instance, add a new appSetting `FileDownload.IgnoreOtherPaths` to the instances **web.config** file and set its value to `1`.
**Example**

```
  <appSettings>
    <!-- ... other settings ... -->
    <add key="FileDownload.IgnoreOtherPaths" value="1" />
  </appSettings>

```

# Map user properties to attributes
## Overview[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Dialog-Web-Services/Map-user-properties-to-attributes.html#overview)
This functionality allows to configure Dialog Web Service and Feature Transaction Service to map claims linked to the OpenID Connect identity to attributes of the updated feature, when updating data via the Dialog Web Service /Feature API or Feature Transaction Service [ProcessTransactions](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Transaction-Service/ProcessTransactions.html) API.
## Requirements[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Dialog-Web-Services/Map-user-properties-to-attributes.html#requirements)
  * OpenID Connect

## Configuration[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Dialog-Web-Services/Map-user-properties-to-attributes.html#configuration)
### Metadata tables[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Dialog-Web-Services/Map-user-properties-to-attributes.html#metadata-tables)
  * [NWG_CONTEXTPROPERTY](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Reference/Metadata-tables/NWG_CONTEXTPROPERTY.html)
  * [NWG_CTXPROPERTYMAP](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Reference/Metadata-tables/NWG_CTXPROPERTYMAP.html)

## Packages[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Dialog-Web-Services/Map-user-properties-to-attributes.html#packages)
  * [NWG_CONTEXT](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Reference/PL-SQL-Packages/NWG_CONTEXT.html)

# Role access based on G3E_FEATURE
Dialog Web Services (since version 11.01.2301) restrict access to data using roles defined in **G3E_FEATURE_OPTABLE** fields **G3E_SELECTROLE** , **G3E_EDITROLE** and **G3E_DELETEROLE**. Previous behavior was role restriction based on **G3E_DIALOGATTRIBUTES_OPTABLE.G3E_ROLE** field.
To run G3E_FEATURES_OPTABLE role filtering off and use only dialog tab attribute roles (original behavior), create a new parameter `DialogWebServiceUseAttributeRolesOnly` in **G3E_GENERALPARAMETER** table and set its value to `1`.

# Use non-default language for metadata
**Overview**
Unless a pLCID parameter is supplied with a request to Dialog Web Services the metadata and data are returned using the default configured language. This is the default language specified in `G3E_METADATALANGUAGE`.
This applies too clients like NetWorks Portal.
**Configuration**
To change the default language for a deployed Dialog Web Services instance, locate the entry
`<add key="pLCID" value="XXXX" />`
in its web.config file. Modify its value to the required LCID.

##### Dynamic-WMS-Service

# Configuration
## Common Parameters[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Dynamic-WMS-Service/Configuration.html#common-parameters)
See [Common Configuration Parameters](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Configuration/Common-Service-Configuration-Parameters.html).
## Specific Parameters[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Dynamic-WMS-Service/Configuration.html#specific-parameters)
**`Storage:Root`**  
Path to root folder of DDC storage.  
Example: `C:\NetWorks\DynamicWMS\data`
###  `Map:ExpandByFixed`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Dynamic-WMS-Service/Configuration.html#mapexpandbyfixed)
Number of ground units to be added to the bounding box when retrieving data. This value enhances retrieval of text and point geometries at low scales. Default is `10`.
###  `Map:ExpandByRelative`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Dynamic-WMS-Service/Configuration.html#mapexpandbyrelative)
Expand factor for for the bbox when reading data from DDCs. Expected value is a decimal number > 1. Use dot `.` as decimal separator. Default is `1.2`.
###  `Map:AttachDDCDisplayScaleRange`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Dynamic-WMS-Service/Configuration.html#mapattachddcdisplayscalerange)
Scale range in which the attached DDC files are visible, formatted as `{min}:{max}`. This value can be overridden for individual source in its [**source.json**](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Dynamic-WMS-Service/Metadata-files/Source-metadata.html) file. Default is `1:10000`.
###  `Map:LocateMaxFeatures`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Dynamic-WMS-Service/Configuration.html#maplocatemaxfeatures)
Maximum number of features to return from the Locate operation. Enter a number > 0. Default is `20`.
###  `Map:UseIndexForLayerNames`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Dynamic-WMS-Service/Configuration.html#mapuseindexforlayernames)
When `true`, layer ordinal is used instead of DDC layer name as WMS layer name. This setting helps fix problems with long URLs caused by attached files with many layers. Default: `false`.
###  `Cache:ExpirationMinutes`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Dynamic-WMS-Service/Configuration.html#cacheexpirationminutes)
Number of minutes to keep DDC source in memory after last access. Default: `20`.
###  `Cache:CleanUpPeriodMinutes`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Dynamic-WMS-Service/Configuration.html#cachecleanupperiodminutes)
Period (minutes) in which expired sources are checked. Default: `10`.
## See also[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Dynamic-WMS-Service/Configuration.html#see-also)
  * [How service locates configuration files](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Configuration/How-service-locates-configuration-files.html)
  * [Configuration System](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Configuration/Configuration-System.html)

###### Deployment

# Command line deployment
Dynamic WMS Service can be semi-automatically deployed and undeployed from the command line using the [DeployDynamicWMSService.exe](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Dynamic-WMS-Service/Deployment/DeployDynamicWMSService.exe.html) tool.
## Workflow - deployment[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Dynamic-WMS-Service/Deployment/Command-line-deployment.html#workflow---deployment)
  1. Create or edit service instance in **NetWorksDeployedServices.xml**.

NetWorks keeps track of service instances in XML file `c:\ProgramData\Intergraph\NetWorks\DeployedServices\NetWorksDeployedServices.xml`.
To register a new instance of the Dynamic WMS Service, open the file in a text editor (e.g. Notepad) and add new element under the `<NetWorksDeployedServices>` element, e.g.:

```
<DynamicWMSService InstanceName="DynamicWMSServiceINSTANCE1" 
               IsInSolution="False" 
               InstanceId="DynamicWMSServiceINSTANCE1"
               Definition="Dynamic WMS Service"
               Storage__Root="C:\NetWorks\DynamicWMS\data"
                />

```

### Additional parameters[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Dynamic-WMS-Service/Deployment/Command-line-deployment.html#additional-parameters)  
| Name  | Description  | Mandatory  | Default Value  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| InstanceName  | Unique name of the service instance.  | Y  |   |  
| IsInSolution  | Flag.  | Y  |   |  
| InstanceId  | GUID of the instance  |   |   |  
| Definition  | Name of service definition  | Y  | Dynamic WMS Service  |  
| ConnectionInfo  | NetWorks connection string formatted as `user/password@configuration`.   
Accepts values encrypted using `GTEncTool.exe`.  | Y  |   |  
| PhysicalPath  | Path to folder where the service will be deployed. The value can contain environment variable placeholders via `%variable%` convention.  | Y  |   |  
| VirtualPath  | Virtual path for IIS deployment. Typically `<site name>`/`<InstanceName>`, where `<site name>` is usually `Default Web Site`.  | Y  |   |  
| AppPoolName  | IIS Application Pool Name. Typically set to `InstanceName` + `Pool`.  | Y  |   |  
| AppPoolIdentityType  | IIS Application Pool identity type. [Allowed values](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/microsoft.web.administration.processmodelidentitytype?view=iis-dotnet).  |   | 4  |  
| AppPoolUserName  | IIS Application Pool User name. When not specified, the built-in ApplicationPoolIdentity is used.  
**Note**  
The account must have access to the published metadata and data files.  |   |   |  
| AppPoolPassword  | IIS Application Pool Password. Accepts values encrypted using `GTEncTool.exe`.  |   |   |  
| LCID  | Locale identifier for metadata access. When not specified, the default locale of the account is used  |   |   |  
| Map__ExpandByFixed  | Number of ground units to be added to the bounding box when retrieving data  |   | 10  |  
| Map__ExpandByRelative  | Expand factor for for the bbox when reading data from DDCs.  |   | 1.2  |  
| CoordinateSystem__Code  | OGC code of the coordinate system (typically `EPSG:NNNN`). If not specified, `G3E_CONFIGURATIONS_OPTABLE`.`G3E_OGCCRSNAME` is used  |   |   |  
| Storage__Root  | Path to root folder of DDC storage  | Y  | C:\NetWorks\DynamicWMS\data  |  
| Cache__ExpirationMinutes  | Number of minutes to keep DDC source in memory after last access.  |   | 20  |  
| Cache__CleanUpPeriodMinutes  | Period (minutes) in which expired sources are checked  |   | 10  |  
| TNS_ADMIN  | Path to folder containing Oracle `tnsnames.ora` file.  |   |   |  
| AuthenticationType  | Type of authentication. Allowed values:   
* `OIDC` - OpenID Connect   
* `Anonymous`  |   | Anonymous  |  
| LoggingType  | Default logging level. Allowed values: `Error`, `Warn`, `Info`, `Trace`.  |   | Error  |  
For more informations, check [Configuration Section](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Dynamic-WMS-Service/Configuration.html).
### Example[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Dynamic-WMS-Service/Deployment/Command-line-deployment.html#example)

```
<DynamicWMSService Definition="Dynamic WMS Service" 
                   InstanceId="NwDynamicWMSService" 
                   InstanceName="NwDynamicWMSService"
                   AppPoolName="NwDynamicWMSServicePool" 
                   PhysicalPath="%SystemDrive%\inetpub\wwwroot\NwDynamicWMSService" 
                   VirtualPath="Default Web Site/NwDynamicWMSService" 
                   AuthenticationType="Anonymous" 
                   LoggingType="Error" 
                   ConnectionInfo="user/password@CONFIGURATION" 
                   Storage__Root="C:\Temp\DynamicWMS\CAD\Output"
                   IsInSolution="True" />

```

  1. Start **Command Prompt** (`cmd.exe`) **as Administrator**
  2. Navigate to NetWorks Program folder, typically `cd c:\Program Files (x86)\Intergraph\NetWorks\Program\`
  3. Deploy the service instance by executing `DeployDynamicWMSService.exe -i <service instance>`

## Workflow - undeployment[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Dynamic-WMS-Service/Deployment/Command-line-deployment.html#workflow---undeployment)
  1. Create or edit service instance in **NetWorksDeployedServices.xml** as in **Workflow - deployment**
  2. Start **Command Prompt** (`cmd.exe`) **as Administrator**
  3. Navigate to NetWorks Program folder, typically `cd c:\Program Files (x86)\Intergraph\NetWorks\Program\`
  4. Deploy the service instance by executing `DeployDynamicWMSService.exe -i <service instance> -u`

## Workflow - redeployment[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Dynamic-WMS-Service/Deployment/Command-line-deployment.html#workflow---redeployment)
As **Deployment** , except for step
  1. Deploy the service instance by executing `DeployDynamicWMSService.exe -i <service instance> -r`

# DeployDynamicWMSService.exe
## Purpose[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Dynamic-WMS-Service/Deployment/DeployDynamicWMSService.exe.html#purpose)
Command line tool which enables redeployment of NetWorks Dynamic WMS Service.
## Usage[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Dynamic-WMS-Service/Deployment/DeployDynamicWMSService.exe.html#usage)
**DeployDynamicWMSService.exe** -i ]
### Options[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Dynamic-WMS-Service/Deployment/DeployDynamicWMSService.exe.html#options)
**-i** Service Instance Name as specified in NetWorksDeployedServices.xml, attribute InstanceName.
**-u** **--undeploy** Undeploy the service.
**-r** **--redeploy** Redeploy the service (undeploy followed by deploy).
**--package-path** Alternative location of the Service Templates folder.
## Return value[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Dynamic-WMS-Service/Deployment/DeployDynamicWMSService.exe.html#return-value)  
| Value  | Meaning  |  
| --- | --- |  
| 0  | Success  |  
| 1  | Invalid parameters  |  
| 2  | Error during deployment  |  
## Configuration[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Dynamic-WMS-Service/Deployment/DeployDynamicWMSService.exe.html#configuration)
### Logging[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Dynamic-WMS-Service/Deployment/DeployDynamicWMSService.exe.html#logging)
File **DeployDynamicWMSService.exe.NLog.config**. By default, the tool logs at Trace level to Console, at Error level to NetWorks logs folder.

# Manual deployment
## Workflow[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Dynamic-WMS-Service/Deployment/Manual-deployment.html#workflow)
  1. Create folder on the disk for the service instance. This will be referred to as `SERVICEDIR` in following text.
  2. Unzip the contents of the service template folder containing `Hxgn.NetWorks.DynamicWMSService.ServiceHost.exe` to `SERVICEDIR`.
  3. [Configure the service](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Dynamic-WMS-Service/Configuration.html).
  4. Open IIS Manager
  5. Create app. pool in IIS Manager with the following properties: 
     * Name: `DynamicWMSServicePool`)
     * .NET CLR Version: _No Managed Code_
     * Managed Pipeline Mode: _Integrated_
     * Identity: Use account which has access to the physical storage folders
  6. Create application under `Default Web Site` (or other site) 
     * Alias: `DynamicWMSService`)
     * Application Pool: Use pool created above
     * Physical path: Use actual `SERVICEDIR` value
  7. The API is available at `http://{server}/{appName}` (e.g. `http://server1/DynamicWMSService`).

# Diagnostics
The service uses **ETW** ([Event Tracing for Windows](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/etw/about-event-tracing)) to produce and collect events during runtime.
**NLog** is used to write events to log files. It is configured using `NLog.config`, which is expected at the same location as other configuration files.
## How to turn on tracing[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Dynamic-WMS-Service/Diagnostics.html#how-to-turn-on-tracing)
  * Locate the file `NLog.config`
  * Open the file in a text editor (e.g. Notepad)
  * Set the log level for `file` output to `Trace`

```
<logger name="*" minlevel="Trace" writeTo="file" />

```

  * Save the file
  * Restart the app. pool for the service
  * Execute diagnosed workflow
  * Check the log file (by default under `c:\ProgramData\Intergraph\NetWorks\Logs\`)

## Related topics[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Dynamic-WMS-Service/Diagnostics.html#related-topics)
  * [ETW Listener configuration](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Diagnostics.html)
  * [ETW Event Sources](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Diagnostics/ETW-Event-Sources.html)

###### Metadata-files

# Capabilities file
## Overview[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Dynamic-WMS-Service/Metadata-files/Capabilities-file.html#overview)
The `capabilities.json` file contains cached capabilities information for this dynamic source.
## Structures[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Dynamic-WMS-Service/Metadata-files/Capabilities-file.html#structures)
### Capabilities[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Dynamic-WMS-Service/Metadata-files/Capabilities-file.html#capabilities)
Root structure of the `capabilities.json` file.  
| Property  | Type  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| Name  | string  | Dynamic source `sid`.  |  
| Title  | string  | Title of this source.  |  
| Abstract  | string  | Abstract of this source.  |  
| CRS  | string  | Coordinate system identifier.  |  
| BoundingBox  | BBOX  | Bounding box in projection coordinates.  |  
| GeographicBoundingBox  | BBOX  | Bounding box in WGS84 coordinates.  |  
| Layers  | [Layer]  | List of layers  |  
### Layer[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Dynamic-WMS-Service/Metadata-files/Capabilities-file.html#layer)
WMS layer descriptor.  
| Property  | Type  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| Name  | string  | Dynamic source `sid`.  |  
| Title  | string  | Title of this source.  |  
| Abstract  | string  | Abstract of this source.  |  
| Queryable  | bool  | When `true`, the layer is queryable.  |

# Source metadata
## Overview[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Dynamic-WMS-Service/Metadata-files/Source-metadata.html#overview)
The `source.json` file contains additional information related to the source of the data and presentation of the DDC data source. The file must be located in the same folder as the DDC file.
## Structures[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Dynamic-WMS-Service/Metadata-files/Source-metadata.html#structures)
### SourceInfo[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Dynamic-WMS-Service/Metadata-files/Source-metadata.html#sourceinfo)
Root structure of the `source.json` file. All properties are optional.  
| Property  | Type  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| source  | string  | Name of the source file from which the DDC was created.  |  
| title  | string  | Title of this source. Used in GetCapabilites response.  |  
| abstract  | string  | Abstract of this source. Used in GetCapabilites response.  |  
| sub  | string  | OpenID Connect "sub" claim of the user which created this package. Not used by the service.  |  
| nominal-paper-scale  | integer  | Nominal paper scale for scale-dependent styles. Default is `500`.  |  
| display-scale-min  | integer  | Minimum display scale denominator at which the source is visible (unless overridden in a layer). Default is `1` (for 1:1).  |  
| display-scale-max  | integer  | Maximum display scale denominator at which the source is visible (unless overridden in a layer). Default is `10000` (for 1:10000).  |  
| sld  | string  | Path to file with style descriptor (see [Symbology](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Dynamic-WMS-Service/Metadata-files/Symbology.html)). The style is used to render geometries only when the DDC data do not contain styles in row data (G3E_STYLEBLOB). The style can be overridden by layer `sld` parameter.  |  
| srno  | integer  |  `G3E_SRNO` value to use for evaluating style rules over row data. If both `sld` and `srno` are specified, `srno` has is used.  |  
| layers  | Dictionary of `LayerInfo`  | Layer-specific configuration parameters. Key is the layer name (case-sensitive).  |  
### LayerInfo[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Dynamic-WMS-Service/Metadata-files/Source-metadata.html#layerinfo)
Root structure of the `source.json` file. All properties are optional.  
| Property  | Type  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| ordinal  | integer  | Display ordinal. Not used at the moment.  |  
| title  | string  | Title of this layer. Used in GetCapabilites response.  |  
| abstract  | string  | Abstract of this layer. Used in GetCapabilites response.  |  
| display-scale-min  | integer  | Minimum display scale denominator at which the source is visible. Default is `1` (for 1:1).  |  
| display-scale-max  | integer  | Maximum display scale denominator at which the source is visible. Default is `10000` (for 1:10000).  |  
| sld  | string  | Path to file with style descriptor (see [Symbology](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Dynamic-WMS-Service/Metadata-files/Symbology.html)). The style is used to render geometries only when the DDC data do not contain styles in row data (G3E_STYLEBLOB).  |  
| srno  | integer  |  `G3E_SRNO` value to use for evaluating style rules over row data. If both `sld` and `srno` are specified, `srno` has is used.  |  
## Example[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Dynamic-WMS-Service/Metadata-files/Source-metadata.html#example)

```
{
    "source": "drawing.dgn",
    "display-scale-min": 1,
    "display-scale-max": 10000,
    "nominal-paper-scale": 500,
    "sld": "style.json",
    "layers": {
        "Default": {
            "ordinal": 1,
            "display-scale-min": 1,
            "display-scale-max": 10000,
            "sld": "style1.json"
        },
        "Level 5": {
            "ordinal": 1,
            "display-scale-min": 1,
            "display-scale-max": 100000,
            "sld": "style2.json"
        }
    }
}

```

## Example 2[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Dynamic-WMS-Service/Metadata-files/Source-metadata.html#example-2)

```
{
    "source": "drawing.dxf",
    "display-scale-min": 1,
    "display-scale-max": 10000,
    "nominal-paper-scale": 500,
    "layers": {
        "Layer1": {
            "ordinal": 1,
            "display-scale-min": 1,
            "display-scale-max": 10000,
            "srno": 50
        },
        "Layer2": {
            "ordinal": 1,
            "display-scale-min": 1,
            "display-scale-max": 100000,
            "srno": 51
        }
    }
}

```

## Data types[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Dynamic-WMS-Service/Metadata-files/Symbology.html#data-types)
### BGRColor[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Dynamic-WMS-Service/Metadata-files/Symbology.html#bgrcolor)
Integer with RGB color encoded as BGR using the following formula: `(B * 65536) + (G * 256) + R`. Special value `-3` used for background color.
### HiMetric[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Dynamic-WMS-Service/Metadata-files/Symbology.html#himetric)
HiMetric = `size in pt` * `35.2778`
See [HiMetric on Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Himetric).
## Example[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Dynamic-WMS-Service/Metadata-files/Symbology.html#example)

```
{
    "Area": {
        "BackColor": 255,
        "BackTranslucency": 50,
        "Boundary": {
            "Color": 16711680,
            "Width": 0
        },
        "ShowBoundary": 1,
        "BoundaryPresent": 1
    },
    "Line": {
        "Color": 0,
        "Width": 0,
        "StyleUnits": 1
    },
    "Point": {
        "Color": 0,
        "Size": 350, 
        "StyleUnits": 1,
        "FontName": "Wingdings",
        "Symbol": "A"
    },
    "Text": {
        "Color": 255,
        "Size": 350,
        "StyleUnits": 1,
        "Font": {
            "Name": "Arial"
        }
    }
}

```

# Metadata files
Each dynamic source can have additional metadata specified the same folder:
## source.json[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Dynamic-WMS-Service/Metadata-files.html#sourcejson)
Dynamic source metadata.
For reference on file structure see [Source metadata](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Dynamic-WMS-Service/Metadata-files/Source-metadata.html).
## capabilities.json[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Dynamic-WMS-Service/Metadata-files.html#capabilitiesjson)
Cached capabilities data (layers, extent) for this source. This file is created automatically by the Dynamic WMS when the capabilities are requested for the first time (e.g. during GetCapabilities or GetRegisteredSources call).
This file can be safely removed if necessary. The file should be removed after changing data in `source.json` to force Dynamic WMS to regenerate it.
For reference on file structure see [Capabilities file](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Dynamic-WMS-Service/Metadata-files/Capabilities-file.html).

# Publish DDC file as WMS
## Overview[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Dynamic-WMS-Service/Publish-DDC-file-as-WMS.html#overview)
This workflow describes the steps to publish a DDC file as WMS for consumption by external applications.
## Steps[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Dynamic-WMS-Service/Publish-DDC-file-as-WMS.html#steps)
### 1. Create the DDC file[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Dynamic-WMS-Service/Publish-DDC-file-as-WMS.html#1-create-the-ddc-file)
Typically, you create the DDC file by converting a 3rd party vector data file (e.g. CAD file like DGN, DWG, DXF or geometry file like Shapefile) using tools provided by NetWorks (**PublishCADFiles.exe** , **PublishShapeToDDC.exe**).
##### Note
The DDC files must be published in the same coordinate system as the NetWorks configuration configured for the Dynamic WMS instance.
### 2. Manually register the source[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Dynamic-WMS-Service/Publish-DDC-file-as-WMS.html#2-manually-register-the-source)
Open folder configured in `Storage:Root` of the Dynamic WMS instance. Follow structure defined in [Storage](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Dynamic-WMS-Service/Storage.html) to create folder for the new dynamic source. Copy DDC and CDT files to the folder.
**Example**
To register new source with **sid** equal to `demo_cadastre`, create folder `de` under `<Storage:Root>`, then folder `mo` under `de` and folder `demo_cadastre` under `mo`.

```
<Storage:Root>/
  de/
    mo/
      demo_cadastre/

```

### 3. Configure the source metadata[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Dynamic-WMS-Service/Publish-DDC-file-as-WMS.html#3-configure-the-source-metadata)
Create file named `source.json` in the dynamic source folder. Follow [Source metadata](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Dynamic-WMS-Service/Metadata-files/Source-metadata.html) and setup source properties (e.g. symbology, scales at which layers are visible).
### 4. Publish the WMS source[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Dynamic-WMS-Service/Publish-DDC-file-as-WMS.html#4-publish-the-wms-source)
The new dynamic source is now available at `<Dynamic WMS URL>/wms/{sid}`, see [API](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Dynamic-WMS-Service.html).
**Example**
If the Dynamic WMS Service is deployed at URL `http://server/dynamicwmsservice`, source with **sid** `demo_cadastre` is available at `http://server/dynamicwmsservice/wms/demo_cadastre`. This value can be pasted to NetWorks Administration Console when configuring NetWorks Portal workspace and adding a WMS source.
## Notes[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Dynamic-WMS-Service/Publish-DDC-file-as-WMS.html#notes)
  * If the `source.json` is changed, it is necessary to restart the Dynamic WMS service app. pool to pick-up changes.

# Storage
The Dynamic WMS expects DDC files to be available in file system structure. The root of this folder is configured in parameter `Storage.Root`.
The directory structure is based on the **source identifier** (`sid`).
  * First level is determined from characters 1 and 2 of the `sid`.
  * Second level is determined from characters 3 and 4 of the `sid`.
  * Third level is the `sid` and the folder contains all files uploaded to the transaction.

**Example**
`sid` is `ns0im266d799odjv8vg5woy91fmbej12`
Client uploads file `cad1.dxf`. These are converted to `cad1.ddc` and `cad1.dxf` and stored as source `ns0im266d799odjv8vg5woy91fmbej12`.

```
<Storage.Root>/
    ns/
        0i/
            ns0im266d799odjv8vg5woy91fmbej12/
                cad1.ddc
                cad1.cdt
                source.json

```

File `source.json` contains optional [metadata](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Dynamic-WMS-Service/Metadata-files.html) for the source.

# Dynamic WMS Service
## Overview[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Dynamic-WMS-Service.html#overview)
The Dynamic WMS Service exposes OGC WMS interface and renders raster geometry from DDC files. The DDC files typically contain data from converted vector files (CAD or other vector formats). One Dynamic WMS Service instance can expose multiple virtual WMS endpoints, one for each _dynamic source_. A dynamic source is a folder containing DDC/CDT files.
Dynamic WMS is typically used in two contexts:
  * Attach CAD functionality of NetWorks Portal - support render part of the upload-convert-render workflow.
  * Generic WMS for rendering geometries from arbitrary DDC files.

## Operation[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Dynamic-WMS-Service.html#operation)
Each _dynamic source_ is uniquely identified by the `sid`, which is an alphanumeric string at least 5 characters long. One dynamic source may contain one or more DDC/CDT pairs. Layer names in all DDCs within one dynamic source must be unique. Each layer in the DDCs is mapped to a WMS layer.
**GetMap** request to the Dynamic WMS looks up the DDC files for the `sid` and renders the requested part of the map. Rendering is by-default done using built-in default styling. It is possible to configure symbology for each dynamic source:
  * Static set of styles (area, line, point, text) for each layer.
  * Use style rules and styles defined in NetWorks metadata to set styling for each layer.

## Coordinate systems[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Dynamic-WMS-Service.html#coordinate-systems)
Each Dynamic WMS instance is linked to a single NetWorks configuration. All DDC files provided by the Dynamic WMS instance must be published in the coordinate system of the NetWorks configuration.
## Standards[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Dynamic-WMS-Service.html#standards)
Dynamic WMS supports OCG WMS version 1.3.0.
## See also[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Dynamic-WMS-Service.html#see-also)
  * [Physical storage of dynamic sources](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Dynamic-WMS-Service/Storage.html)
  * [Source metadata](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Dynamic-WMS-Service/Metadata-files/Source-metadata.html)
  * [Publish DDC file as WMS](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Dynamic-WMS-Service/Publish-DDC-file-as-WMS.html)

# Feature Data Service
Feature Data Service is a web service designed to support data and metadata retrieval workflows for Feature Editor module and 3rd party applications. It provides API to retrieve the following kinds of data and metadata:
**[Metadata](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Data-Service/Metadata.html)**
  * General parameters
  * Feature placement
  * Dialog and dialog tabs
  * Style and label rules
  * Role information

**[Data](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Data-Service/Data.html)**
  * Picklist data
  * Feature data and geometries
  * Feature relationships
  * Dialog tab data
  * Detail data

# Feature Transaction Service
Feature Transaction Service provides public web service API for CUD operations over features in HxGN NetWorks database. Its intended consumers are online clients (Portal) and 3rd party applications.

##### OGC-Services

# Alternative location of Coordinate System Service
When NetWorks Coordinate System Service is hosted on a different URL than `http://localhost/NetWorksCoordinateSystemService`, it is possible to configure the URL using the **ServiceConfig.xml** file by adding setting `CoordSystemServiceUrl`.

```
<provider category="wms" name="gtechnology" type=".\bin\Intergraph.GTechnology.OGCProviders.dll;Intergraph.GTechnology.OgcProviders.Wms.GTWmsProvider">
  <providerSettings>
    <setting name="ConnectionInfo" value="123123..." />
    <!-- ... -->

    <!-- Configure Coordinate System Service URL -->            
    <setting name="CoordSystemServiceUrl" value="http://host1/NetWorksCoordinateSystemService/" />
  </providerSettings>
</provider>

```

# CancelTouchTiles
Cancel running bulk generation of tiles in the tile stack.
## Request[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/OGC-Services/Bulk-generation-of-WMTS-tile-stack/CancelTouchTiles.html#request)
### URI[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/OGC-Services/Bulk-generation-of-WMTS-tile-stack/CancelTouchTiles.html#uri)
GET {WMTS_URL}?SERVICE=WMTS&REQUEST=**CancelTouchTiles**
### Parameters[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/OGC-Services/Bulk-generation-of-WMTS-tile-stack/CancelTouchTiles.html#parameters)
N/A
## Response[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/OGC-Services/Bulk-generation-of-WMTS-tile-stack/CancelTouchTiles.html#response)
### Normal response (200)[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/OGC-Services/Bulk-generation-of-WMTS-tile-stack/CancelTouchTiles.html#normal-response-200)

```
{
    "Success": true,
    "Message": "Tile stack generation cancelled."
}

```

### Response when tile generation is already running (200)[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/OGC-Services/Bulk-generation-of-WMTS-tile-stack/CancelTouchTiles.html#response-when-tile-generation-is-already-running-200)

```
{
    "Success": false,
    "Message": "Tile stack generation not running.",
    "Code": "ERR_OPERATION_NOT_IN_PROGRESS"
}

```

### Authentication failure (401)[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/OGC-Services/Bulk-generation-of-WMTS-tile-stack/CancelTouchTiles.html#authentication-failure-401)
Returned when authorization token is missing or invalid.

# TouchTiles
Start bulk generation of tiles in the tile stack. The bulk generation runs on the background in the server after the request completes.
## Request[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/OGC-Services/Bulk-generation-of-WMTS-tile-stack/TouchTiles.html#request)
### URI[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/OGC-Services/Bulk-generation-of-WMTS-tile-stack/TouchTiles.html#uri)
GET {WMTS_URL}?SERVICE=WMTS&REQUEST=**TouchTiles** &TileMatrixSet=**{TileMatrixSet}** &TileMatrix=**{TileMatrix}** &BBOX=**{BBOX}** &VERSION=1.0.0&LAYER=**{LAYER}** &STYLE=**{style}** &FORMAT=**{format}**[&WORKERS=**{WORKERS}** &TileMatrixMin=**{TileMatrixMin}** &DbUpdate=**{DbUpdate}**]
### Parameters[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/OGC-Services/Bulk-generation-of-WMTS-tile-stack/TouchTiles.html#parameters)  
| Name  | Description  | Mandatory  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| TileMatrixSet  | Name of the tile matrix set  | Y  |  
| TileMatrix  | Identifier of lowest tile matrix (Z) to generate.  | Y  |  
| BBOX  | Bounding box of the area to generate, formatted as {west},{south},{east},{north}. Specified in coordinate system of the WMTS.  | Y  |  
| LAYER  | WMTS layer parameter. See GetCapabilities for values.  | Y  |  
| STYLE  | WMTS style parameter. See GetCapabilities for values.  | Y  |  
| FORMAT  | WMTS format parameter. See GetCapabilities for values.  | Y  |  
| WORKERS  | Number of parallel worker processes. Default is 1.  | N  |  
| TileMatrixMin  | Identifier of starting tile matrix (Z). When not specified, all matrices up to TileMatrix are generated.  | N  |  
| DbUpdate  | Update database when generating. Expected values: 0,1. Default is 1  | N  |  
| Continue  | When 1, generation continues with next row for which directory on disk does not exist yet. Default is 0.  | N  |  
| EmptySize  | Size of PNG file to be ignored. Used to filter out empty PNGs when generating tile stack for export.  | N  |  
## Response[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/OGC-Services/Bulk-generation-of-WMTS-tile-stack/TouchTiles.html#response)
### Normal response (200)[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/OGC-Services/Bulk-generation-of-WMTS-tile-stack/TouchTiles.html#normal-response-200)

```
{
    "Success": true,
    "Message": "Tile stack generation started."
}

```

### Response when tile generation is already running (200)[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/OGC-Services/Bulk-generation-of-WMTS-tile-stack/TouchTiles.html#response-when-tile-generation-is-already-running-200)

```
{
    "Success": false,
    "Message": "Tile stack generation already running.",
    "Code": "ERR_OPERATION_IN_PROGRESS"
}

```

### Bad request (400)[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/OGC-Services/Bulk-generation-of-WMTS-tile-stack/TouchTiles.html#bad-request-400)

```
<ows:ExceptionReport xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:ows="http://www.opengis.net/ows" xsi:schemaLocation="http://schemas.opengis.net/ows/1.1.0/owsExceptionReport.xsd" version="1.1.0">
    <ows:Exception>
        <ows:ExceptionText>Vorgang 'TouchTiles' fehlgeschlagen.</ows:ExceptionText>
    </ows:Exception>
    <ows:Exception exceptionCode="InvalidParameterValue" locator="TileMatrixSet">
        <ows:ExceptionText>Anforderungsparameter TileMatrixSet ist ungültig.</ows:ExceptionText>
    </ows:Exception>
</ows:ExceptionReport>

### Authentication failure (401)[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/OGC-Services/Bulk-generation-of-WMTS-tile-stack/TouchTiles.html#authentication-failure-401)
Returned when authorization token is missing or invalid.

# Bulk generation of WMTS tile stack
NetWorks WMTS service generates the tiles on-demand when a client makes a request. To improve performance it might be necessary to generate the tiles in advance.
WMTS now comes with built-in methods how to generate the tile stack in bulk.
  * TouchTiles
  * CancelTouchTiles
  * GetTouchTilesStatus

**Notes**
The app. pool for the WMTS service must be configured avoid being terminated in case of no requests, otherwise the generation may be terminated by IIS before it completes.
Set up the NetWorks WarmUp service to ping the WMTS service periodically.
Alternatively, configure IIS application pool to keep the application alive. Use this workflow to configure via IIS Manager.
**1.** Find the application pool for your service. **2.** Open Advanced settings and set the following properties:  
| Name  | Value  |  
| --- | --- |  
| Start Mode  | AlwaysRunning  |  
| Idle Time-out (minutes)  | 0  |  
| Idle Time-out Action  | Suspend  |  
**3.** Find the application **4.** Open Advanced settings and set the following properties:  
| Name  | Value  |  
| --- | --- |  
| Preload Enabled  | true  |

# Geographic bounding box of OGC services
The NetWorks OGC (WMS, WFS, WMTS) services determine the geographic service territory from the following sources:
  * ServiceConfig.xml (parameter `GeographicBoundingBox`)
  * **GAONET_SERVICES**
  * **G3E_DATACONNECTION**
  * Actual extent of data

To explicitly specify the extent of data specify parameter **GeographicBoundingBox** in the _ServiceConfig.xml_ of the deployed service. Expected format is `{minx},{miny},{maxx},{maxy}`. Use WGS84 coordinates.

```
<provider category="wmts" name="gtechnology" type=".\bin\Intergraph.GTechnology.OGCProviders.dll;Intergraph.GTechnology.OgcProviders.Wmts.GTWmtsProvider">
  <providerSettings>
    <setting name="GeographicBoundingBox" value="-180.0,-85.0511,180.0,85.0511" />
  </providerSettings>
</provider>

```

# GetMap response cache
In order to enable caching WMS GetMap responses in clients, add following line into file **ServiceConfig.xml** under `/ucServiceConfiguration/providers/provider/providerSettings` :
`<setting name="ResponseCacheTimeoutSeconds" value="X"/>`
where `X` specifies caching timeout in seconds.
**Default behavior:**
By default there is no setting and thus no caching, same as `<setting name="ResponseCacheTimeoutSeconds" value=""/>`

# Set TopLeftCorner of WMTS tile matrix set
By default, the NetWorks WMTS service uses the [service territory](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/OGC-Services/Geographic-bounding-box-of-OGC-services.html) for both the bounding box (extent of data) and the origin (`TopLeftCorner` attribute) of the tile matrices.
However, in many cases, these parameters are independent. The data extent might be much smaller than the tile matrix. A typical example is a WMTS with local data, which produces tiles using the standard [Google Maps/OpenStreetMaps tile matrix set](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tiled_web_map).
An explicit top-left position for the tile matrices can be configured in deployed WMTS service _ServiceConfig.xml_ file via the **TopLeftCorner** property. Expected format is `{x},{y}`.

```
<provider category="wmts" name="gtechnology" type=".\bin\Intergraph.GTechnology.OGCProviders.dll;Intergraph.GTechnology.OgcProviders.Wmts.GTWmtsProvider">
  <providerSettings>
    <setting name="TopLeftCorner" value="-20037508.3427892,20037508.368847" />
  </providerSettings>
</provider>

```

# Use alternative URL in GetCapabilities response
The URL included in the GetCapabilities document is derived from the host name (machine or configured in IIS). For OGC services (WMS, WFS, WMTS) published on the Internet this might not be suitable, because the service is published under a publicly visible address, which differs from the actual hostname.
The OGC services can be configured to use alternative external address in the GetCapabilities response.
**Example**
Service is physically published at: `https://internal.company.com/WmsElectric/wms`. GetCapabilities should provide this external URL: `https://gis.company.com/electric/wms`.
## Workflow[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/OGC-Services/Use-alternative-URL-in-GetCapabilities-response.html#workflow)
When deploying the service via Administration Console, set the **External address** property to the full URL of the service as it appears to external clients.
## Manual configuration[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/OGC-Services/Use-alternative-URL-in-GetCapabilities-response.html#manual-configuration)
In a deployed service instance, open the **web.config** and add a new setting **ExternalUri** under the `<appSettings>` element.
**Example**

```
  <appSettings>
    <add key="ServiceConfigFilePath" value="ServiceConfig.xml" />
    <add key="CacheExpirationInMinutes" value="60" />

    <add key="ExternalUri" value="https://gis.company.com/Electric/wms" />

  </appSettings>

```

# WFS geometry types
NetWorks WFS can return XSD for feature types with a **generic** GML type `gml:GeometryPropertyType`. This is the default behavior.

```
 <xs:complexType name="V_E_CONSEG_30500_I_LNType">
        <xs:complexContent mixed="false">
            <xs:extension base="ucgml:V_E_CONSEG_30500_I_LNSubType">
                <xs:sequence>
                    <xs:element minOccurs="0" maxOccurs="1" name="G3E_GEOMETRY" type="gml:GeometryPropertyType" />
                    <xs:element name="G3E_CID" type="xs:long" />
                    <xs:element name="G3E_CNO" type="xs:long" />
                    <xs:element name="G3E_FNO" type="xs:long" />
                    <xs:element name="G3E_FID" type="xs:long" />
                </xs:sequence>
            </xs:extension>
        </xs:complexContent>
    </xs:complexType>

```

It supports also returning a strongly-typed geometry type (**classic** mode, used by NetWorks 1.3).

```
<xs:complexType name="V_E_CONSEG_30600_I_LNType">
  <xs:complexContent mixed="false">
    <xs:extension base="ucgml:V_E_CONSEG_30600_I_LNSubType">
      <xs:sequence>
        <xs:element name="G3E_GEOMETRY" type="ucgml:CompositePolylineGeometry" />
        <xs:element name="G3E_CID" type="xs:long" />
        <xs:element name="G3E_CNO" type="xs:long" />
        <xs:element name="G3E_FNO" type="xs:long" />
        <xs:element name="G3E_FID" type="xs:long" />
      </xs:sequence>
    </xs:extension>
  </xs:complexContent>
</xs:complexType>

```

The behavior can be configured in deployed WFS service _ServiceConfig.xml_ file via the **UseClassicGeometrySchema** or **UseGeometryPropertyType** properties, in this order of precedence.

```
<provider category="wfs" name="gtechnology" type=".\bin\Intergraph.GTechnology.OGCProviders.dll;Intergraph.GTechnology.OgcProviders.Wfs.GTWfsProvider">
  <providerSettings>
    <setting name="UseGeometryPropertyType" value="false" />
    <setting name="UseClassicGeometrySchema" value="false" />
  </providerSettings>
</provider>

```

##### Password-Vault-Service

###### API

# GetCredentials
Returns password mapped to the provided credentials. The API method expects a valid Bearer token.
## Workflow[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Password-Vault-Service/API/GetCredentials.html#workflow)
  * Validate the Bearer token. If not valid, exit with code 401.
  * If necessary, call the OpenID Connect User Info endpoint and retrieve additional claims.
  * Construct the SELECT statement to retrieve the credential using template from configuration. Use parameter values from: 
    * Request URL query parameters.
    * OpenID Connect claims.
  * Open database connection and execute the SELECT.
  * If nothing is returned, exit with code 404.
  * If one or more rows are returned, pick the first two fields from the first row and return them in response as "user" and "password".

## Request[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Password-Vault-Service/API/GetCredentials.html#request)
### URI[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Password-Vault-Service/API/GetCredentials.html#uri)
GET /[?configuration={configuration}][&application={application}]
### Parameters[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Password-Vault-Service/API/GetCredentials.html#parameters)  
| Name  | Type  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| configuration  | string  | NetWorks configuration. Optional.  |  
| application  | string  | Application type. Optional.  |  
## Response[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Password-Vault-Service/API/GetCredentials.html#response)
### Normal response (200)[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Password-Vault-Service/API/GetCredentials.html#normal-response-200)
Credentials.

```
{
  "user": "johndoe",
  "password": "password1"
}

```

### Authentication failure (401)[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Password-Vault-Service/API/GetCredentials.html#authentication-failure-401)
Returned when authorization token is missing or invalid.
### Not Found (404)[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Password-Vault-Service/API/GetCredentials.html#not-found-404)
Returned when the request is valid, but no mapping to user credentials can be found on the server.

# API
  * [GetCredentials](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Password-Vault-Service/API/GetCredentials.html) Get database credentials for the provided access token.

# Configuration
## Configuration files[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Password-Vault-Service/Configuration.html#configuration-files)
See [How service locates configuration files](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Configuration/How-service-locates-configuration-files.html).
## Parameters[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Password-Vault-Service/Configuration.html#parameters)  
| Name  | Description  | Mandatory  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| infrastructureServiceAuthentication:Mode  | Authentication mode. Allowed values:   
* `Bearer` = OpenID Connect.   
* `Anonymous` = Anonymous  | X  |  
| infrastructureServiceAuthentication:Parameters:RequiredClaims  | Comma separated list of claims expected in Bearer token. If not present, the service contacts OIDC UserInfo endpoint to retrieve them.  | X  |  
| infrastructureServiceAuthentication:Parameters:EnableCaching  | Enable caching of user identities.  
  
When `true`, identities are cached and the OIDC UserInfo endpoint is called only once per unique identity if required claims are missing.  
  
When `false`, UserInfo endpoint is called on each request when required claims are missing. Is is strongly recommended to set this property to `true`.  | X  |  
| ConnectionType  | Type of database connection. Allowed values: `oracle`, `sqlserver`.  | X  |  
| ConnectionString  | Database connection string  | X  |  
| Statement  | SELECT statement used to retrieve the credentials from the database. First two fields in the first row must contain values of **user name** and **password** , in this order. Other fields are ignored. Parameters are passed to the statement **by name** , not by ordinal.  | X  |  
| Parameter:{N}:Name  | Name of parameter {N} (zero-based index) in statement.  | X  |  
| Parameter:{N}:SourceType  | Type of source of parameter {N}. Allowed values are: `query`, `claim`, `gtechnologyDBConnect`.  | X  |  
| Parameter:{N}:Source  | Source of parameter {N}.  
  
When SourceType is set to `query`, the value is the name of the URL query parameter.  
  
When SourceType is set to `claim`, the value is the name of the claim in the access token or OIDC UserInfo response.  
  
When SourceType is `gtechnologyDBConnect`, the only allowed value is `user` and the user name is retrieved from the `gtechnologyDBConnect` claim values using URL parameters `configuration` and `application` (optional).  | X  |  
| Parameter:{N}:Transform  | Regular expression to extract the value passed to statement from the source value of parameter {N}. The first matching group is used.  |   |  
| Certificate:Location  | Location of the X.509 certificate store. Allowed values: `LocalMachine`, `CurrentUser`. Default is `LocalMachine`.  |   |  
| Certificate:Store  | X.509 certificate store name. For allowed values see [StoreName Enum](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.security.cryptography.x509certificates.storename). Default is `My`, which maps to _Personal_ certificates folder.  |   |  
| Certificate:FindType  | Certificate attribute used for lookup. For allowed values see [X509FindType Enum](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.security.cryptography.x509certificates.x509findtype). Default is: `FindByThumbprint`.  |   |  
| Certificate:FindValue  | Value used for certificate lookup.  |   |  
| DecryptUsername  | When `true`, the user name retrieved from database is decrypted using configured certificate. Default is `false`.  |   |  
| UsernameEncoding  | Database storage format for encrypted username. Allowed values are `Base64` (encrypted data stored as base-64 string), `Binary` (value stored as varbinary). Default is `Base64`.  |   |  
| DecryptPassword  | When `true`, the password retrieved from database is decrypted using configured certificate. Default is `false`.  |   |  
| PasswordEncoding  | Database storage format for encrypted password. Allowed values are `Base64` (encrypted data stored as base-64 string), `Binary` (value stored as varbinary). Default is `Base64`.  |   |  
| RSA:OAEPHash  | Hash algorithm used for [OAEP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optimal_asymmetric_encryption_padding) (PKCS#1 v2). For allowed values see [CNG Algorithm Identifiers](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/seccng/cng-algorithm-identifiers). Default is `SHA256`.  |   |  
| RSA:Encoding  | Name of text encoding in which the encrypted data is stored. Default is `utf-8`. For reference on values see [GetEncodings](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.text.encoding.getencodings)  |   |  
| TNS_ADMIN  | Path to folder with `tnsnames.ora` file to resolve Oracle TNS names.  |   |  
## Technical notes[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Password-Vault-Service/Configuration.html#technical-notes)
The service uses .NET Core configuration system. For details on how to format configuration files, see [Configuration in ASP.NET Core](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/aspnet/core/fundamentals/configuration/)
## Example 1 - SQL Server[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Password-Vault-Service/Configuration.html#example-1---sql-server)
The DBUSER parameter for SELECT is retrieved from claim `dbuser`. The GTCONFIG parameter for SELECT is retrieved from URL parameter `configuration`.
ServiceConfig.ini file content:

```
infrastructureServiceAuthentication:Mode=Bearer
infrastructureServiceAuthentication:Parameters:RequiredClaims=dbuser
infrastructureServiceAuthentication:Parameters:EnableCaching=true

ConnectionType=sqlserver
ConnectionString=Server=server1;Initial Catalog=PasswordVault;Trusted_Connection=True

Statement=SELECT DBUSERNAME, DBPASSWORD FROM USERMAPPING WHERE DBUSERNAME=@DBUSER AND GTCONFIG=@GTCONFIG

Parameters:0:Name=DBUSER
Parameters:0:SourceType=claim
Parameters:0:Source=dbuser

Parameters:1:Name=GTCONFIG
Parameters:1:SourceType=query
Parameters:1:Source=configuration

```

## Example 2 - SQL Server, gtechnologyDBConnect[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Password-Vault-Service/Configuration.html#example-2---sql-server-gtechnologydbconnect)
The DBUSER parameter for SELECT is retrieved from claim `gtechnologyDBConnect`. URL query parameters `configuration` and `application` are used when determining the correct _gtechnologyDBConnect_ value if multiple are present.  
The GTCONFIG parameter for SELECT is retrieved from URL parameter `configuration`.  
The GTAPP parameter for SELECT is retrieved from URL parameter `application`.
The SELECT statement tries to find rows with the most matching values. The most relevant row is returned first.
ServiceConfig.ini file content:

```
infrastructureServiceAuthentication:Mode=Bearer
infrastructureServiceAuthentication:Parameters:RequiredClaims=gtechnologyDBConnect
infrastructureServiceAuthentication:Parameters:EnableCaching=true

ConnectionType=sqlserver
ConnectionString=Server=.;Initial Catalog=PasswordVault;Trusted_Connection=True
Statement=SELECT DBUSERNAME, DBPASSWORD, GTConfiguration, GTApplication FROM USERMAPPING WHERE DBUSERNAME = @DBUSER AND GTConfiguration = @GTCONFIG AND GTApplication = @GTAPP UNION ALL SELECT DBUSERNAME, DBPASSWORD, GTConfiguration, GTApplication FROM USERMAPPING WHERE DBUSERNAME = @DBUSER AND GTConfiguration = @GTCONFIG AND GTApplication IS NULL UNION ALL SELECT DBUSERNAME, DBPASSWORD, GTConfiguration, GTApplication FROM USERMAPPING WHERE DBUSERNAME = @DBUSER AND GTConfiguration IS NULL AND GTApplication IS NULL

Parameters:0:Name=DBUSER
Parameters:0:SourceType=gtechnologyDBConnect
Parameters:0:Source=user

Parameters:1:Name=GTCONFIG
Parameters:1:SourceType=query
Parameters:1:Source=configuration

Parameters:2:Name=GTAPP
Parameters:2:SourceType=query
Parameters:2:Source=application

```

## Example 3 - Oracle, gtechnologyDBConnect[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Password-Vault-Service/Configuration.html#example-3---oracle-gtechnologydbconnect)
The DBUSER parameter for SELECT is retrieved from claim `gtechnologyDBConnect`. URL query parameters `configuration` and `application` are used when determining the correct _gtechnologyDBConnect_ value if multiple values are present.  
The GTCONFIG parameter for SELECT is retrieved from URL parameter `configuration`.  
The GTAPP parameter for SELECT is retrieved from URL parameter `application`.
Table used in example:

```
CREATE TABLE USERMAPPING
(
  GTCONFIGURATION VARCHAR2(50) NOT NULL,
  DBUSERNAME VARCHAR2(30) NOT NULL,
  DBPASSWORD  VARCHAR2(200) NOT NULL,
  CONSTRAINT PK_USERMAPPING PRIMARY KEY (GTCONFIGURATION, DBUSERNAME)
);

```

The SELECT statement tries to find rows with the most matching values. The most relevant row is returned first.
ServiceConfig.ini file content:

```
infrastructureServiceAuthentication:Mode=Bearer
infrastructureServiceAuthentication:Parameters:RequiredClaims=gtechnologyDBConnect
infrastructureServiceAuthentication:Parameters:EnableCaching=true

ConnectionType=oracle
ConnectionString=Data Source=PROD;User Id=userxxx;Password=pwdxxx;
TNS_ADMIN=C:\Oracle\network\admin

Statement=SELECT DBUSERNAME, DBPASSWORD FROM USERMAPPING WHERE DBUSERNAME = :DBUSER AND GTConfiguration = :GTCONFIG UNION ALL SELECT DBUSERNAME, DBPASSWORD FROM USERMAPPING WHERE DBUSERNAME = :DBUSER AND GTConfiguration IS NULL

Parameters:0:Name=DBUSER
Parameters:0:SourceType=gtechnologyDBConnect
Parameters:0:Source=user

Parameters:1:Name=GTCONFIG
Parameters:1:SourceType=query
Parameters:1:Source=configuration

Parameters:2:Name=GTAPP
Parameters:2:SourceType=query
Parameters:2:Source=application

```

## Example 4 - SQL Server, encrypted password[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Password-Vault-Service/Configuration.html#example-4---sql-server-encrypted-password)
The DBUSER parameter for SELECT is retrieved from claim `dbuser`. The GTCONFIG parameter for SELECT is retrieved from URL parameter `configuration`.
The X.509 certificate used for decryption is retrieved from the Windows Certificate store for Local machine, Personal (=My).
The DBPASSWORDENCRYPTED field in the database must contain a string with encrypted data encoded in **Base64**.
ServiceConfig.ini file content:

```
infrastructureServiceAuthentication:Mode=Bearer
infrastructureServiceAuthentication:Parameters:RequiredClaims=dbuser
infrastructureServiceAuthentication:Parameters:EnableCaching=true

ConnectionType=sqlserver
ConnectionString=Server=server1;Initial Catalog=PasswordVault;Trusted_Connection=True

Statement=SELECT DBUSERNAME, DBPASSWORDENCRYPTED FROM USERMAPPING WHERE DBUSERNAME=@DBUSER AND GTCONFIG=@GTCONFIG

Parameters:0:Name=DBUSER
Parameters:0:SourceType=claim
Parameters:0:Source=dbuser

Parameters:1:Name=GTCONFIG
Parameters:1:SourceType=query
Parameters:1:Source=configuration

Certificate:Location=LocalMachine
Certificate:Store=My
Certificate:FindType=FindByThumbprint
Certificate:FindValue=34c672813eb54553438b67f896e1ef08415e47c7

RSA:OAEPHash=SHA256

DecryptPassword=true

```

## Example 5 - Oracle, user retrieved from custom claim[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Password-Vault-Service/Configuration.html#example-5---oracle-user-retrieved-from-custom-claim)
The DBUSER parameter for SELECT is retrieved from claim `credentials`, expected in format `user/[password]@configuration`. The value is retrieved from the claim using a regular expression. The GTCONFIG parameter for SELECT is retrieved from URL parameter `configuration`.
ServiceConfig.ini file.

```
infrastructureServiceAuthentication:Mode=Bearer
infrastructureServiceAuthentication:Parameters:RequiredClaims=credentials
infrastructureServiceAuthentication:Parameters:EnableCaching=true

ConnectionType=oracle
ConnectionString=Data Source=PROD;User Id=userxxx;Password=pwdxxx;
TNS_ADMIN=C:\Oracle\network\admin

Statement=SELECT DBUSERNAME, DBPASSWORD, GTConfiguration, GTApplication FROM USERMAPPING WHERE DBUSERNAME = :DBUSER AND GTConfiguration = :GTCONFIG UNION ALL SELECT DBUSERNAME, DBPASSWORD, GTConfiguration, GTApplication FROM USERMAPPING WHERE DBUSERNAME = :DBUSER AND GTConfiguration IS NULL

Parameters:0:Name=DBUSER
Parameters:0:SourceType=claim
Parameters:0:Source=credentials
Parameters:0:Transform=^(\w+)[/]

Parameters:1:Name=GTCONFIG
Parameters:1:SourceType=query
Parameters:1:Source=configuration

```

## See also[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Password-Vault-Service/Configuration.html#see-also)
  * [Microsoft.Data.SqlClient connection strings](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/microsoft.data.sqlclient.sqlconnection.connectionstring)

# Deployment
## Software requirements[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Password-Vault-Service/Deployment.html#software-requirements)

## Manual Deployment[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Password-Vault-Service/Deployment.html#manual-deployment)
  1. Create folder on the disk for the service instance. This will be referred to as `SERVICEDIR` in following text.
  2. Unzip the contents of the folder in _PasswordVaultServicePackage.zip_ which contains _Hxgn.NetWorks.PasswordVault.ServiceHost.exe_ to `SERVICEDIR`.
  3. Open IIS Manager
  4. Create App. pool in IIS Manager with the following properties: 
     * Name: 
     * .NET CLR Version: _No Managed Code_
     * Managed Pipeline Mode: _Integrated_
     * Identity: Use account which has access to databases (if required).
  5. Create application under `Default Web Site` (or other site) 
     * Alias:

     * Physical path: Use actual `SERVICEDIR` value

###### Encryption

# EncryptString.exe
**EncryptString.exe** is a command line tool for encryption of string values using X.509 certificate. It also support decryption when the private key of the X.509 is available.
## Usage[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Password-Vault-Service/Encryption/EncryptString.exe.html#usage)
EncryptString.exe   
| Parameter  | Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
| verb  | Allowed values: `e` - encrypt input string and return Base64 string, `ehex` - encrypt input string and return binary data in hexadecimal format, `d` - decrypt input Base64 string.  |  
| input-string  | String to encrypt or decrypt.  |  
## Configuration[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Password-Vault-Service/Encryption/EncryptString.exe.html#configuration)
File **EncryptString.ini**.  
| Name  | Description  | Mandatory  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| Certificate:Location  | Location of the X.509 certificate store. Allowed values: `LocalMachine`, `CurrentUser`. Default is `LocalMachine`.  |   |  
| Certificate:Store  | X.509 certificate store name. For allowed values see [StoreName Enum](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.security.cryptography.x509certificates.storename). Default is `My`, which maps to _Personal_ certificates folder.  |   |  
| Certificate:FindType  | Certificate attribute used for lookup. For allowed values see [X509FindType Enum](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.security.cryptography.x509certificates.x509findtype). Default is: `FindByThumbprint`.  |   |  
| Certificate:FindValue  | Value used for certificate lookup.  | X when Certificate:File is empty.  |  
| Certificate:File  | Path to X.509 certificate file. When present, the file is loaded form the disk instead of Windows Certificate store.  | X when Certificate:FindValue is empty.  |  
| Certificate:Password  | Password to access private key of the certificate. Can be used in conjunction with Certificate:File to decrypt data using file-based certificate. Designed for testing only.  |   |  
| RSA:OAEPHash  | Hash algorithm used for [OAEP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optimal_asymmetric_encryption_padding) (PKCS#1 v2). For allowed values see [CNG Algorithm Identifiers](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/seccng/cng-algorithm-identifiers). Default is `SHA256`.  |   |  
| RSA:Encoding  | Name of text encoding in which the encrypted data is stored. Default is `utf-8`. For reference on values see [GetEncodings](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.text.encoding.getencodings)  |   |

# Encryption
Password Vault Service supports storage of credentials (user name and password) in encrypted format. The supported encryption algorithm is RSA with OAEP padding as defined in standard PKCS #1 v2.0. An X.509 certificate with private key, stored in the Windows Certificate store must be available to the Password Vault Service app. pool identity.
## Storage[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Password-Vault-Service/Encryption.html#storage)
The encrypted content may be stored in the database as:
  * **strings** VARCHAR/NVARCHAR data type, i.e. binary data with Base64 encoding.
  * **binary** VARBINARY data type.

The decrypted data (byte array) is expected to contain a string value in specified text encoding. Default is **UTF-8** , other values can be configured.
## How Password Vault Service works with encrypted data[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Password-Vault-Service/Encryption.html#how-password-vault-service-works-with-encrypted-data)
  * Read value from database.
  * If Base64, decode to byte array.
  * Decrypt byte array using the private key of the X.509 certificate.
  * Decode decrypted data to string using configured encoding.

## How to encrypt values for Password Vault Service[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Password-Vault-Service/Encryption.html#how-to-encrypt-values-for-password-vault-service)
  * Encode source string using specified text encoding (e.g. UTF-8).
  * Encrypt string binary data using public key of the X.509 certificate.
  * Write to database - as binary or Base64 encoded value.

# Password Vault Service Legacy
## Overview[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Password-Vault-Service-Legacy.html#overview)
Password Vault Service Legacy is a HTTP REST API service. Its purpose is to return credentials mapped to the user identified by the OpenID Connect access token. Unlike [Password Vault Service](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Password-Vault-Service.html), the credentials are stored in **Password Vault Manager** storage on the file system.
For REST API see [Password Vault Service](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Password-Vault-Service.html).

# Password Vault Service
## Overview[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Password-Vault-Service.html#overview)
Password Vault Service is a HTTP REST API service. Its purpose is to return credentials mapped to the user identified by the OpenID Connect access token. The credentials are stored in a database storage (SQL Server or Oracle). The storage data model and query used to retrieve data are fully configurable.
Password Vault Service can be integrated to NetWorks services OpenID Connect workflows. It replaces the existing user mapping architecture based on passing _gtechnologyDBConnect_ claim with Oracle credentials mapped to NetWorks configurations.
## Architecture[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Password-Vault-Service.html#architecture)
[![Password_Vault_Service_Architecture_v01.svg](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/.attachments/Password_Vault_Service_Architecture_v01-f041f792-0eff-4557-83e3-2d42d057cb70.svg)](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/.attachments/Password_Vault_Service_Architecture_v01-f041f792-0eff-4557-83e3-2d42d057cb70.svg)
## Workflow[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Password-Vault-Service.html#workflow)
[![Password_vault_service_sequence.svg](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/.attachments/Password_vault_service_sequence-1eb7c85f-db39-4b58-a4f6-36efac62a1f7.svg)](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/.attachments/Password_vault_service_sequence-1eb7c85f-db39-4b58-a4f6-36efac62a1f7.svg)
### Processing in Networks services[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Password-Vault-Service.html#processing-in-networks-services)
  * Service receives a request with OIDC access token
  * Access token is validated by the service OIDC infrastructure. If not valid, the request execution stops.
  * Service calls the Password Vault Service via HTTP. The access token is sent in the HTTP Authorization header.
  * Password Vault Service resolves the access token and information from request URL to credentials and returns this in the response.
  * Service receives mapped credentials. Any _gtechnologyDBConnect_ claim in current user identity is replaced with the mapped credentials.
  * Subsequent processing in the request works with new _gtechnologyDBConnect_ connect string.
