# Usage Tracking Service
## Overview[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Usage-Tracking-Service.html#overview)
Usage Tracking solution is an Windows Service running in background, which aggregates calls to NetWorks Web Service endpoints in specified time range and records the statistics in CSV files.
## Architecture[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Usage-Tracking-Service.html#architecture)
[![image.png](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/.attachments/image-8292860f-6333-4a8e-b800-34cb037abd5c.png)](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/.attachments/image-8292860f-6333-4a8e-b800-34cb037abd5c.png)
## Components[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Usage-Tracking-Service.html#components)
### Action Filter[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Usage-Tracking-Service.html#action-filter)
  * Invoked every time a networks' endpoint is called
  * Sends service, controller and action names as a metric name to Event Counter

### Event Counter[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Usage-Tracking-Service.html#event-counter)
  * Aggregates incoming metrics into collection: [metric][count of requests]
  * Sends this collections on specific time period into Windows Service that collect them
  * Restarts the counters every time after it sends data into Windows Service

### Usage Tracking Service[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Usage-Tracking-Service.html#usage-tracking-service-1)
  * On specific time period (by default 10 minutes, configurable) collects via Event Tracing For Windows data from Event Counters
  * Writes data into csv files.

## Reports[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Usage-Tracking-Service.html#reports)
Reports are created on daily basis, and can be found in `C:\ProgramData\Intergraph\NetWorks\Reports`.
## Deployment[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Usage-Tracking-Service.html#deployment)
Usage Tracking Service is automatically deployed by the NetWorks Configuration Wizard.

##### Vector-Service

###### Configuration

# Limit number of features in response
For safety reasons, the Vector Service now imposes a limit on the number of features returned in a single response from the `/data` endpoint. The default is 100000. The value is configurable using configuration value `GeoJSON:FeatureLimit`.
This measure is needed to prevent excessive memory allocation when clients request data with scale dependency turned off.

# Role restricted access to data in Anonymous mode
Vector Service uses the default database user configured for the service to restrict access to metadata and data based on database roles of the user. This behavior is the default from version 02.00.2101.
To turn this behavior off, set the `UseDefaultIdentity` setting to `false`. When set to `false`, the database roles of the user are ignored and Vector Service does not restrict metadata by G3E_ROLE.
## Related topics[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Vector-Service/Configuration/Role-restricted-access-to-data-in-Anonymous-mode.html#related-topics)
  * [Vector Service Configuration](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Vector-Service/Configuration.html)

# Configuration
## Common Parameters[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Vector-Service/Configuration.html#common-parameters)
See [Common Configuration Parameters](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Configuration/Common-Service-Configuration-Parameters.html).
## Specific Parameters[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Vector-Service/Configuration.html#specific-parameters)
###  `G3E_LSNO`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Vector-Service/Configuration.html#g3e_lsno)
G3E_LSNO of a pre-loaded legend. Preloading slightly speeds up startup of the service.
###  `Deltas:RefreshMinutes`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Vector-Service/Configuration.html#deltasrefreshminutes)
Number of minutes between checks for new `.deltas` file. Expected: a number > 0. Default: `10`.
###  `GeoJSON:UseVertexReduction`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Vector-Service/Configuration.html#geojsonusevertexreduction)
Turn vertex reduction for GeoJSON on/off. Allowed values: `true`, `false`. Default: `true`.
###  `GeoJSON:PPI`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Vector-Service/Configuration.html#geojsonppi)
PPI used to compute scale from resolution. Default: `96`.
###  `GeoJSON:InchesPerGroundUnit`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Vector-Service/Configuration.html#geojsoninchespergroundunit)
Inches per CS ground unit. Default: `39.37` (=inches per meter).
###  `GeoJSON:Decimals`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Vector-Service/Configuration.html#geojsondecimals)
Number of decimal digits in coordinates. Default: `3`.
###  `GeoJSON:Dimensions`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Vector-Service/Configuration.html#geojsondimensions)
Number of dimensions in coordinates in the output. When set to 3, the Z value is included. Default: `2`.
###  `GeoJSON:Resolution`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Vector-Service/Configuration.html#geojsonresolution)
Default resolution to use for arc densification. Default: `0.01`.
###  `GeoJSON:FeatureLimit`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Vector-Service/Configuration.html#geojsonfeaturelimit)
Maximum number of features to return in a single response. Set to empty string (INI) or `null` (JSON) to disable. Expected: a number > 0. Default: `100000`.
###  `GeoJSON:ClippingMode`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Vector-Service/Configuration.html#geojsonclippingmode)
Clipping mode for polyline geometries in output of APIs restricted by bbox. Allowed values:
  * `VisibleSegments` - Output all polyline segments which intersect the bbox. The segments are not clipped. This is the default.
  * `ClipToView` - Output all polyline segments which intersect bbox, clipped to the bbox.
  * `Disabled` - No clipping. Behavior as in 2101 and before. Polyline geometries are not clipped.

###  `GeoJson:ClipPolygons`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Vector-Service/Configuration.html#geojsonclippolygons)
Clipping mode for polygon geometries in output of APIs restricted by bbox. Allowed values: `true`, `false`. Default is `true`.
###  `Tooltips:ComponentViewTooltipTemplate`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Vector-Service/Configuration.html#tooltipscomponentviewtooltiptemplate)
Alternative format for component view tooltip template. See [Tooltip parameters](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Vector-Service/Configuration.html#tooltip-parameters). Default: `[G3E_TOOLTIP|G3E_USERNAME] [G3E_FID]`.
###  `Tooltips:FeatureClassTooltipTemplate`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Vector-Service/Configuration.html#tooltipsfeatureclasstooltiptemplate)
Alternative format for feature class tooltip template. See [Tooltip parameters](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Vector-Service/Configuration.html#tooltip-parameters). Default: `[G3E_TOOLTIP|G3E_USERNAME]`.
###  `Tooltips:FeatureTooltipTemplate`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Vector-Service/Configuration.html#tooltipsfeaturetooltiptemplate)
Alternative format for feature instance tooltip template. See [Tooltip parameters](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Vector-Service/Configuration.html#tooltip-parameters) Default: `[G3E_TOOLTIP|G3E_USERNAME] [G3E_FID]`.
###  `Tooltips:UseFormattedTooltips`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Vector-Service/Configuration.html#tooltipsuseformattedtooltips)
When `true`, formatted feature instance tooltips based on `G3E_FEATURE`.`G3E_IDENTIFIERVIEW` are produced. Allowed values: `true`, `false`. Default: `true`.
###  `Map:ExpandByFixed`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Vector-Service/Configuration.html#mapexpandbyfixed)
Number of ground units to be added to the bounding box when retrieving data. This value enhances retrieval of text and point geometries at low scales. Expected: a number > 0. Default: `10`.
###  `Map:ExpandByRelative`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Vector-Service/Configuration.html#mapexpandbyrelative)
Expand factor for the bounding box when reading data. 1.0 = no expansion. 1.2 = 20% increase in width/height. Expected: A decimal number >= 1. Default: `1.0`.
###  `Style:FontMetricsFile`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Vector-Service/Configuration.html#stylefontmetricsfile)
Path to JSON file with custom [font metrics](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/portal/Map-display/Use-custom-font-metrics-to-fix-rendering-of-symbol-and-text-fonts.html) file.

| [G3E_CNO]  | G3E_CNO  |

# Deltas and jobs
Vector Service supports both master and job deltas. The mechanism is slightly different in both cases.
## Master deltas[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Vector-Service/Deltas-and-jobs.html#master-deltas)
Vector Service uses the output from the Deltas Service (_.deltas_ files) for master deltas (i.e. posted data). Master deltas are merged with data from DDC to the GeoJSON output. Vector Service checks for new deltas in periodic intervals, not on each request. Location of the _.deltas_ file is determined from the [ConfigurationProperties.txt file](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Configuration/ConfigurationProperties.txt-file.html) file.
**Workflow**
  * Deltas Service runs in the background and periodically checks for deltas in database. If there are new master deltas available, Deltas Service exports them to a new _.deltas_ file. Deltas check interval is configurable using [Configuration](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Deltas-Service/Configuration.html), default is 10 minutes.
  * Vector Service periodically checks for new _.deltas_ files. If there is a new _.deltas_ file, Vector Service loads it and replaces the original deltas loaded in memory. The time interval for checking is configurable using [Configuration](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Vector-Service/Configuration.html), default is 10 minutes.

**Notes**
  * Since both Deltas and Vector Services use periodic checking, it is possible that posted master deltas appear in the Vector Service output with a delay. With default settings (10 + 10 minutes), the change may be delayed up to 20 minutes. It is possible to shorten this interval in configuration to approx. 2 minutes (1+1).

## Job deltas[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Vector-Service/Deltas-and-jobs.html#job-deltas)
Vector Service fetches job deltas directly from database upon first request which includes the job in the parameters. Job deltas are kept in memory for a time. Subsequent requests do not fetch deltas for the same job from database, unless the request includes the `force=1` parameter (see [Vector Service API](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/NetWorks-internal/Obsolete/API/Vector-Service.md)).
Vector Service calls the Coordinate System Service to transform coordinates from storage projection to configuration projection.

###### Deployment

# Command line deployment
The Vector Service can be semi-automatically deployed and undeployed from the command line using the [DeployVectorService.exe](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/Command-line-deployment-tools.html) tool.
## Workflow - deployment[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Vector-Service/Deployment/Command-line-deployment.html#workflow---deployment)
  1. Create or edit service instance in **NetWorksDeployedServices.xml**.

NetWorks keeps track of service instances in XML file `c:\ProgramData\Intergraph\NetWorks\DeployedServices\NetWorksDeployedServices.xml`.
To register a new instance of the Vector Service, open the file in a text editor (e.g. Notepad) and add new element under the `<NetWorksDeployedServices>` element, e.g.:

```
<VectorService InstanceName="VectorServiceINSTANCE1" 
               IsInSolution="False" 
               InstanceId="VectorServiceINSTANCE1"
               Definition="Vector Service"  
                />

```

### Additional parameters[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Vector-Service/Deployment/Command-line-deployment.html#additional-parameters)  
| Name  | Description  | Mandatory  | Default Value  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| InstanceName  | Unique name of the service instance.  | Y  |   |  
| IsInSolution  | Flag. Must be set to `False`  | Y  |   |  
| InstanceId  | GUID of the instance  |   |   |  
| Definition  | Name of service definition  | Y  | Vector Service  |  
| ConnectionInfo  | NetWorks connection string formatted as `user/password@configuration`.   
Accepts values encrypted using `GTEncTool.exe`.  | Y  |   |  
| PhysicalPath  | Path to folder where the service will be deployed. The value can contain environment variable placeholders via `%variable%` convention.  | Y  |   |  
| VirtualPath  | Virtual path for IIS deployment. Typically `<site name>`/`<InstanceName>`, where `<site name>` is usually `Default Web Site`.  | Y  |   |  
| AppPoolName  | IIS Application Pool Name. Typically set to `InstanceName` + `Pool`.  | Y  |   |  
| AppPoolIdentityType  | IIS Application Pool identity type. [Allowed values](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/microsoft.web.administration.processmodelidentitytype?view=iis-dotnet).  |   | 4  |  
| AppPoolUserName  | IIS Application Pool User name. When not specified, the built-in ApplicationPoolIdentity is used.  
**Note**  
The account must have access to the published metadata and data files.  |   |   |  
| AppPoolPassword  | IIS Application Pool Password. Accepts values encrypted using `GTEncTool.exe`.  |   |   |  
| LCID  | Locale identifier for metadata access. When not specified, the default locale of the account is used  |   |   |  
| Deltas__RefreshMinutes  | Period in which the service checks for new .deltas files published by Deltas Service, in minutes.  |   | 10  |  
| CoordinateSystem__Code  | OGC code of the coordinate system (typically `EPSG:NNNN`). If not specified, `G3E_CONFIGURATIONS_OPTABLE`.`G3E_OGCCRSNAME` is used  |   |   |  
| CoordinateSystem__Proj4String  | Proj4 string with specification of the coordinate system parameters. If not specified, the value is extracted from `CRSConfig_v2.xml` for code `CoordinateSystem__Code`  |   |   |  
| TNS_ADMIN  | Path to folder containing Oracle `tnsnames.ora` file.  |   |   |  
| AuthenticationType  | Type of authentication. Allowed values:   
* `OIDC` - OpenID Connect   
* `Anonymous`  |   | Anonymous  |  
| LoggingType  | Default logging level. Allowed values: `Error`, `Warn`, `Info`, `Trace`.  |   | Error  |  
### Example[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Vector-Service/Deployment/Command-line-deployment.html#example)

```
<VectorService 
   InstanceName="VectorServiceINSTANCE1" 
   IsInSolution="False" 
   InstanceId="VectorServiceINSTANCE1" 
   Definition="Vector Service"
   ConnectionInfo="user/password@CONFIGURATION" 
   PhysicalPath="%SystemDrive%\inetpub\wwwroot\VectorServiceINSTANCE1" 
   VirtualPath="Default Web Site/VectorServiceINSTANCE1" 
   AppPoolName="VectorServiceINSTANCE1Pool" 
   AppPoolUserName="" 
   AppPoolPassword="" 
   LCID="0009"
   AuthenticationType="OIDC" 
   LoggingType="Error" 
 />

```

  1. Start **Command Prompt** (`cmd.exe`) **as Administrator**
  2. Navigate to NetWorks Program folder, typically `cd c:\Program Files (x86)\Intergraph\NetWorks\Program\`
  3. Deploy the service instance by executing `DeployVectorService.exe -i <service instance>`

## Workflow - undeployment[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Vector-Service/Deployment/Command-line-deployment.html#workflow---undeployment)
  1. Create or edit service instance in **NetWorksDeployedServices.xml** as in **Workflow - deployment**
  2. Start **Command Prompt** (`cmd.exe`) **as Administrator**
  3. Navigate to NetWorks Program folder, typically `cd c:\Program Files (x86)\Intergraph\NetWorks\Program\`
  4. Undeploy the service instance by executing `DeployVectorService.exe -i <service instance> -u`

## Workflow - redeployment[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Vector-Service/Deployment/Command-line-deployment.html#workflow---redeployment)
As **Deployment** , except for step
  1. Redeploy the service instance by executing `DeployVectorService.exe -i <service instance> -r`

# Manual deployment
## Workflow[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Vector-Service/Deployment/Manual-deployment.html#workflow)
  1. Create folder on the disk for the service instance. This will be referred to as `SERVICEDIR` in following text.
  2. Unzip the contents of the service template folder containing `Hxgn.Intergraph.GTechnology.Vector.ServiceHost.exe` to `SERVICEDIR`.
  3. [Configure the service](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Vector-Service/Configuration.html).
  4. Open IIS Manager
  5. Create App. pool in IIS Manager with the following properties: 
     * Name: 
     * .NET CLR Version: _No Managed Code_
     * Managed Pipeline Mode: _Integrated_
     * Identity: Use account which has access to the published metadata and DDC files
  6. Create application under `Default Web Site` (or other site) 
     * Alias: 
     * Application Pool: Use pool created above
     * Physical path: Use actual `SERVICEDIR` value

# Diagnostics
The service uses **ETW** ([Event Tracing for Windows](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/etw/about-event-tracing)) to produce and collect events during runtime.
**NLog** is used to write events to log files. It is configured using `NLog.config`, which is expected at the same location as other configuration files.
## How to turn on tracing[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Vector-Service/Diagnostics.html#how-to-turn-on-tracing)
  * Locate the file `NLog.config`
  * Open the file in a text editor (e.g. Notepad)
  * Set the log level for `file` output to `Trace`

```
<logger name="*" minlevel="Trace" writeTo="file" />

```

  * Save the file
  * Restart the app. pool for the service
  * Execute diagnosed workflow
  * Check the log file (by default under `c:\ProgramData\Intergraph\NetWorks\Logs\`)

## Related topics[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Vector-Service/Diagnostics.html#related-topics)
  * [ETW Listener configuration](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Diagnostics.html)
  * [ETW Event Sources](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Diagnostics/ETW-Event-Sources.html)

# Filter operators
Vector Service SDK supports the following operators in filter clauses - style, label, legend filter and other filtering rules.
## Comparison operators[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Vector-Service/Filter-operators.html#comparison-operators)  
| Operator  | Description  | Example  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| =  | Equals  | `CATEGORY = '1'`  |  
| <>  | Not equals  | `CATEGORY <> '1'`  |  
| >  | Greater than  | `WIDTH > 10.0`  |  
| <  | Less than  | `WIDTH < 10.0`  |  
| >=  | Greater or equal than  | `WIDTH >= 10.0`  |  
| <=  | Less or equal than  | `WIDTH <= 10.0`  |  
| BETWEEN  | Between `min` and `max`, inclusive  | `WIDTH BETWEEN 10.0 AND 20.0`  |  
| IN  | In a list of values  | `CATEGORY IN ('1', '2', '3')`  |  
| LIKE  | String matching. Use `%` as wildcard for 0..N characters, `_` to match one character.  | `NAME LIKE '%electric%'`  |  
| IS NULL  | NULL check  | `NAME IS NULL`  |  
BETWEEN, IN, LIKE and IS NULL support also negation: `NOT BETWEEN`, `NOT IN`, `NOT LIKE` and `IS NOT NULL`.
All string comparisons are **case-insensitive**.
## Constants[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Vector-Service/Filter-operators.html#constants)  
| Operator  | Description  | Example  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| NULL  | Null value  | `NULL`  |  
## Data types[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Vector-Service/Filter-operators.html#data-types)  
| Data type  | Description  | Example  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| String  | Character string delimited by apostrophes (`'`). Use double apostrophe (`''`) to use an apostrophe within the string constant  | `'ABC'`  |  
| Integer  | Numeric value in -2^32+1..2^32-1 range.  | `123`  |  
| Double  | Floating point value. Dot (`.`) is used as decimal separator. Grouping separators are not allowed.  | `123.45`  |  
##### Note
Care must be taken when using comparison operators which mix integer and double values. Always match the data type of constants with the field data type.
## Logical operators[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Vector-Service/Filter-operators.html#logical-operators)  
| Operator  | Description  | Example  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| AND  | Logical AND  | `VALUE > 1 AND VALUE < 5`  |  
| OR  | Logical OR  | `VALUE > 1 OR VALUE < 5`  |  
| NOT  | Negation  | `NOT (VALUE > 1)`  |  
## Brackets[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Vector-Service/Filter-operators.html#brackets)
Brackets `()` should be used to enclose subexpressions which are evaluated as one unit.
Examples:
`VALUE > 1 AND (CATEGORY = '2' OR CATEGORY = '3')`
## Whitespace[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Vector-Service/Filter-operators.html#whitespace)
Whitespace between operands and operators is not significant.
## Legacy mode[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Vector-Service/Filter-operators.html#legacy-mode)
Beginning with version 11.01.2302, filter parsing and execution was reimplemented. Legacy parsing and execution mode is still available. To turn on Legacy mode, set environment variable `NW_USE_LEGACY_FILTERING` to a non-empty value.

# Vector Service
**Overview**
Vector Service is a Web Service which provides NetWorks feature data in GeoJSON format. The data is read from published DDC files and merged with master Deltas (if configured).
One service instance provides data for a single NetWorks configuration and LCID. A single service is able to provide data for all configured legends, including Detail and Schematic (persisted) legends.
**Features**
  * Style and label rules evaluation
  * Legend entry filters evaluation
  * API for retrieval of style definitions, legend display control, tooltips, coordinate system information
  * OpenID Connect support and role-based authorization
  * Dimension components (since 02.00.2101)
  * Master and job deltas support

**Not supported features**
  * Raster geometries
  * Attached CAD files
  * Attached redlines

**Architecture**
[![VectorService_Architecture_v03.svg](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/.attachments/VectorService_Architecture_v03-45dc3b15-879e-496b-93e6-e7fba2568e95.svg)](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/.attachments/VectorService_Architecture_v03-45dc3b15-879e-496b-93e6-e7fba2568e95.svg)
**Components**
**Vector Service**
  * Deliver vectorized geometry data (e.g. as GeoJSON) to map clients
  * Use published DDC and Deltas to deliver up-to-date map data
  * Evaluate style and label rules, legend entry filters
  * Return legend in granularity matching NetWorks

**Deltas Service**
  * Periodically read deltas from database and export them to `.deltas` files in configured `DELTASDIRECTORY`

**Coordinate System Service**
  * Provide Coordinate information and transformation for export of deltas from database for both Deltas and Vector service.

**Related topics**
  * [Supported functionality](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Vector-Service/Supported-functionality.html)
  * [ConfigurationProperties.txt file](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Configuration/ConfigurationProperties.txt-file.html)
  * [How service locates configuration files](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Configuration/How-service-locates-configuration-files.html)

# Configuration
The service configuration file, `appsettings.json` is located in the instance deployment directory as defined in deployment tool configuration file, typically `C:\ProgramData\Intergraph\NetWorks\ServiceInstances\Default`. Definitions for individual service jobs are located under `Quartz` / `JobDefinitions` section.
## Job Definitions[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/WarmUp-Service/Configuration.html#job-definitions)
**ServiceType** Type of the service that this definition is valid for. This corresponds to the element name of service definition in the `NetWorksDeployedServices.xml` file.
**ServiceName** Name of the specific service, corresponding to the attribute _InstanceName_ in deployed services file. If omitted, definition is valid for all services of given type.
**Command** URL address of requested service resource. The address is relative to the _VirtualPath_ attribute of service definition.
**HttpMethod** HTTP method of the request. Only `GET` (default) and `POST` are supported.
**RequestBody** Content of request body, if needed.
**CronExpression** Expression defining when to fire the request. It is actually six or seven sub-expressions separated with white-space:
  * **Seconds** (0-59)
  * **Minutes** (0-59)
  * **Hours** (0-23)
  * **Day of Month** (0-31)
  * **Month** (0-11) or (JAN-DEC)
  * **Day of Week** (1-7) or (SUN-SAT) note: **1=SUN**
  * **Year** (optional)

Every sub-expression can contain range and/or list. Wildcard '*' can be used for all possible values. For days, '?' means 'no specific value', if either day-of-week or day-of-month is specified, but not the other. Expressions with '/' means increments in given scope, thus '0/15' in minutes sub-expression means 'every 15 minutes', or, in list form '0,15,30,45'. For more details see [Quartz.NET CronTrigger documentation](https://www.quartz-scheduler.net/documentation/quartz-3.x/tutorial/crontriggers.html)

# Deployment
Service Warm-Up Tool is deployed using **DeployWarmUpService.exe** command line tool. The tool is located in the NetWorks Program folder, typically `C:\Program Files (x86)\Intergraph\NetWorks\Program\`.
## Usage[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/WarmUp-Service/Deployment.html#usage)
`DeployWarmUpService.exe [-i <instance-name>] [-u] [-r]`
## Options[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/WarmUp-Service/Deployment.html#options)
**-i** `DeployWarmUpService.exe.config` is used.
**-u** Undeploy service.
**-r** Redeploy service.
## Configuration file[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/WarmUp-Service/Deployment.html#configuration-file)
Some configuration options are available in the _appSettings_ section of the deployment tool configuration file - `DeployWarmUpService.exe.config`.  
| Parameter  | Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
| InstanceName  | Default instance name, if none is provided as a command line argument.  |  
| PhysicalPath  | Path to instance folder typically in NetWorks Service Instances folder: `C:\ProgramData\Intergraph\NetWorks\ServiceInstances\`  |  
| ServiceNameTemplate  | Template for service name.  |  
| ServiceDisplayNameTemplate  | Template for service name, as displayed in the windows services administration console.  |  
> **Note** Both **ServiceNameTemplate** and **ServiceDisplayNameTemplate** use `{InstanceName}` as a placeholder for actual instance name.

# WarmUp Service
WarmUp Service is a simple tool that runs as a Windows service. It provides convenient way to to avoid time-consuming cold start of various NetWorks services by pinging those services in predefined times, before expected workload occurs. It can be also used to keep services alive by periodically access them.
The tool uses [Quartz.NET](https://www.quartz-scheduler.net/) as a scheduling system.
It then combines configuration of deployed NetWorks services, located in `c:\ProgramData\Intergraph\NetWorks\DeployedServices\NetWorksDeployedServices.xml`, and its own configuration file to produce ping or keep-alive messages.
**Related topics**
  * [Deployment](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/WarmUp-Service/Deployment.html)
  * [Configuration](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/WarmUp-Service/Configuration.html)

## General Parameters[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Configuration.html#general-parameters)
###  `URL`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Configuration.html#url)
HTTP endpoint where service API is exposed. **Required.**  
Examples:
  * `http://*:9400`
  * `http://localhost:9400`

###  `Queues:StorageRoot`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Configuration.html#queuesstorageroot)
Path to folder with storage for input request queue. The service account must have RW permissions to this folder. **Required.** Example: `C:\WorkService\Queues\`.
###  `Dispatcher:Workers`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Configuration.html#dispatcherworkers)
Number of allowed parallel workers for each workload. Default value which can be overridden for each workload. Expected value: integer > 0. Default: `3`.
###  `Dispatcher:MaintenancePeriodInMinutes`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Configuration.html#dispatchermaintenanceperiodinminutes)
Interval between queue maintenance (minutes). efault value which can be overridden for each workload. Expected: integer > 0. Default: `120`.
## Convert CAD workload parameters[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Configuration.html#convert-cad-workload-parameters)
###  `ConvertCAD:OutputPath`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Configuration.html#convertcadoutputpath)
Path to storage folder for Dynamic WMS Service. Required if Convert CAD workload is used.
###  `ConvertCAD:InputPath`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Configuration.html#convertcadinputpath)
Path to storage folder for uploaded CAD files. Required if Convert CAD workload is used.
###  `ConvertCAD:TempPath`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Configuration.html#convertcadtemppath)
Path to temporary folder for intermediate files. If not specified, defaults to `%TEMP%`.
###  `ConvertCAD:DefaultCsf`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Configuration.html#convertcaddefaultcsf)
Path to default CSF file used in case no CSF file is provided for the input. Expected: Path to CSF file. Added in version 11.01.2401.
###  `ConvertCAD:Dispatcher:Workers`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Configuration.html#convertcaddispatcherworkers)
Number of allowed parallel workers for ConvertCAD workload. Expected: integer > 0. Default: `3`.
###  `ConvertCAD:Dispatcher:MaintenancePeriodInMinutes`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Configuration.html#convertcaddispatchermaintenanceperiodinminutes)
Interval between queue maintenance (minutes). Default: `120`.
## Executable workload parameters[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Configuration.html#executable-workload-parameters)
Multiple Executable workloads can be registered. Each such workload has its own `{workload}` identifier and parameters.
###  `Executable:{workload}:Path`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Configuration.html#executableworkloadpath)
Path to executable for workload identified by `{workload}`. Required.
###  `Executable:{workload}:WorkDir`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Configuration.html#executableworkloadworkdir)
Path to working directory for the process. Applies to `workload`. Required.
###  `Executable:{workload}:Arguments`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Configuration.html#executableworkloadarguments)
Template for command line arguments. May contain placeholders, see [Executable](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Executable.html).
###  `Executable:{workload}:ArgumentList:{N}`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Configuration.html#executableworkloadargumentlistn)
Command line arguments as array. `{N}` is 0-based index of the argument. If specified, has preference over _Arguments_. May contain placeholders, see [Executable](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Executable.html).
###  `Executable:{workload}:SuccessExitCode`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Configuration.html#executableworkloadsuccessexitcode)
Regular expression to match process exit codes of successful completion.  
Default: `^0$`. Examples:
  * `^(0\|1\|2\|9)$` to match 0, 1, 2 or 9.
  * `^(-?\d+)$` to match any number.

###  `Executable:{workload}:Dispatcher:Workers`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Configuration.html#executableworkloaddispatcherworkers)
Number of allowed parallel workers for `workload`. Default: `3`.
###  `Executable:{workload}:Dispatcher:MaintenancePeriodInMinutes`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Configuration.html#executableworkloaddispatchermaintenanceperiodinminutes)
Interval between queue maintenance (minutes) for `{workload}`. Default: `120`.
## Export data workload parameters[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Configuration.html#export-data-workload-parameters)
###  `ExportData:StoragePath`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Configuration.html#exportdatastoragepath)
Path to storage folder for uploaded JSON files (committed transactions folder of Data Transfer Service).
###  `ExportData:Dispatcher:Workers`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Configuration.html#exportdatadispatcherworkers)
Number of allowed parallel workers for ExportData workload. Default: `3`.
## Features workload parameters[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Configuration.html#features-workload-parameters)
###  `Features:StoragePath`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Configuration.html#featuresstoragepath)
[Features](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Features.html) workload, path to folder with committed transactions of Data Transfer Service. **Required** if Features workload is in use.
###  `Features:JobService`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Configuration.html#featuresjobservice)
Job Service URL. **Required** if Features workload is in use.
###  `Features:FeatureTransactionService`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Configuration.html#featuresfeaturetransactionservice)
Feature Transaction Service URL. May contain placeholder `{configuration}`. The placeholder is dynamically replaced by the NetWorks configuration of the processed workset. **Required** if Features workload is in use.
###  `Features:FeatureTransactionServices:{configuration}`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Configuration.html#featuresfeaturetransactionservicesconfiguration)
Feature Transaction Service URL for configuration identified by `{configuration}`. `{configuration}` must be uppercase.
###  `Features:OnSuccess`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Configuration.html#featuresonsuccess)
Comma-separated list of Work Service workload names to be invoked after successful completion of a submitted workset.
###  `Features:OnError`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Configuration.html#featuresonerror)
Comma-separated list of Work Service workload names to be invoked after failed completion of a submitted workset.
###  `Features:RelayAuthorization`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Configuration.html#featuresrelayauthorization)
Flag (true, false). When set to `true`, Authorization HTTP header from the request is relayed to the post-processing request body.
###  `Features:GeometryFormat`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Configuration.html#featuresgeometryformat)
Geometry format to use when retrieving job data during conversion to workset. Allowed values: `networksjson`, `geojson`, `wkt`. Default: `networksjson`.
###  `Features:Resolution`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Configuration.html#featuresresolution)
Resolution (ground unit per display units) to use when retrieving job data during conversion to workset. Expected: double value > 0. Default: `0.001`.
###  `Features:Dimensions`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Configuration.html#featuresdimensions)
Number of geometry dimensions to retrieve when converting job data to workset. Allowed values: `2`, `3`. Default: `3`.
###  `Features:Dispatcher:Workers`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Configuration.html#featuresdispatcherworkers)
Number of allowed parallel workers for Features workload. Default: `3`.
## Workset workload parameters[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Configuration.html#workset-workload-parameters)

## Examples[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Configuration.html#examples)
### Support multiple configurations in Features workload[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Configuration.html#support-multiple-configurations-in-features-workload)
To support multiple NetWorks configurations when processing submitted Feature Editor worksets, it is necessary to deploy multiple Feature Transaction Service (FTS) instances, one for each configuration. Work Service is able to relay processing of the transaction to the proper FTS instance. There are two ways how to achieve this:
#### A. Use template URLs for Feature Transaction Service[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Configuration.html#a-use-template-urls-for-feature-transaction-service)
Deploy FTS instances with URLs following a template pattern, containing the NetWorks configuration. Example: for configurations `EAST` and `WEST` deploy two instances at URLs `https://server/ftsEAST` and `https://server/ftsWEST`.
In Work Service, Configure FTS URL template:

```
Features:FeatureTransactionService=https://server/fts{configuration}

```

#### B. Map configuration name to FTS instance URL[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Configuration.html#b-map-configuration-name-to-fts-instance-url)
In Work Service configuration, explicitly map NetWorks configuration name to a FTS URL, example:

```
Features:FeatureTransactionServices:EAST=https://server/fts1
Features:FeatureTransactionServices:WEST=https://server/fts2

```

## Technical notes[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Configuration.html#technical-notes)
The service uses .NET Core configuration system. For details on how to format configuration files, see [Configuration in ASP.NET Core](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/aspnet/core/fundamentals/configuration/)

###### Deployment

# Command line deployment
Work Service can be semi-automatically deployed and undeployed from the command line using the [DeployWorkService.exe](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/Command-line-deployment-tools.html) tool.
## Workflow - deployment[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Deployment/Command-line-deployment.html#workflow---deployment)
  1. Create or edit service instance in **NetWorksDeployedServices.xml**.

NetWorks keeps track of service instances in XML file `c:\ProgramData\Intergraph\NetWorks\DeployedServices\NetWorksDeployedServices.xml`.
To register a new instance of the Work Service, open the file in a text editor (e.g. Notepad) and add new element under the `<NetWorksDeployedServices>` element, e.g.:

```
<WorkService InstanceName="WorkServiceINSTANCE1" 
               IsInSolution="False" 
               InstanceId="WorkServiceINSTANCE1"
               Definition="Work Service"
               ConvertCAD__InputPath="C:\NetWorks\CAD\Input"
               ConvertCAD__OutputPath="C:\NetWorks\CAD\Output"
               ConvertCAD__TempPath="C:\NetWorks\CAD\Temp"
               Dispatcher__Workers="10"
               URL="http://*:9400"
                />

```

### Parameters[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Deployment/Command-line-deployment.html#parameters)  
| Name  | Description  | Mandatory  | Default Value  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| InstanceName  | Unique name of the service instance.  | Y  |   |  
| IsInSolution  | Flag. Must be set to `False`  | Y  |   |  
| InstanceId  | GUID of the instance  |   |   |  
| Definition  | Name of service definition  | Y  | Work Service  |  
| ConnectionInfo  | NetWorks connection string formatted as `user/password@configuration`.   
Accepts values encrypted using `GTEncTool.exe`.  | Y  |   |  
| PhysicalPath  | Path to folder where the service will be deployed. The value can contain environment variable placeholders via `%variable%` convention.  | Y  |   |  
| URL  | URL of Work Service REST API endpoint. Must be fo  | Y  | http://*:9400  |  
| AppPoolIdentityType  | IIS Application Pool identity type. [Allowed values](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/microsoft.web.administration.processmodelidentitytype?view=iis-dotnet).  |   | 4  |  
| AppPoolUserName  | IIS Application Pool User name. When not specified, the built-in ApplicationPoolIdentity is used.  
**Note**  
The account must have access to the published metadata and data files.  |   |   |  
| AppPoolPassword  | IIS Application Pool Password. Accepts values encrypted using `GTEncTool.exe`.  |   |   |  
| LoggingType  | Default logging level. Allowed values: `Error`, `Warn`, `Info`, `Trace`.  |   | Error  |  
For service-specific parameters, see [Configuration](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Configuration.html). In all parameter names, replace `:` with double underscore `__` when adding the parameter to XML file.
### Example[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Deployment/Command-line-deployment.html#example)

```
<WorkService Definition="Work Service" 
             InstanceId="NwWorkService" 
             InstanceName="NwWorkService"
             AppPoolName="NwWorkServicePool" 
             PhysicalPath="%SystemDrive%\inetpub\wwwroot\NwWorkService" 
             VirtualPath="Default Web Site/NwWorkService" 
             AuthenticationType="Anonymous" 
             LoggingType="Error" 
             ConnectionInfo="user/password@CONFIGURATION" 
             ConvertCAD__InputPath="C:\NetWorks\CAD\Input"
             ConvertCAD__OutputPath="C:\NetWorks\CAD\Output"
             ConvertCAD__TempPath="C:\NetWorks\CAD\Temp"
             Dispatcher__Workers="10"
             IsInSolution="False"
             URL="http://*:9400" />

```

  1. Start **Command Prompt** (`cmd.exe`) **as Administrator**
  2. Navigate to NetWorks Program folder, typically `cd c:\Program Files (x86)\Intergraph\NetWorks\Program\`
  3. Deploy the service instance by executing `DeployWorkService.exe -i <service instance>`

## Workflow - undeployment[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Deployment/Command-line-deployment.html#workflow---undeployment)
  1. Create or edit service instance in **NetWorksDeployedServices.xml** as in **Workflow - deployment**
  2. Start **Command Prompt** (`cmd.exe`) **as Administrator**
  3. Navigate to NetWorks Program folder, typically `cd c:\Program Files (x86)\Intergraph\NetWorks\Program\`
  4. Deploy the service instance by executing `DeployWorkService.exe -i <service instance> -u`

## Workflow - redeployment[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Deployment/Command-line-deployment.html#workflow---redeployment)
As **Deployment** , except for step
  1. Deploy the service instance by executing `DeployWorkService.exee -i <service instance> -r`

# Diagnostics
The service uses **ETW** ([Event Tracing for Windows](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/etw/about-event-tracing)) to produce and collect events during runtime.
**NLog** is used to write events to log files. It is configured using `NLog.config`, which is expected at the same location as other configuration files.
## How to turn on tracing[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Diagnostics.html#how-to-turn-on-tracing)
  * Locate the file `NLog.config` (See [How service locates configuration files](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Configuration/How-service-locates-configuration-files.html).)
  * Open the file in a text editor (e.g. Notepad)
  * Set the log level for `file` output to `Trace`

```
<logger name="*" minlevel="Trace" writeTo="file" />

```

  * Save the file
  * Restart the service
  * Execute diagnosed workflow
  * Check the log file (by default under `c:\ProgramData\Intergraph\NetWorks\Logs\`)

## Related topics[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Diagnostics.html#related-topics)
  * [ETW Listener configuration](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Diagnostics.html)
  * [ETW Event Sources](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Diagnostics/ETW-Event-Sources.html)

# Publishing Work Service in IIS
Work Service is a Windows Service which exposes its REST API on a HTTP endpoint. The HTTP endpoint is normally not reachable from other machines. To expose it, use the ARR module of the IIS.
  * Install the [Application Request Routing](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/download/details.aspx?id=47333)
  * Open **Internet Information Services (IIS) Manager**
  * On the server node, open the **Application Request Routing Cache**
  * Under **Actions** (right), select **Server Proxy Settings...**
  * Check **Enable proxy**
  * **Apply** the configuration (right)
  * Create an empty folder on the disk
  * Under **Default Web Site** (or other site), create a new _Virtual Directory_
    * Set **Alias** to a unique name, e.g `workservice1`
    * Set **Physical Path** to the path of the folder created in the previous step
  * On the virtual directory node, open **URL Rewrite**
  * Click **Add Rule(s)...** (right)
  * Select **Reverse Proxy**
    * In **Inbound Rules** , set the server name to `localhost:{port}`, where `{port}` is the TCP port on which the Work Service listens. The default is 9400.
    * Confirm with **OK**.
  * Work Service is now available to external requests at URL `http://{hostname}/{virtualdir}` or `https://{hostname}/{virtualdir}`, e.g. `https://myserver.domain.com/workservice1`

# ConvertCAD
## Overview[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/ConvertCAD.html#overview)
The ConvertCAD workload of the Work Service is designed to automate tasks related to conversion of external CAD and vector files (DWG, DXF, DGN, Shapefile (SHP)) to DDC format. All vector files must be accompanied by a CSF file which contains definition of the coordinate system of the uploaded vector file. It is possible to define default CSF file (see configuration) which will be used if no specific CSF is provided for given input.
##### Note
This workload requires NetWorks Core to be installed on the same machine as NetWorks. The version of NetWorks Core must match NetWorks version. Follow HxGN NetWorks Core Administrator's Guide related to configuration parameters (e.g. `SHPComponentNumber`, `SHPFeatureNumber`) needed for usage of tools **PublishCADFiles.exe** and **PublishShapeToDDC.exe**.
[![WorkService_Architecture_AttachCAD_v03.svg](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/.attachments/WorkService_Architecture_AttachCAD_v03-5611f9dd-df85-4ed7-a194-bb3db0d410d5.svg)](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/.attachments/WorkService_Architecture_AttachCAD_v03-5611f9dd-df85-4ed7-a194-bb3db0d410d5.svg)
## Components[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/ConvertCAD.html#components)
### Services[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/ConvertCAD.html#services)  
| Name  | Function  |  
| --- | --- |  
| Portal (client)  | NetWorks Portal on the user's computer.  |  
| Portal (server)  | NetWorks Portal server runtime.  |  
| [Data Transfer Service](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Data-Transfer-Service.html)  | Web service for file uploads.  |  
| [Work Service](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service.html)  | Multi-purpose Windows service used to perform long-running workloads. Here used for conversion of uploaded CAD/Raster files to DDC.  |  
| [Dynamic WMS Service](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Dynamic-WMS-Service.html)  | NetWorks WMS service (new) which renders contents of dynamically attached DDC files as rasters.  |  
| NetWorks Core tooling  | Command line tools delivered with NetWorks Core for conversion of CAD and SHP files to DDC.  |  
| NetWorks DB  | NetWorks database.  |  
### Other[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/ConvertCAD.html#other)  
| Name  | Function  |  
| --- | --- |  
| Uploaded files  | Storage location for files uploaded by the clients.  |  
| DDC files (converted from CAD)  | DDC files which contain vector/raster data converted from CAD by NetWorks command line tools.  |  
## Interface[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/ConvertCAD.html#interface)
### Inputs[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/ConvertCAD.html#inputs)  
| Name  | Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
| Transaction identifier (`tid`)  | Pointer to the physical storage of uploaded files. Resolves to physical path to file system (see [Upload](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Data-Transfer-Service/Upload.html)). For expected contents in the folder see below **Input structures**.  |  
| NetWorks configuration  | The NW configuration name comes from the Work Service configuration as each instance is linked to a single G/T configuration.  |  
| Database credentials (user, password)  | Credentials come from OIDC access token (when gtechnologyDBConnect is available) or from the connection string configured in the service.  |  
### Outputs[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/ConvertCAD.html#outputs)  
| Name  | Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
| DDC/CDT files with converted CAD vector geometries.  | The files are stored in configurable location, typically the Dynamic WMS Service storage. See [Dynamic WMS Service](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Dynamic-WMS-Service.html) for storage specification.  |  
| Mapping descriptor  | JSON file with mapping between up  |  
## Input structures[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/ConvertCAD.html#input-structures)
The CAD files are expected in the following structures:
  1. Single CAD file and single CSF file. CSF file name does not need to match CAD file name.
  2. Multiple CAD files and single CSF file. CSF file name does not need to match CAD file names.
  3. Multiple CAD files and multiple CSF file. CSF file names must match CAD file names.
  4. Single or multiple CAD files without any CSF file. Default CSF file must be defined for ConvertCAD workload and will be used for each input file.
  5. ZIP file containing structures as in 1, 2, 3 or 4.

## Output structures[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/ConvertCAD.html#output-structures)
### Mapping descriptor[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/ConvertCAD.html#mapping-descriptor)

```
{
  "tid": "13456789065406490asdfasdf",
  "sources": [
    {
      "sid": "asdfasdfadsfdsf991651",
      "content": "source1.dgn"
    },
    {
      "sid": "bxeteerrfadsfdsf991623",
      "content": "plan2.dwg"
    }
  ]
}

```

### source.json[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/ConvertCAD.html#sourcejson)

```
{
   "source": "roads.shp",
   "sub": "1234567890"
}

```

## Workflow[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/ConvertCAD.html#workflow)
  * Find the source folder by `tid`.
  * Inspect the files and if needed, unzip.
  * Determine CAD-CSF pairs.
  * Convert files to DDC. 
    * AutoCAD (DXF, DWG) and Microstation (DGN) are converted by command line tool **PublishCADFiles.exe**.
    * Shapefile (SHP) are converted by command line tool **PublishShapeToDDC.exe**.
  * For each produced DDC file: 
    * Create a new `sid` and related folder in output storage.
    * Move the DDC/CDT files to the output folder.
    * Write `source.json` file.
  * Construct and serialize mapping descriptor (JSON) and return to Response management.

# Executable
## Overview[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Executable.html#overview)
The Executable workload is a template workload. It allows registration of an executable and its command line interface in the Work Service configuration and invocation of the workload through the Work Service REST API. It is possible to register multiple workloads based on the Executable template, each with different configuration.
## Configuration[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Executable.html#configuration)
Executable workloads can be registered using standard service [Configuration](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Configuration.html), using the `Executable:{workload}` prefix, where `{workload}` is the name of the workload used in requests.
### Command line arguments[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Executable.html#command-line-arguments)
The **Arguments** string is a template with parameter placeholders. Placeholders are replaced with values received from the request.  
| Placeholder  | Description  | Example  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| `${{parameter.param}}`  | Value of property `param` from top-level JSON object in the request body.  | `${{parameter.package}}`  |  
| `$(RequestPath)`  | Path to file which contains the request body.  |   |  
| `$(ResponsePath)`  | Path to temporary file into which the executable should write content of `response.json`.  |   |  
| `$(DBUser)`  | Name of database user from Work Service configuration.  |   |  
| `$(DBPassword)`  | Password of database user from Work Service configuration.  |   |  
| `$(Configuration)`  | NetWorks configuration from Work Service configuration.  |   |  
**Example**
Configuration:

```
Executable:publishpackage:Path=C:\publish\publish.exe
Executable:publishpackage:Arguments=-p ${{parameter.package}} -c $(Configuration) -u $(DBUser) -p $(DBPassword) -o $(ResponsePath)
Executable:publishpackage:Dispatcher:Workers=1

```

Or

```
Executable:publishpackage:Path=C:\publish\publish.exe
Executable:publishpackage:ArgumentList:0=-p
Executable:publishpackage:ArgumentList:1=${{parameter.package}}
Executable:publishpackage:ArgumentList:2=-c
Executable:publishpackage:ArgumentList:3=$(Configuration)`
Executable:publishpackage:ArgumentList:5=-u
Executable:publishpackage:ArgumentList:6=$(DBUser)
Executable:publishpackage:ArgumentList:7=-p
Executable:publishpackage:ArgumentList:8=$(DBPassword)
Executable:publishpackage:ArgumentList:9=-o
Executable:publishpackage:ArgumentList:10=$(ResponsePath)
Executable:publishpackage:Dispatcher:Workers=1

```

When Work Service receives requests with body:

```
{
   "package": "BERLIN01"
}

```

it starts process with the following command line:
`C:\publish\publish.exe -p BERLIN01 -c PRODUCTION -u user -p password -o C:\WorkService\output\123456789\response.json`
## Interface[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Executable.html#interface)
## Request[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Executable.html#request)
The request body is a JSON. It is stored as `request.json` into `$(InputDir)`. Path to this file can be passed to the executable using the `$(RequestPath)` parameter.
## Response - Success result[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Executable.html#response---success-result)
The executable can produce a JSON file as response into the path provided in `$(ResponsePath)`. Success is determined from the executable exit code. By default `0` is treated as success, other values as failure. This behavior is configurable using the **SuccessExitCode** parameter for the workload (see [Configuration](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Configuration.html)).
## Response - Error result[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Executable.html#response---error-result)
When the executable returns an non-success exit code, the execution results in FAILURE.

# ExportData
## Overview[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/ExportData.html#overview)
The ExportData workflow is used to convert tabular data into [Open XML](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/office/open-xml/open-xml-sdk) format. It consumes a JSON file in well-known structure, described below, and produces a single output .xlsx file with a single worksheet, containing header and data from input. Header is written in the first row of the document. No formatting is applied. Rows are ordered as in source JSON.
## Workflow[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/ExportData.html#workflow)
This workflow is written from the perspective of NetWorks Portal as a consumer of the service
  1. Client prepares data from whatever source (query result, trace result, ...) to the predefined JSON input format.  
Data should be prepared in the following format:

```
{
   "columns": ["Header 1", "Header 2", ... ],
   "rows" : [
      ["Val 1", 123, ... ],
      ["Val 2", 456, ... ],
      ...
  ]
}

```

So "columns" defines the column headers in the resulting excel spreadsheet, "rows" is an array of arrays, each sub array represents a row in the resulting excel spreadsheet. Text encoding must be UTF-8. Each value can one of four JSON types
     * string - Standard unicode string, double quotes are backslash escaped (i.e. \")
     * number - Double precision number
     * boolean - In the file these are represented as unquoted strings true or false.
     * null - In file represented as unquoted string null.
No checks are currently applied to the actual number of columns in header and rows.
  2. Client uses Data Transfer Service to upload JSON file(s). Receives TID of committed upload transaction.  
This steps consists of three steps in [Data Transfer Service](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Data-Transfer-Service/Upload.html):
     * Begin Transaction (resulting in TID)
     * Upload a JSON file (or more)
     * Commit transaction
  3. Client calls Work Service with ExportData workload. Uses TID as an input. Receives WID of ongoing work.  
Request body has the following form:

```
{
   "tid": "q308xjom0q7immcdgygc0cpvyzre2vwu"
}

```

Client receives following response:

```
{
    "success": true,
    "wid": "o9gip3nxk6ytnnbgec38ct0niuhgelzf",
    "workStatus": "QUEUED"
}

```

  4. Client stats polling Work Service for work status using received WID.  
Repeats until the work is completed:

```
{
    "success": true,
    "wid": "o9gip3nxk6ytnnbgec38ct0niuhgelzf",
    "workStatus": "COMPLETED"
}

```

  5. When the work status is COMPLETED, client requests work result from Work Service. Receives TID (the same as before) and file name(s).

```
{
   "tid": "q308xjom0q7immcdgygc0cpvyzre2vwu",
   "files": [
       "sample.xlsx"
   ]
}

```

  6. Client downloads exported file using Data Transfer Service  
Using Data Transfer Service and TID with file name(s) from previous work result.

####### Features

# Interface files
## REQUEST_FILE[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Features/Interface-files.html#request_file)
is a JSON file **.well-known/request.json** in the DTS transaction. The file contains the body of the request to be processed (see [Workset Request](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Features/Interface-structures.html)).
## STATUS_FILE[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Features/Interface-files.html#status_file)
is a JSON file JSON file **.well-known/status.json** in the DTS transaction. The file contains the status of the processing of the CRUD transactions (see [Workset Status](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Features/Interface-structures.html)). The file may not be available before start of the processing.
## RESULT_FILE[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Features/Interface-files.html#result_file)
is a JSON file **.well-known/result.json** in the DTS transaction. The file contains the result of the processing of the CRUD transaction after it has finished (see [Workset Result](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Features/Interface-structures.html)).

# Interface structures
## Workset request[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Features/Interface-structures.html#workset-request)
Root type is [WorksetRequest](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Features/Interface-structures.html#worksetrequest). This structure contains all necessary data to perform job and transaction CRUD processing on the server after submission by the client.
### WorksetRequest[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Features/Interface-structures.html#worksetrequest)
Derived from [ProcessTransactionRequest](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Transaction-Service/ProcessTransactions.html).  
| Name  | Type  | Mandatory  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| job  | [JobData](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Features/Interface-structures.html#jobdata)  |   | Job context.  |  
| transactions  | Array of [Transaction](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Transaction-Service/ProcessTransactions.html)  | Y  | See [ProcessTransactions](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Transaction-Service/ProcessTransactions.html) for details.  |  
### JobData[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Features/Interface-structures.html#jobdata)
HxGN NetWorks Core job data.  
| Name  | Type  | Mandatory  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| id  | string  |   | Job identifier.  
  
When present, the transaction is processed in the context of this job.  
When present with value of null, the transaction is processed in STT mode.  
When not present, a new job is created.  |  
| description  | string  |   | Value for job description field (G3E_DESCRIPTIONFIELD). Only applied when creating a new job.  |  
| attributes  | object  |   | Job properties.  
  
See serialization of attributes property in [ComponentTransactionBase](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Transaction-Service/ProcessTransactions.html).  |  
### Example[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Features/Interface-structures.html#example)

```
{
  "job": {
    "description": "Create Sew-Manhole",
    "attributes": {
      "G3E_JOBCLASS": 11
    }
  },
  "transactions": [
    {
      "type": "CreateFeature",
      "fref": 1,
      "G3E_FNO": 702
    },
    {
      "type": "CreateComponent",
      "fref": 1,
      "G3E_CNO": 19666,
      "attributes": {
        "CATEGORY": "1",
        "SEWAGE_CATEGORY": "1",
        "LOWEST_COVER_HEIGHT": 3.14,
        "BOTTOM_HEIGHT": 2.71
      }
    },
    {
      "type": "CreateComponent",
      "fref": 1,
      "G3E_CNO": 703,
      "attributes": {
        "CONTRACT_HL": {
          "f": "test.jpg"
        }
      }
    }
  ]
}

```

## Workset result[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Features/Interface-structures.html#workset-result)
Root type is JSON object of type [WorksetResult](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Features/Interface-structures.html#worksetresult).
### WorksetResult[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Features/Interface-structures.html#worksetresult)  
| Name  | Type  | Mandatory  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| job  | [JobResult](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Features/Interface-structures.html#jobresult)  |   | Job context.  |  
| transactions  | Array of [Transaction](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Transaction-Service/ProcessTransactions.html)  |   | See See [ProcessTransactions](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Transaction-Service/ProcessTransactions.html) response for details.  |  
| errors  | Array of [Error](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Features/Interface-structures.html#error)  |   | List of errors from processing.  |  
### JobResult[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Features/Interface-structures.html#jobresult)  
| Name  | Type  | Mandatory  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| id  | String  |   | Job identifier in which the job was executed. If null, the job was executed in STT mode.  |  
### Error[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Features/Interface-structures.html#error)  
| Name  | Type  | Mandatory  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| code  | String  | Y  | Error code.  |  
| value  | String  |   | Error detail (additional value or identifier).  |  
### Example 1 - Success[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Features/Interface-structures.html#example-1---success)

```
{
  "transactions": [
    {
      "type": "CreateFeature",
      "fref": 1,
      "G3E_FNO": 702,
      "G3E_FID": 3735361
    },
    {
      "type": "CreateComponent",
      "fref": 1,
      "G3E_CNO": 19666,
      "G3E_CID": 1
    },
    {
      "type": "CreateComponent",
      "fref": 1,
      "G3E_CNO": 703,
      "G3E_CID": 1
    }
  ],
  "job": { "id": "10274" }
}

```

### Example 2 – System error[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Features/Interface-structures.html#example-2--system-error)

```
{
  "job": {
    "description": "Create Sew-Manhole",
    "attributes": { "G3E_JOBCLASS": 11 },
    "id": "10304"
  },
  "transactions": [
    {
      "type": "CreateFeature",
      "fref": 5,
      "G3E_FNO": 7020
    },
    {
      "type": "CreateComponent",
      "fref": 5,
      "G3E_CNO": 19666,
      "attributes": {
        "CATEGORY": "1",
        "SEWAGE_CATEGORY": "1",
        "LOWEST_COVER_HEIGHT": 19.14,
        "BOTTOM_HEIGHT": 2.71
      }
    },
    {
      "type": "CreateComponent",
      "fref": 5,
      "G3E_CNO": 703,
      "attributes": { "CONTRACT_HL": { "f": "http://localhost/attachments/2023/01/19/ft/s0/fts00000000000000000000000000003/test.jpg" } }
    }

### Example 3 – Transaction failed[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Features/Interface-structures.html#example-3--transaction-failed)

```
{
  "transactions": [

    }
