}

```

## Job status[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Features/Interface-structures.html#job-status)
Root type is JSON object of type [WorkSetStatus](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Features/Interface-structures.html#worksetstatus).
### WorkSetStatus[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Features/Interface-structures.html#worksetstatus)  
| Name  | Type  | Mandatory  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| status  | string  | Y  | Processing status. Allowed values:  
  
* INPROGRESS  
* SUCCESS  
* ERROR  |  
**Example**

```
{
  "status": "SUCCESS"
}

```

## Work summary[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Features/Interface-structures.html#work-summary)
Work summary is a JSON document passed in as a request to the post-processing workload.
### WorkSummaryType[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Features/Interface-structures.html#worksummarytype)  
| Name  | Type  | Mandatory  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| request  | object  | Y  | Body of the original request in DTS transaction.  |  
| result  | object  | N  | Body of the response of ProcessTransactions with updated job data.  |  
| tid  | string  | Y  | DTS transaction identifier  |  
| transactionpath  | string  | Y  | Absolute path to folder with current DTS transaction data.  |  
| parentwid  | string  | Y  | Work Identifier (wid) of the currently executed work in Features workload.  |  
| authorization  | string  |   | Authorization HTTP header from the original request. Only added when the [configuration](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Configuration.html) parameter _Features:RelayAuthorization_ is set to true. This allows subsequent processing to continue with the same user context.  |  
**Example**

```
{
  "request": {
    "job": {
      "description": "Create feature in job 587595",
      "attributes": { "G3E_JOBCLASS": 11 }
    },
    "transactions": [
      {
        "type": "CreateFeature",
        "fref": 5,
        "G3E_FNO": 7020
      },
      {
        "type": "CreateComponent",
        "fref": 5,
        "G3E_CNO": 19666,
        "attributes": {
          "CATEGORY": "1",
          "SEWAGE_CATEGORY": "1",
          "LOWEST_COVER_HEIGHT": 19.14,
          "BOTTOM_HEIGHT": 2.71
        }
      }
    ]
  },
  "result": {
    "transactions": [
      {
        "type": "CreateFeature",
        "fref": 5,
        "G3E_FNO": 7020,
        "errors": [
          {
            "code": "ERR_INVALID_FNO",
            "value": "7020"
          }
        ]
      },
      {
        "type": "CreateComponent",
        "fref": 5,
        "G3E_CNO": 19666
      }
    ],
    "job": { "id": "10313" },
    "errors": [ { "code": "ERR_TRANSACTION_FAILED" } ]
  },
  "tid": "fts00000000000000000000000000003",
  "transactionpath": "C:\\Transactions\\committed\\17\\4Z\\174z22epx083fk84889btcfgaorrozlw",
  "parentwid": "orzldov99qo7jx29qizerdxbardlbkd4",
  "authorization": "Bearer eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsInR5cCIgO..."
}

```

# Post processing
Work Service **Features** workload can be configured to automatically submit a new job or jobs after the processing completes with success or with failure.
## Workflow[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Features/Post-processing.html#workflow)
  * Submitted work for Features workload is executed and completes.
  * Work Service evaluates the result. If there is an exception or the processing reports at least one error, the result is error.
  * If there is at least one configured workload name in [configuration](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Configuration.html) parameters _Features:OnSuccess_ and _Features:OnError_. 
    * A [Work summary](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Features/Interface-structures.html) document is constructed. It contains both the original request and the result of the processing and context information.
    * Work Service internally submits a new job to configured workload(s) with the work summary as the request body.
    * Work Service does not wait for completion of the child processes.
    * Workload name and identifier (wid) is added to the result of the current job.
  * Work Service saves the result of the current work.

# Features
Features workload handles the asynchronous server-side processing of the submitted request with a Feature Editor workset.
## Workflow[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Features.html#workflow)
  * Extract `tid` (DTS transaction identifier) from the [SubmitWork](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Work-Service/SubmitWork.html) request body.
  * Using `tid`, find the physical DTS transaction folder with uploaded transaction request.
  * Deserialize the transaction request from the transaction folder (see [REQUEST_FILE](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Features/Interface-files.html)).
  * Create LTT job. 
    * If job identifier is not present, call the JobService [CreateJob](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Job-Service/CreateJob.html)) API to create a new LTT job in the database.
    * If job identifier is null, skip this step and work in STT mode.
    * If the job identifier is present, don’t create a job and use the provided job for context.
  * Execute the transactions. 
    * Call Feature Transaction Service [ProcessTransactions](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Transaction-Service/ProcessTransactions.html) with the job context (or no job if STT was requested) and pass the transaction request.
  * Call Job Service to update the job properties (see [NWG_GENERALPARAMETER](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Reference/Metadata-tables/NWG_GENERALPARAMETER.html#job-to-workset)).
  * Process file attachments. 
    * Read [ProcessTransactions](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Transaction-Service/ProcessTransactions.html) response and find all [mapped links](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Transaction-Service/ProcessTransactions/Hyperlink-mapping.html).
    * Copy the files from transaction folder to the permanent storage location. Environment variable placeholders in mapped paths (destination property) are evaluated.
  * Prepare processing result (see [RESULT_FILE](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Features/Interface-files.html))). 
    * Start with [ProcessTransactions](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Transaction-Service/ProcessTransactions.html) response (if completed) or original request (if errors occurred before completion of ProcessTransactions).
    * Write job identifier.
    * Write errors (if any).
  * Update the processing status (see [STATUS_FILE](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Features/Interface-files.html)).
  * Run asynchronous [post processing](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Features/Post-processing.html) with the [Work summary](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Features/Interface-structures.html) (request and result).

## API[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Features.html#api)
### Submit a request[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Features.html#submit-a-request)
Use [SubmitWork](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Work-Service/SubmitWork.html) with workload **features**. Pass instance of [FeaturesRequest](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Features.html#featuresrequest) in the request body.
#### FeaturesRequest[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Features.html#featuresrequest)  
| Name  | Type  | Mandatory  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| tid  | string  | Y  | DTS transaction identifier. Work Service uses this identifier to locate the physical storage of the submitted transaction.  |  
**Example**

```
{
  "tid": "az08xjom0q7immcdgygc0cpvyzre2vwu"
}

```

#### Response[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Features.html#response)
Standard Work Service [SubmitWork](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Work-Service/SubmitWork.html) response – `wid` of the submitted job.
### Get result of submitted request[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Features.html#get-result-of-submitted-request)
Standard Work Service [GetWorkResult](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Work-Service/GetWorkResult.html) can be used to retrieve the summary of the processing. Features Workload completes with a JSON summary, which contains the tid from the request and an optional list of postprocess jobs (children) which were started after the current one completed.
Summary of the processing of this workload. The complete result of the transaction processing is stored in original transaction folder in [RESULT_FILE](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Features/Interface-files.html).
**Example 1: Success**

```
{
    "tid": "mueb5rg44aamakpr757hbblfyx8inkid",
    "children": [{
            "workload": "featurespostprocess",
            "wid": "y9i8rury664h5jnznlaih6qhbyldx7bj"
        }
    ]
}

```

**Example 2: Failure**

```
{
    "tid": "174z22epx083fk84889btcfgaorrozlw",
    "error": "ERR_TRANSACTION_FAILED",
    "children": [{
            "workload": "featureserror",
            "wid": "y9i8rury664h5jnznlaih6qhbyldx7bj"
        }
    ]
}

```

## Error codes[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Features.html#error-codes)
Error codes which may appear in the error property of the workload result.  
| Code  | Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
| ERR_SYSTEM_ERROR  | Unspecified internal error in processing which caused termination of the execution. System administrators need to examine the logs.  |  
| ERR_INTERNAL_ERROR  | Unspecified internal error in processing which did not cause termination.  
  
System administrators need to examine the logs.  |  
| ERR_BAD_REQUEST  | Badly formed request.  |  
| ERR_NOT_AUTHORIZED  | Outgoing service call failed on authorization.  |  
| ERR_JOB_NOT_CREATED  | Failed to create LTT job.  |  
| ERR_NO_REQUEST  | Request file (REQUEST_FILE) is missing or empty.  |  
| ERR_INVALID_REQUEST  | Request file (REQUEST_FILE) can’t be parsed.  |  
| ERR_FILE_ERROR  | Unspecified error occurred during a file operation. File name is in value property and in the transaction request.  |  
| ERR_FILE_NOT_FOUND  | File referenced in request was not found. File name is in value property and in the transaction request.  |  
| ERR_TRANSACTION_FAILED  | Feature transaction processing failed. Error details are in the errors attribute of items in transaction response.  |

# Trace
## Overview[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Trace.html#overview)
Trace workload is used to offload trace execution as potentially long lasting operation.
## Configuration[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Trace.html#configuration)
Trace workload is configured using the [Executable](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Executable.html) template utilizing [ExecuteTrace.exe](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/ExecuteTrace.exe.html) tool. The workload name is configurable, the default value is **trace**.
**Example**

```
Executable:Trace:Path=c:\ProgramPath\ExecuteTrace.exe
Executable:Trace:ArgumentList:0=-i
Executable:Trace:ArgumentList:1=$(RequestPath)
Executable:Trace:ArgumentList:2=-c
Executable:Trace:ArgumentList:3=$(DBUser)/$(DBPassword)@$(Configuration)
Executable:Trace:ArgumentList:4=-o
Executable:Trace:ArgumentList:5=$(ResponsePath)
Executable:Trace:ArgumentList:6=-m
Executable:Trace:ArgumentList:7=${{parameter.MapRequestUrl}}
Executable:Trace:EnableUserMapping=true

```

## Interface[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Trace.html#interface)
### Request[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Trace.html#request)
Request is sent to the Work Service using [SubmitWork](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Work-Service/SubmitWork.html) method. The request body is a JSON, which is basically the same as in [ExecuteTrace](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Analytical-Service/Trace/ExecuteTrace.html) POST request body. There is one additional property that can be specified (and necessary for Cost Constraint Traces) in request JSON body: **MapRequestUrl**. This is the MapRequestService URL used to compute Cost Constraint traces.
### Result[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Trace.html#result)
Result is requested from Work Service using [GetWorkResult](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Work-Service/GetWorkResult.html) method. Successful result contains trace ID.
## Workflow[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Trace.html#workflow)
  1. Client [submits the work](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Work-Service/SubmitWork.html) to Work Service, receives WID (work id).
Request example:

```
{
    "MappingId": "2135",
    "UserName": "[unique name]",
    "SeedFid": "1352584",
    "SeedFno": "506",
    "GoalFid": "1350054",
    "StartingPointX": "1338510.1091178071",
    "StartingPointY": "7068993.177253875",
    "Attributes" : [],
    "MapRequestUrl" : "http://custom/MapRequestService"
}

```

Response example:

```
{
    "success": true,
    "wid": "d0j512f1sszns9hp8rki9mchdrak0yne",
    "workStatus": "QUEUED"
}

```

  2. Client [polls the Work Service](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Work-Service/GetWorkStatus.html) with WID until the work status is either COMPLETED or FAILED.
Response example:

```
{
    "success": true,
    "wid": "d0j512f1sszns9hp8rki9mchdrak0yne",
    "workStatus": "COMPLETED"
}

```

  3. Client [requests the work result](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Work-Service/GetWorkResult.html) (trace ID) using WID.
Response example:

```
1242

```

####### Workset

# Job-workset relationship
After converting a job to workset, the job can be modified to signalize it is currently being edited in offline mode as a workset.
## Postable flag[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Workset/Job-workset-relationship.html#postable-flag)
If `G3E_JOBDEFINITION.G3E_POSTABLEFIELD` is defined, the field in job table is set to `0` to indicate the job can't be posted while it is edited offline. The flag is reset to `1` when the workset is submitted or abandoned before submit.
To disable setting `G3E_JOBDEFINITION.G3E_POSTABLEFIELD`, configure parameter `JobToWorkset:DontUpdatePostableField` in [NWG_GENERALPARAMETER](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Reference/Metadata-tables/NWG_GENERALPARAMETER.html).
## Workset identifier[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Workset/Job-workset-relationship.html#workset-identifier)
An optional field in job table can be configured to be populated with workset identifier by setting parameter `JobToWorkset:WorksetIdField` in [NWG_GENERALPARAMETER](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Reference/Metadata-tables/NWG_GENERALPARAMETER.html). The workset identifier is set when converting job to a workset and reset to `NULL` when the job is submitted or abandoned.

# Workset
**Workset** workload handles job-workset interoperability operations:
  * Creation of a workset from an existing job.
  * Abandoning a workset without submitting.

## Workflows[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Workset.html#workflows)
The type of workflow is driven by property `command` in the request file (`{tid}_workset.json`).
### Convert job to workset[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Workset.html#convert-job-to-workset)
Command: missing or `job2workset`.
  * Extract `tid` (DTS transaction identifier) from the [SubmitWork](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Work-Service/SubmitWork.html) request body.
  * Using `tid`, find the physical DTS transaction folder with uploaded transaction request.
  * Deserialize the [workset request](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Workset.html#worksetrequest) (file named `{tid}_workset.json`) from the transaction folder. 
    * Extract command type, job identifier and configuration name (optional) from the body.
  * Call [GetJobAsWorkset](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Feature-Transaction-Service/GetJobAsWorkset.html) in Feature Transaction Service to get job edits serialized as workset.
  * Create file `{tid}_data.json` in transaction and store workset content into the file.
  * Call Job Service to update job-workset relationship attributes (see [Job workset relationship](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Workset/Job-workset-relationship.html)).
  * Error case: in case of any error, an empty workset file `{tid}_data.json` with `status` set to `4` (ERROR) is created.

### Abandon workset[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Workset.html#abandon-workset)
Command: `abandonworkset`.
  * Extract `tid` (DTS transaction identifier) from the [SubmitWork](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Work-Service/SubmitWork.html) request body.
  * Using `tid`, find the physical DTS transaction folder with uploaded transaction request.
  * Deserialize the [workset request](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Workset.html#worksetrequest) (file named `{tid}_workset.json`) from the transaction folder. 
    * Extract command type, job identifier and configuration name (optional) from the body.
  * Call Job Service to update job-workset relationship attributes (see [Job workset relationship](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Workset/Job-workset-relationship.html)).

## API[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Workset.html#api)
### Submit a request[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Workset.html#submit-a-request)
Use [SubmitWork](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Work-Service/SubmitWork.html) with workload **workset**. Pass instance of [TransactionRequest](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Workset.html#transactionrequest) in the request body.
#### Response[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Workset.html#response)
Standard Work Service [SubmitWork](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Work-Service/SubmitWork.html) response – `wid` of the submitted job.
## Type Definitions[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Workset.html#type-definitions)
### TransactionRequest[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Workset.html#transactionrequest)  
| Name  | Type  | Mandatory  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| tid  | string  | Y  | DTS transaction identifier. Work Service uses this identifier to locate the physical storage of the submitted transaction.  |  
**Example**

```
{
  "tid": "az08xjom0q7immcdgygc0cpvyzre2vwu"
}

```

### WorksetRequest[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Workset.html#worksetrequest)  
| Name  | Type  | Mandatory  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| command  | string  |   | Type of command. Allowed values: `job2workset` (default when missing), `abandonworkset`.  |  
| jobid  | string  | Y  | Job identifier.  |  
| configuration  | string  |   | Core configuration name. Used to determine proper Feature Transaction Service instance in multi-configuration deployments.  |  
**Example**

```
{
  "jobid": "job123456",
  "configuration": "PROD"
}

```

# Work Service
## Overview[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service.html#overview)
The Work Service is a Windows service running in the background. It's main goal is to handle execution of workloads which do not fit into a single HTTP request/response. The primary client of Work Service is the NetWorks Portal, which offloads long running jobs to this service.
For workload types supported see [Workloads](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads.html).
## External interfaces[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service.html#external-interfaces)
The Work Service exposes a [REST API](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Work-Service.html) interface, accessible over HTTP protocol, by default only for other services running on the same machine. The service is not designed to be exposed to the Internet.
Work Service runs as a Windows Service and opens a HTTP server independent from IIS. During deployment, it is necessary to setup the IP address and TCP port on which is listens. Default is `http://127.0.0.1:9400`. If this port is already occupied, specify a different valid port in the 1024-65535 range.
## Internal architecture[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service.html#internal-architecture)
[![WorkService_Internal_Architecture_v03.svg](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/.attachments/WorkService_Internal_Architecture_v03-b256497d-95c8-43c3-8c25-b9faa07f7f58.svg)](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/.attachments/WorkService_Internal_Architecture_v03-b256497d-95c8-43c3-8c25-b9faa07f7f58.svg)
### Components[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service.html#components)
**REST API** External [REST API](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Work-Service.html) interface for receiving of work requests and retrieval of work state. Passes requests to Dispatcher and pulls work state from the Response management.
**Dispatcher: {workload}** Handles communication between external API (REST, in the future also file system or database) and the internal work queue for each payload. Manages pool of workers and assigns work.
**Workload queues** Individual queues are maintained for different workloads (Convert CAD, Print, Trace). The queue is typically a durable storage (e.g. file system, database) which contains all work requests and tracks the state of each work. Dispatcher pull work requests from the workload queue.
**Workers** Internal worker process for execution of workload requests. Each worker is designed to handle a single workload type (e.g. Convert CAD). Each dispatcher for a workload maintains a pool of workers. Workers execute the work as assigned by the dispatcher and return responses to the queue. The number of jobs running in parallel can be configured by number of workers in pool.
**Scheduler** Internal scheduler for running scheduled work (e.g. archiving, cleanup). Creates new work requests for the Dispatcher. Optional component, not required for first version.

#### Tools

# Command line deployment tools
Command line deployment tools are provided for each of the NetWorks Services and NetWorks Portal. They are used for common deploying tasks, deploy, redeploy and undeploy for services of given type. They follow naming convention: `Deploy{ServiceType}.exe`. They are also used internally by [Administration Console](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Administration-Console.html) for deplying tasks.
## Usage[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/Command-line-deployment-tools.html#usage)

```
Deploy{ServiceType}.exe [-i <instance-name>] [-u] [-r] [-d <deployment configuration path>] 
    [--package-path <template package path>] [-dc]

```

### Options[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/Command-line-deployment-tools.html#options)  
| Switch  | Alias  | Mandatory  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| -i  | --instance-name  |   | Service Instance Name.  |  
| -u  | --undeploy  |   | Undeploy service.  |  
| -r  | --redeploy  |   | Redeploy service.  |  
| -d  | --deployment-configuration-path  |   | Path to alternative NetWorksDeployedServices.xml location.  |  
| -dc  | --disable-customization  |   | Disable post-deployment customization.  |  
|   | --package-path  |   | Path to service template packages location.  |  
## Return value[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/Command-line-deployment-tools.html#return-value)  
| Value  | Meaning  |  
| --- | --- |  
| 0  | Success  |  
| 1  | Invalid parameters  |  
| 2  | Error during deployment  |  
## Deployment configuration[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/Command-line-deployment-tools.html#deployment-configuration)
Default deployment configuration path is `%ProgramData%\Intergraph\NetWorks\DeployedServices\`, where the default `NetWorksDeployedServices.xml` file is located.
### Logging[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/Command-line-deployment-tools.html#logging)
File `Deploy{ServiceType}.NLog.config`. By default, the tool logs activity at `Trace` level to Console, at `Trac`e level to NetWorks logs folder.
For detailed logging configuration, create a JSON file named `Deploy{ServiceType}.logging.json` in the folder containing `Deploy{ServiceType}.exe` and configure listening to ETW sources. See [Diagnostics](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Diagnostics.html) for description of the format.
## See also[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/Command-line-deployment-tools.html#see-also)
  * [Common deployment settings](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Administration-Console/Common-deployment-settings.html)

# CreateDDCFileSubset.exe
## Purpose[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/CreateDDCFileSubset.exe.html#purpose)
Create set of DDC files from published DDC files, spatially restricted by a bounding box or by a list of G3E_FIDs.
## Workflow[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/CreateDDCFileSubset.exe.html#workflow)
  * Read all DDC files in a configuration or in the input folder.
  * For each file: 
    * Read the geometries in the provided range (if provided).
    * Filter by G3E_FID list (if provided).
    * Create new DDC file.

**Deltas**
To include deltas (changes in database after DDCs where published), NetWorks **Deltas Service** must be configured and running. Applicable only with `-c`.
## Command line options[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/CreateDDCFileSubset.exe.html#command-line-options)
  * **`-c <configuration>`**  
NetWorks Core configuration. Required if -i is not present.
  * **`-i <input>`**  
DDC file to read. Required if -c is not present. Accepts also comma separated list of files, which are merged into one output DDC file.
  * **`-o <output>`**  
Path to output folder.
  * `-r <bbox>`  
Bounding box of range to export, in DDC coordinates. Format: `minx,miny,maxx,maxy`. Use `.` as decimal separator.
  * `-f <fid-file>`  
G3E_FID file. When specified, the output is filtered to these G3E_FIDs only.
  * `-p <parallelism>`  
Degree of parallelism. 0 = use all CPU cores. Default is 1 (sequential execution).
  * `--file-unc-paths <file-unc-paths>`  
Alternative path to `FileUNCPaths.xml` file.
  * `--ccm-encoding <ccm-encoding>`  
Encoding of the CCM file. Defaults to current ANSI code page.
  * `--merge-limit <merge-limit>`  
When specified, the output files are merged to DDC/CDT files up to approximately the specified limit in MB. Expected: number > 0.

## Configuration[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/CreateDDCFileSubset.exe.html#configuration)
### Environment variables[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/CreateDDCFileSubset.exe.html#environment-variables)
####  `NW_DDC_TEXT_POINT_ENCODING`[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/CreateDDCFileSubset.exe.html#nw_ddc_text_point_encoding)
Configure encoding for writing TextPoint geometries. For available values see parameter `DDC:TextPointEncoding` in [Common Service Configuration Parameters](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Configuration/Common-Service-Configuration-Parameters.html).
## Return value[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/CreateDDCFileSubset.exe.html#return-value)  
| Value  | Meaning  |  
| --- | --- |  
| 0  | Success  |  
| 1  | Invalid parameters  |  
| 2  | Error during processing  |  
## G3E_FID file[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/CreateDDCFileSubset.exe.html#g3e_fid-file)
Text file with one G3E_FID per line.
**Example**
fids.txt

```
1028440
1262779
1338340
1338342
1338343
1338344
1338345

```

# CreateDDCFromShapefile.exe
Command line tool which reads one or more Shapefiles (.SHP) and creates a DDC/CDT pair of files. Each source Shapefile is transformed to one layer in the DDC. Optionally, a coordinate transformation is done during the conversion.
The tool is delivered in NetWorks Web Services _Program/Tools_ folder.
## Usage[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/CreateDDCFromShapefile.exe.html#usage)

```
CreateDDCFromShapefile.exe -i <input file or folder> -o <output DDC file> 
    [-s <sourcecs>] [-d <destcs>] [-c <configuration>]

```

### Options[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/CreateDDCFromShapefile.exe.html#options)
  * **`-i|--input <input SHP file or folder>`**  
Required. Source Shapefile file or folder path.
  * **`-o|--output <output DDC file>`**  
Required. Destination DDC file path.
  * **`-c|--configuration <configuration>`**  
NetWorks configuration. Used to determine target coordinate system. Can't be used together with -d.
  * **`-s|--sourcecs <sourcecs>`**  
Coordinate system file of source (.csf or .prj). Required if .prj or .csf file does not exist along a .shp file.
  * **`-d|--destcs <destcs>`**  
Coordinate system file of destination (.csf or .prj). Can't be used together with -c.

## Return value[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/CreateDDCFromShapefile.exe.html#return-value)  
| Value  | Meaning  |  
| --- | --- |  
| 0  | Success  |  
| 1  | Invalid parameters  |  
| 2  | Error during processing  |  
## Configuration[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/CreateDDCFromShapefile.exe.html#configuration)
The tool uses Common Platforms Coordinate System SDK from NetWorks. It is possible to override the location by setting environment variable NWCPSDK to alternative folder.

# Deploy.exe
`Deploy.exe` is command line deployment tool for deploying services based on NetWorks Configuration and/or Instance Names. It uses [Command line deployment tools](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/Command-line-deployment-tools.html) internally for deploying individual services.
## Usage[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/Deploy.exe.html#usage)
**Deploy.exe** [-c **< configuration>**] [-i **< instance-name>**] [-u] [-r] [-d **< deployment configuration path>**] [--package-path **< template package path>**] [-dc] [-ce]
### Options[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/Deploy.exe.html#options)  
| Switch  | Alias  | Mandatory  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| -c  | --configuration  |   | NetWorks Configuration.  |  
| -i  | --instance-name  |   | Service Instance Names, comma separated.  |  
| -u  | --undeploy  |   | Undeploy service.  |  
| -r  | --redeploy  |   | Redeploy service.  |  
| -d  | --deployment-configuration-path  |   | Path to alternative NetWorksDeployedServices.xml location.  |  
| -dc  | --disable-customization  |   | Disable post-deployment customization.  |  
|   | --package-path  |   | Path to service template packages location.  |  
| -ce  | --continue-on-error  |   | Continue deploying next service when error occurs.  |  
## Return value[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/Deploy.exe.html#return-value)  
| Value  | Meaning  |  
| --- | --- |  
| 0  | Success  |  
| 1  | Invalid parameters  |  
| 2  | Error during deployment  |  
## Deployment configuration[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/Deploy.exe.html#deployment-configuration)
Default deployment configuration path is `%ProgramData%\Intergraph\NetWorks\DeployedServices\`. This is where `NetWorksDeployedServices.xml` file is located. It is also possible to set [Common deployment settings](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Administration-Console/Common-deployment-settings.html) in `DeploymentConfig.ini` file there.
### Logging[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/Deploy.exe.html#logging)
File **Deploy.NLog.config**. By default, the tool logs activity at Trace level to Console, at Trace level to NetWorks logs folder.
For detailed logging configuration, create a JSON file named `Deploy.logging.json` in the folder containing `Deploy.exe` and configure listening to ETW sources. See [Diagnostics](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Diagnostics.html) for description of the format.

## Overview[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/ExecuteTrace.exe.html#overview)
`ExecuteTrace.exe` is command line tool for executing the trace as a standalone process. It shares the code base with the [Analytical Service](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Analytical-Service.html) and must therefore provide the same results. It is used internally by [Trace](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service/Workloads/Trace.html) workload of [Work Service](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Services/Work-Service.html), allowing trace execution to be run asynchronously.

### Options[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/ExecuteTrace.exe.html#options)  
| Switch  | Alias  | Mandatory  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| -i  | --input-file  | X  | JSON file with input parameters.  |  
| -c  | --connection-string  | X  | Connection string.  |  
| -o  | --output-path  | X  | Output file path.  |  
| -m  | --map-request-url  |   | URL to Map Request Service. Used for cost constraint traces.  |  
## Input[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/ExecuteTrace.exe.html#input)
Input JSON file follows the same structure as [ExecuteTrace](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/api/Analytical-Service/Trace/ExecuteTrace.html) POST body.
## Return value[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/ExecuteTrace.exe.html#return-value)  
| Value  | Meaning  |  
| --- | --- |  
| 0  | Success  |  
| 1  | Error executing the trace  |  
| 2  | Invalid parameters  |

# NetWorks Metadata system
Since version 02.00.2001, NetWorks supports the RAW format used for published metadata tables and also a new, human readable format for published metadata files. Published metadata RAW files can be converted to zipped XML format (serialized DataSet). ZIP files are stored in the same directory as RAW files. If ZIP files are used, conversion from RAW to ZIP must be done after **each** metadata publish to keep RAW and XML/ZIP files synchronized.
##### Note
Beginning with version 11.01.2201, metadata publish from Administration Console does not automatically convert RAW files to XML/ZIP. All ZIP files are from the published metadata folders to avoid usage of obsolete metadata.
There are two new tools available in the NetWorks Program folder:
  * [Raw2Zip.exe](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/NetWorks-Metadata-system/Raw2Zip.exe.html) Converts a RAW file or a folder to ZIP format.
  * [Raw2ZipConfig.exe](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/NetWorks-Metadata-system/Raw2ZipConfig.exe.html) Converts all published languages of a NetWorks configuration.

# PublishDataDDC.exe
Command line tool for publishing data to DDC files from component views in Oracle. The input is an UDB file.
This tool performs the same operation as _PublishMapFiles.exe_ with the following limitations:
  * No support for secondary not-imported data. Only component views in Oracle database are published.
  * CCM file is not changed after publish.
  * No incremental data publish. Only full publish is supported.

Improvements over _PublishMapFiles.exe_ :
  * Parallel processing.
  * Name of the UDB file doesn't have to match configuration name.

The tool is delivered in NetWorks Web Services _Program/Tools_ folder.
##### Note
This is an experimental tool. It is not yet considered to be stable enough for production use.
## Usage[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/PublishDataDDC.exe.html#usage)
**PublishDataDDC.exe** -c **< configuration>** -a **< alias>** -u **< user>** -p **< password>** -i **< Path to UDB file>** [-t **< parallelism>**]
### Options[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/PublishDataDDC.exe.html#options)  
| Parameter  | Alias  | Mandatory  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| -c  | --configuration  | X  | NetWorks configuration. Used to determine target coordinate system.  |  
| -a  | --alias  | X  | TNS alias of the database.  |  
| -u  | --user  | X  | Database user.  |  
| -p  | --password  |   | Database password.  |  
| -i  | --input  | X  | Path to UDB file.  |  
| -t  | --parallelism  |   | Maximum parallelism (number of threads). When not specified, defaults to 1.  |  
## Return value[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/PublishDataDDC.exe.html#return-value)  
| Value  | Meaning  |  
| --- | --- |  
| 0  | Success  |  
| 2  | Error during processing  |  
| 9  | Invalid parameters  |  
## Configuration[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/PublishDataDDC.exe.html#configuration)
The tool uses Common Platforms Coordinate System SDK from NetWorks. It is possible to override the location by setting environment variable `NWCPSDK` to alternative folder.
### Logging[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/PublishDataDDC.exe.html#logging)
File **PublishDataDDC.NLog.config**. By default, the tool logs activity at Warning level to Console, at Info level to NetWorks logs folder.
For detailed logging configuration, create or edit JSON file named `PublishDataDDC.logging.json` in the folder containing `PublishDataDDC.exe` and configure listening to ETW sources. See [Diagnostics](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Diagnostics.html) for description of the format.
## Examples[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/PublishDataDDC.exe.html#examples)

# PublishFonts.exe
Command line tool which creates a folder to be published on IIS and used by NetWorks Portal to render vector data coming from NetWorks Vector Service.
Since version 02.00.2002:
  * Publish font metrics JSON file

Since version 11.01.2401:
  * Input folder path with font files.
  * Export to JSON.

## Usage[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/PublishFonts.exe.html#usage)

```
PublishFonts.exe -c <configuration> [-o <output-folder>] [-i <input-folder>] [-s <css-file>] 
                [-f <formats>] [-ff <fonts-folder>] [-fm <font-metrics-file>] [-je <json-export-file>]

```

### Options[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/PublishFonts.exe.html#options)
  * **`-c|--configuration <configuration>`**
NetWorks configuration.
  * **`-o|--output-folder <output-folder>`**
Path to output folder.
  * **`-i|--input-folder <input-folder>`**
Path to folder with font files. Default value: System fonts folder
  * **`-s|--css-file <css-file>`**
CSS file name. Default is `fonts.css`.
  * **`-f|--formats <formats>`**
Font formats to include in CSS. Comma separated list of values.  
Allowed values: `truetype`, `opentype`, `woff`, `woff2`.  
Default value: `truetype`.
  * **`-ff|--fonts-folder <fonts-folder>`**
Path to folder which will contain the copied font files. The path is relative to **`<output-folder>`**.  
Default value: `fonts`.
  * **`-fm <font-metrics-file>`**
Path to font metrics JSON file. When specified, the tool processes all fonts referenced by styles in the selected configuration and publishes a font metrics JSON file.
  * **`-je <json-export-file>`**
Path to font JSON export file. When specified, the tool creates JSON file with all source font files included in created CSS file.

## Return value[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/PublishFonts.exe.html#return-value)  
| Value  | Meaning  |  
| --- | --- |  
| 0  | Success  |  
| 1  | Invalid parameters  |  
| 2  | Error during processing  |  
## Configuration[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/PublishFonts.exe.html#configuration)
The tool is configured using file **PublishFonts.exe.config**.
### Application settings[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/PublishFonts.exe.html#application-settings)  
| Name  | Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
| ExcludedFontNames  | Regular expression for matching font family names. Fonts with matching names are excluded from processing.  |  
| ExcludedFontNamesFile  | Path to a text file which contains a single line with a regular expression for matching font family names. Fonts with matching names are excluded from processing.  |  
| IncludedFontNamesFile  | Path to a text file which contains a single line with a regular expression for matching font family names. Fonts with matching names are included in processing. Fonts included in this list have priority over fonts in the exclusion lists.  |  
### Logging[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/PublishFonts.exe.html#logging)
Logging is configured in file **PublishFonts.exe.NLog.config**. By default, the tool logs activity at Info level to Console, at Trace level to NetWorks logs folder.
For detailed logging configuration, create a JSON file named `PublishFonts.exe.logging.json` or `logging.json` in the folder containing `PublishFonts.exe` and configure listening to ETW sources. See [Diagnostics](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Diagnostics.html) for description of the format.
## Requirements[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/PublishFonts.exe.html#requirements)
  * Determine list of fonts used by symbology in a NetWorks configuration (all legends) 
    * Each font is identified by name, weight (normal, bold), style (regular, italic)
    * At least the TTF file name is identified for each font
  * Create a CSS file with all `@font-face` references
  * Copy font files (only TTF) to output location together with CSS file

## Workflow 1 - publish CSS for fonts[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/PublishFonts.exe.html#workflow-1---publish-css-for-fonts)
  * Read list of fonts from published metadata table `G3E_STYLEOBJECTS_OPTABLE`
  * Determine list of unique fonts by name, bold and italic characteristics
  * Determine physical location of TTF file
  * Create output folder (if not exists)
  * Create CSS file
  * Copy TTF files to output folder

### Example[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/PublishFonts.exe.html#example)

```
PublishFonts.exe -c GINIUS -o c:\fonts -s fonts.css -f truetype,woff2 -ff fonts

```

## Workflow 2 - publish fonts metrics file[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/PublishFonts.exe.html#workflow-2---publish-fonts-metrics-file)
  * Read list of fonts from published metadata table `G3E_STYLEOBJECTS_OPTABLE`
  * Determine list of unique fonts by name, bold and italic characteristics
  * Determine physical location of TTF file
  * Create font metrics JSON file

### Example[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/PublishFonts.exe.html#example-1)

```
PublishFonts.exe -c GINIUS -fm c:\assets\font-metrics.json

```

## Notes[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/PublishFonts.exe.html#notes)
### Conversion to WOFF and WOFF2 formats[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/PublishFonts.exe.html#conversion-to-woff-and-woff2-formats)
Published TTF files can be converted to other formats (WOFF, WOFF2) using a tool like [fonttools](https://github.com/fonttools/fonttools).
#### Workflow[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/PublishFonts.exe.html#workflow)
  * Setup environment 
    * Install **fonttools** together with Optional requirements
    * Add path to Python to PATH environment variable
  * Create a new text file named **ttf2woff.bat** in 
```
FOR %%F IN (*.ttf) DO ttx %%F 
FOR %%F IN (*.ttx) DO ttx --flavor woff %%F

```

  * Create a new text file named ttf2woff2.bat in 
```
FOR %%F IN (*.ttf) DO ttx %%F 
FOR %%F IN (*.ttx) DO ttx --flavor woff2 %%F

```

  * Run **ttf2woff.bat** and/or **ttf2woff2.bat**

## Excluding and including specific fonts from publishing[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/PublishFonts.exe.html#excluding-and-including-specific-fonts-from-publishing)
Some fonts can't be published to the web due to **license restrictions**. _PublishFonts.exe_ supports configurable blacklist of font family names which are excluded from processing - see application settings `ExcludedFontNames`, `ExcludedFontNamesFile` and `IncludedFontNamesFile`.
**PublishFonts.excluded.txt example** :
Text file with content as below, located at `%ProgramData%\Intergraph\NetWorks\PublishFonts.excluded.txt` will exclude all fonts with prefix `Segoe UI` or named `Tahoma` from processing.

```
Segoe UI.*|Tahoma

```

**PublishFonts.included.txt example** :
Text file with content as below, located at `%ProgramData%\Intergraph\NetWorks\PublishFonts.included.txt` will include all fonts with prefix `Arial` in processing.

```
Arial.*

```

# PublishWSMetadata.exe
Command line tool to republish Networks metadata published in RAW files to DDC/CDT metadata file.
## Usage[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/PublishWSMetadata.exe.html#usage)

```
PublishWSMetadata.exe -c <configuration> [-l <lcid>] [-o <output path>]

```

### Options[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/PublishWSMetadata.exe.html#options)
  * **`-c|--configuration <configuration>`**  
NetWorks configuration name.
  * `-l|--lang <lcid>`  
LCID to export. If not specified, export is done for all currently published LCIDs. When  is specified, this parameter is mandatory if the metadata is published for more than one LCID, otherwise the tool doesn't know which language to export.
  * `-o|--output <output path>`  
Path to output DDC file or folder which contains the DDC file. If not specified, the file (`WSMetadata.ddc`) is created in the same folder as currently published metadata.

## Return value[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/PublishWSMetadata.exe.html#return-value)  
| Value  | Meaning  |  
| --- | --- |  
| 0  | Success  |  
| 1  | Configuration error  |  
| 2  | Runtime error  |  
## Internal Workflow[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/PublishWSMetadata.exe.html#internal-workflow)
For each LCID:
  * Run [PublishAttributeTypes.exe](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/PublishAttributeTypes.exe.html) to create `G3E_ATTRIBUTEDATATYPE.XML` in temp folder. This file contains data type information for attributes.
  * Open G3E_ADDON_OPTABLE metadata table and read `G3E_OPTIMIZEDTABLE` values for rows, where `G3E_NAME IN ('NetWorks', 'GTDWS')`. This list is configurable in the tool's config file.
  * Open the metadata tables referenced in previous step and for each row: 
    * Read optimized table name from `G3E_OPTIMIZEDTABLE`.
    * Run [Raw2Zip.exe](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/NetWorks-Metadata-system/Raw2Zip.exe.html) for the file (input is the RAW file, output is .XML file path in a temp folder, with `--no-zip` parameter).
  * Run [PublishMetadataDDC.exe](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/PublishMetadataDDC.exe.html) for all .XML files created in previous steps.

# RunCustomization.exe
Command line tool for performing post-[Deployment customization](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Administration-Console/Deployment-customization.html) of configuration files.
## Usage[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/RunCustomization.exe.html#usage)
**RunCustomization.exe** -d **< deployment path>** -c **< customization path>** [-s **< configuration path>**]
### Options[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/RunCustomization.exe.html#options)  
| Switch  | Alias  | Mandatory  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| -d  | --deploy-path  | Y  | Path to folder where the service or Portal is physically deployed.  |  
| -c  | --customization-path  | Y  | Path to file or folder with customization.  |  
| -s  | --settings-path  |   | Path to folder with service configuration files.  |  
## Return value[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/RunCustomization.exe.html#return-value)  
| Value  | Meaning  |  
| --- | --- |  
| 0  | Success  |  
| 1  | Invalid parameters  |  
| 2  | Error during processing  |  
## Configuration[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/RunCustomization.exe.html#configuration)
None.
### Logging[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/RunCustomization.exe.html#logging)
File **RunCustomization.NLog.config**. By default, the tool logs activity at Trace level to Console, at Trace level to NetWorks logs folder.
For detailed logging configuration, create a JSON file named `RunCustomization.logging.json` in the folder containing `RunCustomization.exe` and configure listening to ETW sources. See [Diagnostics](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Diagnostics.html) for description of the format.

# ServiceBenchmarkTest.exe
Command line tool for benchmarking Web Service performance simulating parallel requests from clients.
The tool starts `-t` parallel threads and makes a total of `-n` requests to the service.
The tool can replace placeholders in the URL and/or the request payload using these types of value generators:
  * Data file (DA)  
Source of data is a text file. Each line is a comma (or other) separated list of values. The file is traversed in circular way and each request is parameterized with data from the current line.
  * Random extent generator (EX)  
A random extent (minx, miny, maxx, maxy) is selected from the provided world range. The width and height of the extent in world units is specified. Optionally, also the screen size in pixels for tests which require resolution value or pixel size.
  * Random tile generator (TM)  
Generate random tile from a WMTS-compatible tile matrix. The configurable options are tile matrix origin, width/height of the tile, scale denominator.

## Requirements[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/ServiceBenchmarkTest.exe.html#requirements)
  * [.NET 8.0 Runtime](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/8.0)

## Usage[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/ServiceBenchmarkTest.exe.html#usage)
**ServiceBenchmarkTest.exe** -u **< service-url>** [-t **< number-of-threads>**] [-n **< number-of-requests>**] [-b **< world-range>**] [-w **< world-width>**] [-h **< world-height>**] [-x **< pixel-width>**] [-y **< pixel-height>**] [-o **< origin>**] [-s **< scale-denominator>**] [-c **< crs-units-per-meter>**] [--request-log <path-to-file>] [--authorization <authorization header>] [--no-response-compression]
### Options[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/ServiceBenchmarkTest.exe.html#options)  
| Switch  | Alias  | Mandatory  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| -u  | --url  | Y  | Service URL, e.g. `http://server/wms`  |  
| -t  | --threads  |   | Number of parallel threads. Default is `1`.  |  
| -n  | --number-of-requests  |   | Total number of requests. Default is `1`.  |  
| -r  | --request  |   | Request payload file path.  |  
| -b  | --world-range  | EX, TM  | Extent in world coordinates in which the requests will be made. Must match the coordinate system of the service. Formatted as string `minx,miny,maxx,maxy`, with `.` as decimal separator.  |  
| -w  | --world-width  | EX  | Width of the requested bounding box in projection units.  |  
| -h  | --world-height  |   | Height of the requested bounding box in projection units. When not provided, equals to world width.  |  
| -x  | --pixel-width  | TM  | Width of the requested bounding box in screen units (pixels) or tile width in pixels.  |  
| -y  | --pixel-height  |   | Height of the requested bounding box in screen units (pixels) or tile height in pixels. When not provided, equals to screen width.  |  
| -o  | --origin  | TM  | Tile matrix origin (top-left corner). Must match the coordinate system of the service. Formatted as string `x,y`, with `.` as decimal separator.  |  
| -s  | --scale-denominator  | TM  | Display scale denominator for given tile matrix.  |  
| -c  | --crs-units-per-meter  |   | Coordinate system units per meter. Defaults to 1.  |  
| -f  | --data-file  | DA  | Data file path.  |  
| -d  | --delay  |   | Delay between requests in milliseconds.  |  
| -v  | --verb  |   | HTTP verb (GET, POST). If `-r` is specified, defaults to `POST`, otherwise `GET`.  |  
|   | --media-type  |   | Request media type. When not present, automatically determined from Request payload file extension (`.json` -> `application/json`, `.xml` -> `application/xml`).  |  
|   | --data-file-separator  |   | Separator of values in data file. If not present, default is `,`.  |  
|   | --request-log  |   | Path to request log file.  |  
|   | --log-request-body  |   | Turn on logging of request bodies to request log file.  |  
|   | --authorization  |   | Content of the HTTP Authorization header.  |  
|   | --no-response-compression  |   | Turn off requesting HTTP response compression.  |  
## URL Template[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/ServiceBenchmarkTest.exe.html#url-template)
Parameter `-u` and there request payload file content (`-f`) may contain placeholders which are replaced by actual values when the request is made.
Allowed placeholders are:
## Random extent[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/ServiceBenchmarkTest.exe.html#random-extent)  
| Placeholder  | Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
| [[X1]]  | Minimum X coordinate of the random extent.  |  
| [[Y1]]  | Minimum Y coordinate of the random extent.  |  
| [[X2]]  | Maximum X coordinate of the random extent.  |  
| [[Y2]]  | Maximum Y coordinate of the random extent.  |  
| [[RESOLUTION]]  | Resolution of the random extent (ground units / screen units).  |  
| [[SW]]  | Screen (pixel) width.  |  
| [[SH]]  | Screen (pixel) height.  |  
## Random tile[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/ServiceBenchmarkTest.exe.html#random-tile)  
| Placeholder  | Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
| [[ROW]]  | Tile row.  |  
| [[COL]]  | Tile column.  |  
## Data file[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/ServiceBenchmarkTest.exe.html#data-file)  
| Placeholder  | Description  |  
| --- | --- |  
| [[P{index}]]  | Replaced by `{index}`-th item in the current for of the data file. `{index}` is 0-based.  |  
## Output[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/ServiceBenchmarkTest.exe.html#output)
The tool outputs intermediate results to the console output and a total line after the run completes.  
| Column  | Unit  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| Requests  | 1  | Number of requests made so far.  |  
| RPS  | requests per second  | Number of requests completed per second.  |  
| RespTotalBytes  | byte  | Total number of bytes received from service.  |  
| RespAvgBytes  | byte  | Average number of bytes received per request.  |  
| RespAvgDur  | ms  | Average duration of request.  |  
| Errors  | 1  | Number of errors (since last reading).  |

## Usage examples[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/ServiceBenchmarkTest.exe.html#usage-examples)
### WMS GetMap with random extent[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/ServiceBenchmarkTest.exe.html#wms-getmap-with-random-extent)
  * WMS Service available at `https://server/WmsElectric/wms`.
  * Coordinate range: lower left `4500959, 5924807`, upper right `4503663, 5927323`.
  * Bounding box size: 100m x 100m
  * Screen box size: 2048px x 2048px
  * Total number of requests: 10000
  * Parallel requests: 32

```
ServiceBenchmarkTest.exe -t 32 -n 10000 -w 100 -x 2048 -b "4500959, 5924807, 4503663, 5927323" -u https://server/WmsElectric/wms?SERVICE=WMS&VERSION=1.3.0&REQUEST=GetMap&FORMAT=image/png&TRANSPARENT=true&LAYERS=HIGH_VOLTAGE,MIDDLE_VOLTAGE,LOW_VOLTAGE&CRS=EPSG:5678&STYLES=&WIDTH=[[SW]]&HEIGHT=[[SH]]&BBOX=[[X1]],[[Y1]],[[X2]],[[Y2]] --request-log c:\temp\request.log

```

### WMS GetMap with random extent and OIDC authorization[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/ServiceBenchmarkTest.exe.html#wms-getmap-with-random-extent-and-oidc-authorization)
  * Parameters as in Example 1
  * Requests are authorized using the provided OpenID Connect access token.

```
ServiceBenchmarkTest.exe -t 32 -n 10000 -w 100 -x 2048 -b "4500959, 5924807, 4503663, 5927323" -u https://server/WmsElectric/wms?SERVICE=WMS&VERSION=1.3.0&REQUEST=GetMap&FORMAT=image/png&TRANSPARENT=true&LAYERS=HIGH_VOLTAGE,MIDDLE_VOLTAGE,LOW_VOLTAGE&CRS=EPSG:5678&STYLES=&WIDTH=[[SW]]&HEIGHT=[[SH]]&BBOX=[[X1]],[[Y1]],[[X2]],[[Y2]] --authorization "Bearer eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsIn..."

```

**How to create request.json file for testing Vector Service /data endpoint**
  * Open a browser and go to the NetWorks Portal with Vector Service in the legend. Select the legend entries which you want to use for testing.
  * Open the browser (Chrome, Edge) Developer tools (F12) and the Network tab.
  * Move the map to force a request to the Vector Service.
  * Look for the request in the Network tab - the URL ends with `/data`.
  * Copy the Request payload - since Chrome 95 found on the _Payload_ tab.
  * Create a JSON file in a text editor and paste the content into a file.
  * Set `bbox` property value to `[ [[X1]],[[Y1]],[[X2]],[[Y2]] ]`.
  * Set `resolution` property value to `[[RESOLUTION]]`.
  * Save the file as `.json` file.

## Request log file[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/ServiceBenchmarkTest.exe.html#request-log-file)
The request log file is an optional text file into which the tool logs one line for each request, formatted as:
`{URL} {HTTP status code} {Response size in bytes}`
**Example**

```

https://server/WmsElectric/wms?SERVICE=WMS&VERSION=1.3.0&REQUEST=GetMap&FORMAT=image/png&TRANSPARENT=true&LAYERS=HIGH_VOLTAGE,MIDDLE_VOLTAGE,LOW_VOLTAGE&CRS=EPSG:5678&STYLES=&WIDTH=2048&HEIGHT=2048&BBOX=4501344.78487409,5927118.558619009,4501444.78487409,5927218.558619009 200 22246

```

# VectorServiceBenchmarkTest.exe
Command line tool for benchmarking Vector Service performance simulating parallel requests from clients.
The tool starts `-t` parallel threads and makes a total of `-n` requests to the service. The requests use a single request definition (`-r`, request file). Data bounding box is selected randomly for each request within the specified range of world coordinates. The configurable options are width/height of the bounding box in projection units (e.g. meters) and the width/height of the screen units (e.g. pixels), required to compute the correct resolution and scale. By changing these values it is possible to simulate different usage scenarios.
## Requirements[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/VectorServiceBenchmarkTest.exe.html#requirements)
  * [.NET 8.0 Runtime](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/8.0)

## Usage[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/VectorServiceBenchmarkTest.exe.html#usage)
**VectorServiceBenchmarkTest.exe** -u **< service-url>** -r **< request-file>** -t **< number-of-threads>** -n **< number-of-requests>** -b **< world-range>** -w **< world-width>** [-h **< world-height>**] -x **< screen-width>** [-y **< screen-height>**] [--request-log <path-to-file>] [--authorization <authorization header>] [--no-response-compression]
### Options[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/VectorServiceBenchmarkTest.exe.html#options)  
| Switch  | Alias  | Mandatory  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| -u  | --url  | Y  | Service URL, e.g. http://server/vectorservice1  |  
| -r  | --request  | Y  | Path to request file.  |  
| -t  | --threads  |   | Number of parallel threads. Default is `1`.  |  
| -n  | --number-of-requests  |   | Total number of requests. Default is `1`.  |  
| -b  | --world-range  | Y  | Extent in world coordinates in which the requests will be made. Must match the coordinate system of the service. Formatted as string `minx,miny,maxx,maxy`, with `.` as decimal separator.  |  
| -w  | --world-width  | Y  | Width of the requested bounding box in projection units.  |  
| -h  | --world-height  |   | Height of the requested bounding box in projection units. When not provided, equals to world width.  |  
| -x  | --pixel-width  | Y  | Width of the requested bounding box in screen units (pixels). Used to compute resolution and scale.  |  
| -y  | --pixel-height  |   | Height of the requested bounding box in screen units (pixels). When not provided, equals to screen width.  |  
|   | --request-log  |   | Path to request log file.  |  
|   | --authorization  |   | Content of the HTTP Authorization header.  |  
|   | --no-response-compression  |   | Turn off requesting HTTP response compression.  |  
## Request file[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/VectorServiceBenchmarkTest.exe.html#request-file)
The request file (parameter `-r`) is a JSON file with specification of the legend requested from the Vector Service. The content of the file is the request made towards Vector Service when retrieving map data.
`lsno` and `entries` are fixed and specify the G3E_LSNO and G3E_LENOs to be retrieved in the requests. `bbox` and `resolution` are set dynamically by the test tool.
### How to create request file[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/VectorServiceBenchmarkTest.exe.html#how-to-create-request-file)
  * Open a browser and go to the NetWorks Portal with Vector Service in the legend. Select the legend entries which you want to use for testing.
  * Open the browser (Chrome, Edge) Developer tools (F12) and the Network tab.
  * Move the map to force a request to the Vector Service.
  * Look for the request in the Network tab - the URL ends with `/data`.
  * Copy the Request payload - since Chrome 95 found on the _Payload_ tab.
  * Create a JSON file in a text editor and paste the content into a file.

### Example request file[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/VectorServiceBenchmarkTest.exe.html#example-request-file)

```
{
    "lsno": 7,
    "bbox": [1339084.5116740686, 7068933.4419316985, 1339231.0316003289, 7069021.178414488],
    "resolution": 0.09748498087863537,
    "entries": [{
            "l": 2620060
        }, {
            "l": 2620260
        }, {
            "l": 262060
        }, {
            "l": 262460
        }, {
            "l": 2600060
        }, {
            "l": 2600160
        }, {
            "l": 2600260
        }, {
            "l": 260060
        }, {
            "l": 260460
        }, {
            "l": 2460060
        }
    ],
    "filters": null
}

```

## Output[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/VectorServiceBenchmarkTest.exe.html#output)
The tool outputs intermediate results to the console output and a total line after the run completes.  
| Column  | Unit  | Description  |  
| --- | --- | --- |  
| Requests  | 1  | Number of requests made so far.  |  
| RPS  | requests per second  | Number of requests completed per second.  |  
| RespTotalBytes  | byte  | Total number of bytes received from service.  |  
| RespAvgBytes  | byte  | Average number of bytes received per request.  |  
| RespAvgDur  | ms  | Average duration of request.  |  
| Errors  | 1  | Number of errors (since last reading).  |  
**Example**

```
        Requests             RPS  RespTotalBytes    RespAvgBytes      RespAvgDur          Errors
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Usage examples[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/VectorServiceBenchmarkTest.exe.html#usage-examples)
### Basic scenario[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/VectorServiceBenchmarkTest.exe.html#basic-scenario)
  * Vector Service available at `https://server1/VectorService1`.
  * Coordinate range: lower left `4500959, 5924807`, upper right `4503663, 5927323`.
  * Bounding box size: 100m x 100m
  * Screen box size: 2048px x 2048px
  * Total number of requests: 10000
  * Parallel requests: 32

`VectorServiceBenchmarkTest.exe -t 32 -n 10000 -w 100 -x 2048 -b "4500959, 5924807, 4503663, 5927323" -r C:\benchmarks\request.json -u https://server1/VectorService1 --request-log c:\temp\request.log`
### Basic scenario with OIDC authorization[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/VectorServiceBenchmarkTest.exe.html#basic-scenario-with-oidc-authorization)
  * Parameters as in Example 1
  * Requests are authorized using the provided OpenID Connect access token.

`VectorServiceBenchmarkTest.exe -t 32 -n 10000 -w 100 -x 2048 -b "4500959, 5924807, 4503663, 5927323" -r C:\benchmarks\request.json -u https://server1/VectorService1 --authorization "Bearer eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsIn..."`
## Request log file[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/techdoc/Tools/VectorServiceBenchmarkTest.exe.html#request-log-file)

# Technical Support and Information
Hexagon Safety & Infrastructure provides several ways to access information and to contact support, including self-help tools and phone support.
## Self-Help Support Tools[](https://pra-sgiv-mlg403/networksfoundationdoc/doc/TechnicalSupport.html#self-help-support-tools)
Hexagon provides several electronic self-help support tools to answer your support questions 24/7.
  1. Go to the [Support page](https://supportsi.hexagon.com/).
  2. Under the **Please Sign In** heading, type your username and password and click **Login**. If you are not a registered user, click the Not a Registered User? link under the Login section.
  3. Click the **Products** tab.
  4. From the Products list, click the link to your product.
  5. On the product page, click the product release you want to view.
  6. On the product release page, click the document you want to read: 
     * To read about new or enhanced features, click **Release Notes**.
     * To read about defects that have been fixed, click **Issues Resolved**.
     * To read about system requirements, click **Supported Environments**.

**Release Notes** and **Issues Resolved** might not be available for the initial release of a product because an initial release has all new features and no updated features. Some minor releases might not provide **Release Notes** or **Issues Resolved**.
**Phone Numbers**
For worldwide support, please contact your [local Hexagon office](https://supportsi.hexagon.com/help/s/contactsupport?language=en_US).

### troubleshooting

#### Database

# ORA-29283 when running Database Upgrade Wizard
**Symptoms**
Database Upgrade Wizard fails on error:

```
Validates the required metadata
BEGIN ADM_LEGENDBUILDERMETADATA.ValidateMetadata; END;

*
ERROR at line 1:
ORA-29283: invalid file operation 
ORA-06512: at "SYS.UTL_FILE", line 536 
ORA-29283: invalid file operation 
ORA-06512: at "SYS.UTL_FILE", line 41 
ORA-06512: at "SYS.UTL_FILE", line 478 
ORA-06512: at "GTSCHEMA.ADM_LEGENDBUILDERMETADATA", line 156 
ORA-06512: at "GTSCHEMA.ADM_LEGENDBUILDERMETADATA", line 55 
ORA-06512: at line 1

```

**Cause**
The `ADM_LEGENDBUILDERMETADATA` tries to write log file but fails. The default location is `C:\temp\mdval_lb.txt`. It can be overridden by setting `DatabaseLocalDirectory` in `G3E_GENERALPARAMETER`. This value points to disk folder or it contains the name of an Oracle DIRECTORY object.
**Workaround**
  1. Check the `DatabaseLocalDirectory` in `G3E_GENERALPARAMETER` and determine the log folder path.
  2. Create an empty text file `mdval_lb.txt` in the folder.
  3. Set read/write access rights to the folder and the file for the OS user under which the Oracle service is running.
  4. Resume the Database Upgrade Wizard.
